trials.t: Phase 2 Pilot Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Topical MW-III in Thermal Burns
trials.ep: Time to healing (at least 95% re-epithelialization) of the partial-thickness target burn within the 28-day treatment period

fable.r: With only about 30 patients per arm, the trial would need MW-III to nearly double the healing rate against silver sulfadiazine to reach significance, well beyond the effect seen for MEBO-type ointments in earlier controlled trials.

opus.r: A 60-patient pilot with a time-to-healing endpoint has little power to show a modest healing-speed gain over silver sulfadiazine, even if MW-III is somewhat faster.

sonnet.r: A 60-patient pilot against silver sulfadiazine gives little power unless the healing effect is large; recruitment since 2022 has been slow and a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: A 60-patient pilot with 30 per arm shows a healing gain only if the effect is large, and recruitment open since 2022 suggests the trial may end without a clear readout.

carbon.r: With only 30 patients per arm, this pilot study is severely underpowered to detect realistic accelerations in re-epithelialization over silver sulfadiazine.

sol.r: Silver sulfadiazine leaves room for faster healing, but a 60-patient pilot may not distinguish a modest benefit from variation in burn depth and healing time.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Alpha1-Proteinase Inhibitor (Human), Modified Process (Alpha-1 MP) in Subjects With Pulmonary Emphysema Due to Alpha1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD)
trials.c: Pulmonary Emphysema in Alpha-1 PI Deficiency
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 156 in whole-lung CT density at the 15th percentile (PD15)

fable.r: The CT-density benefit of augmentation is real but small against between-patient noise, so a weaker-than-RAPID effect or extra noise from 12 years of multi-country scanning could leave the difference short of significance.

opus.r: CT densitometry is noisy (inspiration level, scanner changes over 3 years) and placebo decline may be slower than assumed, so a real but small density benefit could miss significance.

sonnet.r: RAPID's CT density effect (p=0.03) was modest and likely overestimated; with about 115 per arm and a 3-year PD15 endpoint, a true effect somewhat below RAPID would leave power near 50-60%, helped by two active doses.

haiku.r: The CT density effect of a weekly augmentation dose over three years is small relative to measurement noise, so a 115-patient arm may miss the superiority test even if the product works.

carbon.r: Three years of weekly intravenous infusions carry notable patient attrition that could dilute treatment differences or increase missing CT densitometry data.

sol.r: A structural treatment effect is plausible, but CT-density measurement variability and attrition could obscure a modest difference over three years.

trials.t: An Efficacy and Safety Study of JNJ-56021927 (Apalutamide) in High-risk Prostate Cancer Subjects Receiving Primary Radiation Therapy: ATLAS
trials.ep: Metastasis-free survival (distant metastasis on conventional imaging by blinded central review, or death), follow-up up to 108 months

fable.r: Patients given radiotherapy plus 30 months of GnRH agonist already have few metastases and many non-cancer deaths, so the added effect of apalutamide on MFS may be near a hazard ratio of 0.8 and miss significance, as in ENZARAD.

opus.r: The comparator already gets GnRH agonist plus bicalutamide and radiotherapy, so metastasis and death events are rare and partly non-cancer deaths, diluting the apalutamide advantage.

sonnet.r: Adding a potent androgen receptor inhibitor to RT plus ADT in high-risk disease is likely to cut metastasis or death, but the long-delayed event-driven readout suggests few events and a possibly smaller effect than in metastatic or nmCRPC settings.

haiku.r: Radiotherapy plus GnRH agonist already controls most distant disease, so the apalutamide increment must show against an event rate near 18 percent at five years; sample size is adequate for a hazard ratio near 0.75.

carbon.r: Over nearly a decade of follow-up in older localized prostate cancer patients, competing non-cancer deaths can substantially dilute the metastasis-free survival hazard ratio.

sol.r: Radiation plus prolonged androgen deprivation leaves fewer preventable metastases, while competing non-cancer deaths can dilute the benefit of additional androgen-receptor blockade.

trials.t: A Study to Check the Safety of Dexlansoprazole and Learn if it Can Treat Symptomatic Nonerosive Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease in Children 2 to 11 Years Old
trials.ep: Percentage of Days Without Hurting or Burning in the Stomach, Chest or Throat Over the 12 Weeks of Treatment

fable.r: Completed pediatric study from a sponsor that routinely posts results; posting is expected around the July 2027 due date, with a possible delay certification or late submission the main uncertainty for the 31 August 2027 read.

opus.r: Completed Takeda pediatric PREA study; results likely posted on ClinicalTrials.gov around the one-year deadline (July 2027), with little reason to stop or rewrite the primary outcome.

sonnet.r: Descriptive pediatric phase 2 already completed; Takeda normally posts results within the 12-month window after primary completion (July 2027), so posting by end of August 2027 is likely, and primary outcomes are unlikely to change.

haiku.r: A completed pediatric phase 2 with a registered results duty, so the likely path is a posted results summary and no change to its descriptive primary outcome.

carbon.r: This completed pediatric Phase 2 GERD study by Takeda has passed its July 2026 completion date and is very likely to post summary results on ClinicalTrials.gov within roughly one year.

sol.r: The completed pediatric dose-ranging study is likely to post descriptive results near its one-year reporting deadline, with little risk of a subsequent stop or substantive endpoint change.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study of Pacritinib in Patients With Primary Myelofibrosis, Post Polycythemia Vera Myelofibrosis, or Post-Essential Thrombocythemia Myelofibrosis
trials.c: Primary Myelofibrosis; Post-polycythemia Vera Myelofibrosis; Post-essential Thrombocythemia Myelofibrosis
trials.ep: Proportion achieving at least 35% spleen volume reduction from baseline by MRI or CT at week 24

fable.r: Spleen response should be met comfortably, but the second listed primary, 50% symptom-score reduction at week 24, may miss because low-dose ruxolitinib in the control arm improves symptoms and pacritinib's symptom effect has been inconsistent.

opus.r: Spleen response should clearly favour pacritinib, but the second primary (TSS50 at week 24) is noisy and the physician's-choice arm, including low-dose ruxolitinib, can improve symptoms, so the symptom co-primary may miss.

sonnet.r: SVR35 should be met easily versus physician's choice, but the co-primary TSS50 was not significant in PERSIST-2 (25% vs 14%, p=0.08); both must be met, and low-dose ruxolitinib in control could narrow the gap.

haiku.r: The spleen co-primary should separate the arms, but the symptom co-primary (50 percent cut in total symptom score at week 24) can fail in this open-label design, and both must be met.

carbon.r: Meeting both registered primary endpoints requires statistically significant Week-24 symptom reduction alongside spleen volume response despite high early dropout and open-label control reporting.

sol.r: Spleen responses should separate clearly, but the co-primary symptom response is less certain and may be diluted by advanced disease and treatment discontinuation.

trials.t: A Clinical Efficacy and Safety Study of OHB-607 in Preventing Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in Extremely Premature Infants
trials.c: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia; Chronic Lung Disease of Prematurity; Intraventricular Hemorrhage
trials.ep: Severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (modified NICHD grading) at 36 weeks postmenstrual age, or death at or before 36 weeks PMA

fable.r: The BPD benefit rests on a secondary finding from a small phase 2 trial that missed its primary endpoint, so the true reduction in severe BPD or death is probably smaller than the roughly 11 points this trial needs.

opus.r: The BPD signal from the earlier phase 2 was a secondary finding in a small trial; a smaller true effect on severe BPD or death cannot reach significance with about 148 infants per arm.

sonnet.r: BPD-or-death at 36 weeks has repeatedly resisted drug prevention; with about 148 per arm and roughly 38% control incidence, an absolute reduction of about 11 points is needed for significance, above the modest effect likely.

haiku.r: Death or severe BPD at 36 weeks is hard to move in extremely preterm infants, and about 148 infants per arm can detect only a sizable risk difference, so a benefit under about 8 points would likely be missed.

carbon.r: The secondary BPD signal from the prior Phase 2a ROP trial may regress substantially toward the null in a larger multicenter extremely preterm cohort.

sol.r: The earlier BPD signal was secondary, and including death may substantially shrink the apparent lung benefit in this very high-risk population.

trials.t: Study to Explore the Therapeutic Effect of Eluxadoline in Treating Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Diarrhea in Children
trials.ep: Change from baseline in stool consistency (Pediatric Bristol Stool Form Scale, 1-7) averaged over the 4-week treatment period

fable.r: A four-week exploratory dose-ranging study with patients spread over several dose and age groups has little power against the high placebo response typical of pediatric functional bowel trials, and may report no formal test at all.

opus.r: Pediatric functional GI trials have high placebo responses on diary-based stool scores, and with several dose arms the per-arm sample is small, so a modest eluxadoline effect is unlikely to separate.

sonnet.r: Mu-opioid agonism should firm stools, but a dose-ranging pediatric phase 2 splits 272 patients over several arms, enrolment was cut short in the older group, and placebo response is large; the study is labelled exploratory.

haiku.r: Adult eluxadoline effects on stool consistency were modest, and a four-week pediatric dose-ranging trial with about 136 per arm has limited power for a small difference, so a small or null result is likely.

carbon.r: Large placebo responses in pediatric functional gastrointestinal trials combined with small per-dose sample sizes make statistical separation on stool consistency difficult.

sol.r: A substantial pediatric placebo response could overwhelm a modest stool-consistency effect, especially after enrollment is divided across doses and age cohorts.

trials.t: A Study of Pazopanib With or Without Abexinostat in Patients With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma (RENAVIV)
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review committee (RECIST 1.1) or death, up to about 4 years

fable.r: The sponsor has limited resources and has been recruiting since 2018, so the trial may stop or never reach its event target; if analysed, adding an HDAC inhibitor to pazopanib is unlikely to give a large PFS gain.

opus.r: HDAC inhibitors have no randomized proof of benefit in RCC; abexinostat's added PFS benefit over pazopanib is likely small and toxicity may limit dose intensity.

sonnet.r: An HDAC inhibitor added to pazopanib has only single-arm phase 1b/2 support, TKI add-on phase 3 trials mostly fail, and the combination adds toxicity; the sponsor is small and the trial is slow, so reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Abexinostat adds toxicity to a pazopanib control with about ten months of progression-free survival, and slow recruitment since 2018 suggests the trial may stop or read out late.

carbon.r: Adding HDAC inhibition with abexinostat to pazopanib increases hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity, forcing dose interruptions and discontinuations that undermine combination efficacy.

sol.r: An uncontrolled early signal may not translate into an incremental PFS benefit, and HDAC-related toxicity can reduce delivery of an already effective VEGF inhibitor.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Cariprazine in the Treatment of Adolescent Participants (13 to 17 Years of Age) With Schizophrenia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at week 6

fable.r: Placebo response in adolescent schizophrenia trials is large and variable, and with about 110 patients per arm recruited over seven years across many countries a 5-6 point PANSS difference could miss significance.

opus.r: Adolescent schizophrenia trials, especially at Eastern European and Latin American sites, show large placebo responses that can swamp a 5-7 point PANSS drug effect.

sonnet.r: Cariprazine has a robust adult schizophrenia effect (about 7 PANSS points), but adolescent trials run large placebo responses and sites in Eastern Europe and Latin America add noise; multiple doses help the chance of at least one hit.

haiku.r: A large placebo response in adolescent schizophrenia trials can narrow the gap, and recruitment still open in 2026 after a 2019 start points to a late readout or an early stop.

carbon.r: Substantial placebo improvement on the PANSS scale across multinational adolescent psychiatry sites frequently narrows drug-placebo separation below statistical significance.

sol.r: Cariprazine should retain antipsychotic activity in adolescents, but a large and variable placebo PANSS improvement could prevent a clear six-week separation.

trials.t: A Study of Nivolumab Combined With Ipilimumab Versus Nivolumab Alone in Participants With Advanced Kidney Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review

fable.r: Ipilimumab's incremental benefit over nivolumab alone is probably modest (hazard ratio about 0.85, about 10 points of response), too small for about 440 patients to show on both PFS and response rate.

opus.r: Ipilimumab's added benefit over nivolumab alone may be modest for PFS (HR ~0.8), and both PFS and ORR must succeed; with ~437 patients and split alpha the PFS primary could miss.

sonnet.r: Adding ipilimumab to nivolumab probably raises response and PFS, but both PFS and ORR must be significant, and the incremental benefit over nivolumab alone may be modest (cf. melanoma, where PFS HR was about 0.88).

haiku.r: Both co-primaries must be met by the same arm; the response-rate co-primary is the likelier miss if the ipilimumab add-on effect over nivolumab alone is modest.

carbon.r: With N=437 and two listed primary endpoints (PFS and ORR), modest sample size and potential co-primary multiplicity hurdles could prevent both from reaching formal significance.

sol.r: Nivolumab alone has meaningful first-line activity, so the incremental ipilimumab benefit may be insufficient to satisfy both PFS and response co-primary objectives.

trials.t: A Study to Compare Safety and Efficacy of High Doses of Eteplirsen in Participants With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) (MIS51ON)
trials.ep: Part 1: Incidence of Adverse Events (AEs)

fable.r: Last 144-week visits fall around the registered October 2026 date, so the record should move to completed, with results posted near the 12-month deadline, after the read date.

opus.r: Large-sponsor phase 3 already past enrolment and at its registered primary completion; it should run to completion, with results posting more likely near the 12-month FDAAA deadline than before August 2027.

sonnet.r: Fully enrolled phase 3 near its registered October 2026 primary completion; Sarepta tends to post results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is possible but unlikely, and a small clean-up of the three primary outcomes is the main amendment risk.

haiku.r: Primary completion passed in October 2026 with the trial closed to enrolment, so the open questions are whether results are posted within the one-year window and whether the interim efficacy outcome is dropped from the primary list.

carbon.r: As an active, non-recruiting industry Phase 3 study reaching its registered October 2026 completion date, the trial is very likely to finish without termination or outcome amendments and moderately likely to post results by August 2027.

sol.r: With recruitment finished and the long follow-up nearly complete, routine closeout is likelier than termination, although registry results may lag.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of XyloCore Peritoneal Dialysis Solution.
trials.ep: Total weekly Kt/V urea (peritoneal plus renal) at week 24

fable.r: Dropouts over six months and a wider between-patient spread in Kt/V than planned could leave the confidence interval crossing the non-inferiority margin even if XyloCore truly matches glucose solutions.

opus.r: Both arms are titrated to keep total Kt/V above 1.7, so equivalence in adequacy is expected; failure would most likely come from dropouts, PD transfer and residual renal function decline widening the interval past an unstated margin in a modest sample.

sonnet.r: Both arms are titrated to keep total Kt/V above 1.7, so a non-inferiority comparison should usually succeed; the main risk is a lower Kt/V in the glucose-sparing arm or a stricter margin than assumed, plus a small sponsor reporting selectively.

haiku.r: The main risk is a tight non-inferiority margin on weekly Kt/V with 85 patients per arm, since residual renal clearance varies widely between patients; timing is also a problem, as recruitment was still open at the snapshot.

carbon.r: Although osmotic matching and titration above Kt/V 1.7 strongly favor non-inferior dialysis adequacy, unexpected residual renal function loss or inter-patient variance in N=170 could widen the confidence interval past a tight margin.

sol.r: Variable residual renal clearance, attrition and an unstated non-inferiority margin could prevent a precise demonstration that dialysis adequacy is maintained.

trials.t: A Study of Baricitinib (LY3009104) in Participants From 1 Year to Less Than 18 Years Old With Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (sJIA)
trials.ep: Percentage of Participants Achieving Adapted Pediatric American College of Rheumatology 30 Responder Index (PediACR30) Response Criteria at Week 12

fable.r: Enrolment closed at 58 and both completion dates are registered for October 2026, so the record should move to completed, with results posted about a year later, after the read date.

opus.r: Lilly paediatric phase 3 at its registered primary completion with enrolment closed; expected to complete normally, with results posting likely close to the 12-month deadline.

sonnet.r: Lilly paediatric study near completion with no efficacy hypothesis; Lilly usually posts results within about a year of primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is roughly a one-in-three event, and termination or primary-outcome changes are unlikely.

haiku.r: A Lilly trial that has closed enrolment and passed its October 2026 primary completion, so the questions are whether results are posted within the one-year window and whether the primary list changes; neither is likely to move much.

carbon.r: Eli Lilly's pediatric sJIA study is active, not recruiting, at its registered October 2026 completion date and has low termination or amendment risk alongside high sponsor compliance with ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.

sol.r: The completed recruitment and imminent end of follow-up favour normal completion, with registry posting more uncertain than trial completion.

trials.t: Efficacy Against Oral Persistent Infection, Immunogenicity and Safety of the 9-valent Human Papillomavirus Vaccine (9vHPV) in Men Aged 20-45 Years (V503-049)
trials.ep: HPV 16/18/31/33/45/52/58-related 6-month persistent oral infection (oral rinse PCR) after Month 7, followed up to Month 90

fable.r: A case-driven analysis on roughly 20 to 30 oral infections leaves little room if efficacy in the mouth is nearer 65% than 85%, for instance through reactivated latent infection.

opus.r: Persistent oral HPV infection is rare in adult men, so the main threat is too few placebo cases for a tight interval, not vaccine weakness.

sonnet.r: HPV vaccines are about 90 to 98% effective against persistent infection with vaccine types in HPV-naive people, so success is likely; the risk is that persistent oral infection is rare, leaving few events and a wide interval.

haiku.r: Persistent oral infections are uncommon in men, so the 90-month analysis may have too few events to reach significance even if the vaccine works, and protection against oral infection may be lower than against genital disease.

carbon.r: The 9vHPV vaccine induces potent neutralizing antibodies in saliva that prevent persistent oral HPV infection, leaving lower-than-projected event accrual or prevalent baseline latent infections as the only plausible risks.

sol.r: Persistent oral infections are uncommon, so insufficient events are a more credible threat than inadequate vaccine activity.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Pembrolizumab (MK-3475) in Combination With Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) Versus CRT Alone in Muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (MIBC) (MK-3475-992/KEYNOTE-992)
trials.ep: Bladder-intact event-free survival (residual/recurrent MIBC, nodal or distant metastasis, radical cystectomy, or death) by central review, up to about 76 months

fable.r: Adding a PD-1 inhibitor to concurrent chemoradiotherapy has usually produced hazard ratios of 0.8 to 0.9, too small for a 520-patient trial to detect.

opus.r: Concurrent PD-1 blockade with chemoradiotherapy has a mixed record (positive in cervix, negative in head and neck and lung); a modest HR near 0.8 with about 230 events would sit right at the significance boundary.

sonnet.r: Adding PD-1 blockade to chemoradiation has repeatedly failed to improve disease control in other tumours, and chemoradiation in bladder cancer already controls disease well; a hazard ratio near 0.65 is needed for the trial design to succeed.

haiku.r: Chemoradiotherapy alone already keeps many patients bladder-intact, so the placebo arm is strong, and a hazard ratio near 0.7 leaves a modest margin on a composite endpoint that also counts cystectomy and death.

carbon.r: Adding PD-1/PD-L1 blockade concurrently to definitive chemoradiotherapy failed to improve bladder-intact event-free survival in SWOG/NRG S1806, indicating modest incremental activity over effective trimodality therapy.

sol.r: Effective chemoradiotherapy may leave only a modest incremental immunotherapy benefit, insufficient for the required bladder-intact EFS separation.

trials.t: Evaluation of the Structural Modification Effect of Diacerein (Artrodar®) in Knee Osteoarthritic Patients
trials.ep: Change from baseline in MRI-measured cartilage volume of the affected knee at Day 672 (about 24 months)

fable.r: Diacerein has no convincing structural effect in the knee, and any true slowing of cartilage loss is likely too small to show in 128 patients, let alone on all four primary outcomes.

opus.r: Diacerein's structure-modifying effect is small and unproven in the knee, and the trial lists four structural primary outcomes that would all have to be significant in about 60 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Four MRI and X-ray structural outcomes must all be significant with only 64 patients per arm, and diacerein's structure-modifying effect is small at best, so meeting all four is very unlikely.

haiku.r: Four co-primary MRI and X-ray outcomes must all be met in a trial of 64 per arm, and a diacerein effect on cartilage over two years is modest, so at least one of them is likely to miss.

carbon.r: Diacerein has weak disease-modifying activity in knee osteoarthritis, high GI dropout rates, and N=128 with four registered structural primary outcomes makes meeting strict primary criteria unlikely.

sol.r: Diacerein has not established robust knee structure modification, and simultaneous success across four noisy structural primary outcomes is unlikely.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety Evaluation for the Treatment of Allergy Against Mites
trials.ep: Combined symptom and medication score (CSMS) for rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis over 12 months of treatment

fable.r: With 50 patients per arm, the modest symptom and medication benefit usual for mite immunotherapy is unlikely to reach significance, and a slow trial may stop before reporting.

opus.r: About 50 patients per arm against a high placebo response on a noisy symptom-medication score gives limited power for the modest effects mite SCIT typically shows in its first year.

sonnet.r: Mite subcutaneous immunotherapy usually beats placebo on combined symptom-medication score and two doses give two chances, but 50 per arm leaves a noisy score and a large placebo response.

haiku.r: Fifty patients per arm is a small sample for a symptom and medication score in a seasonal allergy trial, so a real but moderate effect of the 30,000 dose could miss significance.

carbon.r: Field combined symptom and medication scores over 12 months exhibit substantial patient-level variability, so 50 patients per arm carries meaningful false-negative risk despite active mannan-allergoid immunotherapy.

sol.r: With only about 50 participants per dose, variable mite exposure, rescue-medication use and multiplicity could obscure a moderate SCIT effect.

trials.t: A Combination of Acalabrutinib With R-CHOP in Subjects With Previously Untreated Non-GCB DLBCL (ACE-LY-312)
trials.ep: Progression-free survival per Lugano Classification, assessed at every visit up to 60 months

fable.r: The benefit of BTK inhibition with R-CHOP seen in PHOENIX was confined to younger patients and particular genetic subtypes, so an all non-GCB population up to age 75 dilutes it.

opus.r: Non-GCB by GEP mixes BTK-dependent (MCD-like) and BTK-independent tumours, R-CHOP already cures ~70%, and PHOENIX showed BTK inhibitor benefit only in younger patients; patients aged 60-75 may again lose chemo dose intensity, diluting the PFS effect.

sonnet.r: BTK inhibitor added to R-CHOP in non-GCB DLBCL; ibrutinib in PHOENIX missed in the overall non-GCB group and only helped younger patients, and the ABC enrichment here is incomplete (unclassified included), so the effect may be diluted.

haiku.r: PHOENIX's ibrutinib add-on missed its overall event-free survival test, so a modest PFS gain from acalabrutinib is the main risk, and the registered February 2027 completion leaves little margin before June.

carbon.r: Molecular heterogeneity within non-GCB DLBCL and potential toxicity-related R-CHOP dose reductions among patients aged 60 to 75 could dilute BTK-sensitive MCD/N1 subgroup benefit.

sol.r: Non-GCB selection does not isolate BTK-dependent molecular subtypes, so benefit may be diluted while added toxicity reduces R-CHOP delivery.

trials.t: Study Assessing the Efficacy and Safety of Treatment With Alpelisib Plus Fulvestrant Versus Placebo Plus Fulvestrant in Chinese Men and Postmenopausal Women With Advanced Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by local radiology review per RECIST 1.1, from randomization to progression or death, up to about 34 months

fable.r: Randomisation ended at about 54 patients, so even a hazard ratio like SOLAR-1's 0.65 would leave the confidence interval crossing 1.

opus.r: Enrolment fell to ~54 randomized patients versus ~120 planned, so with ~40 PFS events even a SOLAR-1-like HR of 0.65 would reach two-sided significance only about a third of the time.

sonnet.r: Only about 54 patients were randomized instead of the planned 120, so even a true HR near the SOLAR-1 value of 0.65 gives roughly one-in-three power for a significant PFS result.

haiku.r: A tiny randomized trial (27 per arm planned, about 54 randomized) gives low power on PFS, and the record is closed with a January 2027 completion, so reporting depends on the sponsor.

carbon.r: Actual enrollment of 69 including the PK cohort leaves roughly 54 randomized patients, giving modest statistical power at alpha=0.05 even with SOLAR-1's true PFS hazard ratio near 0.60.

sol.r: The randomized cohort appears much smaller than originally planned, so even a SOLAR-1-sized benefit may not achieve statistical significance.

trials.t: ADI-PEG 20 Plus Radiotherapy and Temozolomide in Subjects With Glioblastoma Multiforme
trials.ep: Overall survival, followed through study completion (about 2.5 years)

fable.r: The survival effect of arginine deprivation in unselected glioblastoma is probably modest, well short of the hazard ratio near 0.6 that a 100-patient trial needs.

opus.r: Arginine deprivation helps only ASS1-deficient tumours, a minority of GBM, and add-ons to Stupp have almost all failed; with ~100 patients the trial needs an HR near 0.6 for OS significance.

sonnet.r: ADI-PEG 20 has no established efficacy in GBM, and a 100-patient phase 2 with an OS endpoint in Stupp-treated patients has low power for any realistic effect; most such add-ons fail.

haiku.r: A 100-patient phase 2 on overall survival needs a large effect to reach significance, and the registry shows a small sponsor with a February 2027 completion, so reporting may lag.

carbon.r: Unselected newly diagnosed glioblastoma has low overall ASS1 auxotrophy, poor blood-brain barrier macromolecule penetration, and a small N=100 Phase 1-2 sample size for overall survival.

sol.r: Arginine depletion may not produce a durable survival benefit across unselected glioblastoma, and approximately 74 deaths provide limited power for a modest effect.

trials.t: A Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of Entrectinib and Crizotinib in Participants With Advanced or Metastatic ROS1 Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) With and Without Central Nervous System (CNS) Metastases
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review (RECIST 1.1) in participants with CNS metastases at baseline

fable.r: The primary analysis is confined to patients with baseline CNS metastases (perhaps 80-100 of 217, about 60-70 events), so only a large effect (hazard ratio near 0.6 or better) reaches significance, while cross-trial data suggest entrectinib's PFS edge over crizotinib in these patients is moderate.

opus.r: The primary analysis is restricted to the CNS-metastasis subset of 217 patients, perhaps 80-100 patients and ~65 events, so a true HR of 0.65 gives only about 40-60% power even though entrectinib's CNS advantage over crizotinib is real.

sonnet.r: The primary test is limited to the baseline-CNS-metastases subgroup of 217 patients, perhaps 80-110 patients and about 55 events, so a true HR near 0.65 reaches significance only about half the time.

haiku.r: The subgroup is smaller than the full trial and its size is not stated, so power is limited, though entrectinib's intracranial activity favours a clear PFS gain.

carbon.r: Restricting the primary PFS analysis to patients with baseline CNS metastases within a 217-patient trial leaves a modest event count that increases sampling variability.

sol.r: The primary CNS-metastasis subset is small, and entrectinib's intracranial activity may not produce a large enough reduction in whole-body progression versus active crizotinib.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Camrelizumab Plus Rivoceranib (Apatinib) as Adjuvant Therapy in Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) at High Risk of Recurrence After Curative Resection or Ablation
trials.ep: Recurrence-free survival by blinded independent review committee (recurrence or death from any cause), follow-up up to about 43 months

fable.r: Adjuvant PD-(L)1 plus anti-VEGF therapy delays early recurrence, but the benefit faded with follow-up in IMbrave050; a mature final analysis here may give a hazard ratio near 0.8-0.85 that misses significance.

opus.r: Adjuvant immunotherapy-plus-antiangiogenic benefit in HCC has proved fragile (IMbrave050's early RFS gain faded) and apatinib toxicity drives early discontinuation, so the BIRC-assessed RFS effect may be too small or too transient for significance.

sonnet.r: Adjuvant immunotherapy in HCC has a mixed record (IMbrave050 interim positive then eroded, CheckMate-9DX and EMERALD-2 negative), but a PD-1 plus anti-angiogenic TKI in a high-risk Chinese population versus open-label surveillance has a good chance on BIRC-assessed RFS.

haiku.r: The main risk is a modest adjuvant effect over active surveillance, with apatinib tolerability adding dropouts; a Chinese sponsor with a July 2026 primary completion is likely to announce early.

carbon.r: Delayed recurrences after stopping fixed-duration adjuvant anti-PD-1 plus anti-angiogenic therapy may erode an early recurrence-free survival separation at longer follow-up, as seen in IMbrave050.

sol.r: Activity in unresectable HCC may not translate into durable eradication of micrometastases, as illustrated by the fading adjuvant benefit in IMbrave050.

trials.t: A Study of the Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics of a 36-Week Refill Regimen for the Port Delivery System With Ranibizumab in Patients With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration (Velodrome)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) score averaged over Weeks 68 and 72, as assessed using the ETDRS chart starting at a distance of 4 meters

fable.r: Fully enrolled Roche phase 3b with fixed visit schedules should finish on its registered date, run to completion, and post results about a year after primary completion, which is after the August 2027 read date.

opus.r: Roche's Phase IIIb PDS refill-interval study is fully enrolled with a fixed Week 72 primary endpoint, so it should complete near February 2027, with CT.gov results likely posted toward the 12-month deadline in early 2028.

sonnet.r: Roche phase 3b in active-not-recruiting status with a firm 2027-02 primary completion; schedule comparison with no hypothesis, so the main uncertainty is slippage of the date and CT.gov posting timing.

haiku.r: A refill-interval comparison with no efficacy goal that is already active, not recruiting, and due to complete in February 2027, so late or stopped outcomes are unlikely.

carbon.r: Enrollment is complete with 451 participants and a fixed 72-week primary assessment, so this Roche global Phase 3b trial should finish close to its February 2027 target date.

sol.r: With recruitment closed, completion near the revised schedule is likely, although prior PDS manufacturing and implant issues remain potential sources of delay.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Brivaracetam as Monotherapy in Patients 2 to 25 Years of Age With Childhood Absence Epilepsy or Juvenile Absence Epilepsy
trials.c: Childhood Absence Epilepsy; Juvenile Absence Epilepsy
trials.ep: Percentage of participants free of absence seizures during the awake hours of the Day-14 24-hour ambulatory EEG (with no benzodiazepine use in the 4 days before)

fable.r: SV2A ligands have only modest anti-absence efficacy (levetiracetam 24% vs 5% seizure-free at 2 weeks, not significant), and seizure freedom on a 24-hour EEG with hyperventilation is a strict bar, so brivaracetam's responder rate may be too low to separate from placebo in about 150 patients.

opus.r: SV2A ligands have only modest activity against typical absences (levetiracetam is clearly inferior to ethosuximide/valproate), and complete EEG-verified seizure freedom after only 14 days is a strict bar that a modest drug effect may not clear.

sonnet.r: Racetam-class SV2A ligands, including levetiracetam, have shown little efficacy against human absence seizures, so brivaracetam may fail to beat placebo on EEG seizure freedom despite its higher SV2A affinity.

haiku.r: A randomized-withdrawal design on a two-week EEG seizure-free endpoint with 77 versus 76 patients should detect a 15-point gain if brivaracetam works in absence epilepsy, which is less certain than for ethosuximide.

carbon.r: SV2A ligands have historically shown much weaker anti-absence efficacy than T-type calcium channel blockers, as seen in the borderline placebo-controlled trial of levetiracetam.

sol.r: SV2A modulation has shown only modest absence-seizure efficacy, and complete freedom on a provoked 24-hour EEG is substantially harder than reducing seizure counts.

trials.t: Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Efficacy Study of Radotinib in Parkinson's Disease
trials.ep: Evaluation of safety parameters: Adverse Events

fable.r: Small France-only phase 2 from a Korean sponsor with dosing finished: likely to run to its end without stopping, with no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 and no change to its safety primary outcome.

opus.r: A small Korean sponsor's France-only Phase 2 safety study past primary completion will likely finish quietly in 2027, with results reported in a congress or press release rather than posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.

sonnet.r: Small safety-focused phase 2 by a Korean sponsor, active-not-recruiting with a past primary completion and study completion in April 2027, so results posting by August 2027 is unlikely and primary outcome changes are rare.

haiku.r: A completed safety-primary study with no efficacy goal from a small sponsor, where results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is not required for a non-FDA trial, so posting is uncertain.

carbon.r: This 43-patient Phase 2 PD study in France has passed its registered September 2026 primary completion date and is scheduled for full study completion in April 2027 with low termination risk.

sol.r: The small cohort is likely to finish follow-up, but prompt ClinicalTrials.gov posting is less certain for this non-US exploratory study.

trials.t: TATE and Pembrolizumab (MK3475) in mCRC and NSCLC
trials.ep: Overall survival in the metastatic colorectal cancer cohort, from first day of treatment to death (assessed at 24 months)

fable.r: A slowly enrolling open-label phase 2 with about 37 patients per arm and an overall-survival endpoint has little power, pembrolizumab is inactive in MSS colorectal cancer, and anything public by mid-2027 is more likely an interim descriptive report or a stop than a formally met primary endpoint.

opus.r: Pembrolizumab is inactive in MSS colorectal cancer and liver metastases blunt immunotherapy further; a tirapazamine embolization add-on is unproven, and about 37 patients per arm can only detect a very large overall survival effect.

sonnet.r: About 37 patients per arm in an open-label randomized phase 2 of a small sponsor; an OS hazard ratio needs roughly 0.5 to reach significance, and the trial is slow and likely to slip or report quietly.

haiku.r: Small open-label phase 2 with about 37 patients per arm on an OS primary: too few patients for a convincing OS gain, and any public report is likely to be framed positively.

carbon.r: Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer with liver metastases is profoundly resistant to PD-1 checkpoint blockade, and local embolization has repeatedly failed to sensitize systemic or intrahepatic disease enough to improve overall survival.

sol.r: MSS colorectal cancer with liver metastases is strongly resistant to checkpoint blockade, and local embolization may not improve survival enough in this small randomized cohort.

trials.t: Pivotal 1 Study of ABBV-RGX-314 (Also Known as RGX-314) Gene Therapy Administered Via Subretinal Delivery One Time in Participants With nAMD
trials.c: AMD; nAMD; Wet Age-related Macular Degeneration
trials.ep: Mean change from baseline in best corrected visual acuity (ETDRS letters) at week 54

fable.r: Non-inferiority could fail if a subset of gene-therapy eyes loses vision after subretinal surgery or delayed rescue injections, pulling the mean 2-3 letters below monthly ranibizumab and the confidence bound past the margin.

opus.r: Failure would come from insufficient sustained anti-VEGF expression or vitrectomy-related vision loss leaving gene-therapy eyes a few letters behind monthly ranibizumab, so the lower confidence bound crosses the non-inferiority margin.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority against monthly ranibizumab with an assumed margin of about 4.5 letters; one-time gene therapy with rescue injections should be close, but a 1-2 letter deficit with a 12-letter SD leaves the lower bound near the margin.

haiku.r: One-time subretinal gene therapy against ranibizumab on a non-inferiority BCVA endpoint; the likeliest failure is a modest or fading transgene effect that falls short of the margin.

carbon.r: Frequent ranibizumab maintains visual acuity reliably in anti-VEGF-responsive eyes, whereas subretinal vitrectomy delivery can induce subtle retinal or pigmentary changes that narrow the non-inferiority margin cushion.

sol.r: Subretinal surgery, inflammation or retinal injury could leave a persistent visual-acuity deficit large enough to exceed the non-inferiority margin.

trials.t: A Study to Assess Change in Disease Activity and Adverse Events (AEs) With Cariprazine in the Treatment of Depressive Episodes in Pediatric Participants Participants (10 to 17 Years of Age) With Bipolar I Disorder.
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R) total score at week 6

fable.r: Placebo response on the CDRS-R in pediatric bipolar depression is large and variable (quetiapine XR failed for this reason) and cariprazine's adult effect is modest, so a 2-3 point difference may not reach significance.

opus.r: Pediatric bipolar depression trials often fail because placebo improvement on the CDRS-R is large (15-27 points), shrinking the drug-placebo gap; cariprazine's modest adult antidepressant effect leaves little margin.

sonnet.r: Pediatric bipolar depression trials have high placebo response and mixed outcomes (lurasidone positive, quetiapine negative); a true effect near 3 CDRS-R points gives only about 50-55 percent power with 190 per arm.

haiku.r: Pediatric bipolar depression trials show large placebo responses and the drug effect is modest; the trial was still recruiting in late 2026, so a public primary result by June 2027 is unlikely.

carbon.r: Large, variable placebo improvements on the CDRS-R across 81 pediatric psychiatric sites frequently dilute drug-placebo separation at 6 weeks, as occurred in pediatric quetiapine trials.

sol.r: Large and variable placebo improvement in pediatric bipolar depression could overwhelm cariprazine's modest antidepressant effect, especially across many low-enrolling sites.

trials.t: Perivenous Dexamethasone Therapy: Examining Reduction of Inflammation After Thrombus Removal to Yield Benefit in Acute Femoropopliteal DVT
trials.ep: Clinically relevant primary patency (freedom from symptomatic loss of patency on duplex ultrasound or angiogram) at 6 months

fable.r: With about 40 patients per arm, high expected patency in the sham arm and three primary outcomes, this pilot cannot plausibly show statistical superiority; it is also still recruiting close to its registered completion date.

opus.r: With patency around 80-90% in the sham arm and 40 patients per arm, only an implausibly large improvement could reach significance, and the patency, PTS and safety primaries would all need to be met.

sonnet.r: Only 40 patients per arm for a 6-month patency endpoint where sham patency is already high; an absolute gain of 10-15 points would be needed for significance, and recruitment still seems ongoing.

haiku.r: Sham-controlled device-drug study with 40 patients per arm on a patency responder endpoint; underpowered for a moderate effect, and slow enrolment makes a late, unpublished readout likely.

carbon.r: With only 40 patients per arm, background 6-month patency around 70-80% on modern anticoagulation, and multiple registered primary outcomes, the trial lacks statistical power for realistic treatment effects.

sol.r: Successful recanalization and sustained anticoagulation should produce high sham patency, leaving 40 patients per arm unlikely to demonstrate significant benefits on both patency and PTS.

trials.t: A Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Adjuvant Atezolizumab or Placebo and Trastuzumab Emtansine for Participants With HER2-Positive Breast Cancer at High Risk of Recurrence Following Preoperative Therapy
trials.ep: Invasive disease-free survival in the full analysis set (time to invasive recurrence, contralateral invasive breast cancer or death), primary analysis

fable.r: Atezolizumab added little to T-DM1 in metastatic HER2-positive disease (KATE2) and to neoadjuvant HER2 therapy (IMpassion050); in a PD-L1-unselected trial cut to 1188 patients the IDFS hazard ratio is likely near 0.9 and not significant.

opus.r: Atezolizumab has added nothing in several breast cancer trials, including with T-DM1 in KATE2 and neoadjuvant HER2+ IMpassion050; the T-DM1 control is strong with few IDFS events, so a modest effect confined to PD-L1+ tumours would not reach significance overall.

sonnet.r: Adding a PD-L1 inhibitor to an already effective T-DM1 backbone has little precedent in HER2-positive disease; neoadjuvant IMpassion050 showed no pCR gain and adjuvant atezolizumab failed in TNBC (IMpassion030).

haiku.r: Adding atezolizumab to T-DM1 after residual disease: T-DM1 is already strong here, leaving little room for a checkpoint gain, and the trial's own IDFS test needs a larger effect than I expect.

carbon.r: Adding atezolizumab to HER2-directed therapy previously failed in early HER2-positive breast cancer (IMpassion050) and unselected metastatic disease (KATE2), and capped enrollment at 1,188 reduces power for modest effects.

sol.r: Atezolizumab has not established benefit in unselected HER2-positive disease, and excellent T-DM1 outcomes plus additional immune toxicity leave limited room for incremental gain.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About the Safety of Litifilimab (BIIB059) Injections and Whether They Can Improve Symptoms of Adult Participants Who Have Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving SLE Responder Index 4 (SRI-4) response at week 52

fable.r: Background therapy and steroids lift placebo SRI-4 to the low-to-mid 40s at week 52, so a true gain of about 10 points would land right at the significance boundary with about 183 patients per arm.

opus.r: SLE trials on SRI-4 often fail because placebo response on background therapy is high and disease is heterogeneous; litifilimab's phase 2 SRI-4 signal was modest, so its effect may be too small to separate at week 52.

sonnet.r: SLE phase 3 trials fail often on SRI-4 at week 52 because of high placebo response; litifilimab had supportive phase 2 data but an effect of about 10 points is needed with roughly 183 per arm for reliable significance.

haiku.r: Litifilimab's mechanism has shown modest effect in lupus so far, and SRI-4 at week 52 is a demanding composite; a 10-point gap is needed to be convincing.

carbon.r: High and variable placebo SRI-4 response rates on background standard-of-care therapies routinely dilute treatment differences in global Phase 3 SLE trials.

sol.r: The modest phase 2 joint and skin signals may not translate into a sufficiently large SRI-4 advantage over background treatment at week 52.

trials.t: Study to Assess the Safety and Immunogenicity of TPOXX® When Administered Orally for 28 Days With JYNNEOS
trials.ep: Adverse Events

fable.r: Dosing of the 100 healthy volunteers ended long ago; the 2027-01-01 date looks like a rolled-forward placeholder while assay work and the post-exposure filing plan are pending, so another roll-forward is about as likely as a clean close.

opus.r: A short drug-vaccine interaction study with enrollment closed; the January 2027 date looks like a placeholder, so either a slipped date or an un-updated estimate is plausible, with posting due a year after completion.

sonnet.r: Small two-site drug-vaccine interaction study, active not recruiting with a 59-day follow-up; completion date likely accurate or already past, with slow results posting by a small sponsor.

haiku.r: Small two-site drug-vaccine interaction study, not recruiting, registered to complete in January 2027; likely to finish on schedule and post results within about a year.

carbon.r: Active, not recruiting 100-subject DoD/SIGA Phase 2 interaction study with January 2027 completion should finish roughly on schedule with moderate timely registry posting.

sol.r: Closed recruitment and a 59-day endpoint window favor completion near January 2027, although registry results may appear substantially later.

trials.t: To Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of SHR0302 Tablet in Subjects of Active Psoriatic Arthritis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving ACR20 response at week 24

fable.r: JAK1 inhibition is very likely to separate from placebo on ACR20; the residual risk is an unusually high placebo response at week 24 in a slow-enrolling single-country study.

opus.r: Failure would most likely come from an unusually high placebo ACR20 at week 24 in a single-country Chinese population, though JAK1 inhibition has produced large ACR20 gains in every psoriatic arthritis phase 3 so far.

sonnet.r: JAK inhibitors consistently beat placebo on ACR20 at week 24 in PsA by 25-35 points; with about 139 per arm failure would require an unusually high placebo response or a weak dose.

haiku.r: JAK1 inhibitors separate strongly from placebo on ACR20 in psoriatic arthritis; the main risk is a high placebo response in this single-country cohort, and the readout should come early in 2027.

carbon.r: Although JAK1 inhibition is highly validated in psoriatic arthritis, sub-optimal dosing or unexpectedly high placebo ACR20 response could narrow the margin.

sol.r: An unusually high week-24 placebo ACR20 response could compress an otherwise class-consistent JAK1 treatment effect.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About the Safety of Litifilimab (BIIB059) Injections and Whether They Can Improve Symptoms of Adult Participants Who Have Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving SLE Responder Index 4 (SRI-4) response at week 52

fable.r: Placebo SRI-4 on background therapy typically reaches the low 40s at week 52, so a true gain of about 10 points would sit at the edge of significance with about 187 patients per arm.

opus.r: Global SLE trials on background standard of care often show placebo SRI-4 responses of 40-50% at week 52, and litifilimab's phase 2 benefit was clearest in joints and skin, so the roughly 10-point SRI-4 gap needed may not appear.

sonnet.r: SLE phase 3s often fail on a placebo SRI-4 response of 35-45%; litifilimab had a clear phase 2 joint and skin signal, but about a 10 point difference is needed for significance at roughly 187 per arm.

haiku.r: Three-arm phase 3 with a 52-week composite SRI-4 primary; a 187-per-arm superiority test needs about a 10-point gap, which a modest high-dose effect rarely gives in SLE.

carbon.r: Substantial placebo SRI-4 responses on background immunosuppressants and steroids frequently mask moderate biologic efficacy in 52-week global SLE trials.

sol.r: Improvement in joints and skin may be insufficiently broad or consistent to generate a significant week-52 SRI-4 response advantage.

trials.t: A Study With Eptinezumab in Adolescents (12-17 Years) With Chronic Migraine
trials.ep: Change from baseline in monthly migraine days averaged over Weeks 1-12 after a single IV infusion

fable.r: Adolescents with chronic migraine improve by about 6 migraine days a month after a placebo infusion, leaving roughly 1.5 days of drug effect to detect with only about 95 patients per arm.

opus.r: Adolescent migraine prevention trials routinely see large placebo responses that shrink drug-placebo differences, and with about 95 per arm a 1.5-day gap in monthly migraine days is near the detection limit.

sonnet.r: Adolescent migraine trials show large placebo responses and pediatric CGRP antibody trials have been mixed; the adult effect of about 2 days could shrink with only 95 per arm.

haiku.r: Pediatric trial with 95 per arm; the adult effect of about 1.5 monthly migraine days sits near the detection threshold, and adolescent placebo responses tend to be high.

carbon.r: Pediatric and adolescent migraine trials notoriously exhibit large placebo responses, compounded here by an intravenous infusion placebo and modest 95-per-arm sample size.

sol.r: A large adolescent placebo response, potentially enhanced by an IV intervention, could erase much of the adult-sized treatment separation.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of Immuncell-LC With Gemcitabine in Resectable Pancreatic Cancer
trials.ep: Recurrence-free survival by independent review, up to about 36 months after last patient in

fable.r: Cell-based immunotherapy has not improved adjuvant outcomes in pancreatic cancer, and the trial needs an observed recurrence hazard ratio below about 0.80, beyond the effect I expect (about 0.87).

opus.r: Cytokine-induced killer cell therapy has no randomized evidence in pancreatic cancer, and adding it to adjuvant gemcitabine may not shift recurrence enough in such an aggressive disease.

sonnet.r: CIK-cell add-on to adjuvant gemcitabine has a prior HCC phase 3 signal but no proven pancreatic effect, and delays make a 2027 read unlikely.

haiku.r: Open-label add-on immunotherapy with 204 per arm needs a hazard ratio near 0.79 or lower to reach significance; pancreatic adjuvant data for this product are thin and enrollment looks slow.

carbon.r: Adoptive CIK cell immunotherapy has limited systemic activity against micrometastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, where nearly all Phase 3 adjuvant add-on trials have failed.

sol.r: The adjuvant liver-cancer CIK-cell signal may not translate into a clinically meaningful recurrence reduction in immunologically resistant pancreatic cancer.

trials.t: Pembrolizumab Plus Lenvatinib in Combination With Belzutifan in Solid Tumors (MK-6482-016)
trials.ep: Arm 1: Number of Participants Who Experience at Least One Dose-limiting Toxicity (DLT)

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the registered end sits exactly 67 months after start, matching the outcome time frame; Merck usually keeps such dates or closes earlier, and posts results about a year after completion.

opus.r: Enrolment is closed and primary completion is aligned with the study end in March 2027, so the trial should complete near schedule; results posting and changes to primary outcomes before August 2027 are unlikely.

sonnet.r: Active, not recruiting phase 2 with no formal hypothesis; Merck keeps registered dates fairly stable but may close a multi-cohort exploratory study early, and results are unlikely to be posted before the registered March 2027 completion plus several months.

haiku.r: Multi-tumour phase 2 with no formal testing; primary completion 2027-03-22 sits close to the 2027-06-20 late threshold, and the protocol was already amended in 2025 to close ESCC enrollment.

carbon.r: Multi-cohort Merck oncology Phase 2 basket trials frequently extend primary completion dates to allow mature BICR response duration follow-up across cohorts.

sol.r: Closed recruitment favors analysis in 2027, but continuing responders across multiple cohorts could extend follow-up and delay registry posting.

trials.t: ZEN003694 and Enzalutamide Versus Enzalutamide Monotherapy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
trials.ep: Radiographic progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in Cohort A (poor responders to prior abiraterone), up to 30 months

fable.r: Single-arm rPFS signals for a BET inhibitor plus enzalutamide may not hold in a randomised comparison, and the Cohort A sample (about 100 events) can only detect a hazard ratio near 0.6.

opus.r: Cohort A is a small open-label subset of a 200-patient phase 2b, so even a real HR near 0.7 may miss two-sided 0.05; BET-inhibitor toxicity may also limit dosing.

sonnet.r: BET inhibitor plus enzalutamide in post-abiraterone poor responders has only single-arm support; the open-label randomized phase 2b is still recruiting and the small sponsor faces funding and timing risk.

haiku.r: Small phase 2b add-on with an unstated cohort size; a readout before mid-2027 is unlikely, and recruitment appears to be behind its registered timetable.

carbon.r: BET inhibitors have shown modest clinical efficacy and dose-limiting hematologic/GI toxicities in mCRPC, while Cohort A alone provides a small sample size.

sol.r: The uncontrolled BET-inhibitor signal may shrink substantially against randomized enzalutamide control, while only Cohort A contributes to the primary test.

trials.t: A Trial to Assess Efficacy and Safety of Octreotide Subcutaneous Depot in Patients With GEP-NET
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review (RECIST 1.1), from randomization to progression or death, assessed up to 48 months

fable.r: Standard-dose octreotide LAR or lanreotide already gives long progression-free survival and no randomised evidence shows that higher octreotide exposure adds antitumour effect, so an observed hazard ratio below 0.75 is a stretch.

opus.r: Higher octreotide exposure from CAM2029 may not translate into longer PFS than standard-dose somatostatin analogues, whose antiproliferative effect may plateau at current doses.

sonnet.r: A higher-exposure octreotide depot beating standard SSAs on PFS is plausible but the likely hazard ratio is modest; the active control is slow to progress in a mostly grade 1-2 population.

haiku.r: Active-controlled superiority test of a depot against established somatostatin analogues with 166 per arm; the depot's main value is convenience, so a significant PFS gain is hard to show.

carbon.r: Demonstrating PFS superiority of high-exposure octreotide depot over active somatostatin analogues is challenging because somatostatin receptors saturate and high-dose SSAs have rarely beaten standard doses.

sol.r: Two established active somatostatin analogues may leave too little incremental tumor-control benefit for a higher-exposure octreotide depot to demonstrate superiority.

trials.t: An Efficacy and Safety Study of Clemizole HCl in Patients With Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in countable major motor seizures per 28 days (CMMS-28) over the 16-week double-blind period

fable.r: No randomised efficacy data exist for clemizole in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome; a serotonergic effect of about 8 points over placebo would not reach significance with 130 per arm and highly variable seizure counts.

opus.r: Clemizole's anti-seizure effect rests mainly on zebrafish data and serotonergic rationale; with little human efficacy evidence and variable LGS seizure counts, a 260-patient trial may not detect a modest effect.

sonnet.r: Clemizole is a repurposed serotonergic antihistamine with no randomized LGS efficacy data; many LGS candidates fail, and the registered completion date is likely optimistic for a rare-disease trial.

haiku.r: Adjunctive LGS trials carry high placebo responses and a mixed history; 130 per arm on a percent-change endpoint gives limited power for a modest effect, and the trial is still recruiting.

carbon.r: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome has heterogeneous etiologies where serotonergic modulation shows much smaller seizure reductions than in SCN1A-driven Dravet syndrome, as seen when fenfluramine barely cleared Phase 3 and soticlestat failed.

sol.r: Preclinical serotonergic activity may not produce a sufficiently large antiseizure effect across the heterogeneous, treatment-resistant LGS population.

trials.t: A Study to Test the Efficacy and Safety of Staccato Alprazolam in Study Participants 12 Years of Age and Older With Stereotypical Prolonged Seizures
trials.ep: Treatment success: termination of the treated prolonged seizure within 90 seconds after a single dose of study drug

fable.r: Prolonged seizures often stop on their own within 90 seconds of dosing (placebo responders were 42.5% in phase 2b) and home dosing by caregivers during a seizure may blunt delivery, so the drug-placebo gap could be too small for both primaries.

opus.r: Many prolonged seizures stop on their own soon after dosing, so a high placebo success rate in caregiver-judged outpatient episodes could narrow the gap, and both co-primaries must be met.

sonnet.r: Inhaled alprazolam should stop prolonged seizures faster than placebo, but both co-primaries must be met and a slow, event-driven outpatient trial adds noise and timing risk.

haiku.r: A rapid-acting benzodiazepine should beat placebo on early seizure cessation; the main risk is the second co-primary (no recurrence to 2 hours), which must also be met by the same arm.

carbon.r: Caregiver-observed seizure termination within 90 seconds in an outpatient setting is vulnerable to administration delays and subjective timing errors compared with inpatient video-EEG monitoring.

sol.r: Very rapid spontaneous seizure cessation and caregiver/device delays could narrow the 90-second treatment difference despite established benzodiazepine activity.

trials.t: Safety, Tolerability, and Immunogenicity of MenABCWY Administered on Different Dosing Schedules in Healthy Adolescents
trials.ep: Percentage of participants with human serum bactericidal assay (hSBA) titers ≥ lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ) for each N. meningitidis serogroup B indicator strains

fable.r: The fixed 0-, 48-month schedule with enrolment closed makes the last visits predictable, so completion near March 2027 is likely, with results posted around GSK's usual 12-month mark, after the read date.

opus.r: Enrolment is complete and the last primary visit is the 48-month group's Day 1471, so the trial should complete around March 2027 as registered; GSK usually posts within a year, often not within six months.

sonnet.r: Fixed-schedule vaccine study already past enrolment, so the final visits are set by the dosing calendar; GSK usually posts results within about a year of completion and rarely changes primary outcomes late.

haiku.r: Descriptive vaccine phase 2 with no efficacy hypothesis; the registered primary completion of 2027-03-10 is likely to be updated to an actual date, and GSK usually posts results promptly.

carbon.r: As an active, non-recruiting GSK vaccine schedule trial with fixed 24- and 48-month dosing intervals started in late 2021, completion near March 2027 aligns closely with protocol follow-up.

sol.r: Closed enrolment and fixed long-interval vaccine visits favour near-scheduled completion, although registry posting may lag the March 2027 endpoint.

trials.t: Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant Therapy Studies of Sindilizumab in Resectable Lung Cancer
trials.ep: Event-free survival in stage III resectable NSCLC, up to about 2 years

fable.r: The class effect on EFS is consistent, so failure would most likely come from an immature interim analysis or from only the stage III primary being reported while the ITT primary is still pending.

opus.r: Perioperative PD-1 benefit is well established, so the main risk is that the ITT EFS primary is immature or not formally declared when the stage III EFS result is reported.

sonnet.r: Perioperative PD-1 plus chemotherapy has repeatedly won on EFS in resectable stage III NSCLC; the uncertainty is the timing of an interim read and that a second primary (ITT EFS at 3 years) may be reported later.

haiku.r: Two co-primary EFS endpoints in a smaller stage III subgroup; a perioperative PD-1 benefit is plausible, but both must reach significance, and single-centre Chinese disclosure may be selective.

carbon.r: Because both stage III EFS and overall ITT EFS are registered as co-primary outcomes, an early readout reporting only stage III while ITT EFS remains immature would not satisfy both co-primaries by the deadline.

sol.r: Two EFS populations with different maturity windows create a risk that only one primary analysis is formally positive at an early readout.

trials.t: Phase 2a Multiple Ascending Dose Study in Hospitalized Patients With Pneumonia.
trials.c: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome; Viral or Bacterial Infections; Pneumonia
trials.ep: Safety and tolerability of multiple doses of IV administrations of AV-001 Injection compared with AV-001 placebo Injection in hospitalized patients with pneumonia due to COVID-19 and/or other respiratory infections.

fable.r: A 60-patient phase 2a from a small sponsor with enrolment closed and the registered completion date already passed will most likely move to completed, with results posted late or not by the read date.

opus.r: Enrolment is closed and the registered primary completion (Sept 2026) has passed, so the record will most likely move to completed; a small sponsor may post results near the one-year deadline or late.

sonnet.r: Small phase 2a safety study from a small private sponsor; enrolment is closed, so it most likely just finishes, with results posted slowly or only after a later publication.

haiku.r: Safety-only Phase 2a that is active, not recruiting, and past its registered completion date; the open questions are a late status change to terminated or withdrawn and whether results get posted.

carbon.r: The small Phase 2a trial is active and no longer recruiting with its September 2026 primary completion date already passed, pointing to routine closeout with modest near-term ClinicalTrials.gov posting.

sol.r: Enrolment appears closed after a prolonged recruitment period, but a small sponsor may delay registry results while analysing the three dose cohorts.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of IMU-838 in Patients With Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis
trials.ep: Time to first relapse after start of study treatment during the double-blind period, censored at a maximum of 72 weeks

fable.r: As a DHODH inhibitor vidofludimus may cut relapses by only 20-30%, and with about 250 first relapses a true hazard ratio above 0.75 leaves the trial short of significance.

opus.r: A DHODH inhibitor with mild lymphocyte effects may cut relapses by only about 20%, which roughly 260 events over 72 weeks cannot reliably detect, especially if modern placebo relapse rates run low.

sonnet.r: A realistic hazard ratio of 0.75-0.85 with roughly 250-300 relapse events puts the significance threshold near HR 0.79, so the result is close to a coin flip with a lean to missing.

haiku.r: A modest oral DMT with a relapse-time effect of about 20 percent; if the true hazard ratio is near 0.9 or above, the 0.05 test fails. The two ENSURE trials share one drug, so they would fail together.

carbon.r: DHODH inhibitors generally produce modest ~30% reductions in clinical relapse rates, and low placebo relapse rates in contemporary MS cohorts could leave the hazard ratio short of significance.

sol.r: A low placebo relapse rate could leave too few events to demonstrate the moderate clinical benefit expected from DHODH inhibition.

trials.t: Phase 3 Study of Anifrolumab in Adult Patients With Active Proliferative Lupus Nephritis
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with complete renal response (UPCR <=0.5 mg/mg and eGFR >=60 or no >=20% decline) at week 52

fable.r: The phase 2 trial missed its primary and the 14-point complete-response gain for the intensified regimen came from about 45 patients per arm, so the true gain may be under the 10 points this trial can detect.

opus.r: Type I interferon blockade may add only a few points of complete renal response on top of MMF and steroids, below what about 360 patients can detect at week 52.

sonnet.r: The phase 2 TULIP-LN missed its primary endpoint, and add-on effects on top of MMF and steroids in lupus nephritis have been about 10 points; with 180 per arm this is borderline powered.

haiku.r: Anifrolumab's renal-response effect is unproven in phase 3. An effect of about 9 points with a standard error near 5 gives roughly even odds of significance, so the main risk is a true effect that is too small.

carbon.r: Proteinuria-driven monoclonal antibody clearance and a responsive mycophenolate-plus-glucocorticoid background arm could compress the Week 52 complete renal response delta below ~10 percentage points.

sol.r: Strong renal responses to optimized mycophenolate and glucocorticoids could erase the modest incremental benefit suggested by the intensified phase 2 regimen.

trials.t: A Study to Explore the Therapeutic Effect of HEC585 on Delaying Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) Decline and Tolerance in Progressive Fibrosing Interstitial Lung Disease (PF-ILD) Patients
trials.c: Progressive Fibrosing Interstitial Lung Disease (PF-ILD) / Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis (PPF)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in forced vital capacity (mL) at Week 24

fable.r: About 37 patients per arm and a 24-week FVC endpoint with a between-patient SD near 200 mL give low power unless the treatment difference exceeds 100 mL.

opus.r: With about 37 patients per arm over 24 weeks, a realistic 40-60 mL FVC benefit has well under 50% power, and dose B may be the lower dose.

sonnet.r: A 24-week FVC endpoint with about 37 per arm and SD near 160 mL has a standard error near 37 mL, so only an effect above about 75 mL reaches significance, and the dose B arm may be the lower dose.

haiku.r: About 37 patients per arm at one centre: significance needs an FVC gap of roughly 70 mL at week 24, and a benefit as large as nintedanib's in INBUILD would only just reach it. Power is the main risk.

carbon.r: With roughly 37 patients per arm and typical 24-week FVC change standard deviation near 200 mL, only an unusually large >90 mL treatment difference reaches two-sided 0.05 significance.

sol.r: About 37 participants per arm and heterogeneous progression make a modest six-month FVC benefit difficult to distinguish from noise.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Daily Subcutaneous Metreleptin Treatment in Subjects With PL
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Month 6 in patients with partial lipodystrophy

fable.r: Only 69 patients for two primaries (HbA1c and triglycerides at month 6) with wide between-patient variability, and open-label HbA1c falls of 0.6-0.9 points may shrink against placebo on optimized background therapy.

opus.r: Two primary endpoints (HbA1c and fasting triglycerides) in only about 35 patients per arm, with modest expected metreleptin effects in partial lipodystrophy, leave limited power to win both.

sonnet.r: Co-primary HbA1c and triglycerides must both be significant with only 69 patients; the HbA1c effect is diluted in patients who enrolled on triglycerides alone, and benefit in partial lipodystrophy is milder than in generalised disease.

haiku.r: Two co-primary outcomes (HbA1c and triglycerides) must both be significant in 69 patients over six months. The main risk is noise in a small trial, not a weak drug.

carbon.r: Allowing baseline leptin up to 20 ng/mL and entry via either elevated HbA1c or triglycerides dilutes metreleptin's metabolic effect while requiring both co-primaries to win in 69 patients.

sol.r: The small, metabolically heterogeneous cohort must establish both HbA1c and highly variable triglyceride benefits, not merely one.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Light Dose in Subjects With PWB Treated With Hemoporfin PDT
trials.c: Port-wine Birthmarks; Port-Wine Stain; Nevus Flammeus
trials.ep: Stage Two (face/neck port-wine birthmarks): change from baseline in PWB-IGA score, assessed up to about 44 weeks

fable.r: Stage Two splits a small sample across several light fluences and vehicle and the analysis may be descriptive, so a clear statement that the efficacy primary was met is uncertain despite a strong drug effect.

opus.r: Stage Two face/neck arms will be small, and a dose-finding phase 2 may report only descriptive IGA changes rather than a formal significant comparison with vehicle PDT.

sonnet.r: A small sequential phase 2 light-dose study with an unclear primary hypothesis; hemoporfin PDT works, but the arms are small and the Stage Two efficacy test may not be formally powered.

haiku.r: Stage Two compares the highest light fluence with vehicle on a PWB-IGA scale that is not established, and the arms are likely smaller than the 42 planned. The risk is the endpoint and sample size rather than the drug.

carbon.r: Splitting 84 total participants across two sequential anatomical stages and multiple light-fluence cohorts leaves small per-arm sample sizes in Stage Two.

sol.r: Splitting 84 participants between stages and several light fluences could leave the formally tested stage-two comparison too small despite a large biological effect.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of LT3001 Drug Product in Subjects AIS Undergoing EVT
trials.ep: The occurrence of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 hours after the single dosing; clinical deterioration defined as an change in the NIHSS of 4 points or more and confirmed by MRI

fable.r: Enrolment is closed at 66 and the primary is a 24-hour safety outcome, so completion by the end of 2026 is likely, and the small sponsor is unlikely to post results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027.

opus.r: Enrolment of 66 is complete and the primary outcome is measured at 24 hours, so primary completion by Dec 2026 is likely; FDAAA posting falls due around Dec 2027, so posting by Aug 2027 is less likely.

sonnet.r: Recruitment is closed and the primary safety outcome covers only 24 hours after dosing, so the trial is expected to finish roughly on time; a small Taiwan-based sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.

haiku.r: A safety-only Phase II that is closed to enrolment. The open questions are whether the registry completion date gets updated and whether results are posted.

carbon.r: Because enrollment is already complete (active, not recruiting) and the primary safety endpoint is assessed within 24 hours of dosing, completion on or shortly after December 2026 is highly likely.

sol.r: Closed enrolment and the short primary safety window support completion near schedule, but registry posting may trail sponsor communications.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of IMU-838 in Patients With Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis
trials.ep: Time to first relapse after start of study treatment during the double-blind period, censored at a maximum of 72 weeks

fable.r: The relapse effect may be only teriflunomide-like or smaller (hazard ratio near 0.8) while low modern placebo relapse rates leave too few first-relapse events to show it.

opus.r: A DHODH inhibitor with mild lymphocyte effects may cut relapses by only about 20%, which roughly 255 events over 72 weeks cannot reliably detect, especially if modern placebo relapse rates run low.

sonnet.r: Same design as ENSURE-1: a true HR near 0.8 with about 250-300 relapse events puts the significance threshold near HR 0.79, so success is roughly a coin flip with a lean to missing.

haiku.r: A twin of ENSURE-1 with the same design. With a modest relapse effect both trials can miss together, so the main risk is a drug too weak to reach significance.

carbon.r: Contemporary relapsing MS populations frequently exhibit lower-than-planned on-study clinical relapse rates, reducing statistical power for time to first relapse within a 72-week window.

sol.r: The strong phase 2 MRI signal may translate into only a modest relapse reduction, leaving insufficient separation on time to first relapse.

trials.t: Investigate Efficacy and Safety of Carisbamate as Adjunctive Treatment for Seizures Associated With LGS in Children and Adults
trials.ep: Percentage change from baseline in drop-seizure frequency (tonic, atonic, tonic-clonic) per 28 days during the double-blind treatment period

fable.r: Carisbamate showed only modest, inconsistent efficacy in focal epilepsy and has no controlled data in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, so its drop-seizure effect may not clear a 10-20% placebo response.

opus.r: Carisbamate showed only modest efficacy in focal epilepsy and its LGS evidence is open-label; drop-seizure percent change is noisy and placebo arms vary, so a 15-point median difference may not reach significance.

sonnet.r: LGS drop-seizure trials succeed about half the time; carisbamate has a mixed history in focal epilepsy and a sodium-channel-like profile, so an effect over a 15-20% placebo response may fall short of significance.

haiku.r: Adjunctive LGS trial still recruiting at launch, so a readout by June 2027 is unlikely; if it reads out, an effect of about 12 points on percent drop-seizure change is near the significance edge at 126 per arm.

carbon.r: Carisbamate previously showed modest and inconsistent seizure-reduction efficacy in focal epilepsy Phase 3 studies, and refractory LGS drop seizures often exhibit high variability and notable placebo responses.

sol.r: Carisbamate has antiseizure activity, but its incremental effect in heavily treated LGS may be too small to separate from variable caregiver-recorded placebo responses.

trials.t: A Global Study to Assess the Effects of Durvalumab With Oleclumab or Durvalumab With Monalizumab Following Concurrent Chemoradiation in Patients With Stage III Unresectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review (RECIST 1.1) after chemoradiation in unresectable stage III NSCLC

fable.r: The COAST signal came from about 60 patients per arm against an underperforming durvalumab arm, and the true add-on benefit of oleclumab is probably too small (hazard ratio near 0.85) to reach significance.

opus.r: COAST's PFS gain came from a small phase 2 whose durvalumab arm did far worse than PACIFIC; IO add-ons to PD-(L)1 consolidation (tiragolumab in SKYSCRAPER-03) have failed, and CD73 blockade has no phase 3 win.

sonnet.r: Add-on checkpoint combinations after chemoradiation on top of durvalumab have mostly failed, and the strong phase 2 COAST signal (HR 0.44, small and randomized in a modest sample) usually shrinks sharply in phase 3.

haiku.r: Oleclumab is added to durvalumab, whose PFS benefit after chemoradiation is already strong, so the control is hard to beat; few add-ons to durvalumab have shown a clear PFS gain.

carbon.r: Phase 2 COAST benefits were amplified by an unusually weak durvalumab control arm (median PFS ~6-7 months), whereas Phase 3 EGFR/ALK wild-type post-cCRT durvalumab control arms typically achieve ~17 months median PFS.

sol.r: COAST's unusually poor durvalumab control performance may have exaggerated the incremental benefit of oleclumab, which could shrink substantially against a modern phase 3 control arm.

trials.t: A Masked, Placebo-controlled Study to Assess Iptacopan in Age-related Macular Degeneration
trials.ep: Conversion of the early/intermediate AMD study eye to new iRORA or late AMD on OCT and multimodal imaging through month 24

fable.r: Oral systemic factor B inhibition is unproven in the retina, and a proof-of-concept study of about 73 per arm needs roughly a halving of conversion to iRORA or late AMD to succeed.

opus.r: Even intravitreal complement inhibitors only slow geographic atrophy growth by 15-20%, and it is unproven that oral factor B inhibition prevents iRORA; with about 146 eyes the trial can only detect a large effect.

sonnet.r: Proof-of-concept with about 70-80 per arm in a slowly progressing disease; oral factor B inhibition may only modestly slow conversion to iRORA, and the conversion rate in placebo eyes may be too low for 24-month power.

haiku.r: A 168-eye proof-of-concept with a slow conversion endpoint; the placebo arm will likely have only about 15 to 20 events, so the trial lacks power for a hazard ratio near 0.5.
