carbon.r: Systemic complement Factor B inhibition has modest expected impact on preventing conversion to composite iRORA or late AMD (which includes neovascular AMD in fellow eyes of nAMD patients) in a ~146-168 patient trial.

sol.r: Systemic complement inhibition may not sufficiently alter early AMD conversion, and this small prevention study requires a large effect despite imaging-based risk enrichment.

trials.t: Effect of Testofen on Erectile Function in an Adult Male Population
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-15) total score

fable.r: Only 64 men were enrolled across three arms (about 21 each), too few to show a plausibly small effect of fenugreek extract on both IIEF and Erection Hardness Score over a sizeable placebo response.

opus.r: Only 64 men across three arms (about 21 per arm) with two co-primary outcomes (IIEF and EHS) that must both separate from placebo, against a sizeable placebo response in erectile function questionnaires.

sonnet.r: About 20 men per arm, two co-primaries (IIEF and EHS) that must both be met by the same dose, and a large placebo response in erectile dysfunction make a clean double win unlikely despite company-friendly priors.

haiku.r: Small single-site herbal trial with two co-primary endpoints; about 40 patients per arm may not resolve a few IIEF points, and the sponsor may not publish a result by mid-2027.

carbon.r: Final enrollment reached only 64 participants across three arms (~21 per arm), severely limiting statistical power to achieve significance simultaneously on both co-primary outcomes (IIEF and EHS).

sol.r: Enrollment is only 64 across three arms, so placebo-responsive sexual-function scores and the co-primary Erection Hardness Score may not both separate reliably.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Depemokimab Compared With Mepolizumab in Adults With Relapsing or Refractory Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis (EGPA)
trials.ep: Percentage of participants in remission (BVAS 0 and oral corticosteroid <=4 mg/day) at both weeks 36 and 52

fable.r: With about 80 patients per arm, a chance deficit of around 10 points in remission, or slightly lower efficacy at the trough of twice-yearly dosing, could push the confidence bound past the non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: With about 82 patients per arm the 95% interval on the remission difference spans roughly plus or minus 15 points, so even a true tie could breach a 20-25 point margin by chance; the 26-week dosing interval may also give less trough suppression than monthly mepolizumab 300 mg.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority with about 80 per arm and a roughly 30% remission rate gives a wide interval; passing depends on how generous the unstated margin is, though depemokimab's potency makes a true gap near zero likely.

haiku.r: Non-inferiority responder trial of 163 patients with the margin not stated; a small sample leaves wide intervals around the difference, so a non-inferiority margin could be missed even with similar drugs.

carbon.r: With ~81 patients per arm, sampling variation in remission rates is the primary residual risk to crossing the non-inferiority margin despite equivalent IL-5 neutralization.

sol.r: A small active-controlled study can miss its non-inferiority bound through remission-rate imbalance even if the two anti-IL-5 agents are clinically similar.

trials.t: Endoscopic Evidence of Maintenance of Healing With Oral NEXIUM in Patients 1 to 11 Years Old With Erosive Esophagitis.
trials.ep: Presence / absence of Erosive Esophagitis

fable.r: The study is completed and results are due on the registry around 10 August 2027, so whether they show by 31 August depends on AstraZeneca submitting on time and on processing lag.

opus.r: Completed sponsor-run paediatric study designed with FDA; results will likely be posted around the 12-month deadline, possibly delayed if AstraZeneca certifies a pending US filing for this use.

sonnet.r: Completed pediatric AstraZeneca study run with FDA input; AstraZeneca normally posts results near the 12-month deadline (August 2027) and the primary outcome is simple and unlikely to be edited.

haiku.r: Dose-comparison maintenance trial in children that is already completed, so the registry should move little; the open question is whether AstraZeneca posts results by the one-year US deadline of 2027-08-10, just before the read date.

carbon.r: This FDA-discussed pediatric esomeprazole maintenance study has already completed enrollment and follow-up, making timely ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by AstraZeneca highly likely before August 2027.

sol.r: The trial is already completed, and its FDA-oriented pediatric purpose and large sponsor favor registry reporting around the one-year deadline with little further protocol change.

trials.t: Effect of Ensifentrine on Sputum Markers of Inflammation in COPD
trials.sp: Verona Pharma, Inc., a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc. (Rahway, New Jersey USA
trials.ep: Change from baseline in absolute sputum neutrophil count after 8 weeks of twice-daily nebulized treatment

fable.r: Induced-sputum neutrophil counts are highly variable and ensifentrine's anti-inflammatory effect in COPD airways is unproven, so 56 crossover patients may not show a significant fall at week 8.

opus.r: Absolute sputum neutrophil counts are highly skewed and variable between visits, and nebulized ensifentrine's anti-inflammatory effect in COPD airways is unproven; 56 patients in a crossover may not show a significant change.

sonnet.r: Sputum neutrophil counts are highly skewed and variable; a 56-patient crossover may miss a modest PDE4-mediated anti-inflammatory effect of nebulized ensifentrine on top of maintenance bronchodilators.

haiku.r: A small 8-week crossover on noisy sputum neutrophil counts; anti-inflammatory effects of an inhaled PDE3/4 inhibitor are unproven, and a public readout before late 2027 is unlikely.

carbon.r: Induced sputum absolute neutrophil counts in stable COPD exhibit high within-subject biological and processing variability that can obscure moderate airway PDE3/4 anti-inflammatory effects.

sol.r: Absolute induced-sputum neutrophil counts are noisy, and anti-inflammatory effects seen in an acute challenge model may not reproduce after eight weeks in stable, maintenance-treated COPD.

trials.t: Efficacy & Safety of Olvi-Vec and Platinum-doublet + Bevacizumab Compared to Physician's Choice of Chemotherapy and Bevacizumab in Platinum-Resistant/Refractory Ovarian Cancer (PRROC) (OnPrime, GOG-3076)
trials.c: Platinum-resistant Ovarian Cancer; Platinum-refractory Ovarian Cancer; Fallopian Tube Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by RECIST 1.1 (blinded independent central review) in the intention-to-treat population, up to 12 months

fable.r: The 11-month PFS in a 27-patient, single-arm, largely single-centre phase 2 is likely to shrink in a randomized multicentre trial, leaving a benefit too small for 186 patients to show.

opus.r: The phase 2 VIRO-15 signal comes from 27 selected, single-arm patients; platinum rechallenge in heavily pretreated platinum-resistant disease often fails, and the control of chemotherapy plus bevacizumab is not trivial.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 VIRO-15 was a small single-arm study (n=27); in heavily pretreated platinum-resistant disease control PFS is about 4 months, and open-label randomization with BICR PFS makes a modest oncolytic effect hard to confirm.

haiku.r: Open-label intraperitoneal oncolytic virus added before chemotherapy; the trial was still recruiting at launch, so a June 2027 readout is unlikely, and a modest virus effect over a strong control is the main risk.

carbon.r: Uncontrolled Phase 2 VIRO-15 PFS gains may reflect patient selection and platinum-doublet rechallenge rather than true viral platinum resensitization, while platinum-refractory tumors often progress rapidly on platinum.

sol.r: Single-arm VIRO-15 may overstate genuine platinum re-sensitization, and heavily pretreated patients may progress before the virus–chemotherapy sequence adds meaningful benefit.

trials.t: RNS System LGS Feasibility Study
trials.c: Epilepsy; Lennox Gastaut Syndrome; Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome, Intractable
trials.ep: Safety: Annual device-related serious adverse event (SADE) rate

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and follow-up should finish close to the registered November 2026 date, with results posting due only in late 2027.

opus.r: Small NIH-funded device feasibility study, active not recruiting, whose 24-month post-implant safety follow-up may push primary completion past the registered November 2026 date.

sonnet.r: Small NINDS-funded device feasibility study with 24-month safety follow-up; the registered December 2026 completion may be extended as final visits are confirmed, and device-study results posting is unlikely before late 2027.

haiku.r: Device feasibility study of 24 patients with a 24-month safety endpoint; the main operations risk is that the completion date moves past February 2027 to cover second-year follow-up, while results posting is due only after the read date.

carbon.r: Because enrollment of implanted cohorts is already complete (active, not recruiting) with fixed 12-to-24-month post-implant follow-up ending late 2026, completion should stay near schedule with moderate results posting by August 2027.

sol.r: With recruitment closed, the main remaining operational risk is delayed completion of long post-implant assessments; registry results may lag beyond August 2027.

trials.t: Coronary Computed Tomography Study to Assess the Effect of Inclisiran in Addition to Maximally Tolerated Statin Therapy on Atherosclerotic Plaque Progression in Participants With a Diagnosis of Non-obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Without Previous Cardiovascular Events
trials.ep: Percent change in total coronary atheroma volume on coronary CT angiography from baseline to month 24

fable.r: CCTA total atheroma volume includes calcified plaque, which rises under intensive LDL lowering, and reading noise over 24 months could shrink a real regression effect below significance.

opus.r: CCTA percent change in total atheroma volume is noisy and includes calcified plaque that LDL lowering barely shrinks, so a true 3-4 point benefit may not reach significance with about 280 evaluable patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Inclisiran lowers LDL-C about 50% on top of statins, and PCSK9 imaging trials (GLAGOV, PACMAN-AMI) showed plaque benefit, but CCTA volume change is noisy and plaque burden in non-obstructive disease is low, so the 24-month difference may not reach significance.

haiku.r: A roughly 50 percent LDL-C cut over 24 months on top of statins may move CCTA atheroma volume by only about one point, near the detection limit for 305 patients per arm.

carbon.r: Serial coronary CT angiography measurements of total atheroma volume carry imaging noise and attrition over 24 months in lower-risk primary prevention patients already on optimized statins.

sol.r: LDL lowering should be substantial, but total CT plaque volume includes calcified plaque and may show only a small, noisy incremental change over optimized statin therapy.

trials.t: Clinical Trial With Donor Modified Immune Cells in Living Donor Kidney Transplantation
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with an operational tolerance-like phenotype (all four criteria: no rejection/graft loss/dysfunction/death, no de novo DSA, Breg ≥3%, reduced immunosuppression) at Day 367

fable.r: Breg induction of at least 3% plus completed immunosuppression reduction without rejection may be reached by too few MIC patients; a result by mid-2027 is also unlikely because the trial is still listed as recruiting.

opus.r: The composite needs no rejection, no DSA, Breg of at least 3% and steroid-free reduced immunosuppression; MIC patients may fail one criterion, and any statement by mid-2027 would more likely be an early stop than a final read.

sonnet.r: Small open-label phase 2 (42 vs 21) with a four-part composite that requires Breg induction, no de novo DSA, no rejection and minimal immunosuppression; the cell product plausibly moves Breg but the composite is demanding and recruitment is still running, so a result is unlikely before late 2027.

haiku.r: Four criteria must all hold in a composite with only 42 treated and 21 control patients, so a significant gain over a low standard-of-care rate is unlikely.

carbon.r: Requiring simultaneous fulfillment of all four stringent composite criteria including Breg >=3% and corticosteroid-free reduced immunosuppression at Day 367 creates a high hurdle in a small open-label cohort.

sol.r: The favorable composite depends on reproducible regulatory B-cell induction and successful immunosuppression reduction, which may not reproduce the small phase I experience.

trials.t: Thrombolysis With Recombinant Non-immunogenic Staphylokinase vs Surgery in Patients With Acute Limb Ischemia FORAT Trial
trials.ep: Percentage of patients without amputation at 30 days after randomization

fable.r: If the hypothesis is superiority, 85 patients per arm cannot show a difference when about 90% of surgical patients keep the limb at 30 days; success depends on a non-inferiority design with a wide margin.

opus.r: Surgery already saves over 90% of limbs at 30 days, so if the trial is judged as superiority there is no room to win; the sponsor most likely framed it as non-inferiority, which it has met in every prior Fortelyzin trial.

sonnet.r: Surgical revascularisation already gives about 90% amputation-free at 30 days in Rutherford I-IIb, leaving little room for superiority with 85 per arm; a sponsor report of non-inferiority is the likelier positive route.

haiku.r: With 85 patients per arm, a superiority gap over surgery of roughly 15 points is needed, and a surgical arm already near 78 percent without amputation leaves little room.

carbon.r: Historical randomized trials comparing catheter-directed thrombolysis with surgery in acute limb ischemia show very similar 30-day limb-salvage rates around 85-90%, leaving 170 patients underpowered for superiority unless tested for non-inferiority.

sol.r: Surgery already achieves high short-term limb salvage, so 170 patients are unlikely to establish superiority for a modest thrombolysis benefit unless the actual protocol uses non-inferiority.

trials.t: Masupirdine for the Treatment of Agitation in Dementia of the Alzheimer's Type
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 12 in CMAI items score for IPA agitation domains (physical aggression, excessive motor activity, verbal aggression)

fable.r: The agitation signal comes from post hoc phase 2 subgroups; a 5-HT6 antagonist may not beat the large placebo response seen in Alzheimer's agitation trials.

opus.r: The agitation hypothesis for masupirdine rests on a post hoc analysis of a failed cognition trial, and agitation trials carry large placebo responses that swamp modest drug effects.

sonnet.r: Agitation-in-Alzheimer's trials have large placebo responses, and an earlier masupirdine phase 3 did not meet its primary; this repeat rests on a subgroup-driven rationale and a 5-HT6 antagonist with modest activity.

haiku.r: Placebo-adjusted gains on agitation scales are usually small, and the 100 mg effect must be about 1.6 CMAI points with 125 per arm to reach significance.

carbon.r: Masupirdine is a 5-HT6 antagonist pivoted to Alzheimer's agitation after failing its Phase 2 cognitive trial on the basis of post-hoc NPI subgroup signals, which rarely replicate against large CMAI placebo responses.

sol.r: Agitation development rests largely on exploratory behavioral findings from a cognitively negative study, and substantial placebo improvement may obscure a modest 5-HT6 effect.

trials.t: Pivotal 2 Study of RGX-314 Gene Therapy in Participants With nAMD
trials.c: AMD; nAMD; Wet Age-related Macular Degeneration
trials.ep: Mean change from baseline in best corrected visual acuity (ETDRS letters) in the study eye at week 54

fable.r: Gene therapy eyes may lose letters from surgery or from under-suppressed disease before rescue, pushing the lower confidence bound past the non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: One-time subretinal gene therapy plus vitrectomy may let vision drift 1-3 letters below fixed aflibercept dosing by week 54, and a lower CI bound beyond a roughly 4-5 letter margin would fail non-inferiority.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority needs the gene therapy to stay within the margin (likely 4.5 letters) of aflibercept at week 54; supplemental-injection rescue keeps vision stable, but variable expression or a slow start could widen the gap.

haiku.r: A one-time subretinal gene therapy has to hold aflibercept's BCVA gain within a non-inferiority margin that is not stated, and an expression or durability shortfall is the likely failure route.

carbon.r: Subretinal vitrectomy delivery and macular pigmentary or inflammatory changes in a multi-surgeon global trial can cause modest early letter loss relative to nonsurgical intravitreal aflibercept, narrowing the non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: Subretinal delivery and dose-related retinal changes could cost a few letters, exhausting the non-inferiority margin despite substantial injection reduction.

trials.t: Novel α2-Antiplasmin Inactivation for Lysis of Intravascular Thrombi (NAIL-IT) Trial
trials.ep: Change in right-to-left ventricular diameter ratio (RV/LV) on CT pulmonary angiography from baseline to 48 hours after treatment

fable.r: With 64 patients split across ascending doses and placebo, and anticoagulation alone already lowering RV/LV by about 0.2 at 48 hours, only a large drug effect would be significant.

opus.r: 64 patients spread over ascending TS23 doses against heparin, which already lowers RV/LV over 48 hours, leaves little power, and low-dose cohorts dilute any pooled effect.

sonnet.r: Ascending-dose phase 2 with only 64 patients, so cohorts are small; the RV/LV effect of an alpha2-antiplasmin inactivator at 48 hours must beat heparin-alone improvement, and a small private sponsor may report late or only numerically.

haiku.r: Sixty-four patients with an unstated dose cohort give limited power for a small RV/LV change, and the measure itself is not clearly defined in the record.

carbon.r: Splitting 64 patients across ascending TS23 dose cohorts and placebo yields small per-dose sample sizes where lower ascending doses may have submaximal fibrinolytic activity at 48 hours.

sol.r: Anticoagulation alone improves RV/LV rapidly, while a small ascending-dose study may dilute an effective dose and lack power to establish a significant incremental reduction.

trials.t: A Study of Oral EX039 in Subjects with Mild Alzheimer's Disease
trials.ep: Mean change from baseline in ADAS-Cog (0-70 scale) at week 28

fable.r: Both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB must be met at 28 weeks in 60 patients per arm, which needs a large effect from an unproven agent; slow single-site recruitment also threatens completion.

opus.r: An uncharacterised oral add-on in a single-site 120-patient trial must beat placebo on both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB at 28 weeks, a bar almost no symptomatic Alzheimer's agent has cleared.

sonnet.r: Two co-primary cognitive and functional endpoints must both be met in a single-site phase 2 of 120 patients over 28 weeks; add-on to cholinesterase inhibitors with unproven mechanism and a slow-progressing mild population make this unlikely.

haiku.r: Add-on drugs to cholinesterase inhibitors in mild Alzheimer's have a poor phase 2 record, and both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB must favour the drug.

carbon.r: Detecting statistically significant superiority on both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB co-primary endpoints at 28 weeks as add-on to cholinesterase inhibitors is severely underpowered with only 120 mild Alzheimer's patients.

sol.r: An unestablished oral add-on must produce concordant cognitive and functional benefits over only 28 weeks, with little expected placebo decline and just 60 patients per arm.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study to Evaluate the Effect of Resmetirom on Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Well-compensated NASH Cirrhosis (MAESTRO-NASH-OUTCOMES)
trials.ep: Time to first adjudicated composite clinical outcome event (death, transplant, decompensation, MELD increase to ≥15), up to Month 36

fable.r: Lowering liver fat and stiffness may not translate into fewer decompensation, MELD or death events within about 3 years in cirrhosis, and 3:1 randomisation leaves few placebo events.

opus.r: No antifibrotic or metabolic drug has yet reduced clinical events in compensated NASH cirrhosis; resmetirom's fat and stiffness reductions may not translate into fewer decompensations within about three years, and a modest event count with 3:1 allocation limits power.

sonnet.r: Three-year event-driven outcomes trial in compensated cirrhosis; resmetirom's fibrosis effect may be too modest to move a composite driven by MELD rise and decompensation, and earlier cirrhosis outcome trials of other agents failed.

haiku.r: Event-driven composite in compensated cirrhosis with 211 placebo patients: the event count is limited, so a hazard ratio near 0.78 sits at the edge of significance, and a late or ambiguous readout threatens the June 2027 window.

carbon.r: A 3:1 randomization with only about 211 placebo patients in well-compensated MELD <12 cirrhosis limits statistical efficiency unless resmetirom achieves a large hazard reduction (>30-35%) on hard hepatic decompensation events within 3 years.

sol.r: Histologic efficacy in noncirrhotic NASH may not translate into sufficiently rapid prevention of decompensation once cirrhosis and portal hypertension are established.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, Pharmacokinetics (PK), and Pharmacodynamics (PD) of Satralizumab in Participants With Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartic Acid Receptor (NMDAR) or Anti-leucine-rich Glioma-inactivated 1 (LGI1) Encephalitis
trials.c: NMDAR Autoimmune Encephalitis; LGI1 Autoimmune Encephalitis
trials.ep: NMDAR encephalitis cohort: proportion with mRS improvement of at least 1 point from baseline and no rescue therapy at week 24

fable.r: Small NMDAR cohort with a sizeable placebo response to first-line immunotherapy; a 20-25 point responder difference is needed, and the LGI1 cohort primary must also succeed if both count.

opus.r: NMDAR encephalitis often improves after first-line immunotherapy, so a high placebo responder rate at week 24 with about 30 patients per arm leaves little room to show an add-on IL-6 receptor benefit; the separate LGI1 cohort primary adds a further hurdle.

sonnet.r: Small cohorts with a high placebo response from background first-line immunotherapy; both cohort primaries (NMDAR at wk 24, LGI1 at wk 52) must be met, and an IL-6R blocker's added effect over steroids/IVIG is unproven.

haiku.r: Thirty-one and thirty patients per arm on a responder endpoint where placebo patients recover substantially on standard treatment, so the gap needed is large; both co-primaries (NMDAR at week 24, LGI1 at week 52) must also succeed.

carbon.r: Splitting 122 participants across NMDAR and LGI1 cohorts leaves roughly 30 patients per arm per cohort against active background immunotherapies, requiring very large responder differences, especially if both cohort primaries must succeed.

sol.r: Small antibody-specific cohorts and substantial recovery with background immunotherapy make a significant incremental functional benefit difficult to establish in both cohorts.

trials.t: Assess Safety and Efficacy of Sovateltide in Hypoxic-ischemic Encephalopathy
trials.c: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy; Neonatal Asphyxia; Neonatal Encephalopathy
trials.ep: Death or moderate/severe disability (Bayley cognitive score, GMFCS level, hearing or vision impairment) at 24 months

fable.r: Twenty infants per arm cannot show a significant difference in death or disability unless the effect is very large; the 24-month endpoint will not be ready by mid-2027.

opus.r: Forty neonates give power only for a very large drop in death or disability; with a 24-month endpoint the trial is unlikely to finish on time, and any early report would rest on interim or partial follow-up.

sonnet.r: Twenty infants per arm with a 24-month composite endpoint: only a very large difference reaches significance, and the trial is still recruiting so any 24-month result is unlikely before 2028.

haiku.r: Twenty per arm on a 24-month composite of death or moderate-to-severe disability: even a real ten-point benefit is hard to resolve at this size, and the record still shows recruitment, so the 24-month outcome is unlikely to report before late 2027.

carbon.r: With only 20 neonates per arm evaluated on a binary 24-month death or moderate/severe disability outcome, statistical significance requires an implausibly large absolute risk reduction of roughly 35-40 percentage points.

sol.r: With only 20 infants per arm, the trial needs an exceptionally large reduction in death or disability, and two-year follow-up creates substantial delay and attrition risk.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Mezigdomide, Bortezomib and Dexamethasone (MEZIVd) Versus Pomalidomide, Bortezomib and Dexamethasone (PVd) in Participants With Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma (RRMM)
trials.ep: Progression-free survival from randomisation to progression or death, up to about 5 years

fable.r: PVd may do well in this proteasome-inhibitor-sensitive population with 1-3 prior lines, so swapping pomalidomide for mezigdomide has to deliver a clear PFS gain despite more neutropenia, infections and dose reductions.

opus.r: PVd is an active comparator sharing the bortezomib-dexamethasone backbone, so mezigdomide must beat pomalidomide head to head; neutropenia-driven dose reductions could erode the potency advantage seen in early-phase studies.

sonnet.r: Mezigdomide is a more potent CELMoD than pomalidomide with encouraging phase 1/2 MeziVd data; failure would most likely come from a PVd arm doing better than historical and toxicity limiting dose intensity.

haiku.r: Mezigdomide adds a cereblon modulator to bortezomib and dexamethasone against an active pomalidomide regimen, so the gain over PVd has to be large enough to show on PFS, and the readout timing depends on events in a two-stage design.

carbon.r: Higher rates of mezigdomide-induced neutropenia and infection could require frequent dose reductions or discontinuations that attenuate the progression-free survival advantage over pomalidomide.

sol.r: Mezigdomide must improve meaningfully on an active pomalidomide triplet without losing its potency advantage to cytopenias, infections and dose interruptions.

trials.t: A Study of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) in Participants With Overweight or Obesity and Chronic Kidney Disease With or Without Type 2 Diabetes
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline to week 52 in renal sinus fat content measured by MRI

fable.r: Renal sinus fat on MRI is a noisy measure in a small trial, and weight loss is blunted in CKD patients with type 2 diabetes, so the fall could be too small or too variable to reach significance.

opus.r: Renal sinus fat is a small MRI compartment with noisy segmentation; measurement variability and missing scans could blur an otherwise large weight-loss-driven reduction.

sonnet.r: Tirzepatide's large weight loss should reduce renal sinus fat, but MRI fat percent change is noisy and the arms are modest (about 67 each), so a smaller-than-expected effect could miss significance.

haiku.r: With 67 patients per arm, an MRI renal sinus fat endpoint is noisy, but tirzepatide's large weight loss should move ectopic fat enough to show. The risk is a modest effect masked by MRI variability, or a sponsor who reports it only as directional.

carbon.r: Multiparametric MRI quantification of renal sinus fat in CKD patients can exhibit technical measurement variability that narrows signal-to-noise despite robust systemic weight loss.

sol.r: Renal sinus fat may respond less consistently than body weight or liver fat, and MRI variability plus missing scans could weaken the week-52 comparison.

trials.t: Artesunate Suppositories for the Treatment of HIV-negative Patients With Intra-anal HSIL
trials.c: Anal High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion; Anal Precancerous Condition; AIN 2/3
trials.ep: Complete or partial histopathologic response of intra-anal HSIL on HRA-directed biopsy at week 18, after four 5-day suppository cycles

fable.r: With about 11 artesunate and 6 placebo patients, only a near-complete separation in response rates would be statistically significant, and some placebo lesions regress after biopsy.

opus.r: With 11 versus 6 patients and spontaneous or biopsy-related HSIL regression in the placebo arm, only a very large difference in histologic response would reach p<0.05.

sonnet.r: With 11 vs 6 patients, significance needs a very large response difference; spontaneous partial regression in the placebo arm further limits power.

haiku.r: Eleven artesunate and six placebo patients: a significant histologic difference needs most treated patients to respond while placebo stays low, and HRA biopsy reads are noisy. A small sponsor may report a directional result, which does not count as met.

carbon.r: With only 17 enrolled participants split 2:1 (roughly 11 active versus 6 placebo), the study lacks statistical power to achieve two-sided p<0.05 even if true response exceeds placebo by 35 percentage points.

sol.r: With only about six placebo participants, spontaneous regression and biopsy sampling variation can overwhelm a clinically interesting artesunate response advantage.

trials.t: To Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of TYNADOTE® in the Treatment of Acetaminophen Overdose
trials.ep: Percentage change from baseline in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) at Day 3

fable.r: Twelve patients per arm on top of full-dose acetylcysteine cannot separate the arms on a highly skewed ALT percent change that one or two late presenters dominate.

opus.r: Most overdose patients given IV NAC early never develop hepatotoxicity, so percent ALT change at day 3 is near zero for many and huge for a few; with 12 per arm this skewed outcome will rarely separate.

sonnet.r: Percent change in ALT at Day 3 is extremely skewed and noisy in 12 vs 12 patients who all receive standard IV NAC, which already prevents most liver injury.

haiku.r: Twelve patients per arm at one site, with an ALT percent change at day 3 that spreads widely in acetaminophen-injured livers; the effect would need to be large, and an exploratory study may not give the formal test needed to call it met.

carbon.r: With only 12 patients per arm all receiving effective standard IV N-acetylcysteine, extreme right-skewed variability in Day 3 ALT trajectories leaves minimal power to demonstrate superiority.

sol.r: Effective background NAC and highly skewed, baseline-dependent ALT surges leave little reliable power to demonstrate an additional benefit in 24 patients.

trials.t: Phosphatase Inhibition by Intracoronary Gene Therapy in Subjects With Non-Ischemic NYHA Class III Heart Failure
trials.ep: Cardiovascular-related death within 52 weeks after a single intracoronary infusion

fable.r: A single intracoronary AAV dose has to improve death, NYHA class, LVEF and walk distance together against a blinded placebo arm that usually improves on the soft measures, and earlier calcium-cycling gene therapy failed.

opus.r: Cardiac gene therapy has failed before (CUPID 2), and with about 50 patients per arm and only a handful of cardiovascular deaths, the listed primaries cannot all reach significance unless a hierarchical composite carries a large benefit.

sonnet.r: Four co-primary outcomes must all be met, including CV death, which will have only a handful of events at 52 weeks in a 150-patient phase 2, so a formal win on all of them is very unlikely.

haiku.r: Fifty per arm with a 52-week cardiovascular death endpoint gives only a handful of events, and the card's co-primary rule means LVEF, NYHA class and six-minute walk must all move as well, so meeting every primary is very unlikely.

carbon.r: Antegrade intracoronary AAV gene delivery historically achieves low cardiomyocyte transduction in humans, making significant clinical or composite improvements over modern heart failure therapy unlikely.

sol.r: Very few cardiovascular deaths are expected in these small arms, making success across all four registered primary outcomes especially difficult.

trials.t: A Trial to See if the Combination of Fianlimab With Cemiplimab Works Better Than Pembrolizumab for Preventing or Delaying Melanoma From Coming Back After it Has Been Removed With Surgery
trials.ep: Relapse-free survival (recurrence at any site, excluding new primary melanoma, or death), up to 5 years

fable.r: Adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 gave no relapse-free survival gain in adjuvant melanoma in RELATIVITY-098, and pembrolizumab is a strong active control.

opus.r: LAG-3 blockade added to PD-1 failed to improve RFS in the analogous adjuvant RELATIVITY-098 trial; an active pembrolizumab control leaves little room for an incremental effect large enough to detect.

sonnet.r: Adding anti-LAG-3 to PD-1 has not beaten a PD-1 backbone in adjuvant melanoma (RELATIVITY-098 failed) and pembrolizumab is a strong comparator, so a significant RFS gain is unlikely.

haiku.r: Adding a LAG-3 antibody to adjuvant PD-1 therapy (relatlimab) did not beat nivolumab alone on relapse-free survival, so fianlimab is probably too weak to beat a strong pembrolizumab control.

carbon.r: After complete surgical resection removes bulk tumor antigen, adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 inhibition may confer limited incremental relapse protection over pembrolizumab while increasing immune-related discontinuations.

sol.r: The added activity of LAG-3 blockade in measurable melanoma may not translate to patients rendered disease-free by surgery, as the negative adjuvant relatlimab trial illustrates.

trials.t: A Study to Assess Effectiveness and Safety of Deucravacitinib Compared With Placebo in Participants With Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
trials.ep: Proportion achieving Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Responder Index-4 (SRI-4) response at week 52

fable.r: A placebo SRI(4) rate in the mid-40s, common in global lupus trials on background therapy, would shrink the phase 2 difference below what 516 patients can detect.

opus.r: A high and variable placebo SRI(4) response on stable background therapy can erase a modest TYK2 effect, as when baricitinib and anifrolumab each missed in one of their two phase 3 trials.

sonnet.r: SRI-4 at week 52 carries a large placebo response (about 35-45%) and SLE phase 3 trials fail often, so the 24-point phase 2 gap may shrink to an unconvincing 8-12 points.

haiku.r: SLE trials of new mechanisms have a poor record and placebo arms respond near 35 to 45 percent; the phase 2 signal is the main reason to expect a benefit, but a TYK2 effect in SLE may be modest at this size.

carbon.r: High and regionally variable Week 52 SRI(4) placebo response rates on background immunosuppressants and corticosteroids in global SLE trials can compress the observed treatment difference below ~8.5 percentage points.

sol.r: High and geographically variable SRI-4 response to background treatment could erase much of the strong phase 2 separation.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Effectiveness and Safety of Deucravacitinib (BMS-986165) Compared With Placebo in Participants With Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Share of patients achieving SLE Responder Index-4 (SRI(4)) response at week 52

fable.r: A high placebo SRI(4) rate in a global trial on stable background therapy, as in TULIP-1 and SLE-BRAVE-II, could leave the difference below the roughly 8.5 points this sample can detect.

opus.r: Placebo SRI(4) responses can reach 45-55% in trials with many Latin American and Asian sites on background therapy, leaving a modest TYK2 effect short of significance at 257 per arm.

sonnet.r: SRI-4 at week 52 carries a large placebo response (about 35-45%) and SLE phase 3 trials fail often, so the 24-point phase 2 gap may shrink to an unconvincing 8-12 points.

haiku.r: Sister trial to POETYK SLE-1 with the same design; placebo arms respond near 35 to 45 percent and SLE trials of new mechanisms often miss, so a modest true effect could fail to reach significance.

carbon.r: Elevated placebo SRI(4) responder rates on background antimalarials, immunosuppressants, and steroids across multinational SLE sites could narrow the treatment delta below statistical significance.

sol.r: High and geographically variable SRI-4 response to background treatment could erase much of the strong phase 2 separation.

trials.t: Phase 3 Study of KP-100LI in Subjects With Vocal Fold Scar
trials.ep: Improvement rate in Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10) score from baseline to week 24

fable.r: A subjective voice-handicap score in 62 patients with a sham injection control leaves little room: placebo improvement may be large and the true HGF effect on established scar modest.

opus.r: With 31 patients per arm and a noisy patient-reported percent-change endpoint, a modest true regenerative effect may not reach significance against a placebo intracordal injection.

sonnet.r: With 31 patients per arm and a subjective, noisy patient-reported VHI-10 percent change, a real but moderate effect often misses significance, and placebo injections carry a large response.

haiku.r: Only 62 patients (31 per arm) against a subjective 24-week VHI-10 endpoint with a likely large placebo response; a real benefit could easily be missed at this size.

carbon.r: Sham intracordal injections and voice care produce substantial subjective VHI-10 placebo improvements while refractory vocal fold sulcus patients may dilute the antifibrotic drug signal in a 62-patient sample.

sol.r: Subjective VHI-10 improvement after placebo injection may be substantial, leaving too little separation in just 62 patients.

trials.t: Phase 3 Study to Evaluate Two Regimens of Ianalumab on Top of Standard-of-care Therapy in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SIRIUS-SLE 1)
trials.ep: Proportion of participants achieving SRI-4 response at Week 60

fable.r: The trial has about 145 patients per arm, so a true SRI-4 gain of around 12 points over a placebo rate near 40% could miss significance by chance.

opus.r: About 145 patients per arm gives limited power for the 10-12 point SRI-4 gain typical of successful SLE biologics, and a high, variable placebo response at week 60 can push the difference below significance.

sonnet.r: SRI-4 placebo response of around 40% at week 60 narrows the gap; a depleting anti-BAFF-R antibody should give a belimumab-sized or larger effect, but SLE phase 3 trials fail often.

haiku.r: Anti-BAFF-R B-cell depletion is a plausible route in SLE, but SRI-4 at week 60 against a placebo response near 40 percent and a 145-per-arm comparison leave a real chance of a miss.

carbon.r: Splitting 436 participants across three arms (~145 each for monthly ianalumab and placebo) requires an observed Week 60 SRI-4 difference above ~11.4 percentage points amidst typical SLE placebo variability.

sol.r: Background therapy and corticosteroid management can generate substantial SRI-4 improvement, making the roughly 145-patient monthly comparison vulnerable to a high placebo response.

trials.t: Study of 2 Medicines (Aztreonam and Avibactam) Compared to Best Available Therapy for Serious Gram-negative Infections
trials.ep: Maximum Predicted Plasma Concentration (Cmax) of ATM and AVI

fable.r: Slow paediatric enrolment across four sequential age cohorts (down to 9 months) makes a slip of the March 2027 primary completion date about as likely as not; termination and early results posting are unlikely.

opus.r: Enrolment across four age cohorts, the youngest last, has run since April 2023 and is still open; the March 2027 completion date will more likely be extended than the study stopped.

sonnet.r: Small pediatric phase 2a of 48 patients in rare serious infections across 8 countries and 4 age cohorts; registered primary completion of March 2027 while still recruiting in October 2026 makes a slip past June 2027 likely, and results are unlikely to be posted by August 2027.

haiku.r: Still recruiting in a pediatric Phase 2a with 48 planned participants and a 31 March 2027 completion date, so slipped enrollment is the likely path; posting results by the read date is unlikely.

carbon.r: Enrolling hospitalized pediatric patients down to 9 months of age with acute serious Gram-negative infections within narrow prior-antibiotic windows frequently causes substantial recruitment delays.

sol.r: Four small age cohorts and a narrow antibiotic-treatment window make a recruitment extension more likely than termination.

trials.t: Study to Assess Safety and Efficacy of Tenapanor for Treatment of IBS-C in Pediatric Patients 12 to Less Than 18 Years
trials.ep: Share of patients with weekly combined response (≥30% abdominal pain reduction plus ≥2 more spontaneous bowel movements) in at least 6 of 12 weeks

fable.r: About 60 patients per arm against an adult effect of only 8-13 percentage points and a variable paediatric placebo response leaves power well under 50%.

opus.r: Sixty adolescents per arm gives little power for the 8-13 point gain seen in adults, and pediatric functional GI trials often show high placebo responses.

sonnet.r: About 60 per arm and a high adolescent pain placebo response mean a roughly 10-15 point responder gap, as seen in adults, would only just reach significance.

haiku.r: About 60 patients per arm in pediatric IBS-C with a high placebo response on the combined pain and stool endpoint; with two active doses, one clearing the bar is enough, which helps somewhat.

carbon.r: With roughly 60 patients per arm across two active doses and high pediatric IBS-C placebo response rates, achieving statistical significance on the stringent composite responder endpoint is challenging.

sol.r: With about 60 patients per arm, adult-sized response gains may not overcome adolescent placebo response on the combined pain-and-stool endpoint.

trials.t: A Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Inavolisib Plus Fulvestrant Compared With Alpelisib Plus Fulvestrant in Participants With HR-Positive, HER2-Negative, PIK3CA Mutated, Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer Post CDK4/6i and Endocrine Combination Therapy
trials.ep: Progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review, from randomization to progression or death (follow-up up to about 64 months).

fable.r: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant is an active same-class comparator and cross-trial efficacy looks similar, so the hazard ratio may not be far enough below 1 to reach significance with about 270 events.

opus.r: The comparator inhibits the same target; if alpelisib keeps its efficacy when toxicity is managed, inavolisib's advantage may be too small (HR near 0.8) to reach significance.

sonnet.r: Inavolisib may only modestly out-last alpelisib in a post-CDK4/6 population; the gain likely comes mostly from better tolerability, so the hazard ratio could land near 0.8 and miss.

haiku.r: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant is an active comparator with real PIK3CA benefit, so inavolisib must beat a PI3K-alpha inhibitor, not placebo, to show superiority on PFS at 0.05.

carbon.r: Demonstrating statistically significant PFS superiority over an active same-class PI3K-alpha inhibitor (alpelisib) plus fulvestrant requires substantial potency or dose-intensity advantages.

sol.r: Inavolisib may improve tolerability without adding enough antitumor activity to beat an active PI3K inhibitor in post-CDK4/6 disease.

trials.t: A Research Study to Evaluate the Effects of a New Oral Medicine Called Cenerimod in Adults With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Proportion of patients achieving SRI-4 response (based on mSLEDAI-2K) at Month 12

fable.r: The phase 2b signal was small and only nominally significant at 4 mg, so the true SRI-4 gain over a placebo rate near 45% may be too small to reach significance.

opus.r: Phase 3 rests on a dose and subgroup signal from a phase 2b that missed its primary analysis; S1P1 modulation may not move SRI-4 beyond a placebo response near 40%.

sonnet.r: Cenerimod missed its primary endpoint in phase 2 CARE, with benefit seen mainly post hoc in high-interferon patients, so an all-comer SRI-4 gain over a ~40% placebo response is likely small.

haiku.r: Oral S1P1 modulator working through lymphocyte trapping rather than B-cell depletion; S1P modulators have a poor lupus record, and a 235-per-arm trial needs a gap of about 10 points to win.

carbon.r: High and variable 12-month SRI-4 placebo response rates on background immunosuppressants and belimumab frequently obscure modest treatment effects in global Phase 3 lupus trials.

sol.r: Background immunosuppression and variable SRI-4 scoring could produce a high placebo response, leaving insufficient Month-12 separation.

trials.t: Study of Ianalumab Versus Placebo in Addition to First-line Corticosteroids in Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
trials.ep: Stable response off treatment at 12 months (SROT-12): at least 75% of platelet counts ≥50 G/L without rescue between Weeks 53 and 65

fable.r: With about 75 patients per arm, two doses sharing alpha and a stringent 12-month off-treatment endpoint, a real benefit of 15-20 points could still miss significance.

opus.r: If B cells recover by month 12, the off-treatment remission gap may shrink below the roughly 18 points detectable with about 75 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Patients must already respond to steroids, so many placebo patients keep a stable response off treatment; a 12-month off-treatment endpoint also carries more dropout and rescue noise with about 75 per arm.

haiku.r: The primary was switched in May 2026 to a strict off-treatment endpoint (at least 75 percent of counts at or above 50 G/L with no rescue, weeks 53 to 65); placebo arms rarely hold response off treatment, so the outcome hinges on ianalumab's durable effect.

carbon.r: Because eligibility selects patients who already responded to initial corticosteroids prior to randomization, higher-than-expected 12-month remission in the control arm could narrow the treatment difference.

sol.r: Requiring an initial steroid response enriches for patients who may remain in remission without B-cell depletion, potentially shrinking the late off-treatment benefit.

trials.t: Clinical Study of Tumor Treating Fields Combined with Gemcitabine and Albumin-bound Paclitaxel in the First-line Treatment of Locally Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
trials.sp: Jiangsu Healthy Life Innovation Medical Technology Co., Ltd
trials.ep: Overall survival from enrolment to death from any cause (follow-up up to 12 months after last study treatment)

fable.r: PANOVA-3 suggests only a modest survival effect (HR 0.82), so a trial of this size could easily miss significance; the final analysis is also unlikely to be ready by mid-2027.

opus.r: TTFields added only a modest OS gain over gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in LAPC in PANOVA-3 (HR about 0.82, p=0.039); with 512 patients the trial has roughly coin-flip power for an effect of that size, and device adherence is uncertain.

sonnet.r: Chinese PANOVA-3 replication in locally advanced pancreatic cancer with a modest expected OS gain (PANOVA-3 HR 0.82, p=0.039); open-label device trial, 5 sites, still recruiting, so result unlikely before mid-2027 and effect likely near the significance edge.

haiku.r: Overall survival is likely underpowered for a realistic hazard ratio near 0.8 with about 380 deaths, and the registry completion date is already past while the record still says recruiting.

carbon.r: Tumor treating fields confer only a modest overall survival benefit on top of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in locally advanced pancreatic cancer, leaving moderate risk of missing statistical significance.

sol.r: The class-level survival benefit is modest and could be diluted by device adherence or differences in field delivery.

trials.t: A Safety and Efficacy Study of Bevacizumab, Paclitaxel, Carboplatin Compared to Avastin® in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
trials.ep: Objective response rate at week 18 by independent review (RECIST 1.1)

fable.r: Equivalence is very likely if the product is truly similar; the main risk is a chance difference in response rates pushing the confidence interval outside the margin.

opus.r: Bevacizumab biosimilar trials nearly always show ORR equivalence; the main way this fails is chance or slow, uneven accrual pushing the ORR difference interval past the margin.

sonnet.r: Bevacizumab biosimilar equivalence trial on week-18 ORR; such trials usually succeed and the main risk is a chance miss of the ORR margin. Russian sponsor with little public disclosure, and enrolment still recruiting so completion likely slips.

haiku.r: Equivalence on week-18 ORR is the usual outcome for a bevacizumab biosimilar with 620 patients; the main uncertainty is whether a Russian sponsor publishes the result by mid-2027.

carbon.r: Sampling variability in Week-18 radiological response rates could cause the confidence interval to narrowly cross a biosimilar equivalence margin despite analytical similarity.

sol.r: Unknown equivalence margins and a chance imbalance in Week-18 response could prevent equivalence despite similar biological activity.

trials.t: Study of Dapansutrile Tablets in Subjects With an Acute Gout Flare
trials.c: Acute Gout Flare; Gout Attack; Gout Flare
trials.ep: Change from baseline in target-joint pain on a 100-mm visual analogue scale at 72 hours after the loading dose

fable.r: Efficacy rests on an uncontrolled open-label study; against a placebo arm that improves naturally by 72 hours with rescue analgesia, the true difference may be only a few millimetres.

opus.r: Acute gout flares improve quickly on their own and placebo patients get paracetamol rescue, so the placebo pain drop at 72 hours is large and can swamp a moderate NLRP3-inhibitor effect.

sonnet.r: Oral NLRP3 inhibitor with modest phase 2 signal in gout flare; placebo response on the 72-hour VAS is large with rescue medication available, so a 7-10 mm difference is needed and may not materialize. Private sponsor, slow recruiting.

haiku.r: With 200 active and 100 placebo patients, a 72-hour pain difference of about 6 mm is needed for significance, and the central effect estimate sits close to that, so the result is close to a coin flip.

carbon.r: Allowing enrollment up to 96 hours after gout flare onset alongside rescue medication access in both arms risks substantial spontaneous and rescue-driven pain resolution on placebo by 72 hours.

sol.r: Allowing flares up to 96 hours old and measuring pain 72 hours later risks substantial spontaneous improvement and rescue use in the placebo arm.

trials.t: A Research Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Cenerimod in Subjects Suffering From Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Share of patients with SLE Responder Index 4 (SRI-4) response at month 12 versus baseline

fable.r: The phase 2b signal was small and only nominally significant at 4 mg, so the true SRI-4 gain over a placebo rate near 45% may be too small to reach significance.

opus.r: Cenerimod's phase 2b signal was a small mSLEDAI-2K difference (about 1.2 points), and SLE phase 3 trials with SRI-4 at month 12 often fail against high placebo response on background therapy.

sonnet.r: S1P1 modulator whose phase 2 CARE study missed the overall SRI-4 endpoint and showed benefit only in a high-IFN, low-steroid subgroup. SLE trials with 12-month SRI-4 and a 40-45 percent placebo response fail often.

haiku.r: Lupus phase 3 trials on an SRI-4 endpoint often fail, and a single cenerimod dose may add only a modest response gain over a placebo response near 37 percent.

carbon.r: Substantial 12-month SRI-4 placebo response rates on concomitant standard-of-care SLE immunosuppressants make reaching the ~9-percentage-point threshold for significance difficult.

sol.r: A substantial background-therapy response could erase a modest cenerimod advantage on the variable SRI-4 composite.

trials.t: 24 Weeks Double-blind Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial to Evaluate Efficacy, PK, Safety of LOU064 in Adolescents (12 - <18) With CSU and Inadequate Response to H1-antihistamine Followed by Optional 3 Years Open-label Extension and an Optional 3 Years Safety Long-term Treatment-free Follow-up
trials.ep: Change from baseline in weekly Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7) at Week 12 in adolescents aged 12 to under 18

fable.r: Only 100 patients (2:1) and three registered primary measures: the itch score, with the smallest adult effect, could miss significance even if UAS7 succeeds.

opus.r: Only 100 adolescents (67 vs 33) and three co-primary endpoints (UAS7, ISS7, HSS7) must all reach significance; a higher placebo response in teenagers could leave one component short.

sonnet.r: Remibrutinib clearly beat placebo in adult CSU (REMIX-1/2, UAS7 difference about 7-8), but this adolescent study has only about 100 patients and needs UAS7, ISS7 and HSS7 all significant; a high adolescent placebo response is the main risk.

haiku.r: Three co-primary changes (UAS7, ISS7, HSS7) must all reach significance in 67 versus 33 adolescents; the adult effect is large enough that the 33-patient control arm is the binding constraint.

carbon.r: With only about 33 placebo patients and three registered primary outcomes (UAS7, ISS7, and HSS7), chance variability in adolescent placebo improvement could leave one component short of p<0.05.

sol.r: Only about 33 placebo patients and the requirement to succeed on both itch and hives components leave room for a chance failure despite established adult activity.

trials.t: Study of XL092 + Nivolumab vs Sunitinib in Subjects With Advanced or Metastatic Non-Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma
trials.ep: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent radiology committee, analysed about 27 months after first randomization

fable.r: Mixed non-clear-cell histologies (papillary, unclassified, translocation) may dilute the TKI plus checkpoint-inhibitor benefit, and early censoring in an open-label sunitinib arm under central review could narrow the PFS gap in a 317-patient trial.

opus.r: Sunitinib is a weak comparator in papillary-dominant nccRCC (PFS about 5-6 months), so failure would mostly need zanzalintinib plus nivolumab to underperform the cabozantinib-nivolumab benchmark in a mixed histology population.

sonnet.r: Strong phase 1b/2 evidence for cabozantinib/zanzalintinib plus nivolumab in non-clear cell RCC against a weak sunitinib control (mPFS 6-8 months); risk is that both PFS and ORR must be significant with split alpha, and event-driven timing may slip.

haiku.r: Both PFS and ORR must be significant as co-primaries with an unstated alpha, and the overall survival key secondary is unlikely to be mature by mid-2027, so it is probably void.

carbon.r: Requiring success across dual primary endpoints or high sunitinib performance in indolent papillary subsets could dilute the observed progression-free survival difference.

sol.r: Related kinase inhibitor–immunotherapy combinations are active, but XL092 lacks randomized evidence in this population, and both PFS and response must succeed despite heterogeneous histology and possible alpha splitting.

trials.t: A Multicentre, Randomised, Double-blind, Parallel Group, Placebo-controlled, Time-to-first Asthma Exacerbation Phase III Efficacy and Safety Study of Benralizumab in Paediatric Patients With Severe Eosinophilic Asthma
trials.ep: Time to first asthma exacerbation during the double-blind treatment period (at least 16 weeks, event-driven)

fable.r: With only 94 children and an event-driven time-to-first-exacerbation endpoint, the trial has power only for a very large effect, while anti-IL-5 pathway drugs have shown modest or no exacerbation benefit in children and adolescents.

opus.r: With only 94 children and an event-driven design that may close with about 40-50 exacerbations, even a true hazard ratio near 0.6 gives under 50% power.

sonnet.r: Benralizumab cuts exacerbations 30-50 percent in adults, but this paediatric event-driven trial has only 94 patients and perhaps 40-50 events, giving limited power unless the HR is below about 0.5.

haiku.r: An event-driven trial of 94 children may end with fewer exacerbations than planned, so a significant hazard ratio is plausible but not assured.

carbon.r: With only 94 randomized pediatric patients, moderate chance variation or viral-driven non-eosinophilic exacerbations could prevent statistical significance despite genuine biological activity.

sol.r: Benralizumab has established anti-exacerbation activity, but only 94 children and adolescents are randomized; limited first-event counts and improved background-treatment adherence could prevent significance.

trials.t: A Study of Milvexian in Participants After an Acute Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk Transient Ischemic Attack- LIBREXIA-STROKE
trials.ep: Time to first ischemic stroke, followed up to the global targeted endpoint date (about 41 months)

fable.r: Milvexian 25 mg twice daily gives less factor XIa inhibition than the asundexian dose that worked in OCEANIC-STROKE, the same dose was futile in LIBREXIA-ACS, and the trial includes lacunar strokes, so the stroke reduction may be too small to reach significance.

opus.r: Factor XIa inhibition must add meaningful protection on top of antiplatelets; LIBREXIA-ACS was stopped for futility, though asundexian's positive OCEANIC-STROKE supports the stroke setting.

sonnet.r: Factor XIa inhibition just reduced recurrent ischemic stroke in OCEANIC-STROKE (asundexian HR 0.74), supporting the class; risk is that milvexian's dose or the antiplatelet background gives a smaller effect, as in the stopped ACS trial.

haiku.r: A 12,523-patient event-driven trial is well powered, so the question is mainly whether milvexian reduces ischemic stroke on top of antiplatelet therapy, with a central hazard ratio near 0.78.

carbon.r: Factor XIa inhibition added to standard antiplatelet therapy may provide only a modest reduction across heterogeneous non-cardioembolic stroke subtypes such as small-vessel lacunar strokes.

sol.r: The phase 2 clinical-stroke signal was promising but its MRI-inclusive primary endpoint was negative; incremental protection on contemporary antiplatelet therapy could be smaller than the phase 3 design requires.

trials.t: Study of Futibatinib in Patients With Advanced Cholangiocarcinoma With FGFR2 Fusion or Rearrangement
trials.c: Advanced Cholangiocarcinoma; FGFR2 Fusions; Gene Rearrangement
trials.ep: ORR by independent central review

fable.r: The trial is still recruiting a rare FGFR2-rearranged population weeks before its registered December 2026 primary completion, so the date will most likely slip well into 2027; termination is unlikely because the study is a post-approval commitment.

opus.r: Still recruiting in late 2026 in a rare FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma population, so the December 2026 primary completion date will very likely be pushed back, with results posted only well after the read date.

sonnet.r: Rare FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma phase 2 still recruiting 120 patients; registered primary completion of December 2026 is unlikely to hold, and the ORR primary is generally unchanged.

haiku.r: The trial is still listed as recruiting past its registered December 2026 primary completion date, so the record will probably be updated late and the primary outcome time frame may be cleaned up.

carbon.r: Because this rare-biomarker FGFR2-rearranged cholangiocarcinoma dose-optimization trial was still recruiting in October 2026 against a December 2026 target, primary completion will very likely slip past March 2027.

sol.r: Recruitment in an uncommon molecular subset is the likely bottleneck; the approved drug and straightforward dose-optimization design favor eventual completion but not the current date.

trials.t: A Study of Milvexian Versus Apixaban in Participants With Atrial Fibrillation
trials.ep: Time to first stroke or non-CNS systemic embolism in atrial fibrillation, over up to 4 years of follow-up

fable.r: Factor XIa inhibition may protect less against cardioembolic stroke than factor Xa inhibition, as asundexian showed in OCEANIC-AF, so even a modest excess of strokes over apixaban would breach the non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: Factor XIa inhibition may not prevent cardioembolic stroke as well as factor Xa inhibition; asundexian was clearly inferior to apixaban in OCEANIC-AF, and with about 850 events a tight margin needs milvexian to match apixaban almost exactly.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority to apixaban should be met if milvexian 100 mg BID inhibits factor XIa adequately; the main failure path is under-inhibition as seen with asundexian 50 mg in OCEANIC-AF, or a tight margin with few events.

haiku.r: Factor XIa inhibition may protect less against stroke than apixaban, as the OCEANIC-AF failure suggested, and the non-inferiority margin is unstated, so the margin may decide the result.

carbon.r: Apixaban sets a high antithrombotic bar in atrial fibrillation, and even modest excess cardioembolic stroke risk with Factor XIa inhibition could miss the non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: Another factor XIa inhibitor substantially underprotected against AF-related embolism versus apixaban; milvexian may also sacrifice more efficacy than the non-inferiority margin permits despite reducing bleeding.

trials.t: A Study of the Effect of ZT-01 on Night-time Hypoglycemia in Type 1 Diabetes
trials.ep: Rate of nocturnal (midnight to 06:00) hypoglycemic events below 54 mg/dL lasting at least 15 minutes, per 28-day treatment period

fable.r: Boosting the glucagon response with a somatostatin receptor 2 antagonist may blunt rather than prevent CGM-defined events below 54 mg/dL, leaving a rate reduction too small to detect over a 28-day crossover period.

opus.r: It is unproven that an SSTR2 antagonist restores glucagon counterregulation well enough to cut nocturnal hypoglycemia in long-standing type 1 diabetes, and placebo-period counts are noisy and overdispersed with only about 62 participants per dose.

sonnet.r: Phase 2a crossover with three doses where any dose may win; the drug augments counter-regulatory glucagon, but nocturnal CGM events are noisy and the effect could be modest. Recruitment was still open in late 2026, so reporting before mid-2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: The crossover with 62 per arm gives reasonable power on a frequent event, but the record is still recruiting past its registered 2026-12 completion, so the timeline will slip.

carbon.r: Somatostatin receptor 2 antagonism at bedtime may not overcome alpha-cell suppression during real-world nocturnal hyperinsulinemia enough to significantly cut CGM-detected hypoglycemic episodes.

sol.r: Restoring glucagon during a low may shorten hypoglycemia without preventing enough 15-minute CGM-defined nocturnal events, particularly when participants already use personal CGM and adjust insulin.

trials.t: Oral Pooled Fecal Microbiotherapy to Prevent Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation Complications (PHOEBUS Trial)
trials.ep: Overall survival at 12 months after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation

fable.r: An oral microbiome product is unlikely to cut 12-month all-cause mortality by the 35-40% that a 387-patient trial needs, since relapse and causes unrelated to the gut microbiota account for many deaths after reduced-intensity transplant.

opus.r: Restoring gut microbiota diversity has to translate into a mortality benefit at 12 months, with only about 90 deaths; a realistic effect (HR about 0.8) is far below what this phase 2b can detect.

sonnet.r: An overall survival gain from a microbiome product at 12 months after reduced-intensity transplant is a high bar: deaths are driven by relapse, infection and GvHD, and the trial has only about 100 expected events.

haiku.r: A 387-patient phase 2b on 12-month overall survival has little power for a survival gap, and the registry still shows recruiting although the registered primary completion date has passed.

carbon.r: Demonstrating a statistically significant 12-month overall survival improvement in 387 allogeneic transplant recipients requires a large hazard reduction rarely achieved by supportive microbiome interventions.

sol.r: Microbiome restoration may not reduce all-cause mortality when relapse and other transplant hazards dilute the addressable benefit, while subsequent antibiotics can disrupt engraftment.

trials.t: Iltamiocel Compared to Placebo for Chronic Fecal Incontinence in Females With Obstetric Injury
trials.ep: Change from baseline in frequency of fecal incontinence episodes at 12 months

fable.r: Diary-based incontinence endpoints show large placebo and sham-injection responses, which sank the sponsor's earlier stress urinary incontinence trial, so a real cell effect may not separate from placebo at 12 months.

opus.r: Sham and placebo injections into the anal sphincter produce large reductions in incontinence episodes, so a one-time autologous cell injection has to beat a strong placebo response at 12 months with only 100 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Invasive-injection placebo responses in fecal incontinence are large and the OASI-restricted population looks like a post hoc enrichment; the sponsor is private and rarely issues press releases, so public results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

haiku.r: A 200-patient two-arm cell trial on a diary endpoint with a large placebo response, and the registry gives no scale for episode frequency, so the variability answer assumes an SD of 3 episodes per week.

carbon.r: Sham intrasphincteric injection and diary monitoring in chronic fecal incontinence historically produce large 40-55% placebo episode reductions that obscure modest cell-therapy benefits.

sol.r: Sham injection, diary effects and regression to the mean could produce a substantial placebo improvement, leaving insufficient separation for a cell therapy whose functional benefit remains uncertain.

trials.t: Clinical Study on Adjuvant Therapy of TQB3616 Combined With Endocrine Therapy Compared With Placebo Combined With Endocrine Therapy in Patients With Breast Cancer
trials.sp: Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Invasive disease-free survival from randomization, up to 60 months

fable.r: The registered December 2026 date implies an early look when invasive disease events are still few, so a true benefit of the size seen with abemaciclib or ribociclib may not yet cross an interim boundary.

opus.r: The adjuvant CDK4/6 class record is mixed: abemaciclib and ribociclib succeeded, but palbociclib failed twice. If TQB3616 has weaker exposure, tolerability or adherence, or the population is low-risk with few events, IDFS may not separate.

sonnet.r: Adjuvant CDK inhibitor benefit is real in monarchE and NATALEE but PALLAS and PENELOPE-B failed; with an early analysis and few IDFS events the HR may not reach significance, and a Chinese sponsor may not report by mid-2027.

haiku.r: An add-on to endocrine therapy with a low placebo three-year event rate needs a large hazard reduction to reach significance, and the registered completion has passed while the trial is still listed as active.

carbon.r: With 1,946 patients rather than the 5,000+ enrolled in global adjuvant CDK4/6 trials, fewer than expected early recurrence events could limit statistical power at the primary analysis.

sol.r: A class-consistent IDFS benefit may still miss significance in this 2:1 adjuvant study if early recurrence rates are low; adjuvant CDK4/6 benefit has not been uniform across agents.

trials.t: Program to Assess Adverse Events and Change in Disease Activity of Oral Upadacitinib in Adult Participants With Moderate to Severe Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving BICLA (British Isles Lupus Assessment Group-based Composite Lupus Assessment) response at week 52

fable.r: Lupus trials on background therapy often see placebo BICLA responses of 30-40%, and with two replicate studies of about 250 per arm one of them could miss even if the drug works, as happened with baricitinib.

opus.r: SLE phase 3 trials often fail because of high placebo response on background therapy and heterogeneity between regions; baricitinib succeeded in one replicate trial and failed in the other, and here both replicate studies need to succeed.

sonnet.r: SLE phase 3 trials fail often because of high placebo BICLA response and background therapy effects; upadacitinib has phase 2 support, but two replicate studies must both show benefit and results are unlikely before July 2027.

haiku.r: BICLA is a demanding composite and lupus placebo responses run high, so a clear week-52 gap is uncertain even for an active JAK inhibitor.

carbon.r: High and variable week-52 BICLA placebo response rates on permissive background immunosuppressants frequently erode treatment differences across replicate Phase 3 lupus trials.

sol.r: Background therapy and glucocorticoid management can generate high, variable placebo responses in SLE, potentially producing discordant replicate studies despite genuine JAK1 activity.

trials.t: A Phase II Study of AAA617 Alone and AAA617 in Combination With ARPI in Patients With PSMA PET Scan Positive CRPC
trials.ep: PSA response

fable.r: Small non-comparative Novartis phase 2 with enrolment closed at 49 and a fixed end date of 23 Dec 2026; it should end on schedule, with some chance it is labelled terminated and little chance results post before late 2027.

opus.r: Novartis stopped enrolment at 49 and set study completion equal to primary completion (Dec 2026), which points to a planned close-out on schedule; results posting is likely near the 12-month deadline, after August 2027.

sonnet.r: Small (49 patients) non-comparative Novartis phase 2, enrolment closed; primary completion should be met or updated to an actual date near Dec 2026, with results posting more likely after the August 2027 read date.

haiku.r: No efficacy goal, so the risk is operational: the registered primary completion of Dec 2026 may be pushed past March 2027, and results posting may fall after the read date.

carbon.r: Although enrollment of 49 patients is complete and registered primary completion is December 2026, tracking confirmed PSA nadir responses can slightly delay final primary completion updates.

sol.r: Enrollment is closed and treatment courses are finite, but extended PSA follow-up and exploratory reporting could delay the final data cut or registry posting.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety Study of Povorcitinib in Participants With Inadequately Controlled Moderate to Severe Asthma
trials.ep: Absolute change in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 from baseline to week 24.

fable.r: About 62 patients per arm gives a standard error near 70 mL on FEV1, so a dose must show roughly 140 mL over placebo; an oral JAK1 inhibitor in a population not enriched for eosinophilic disease may deliver only about 100 mL.

opus.r: Oral JAK1 inhibition has no proven lung-function benefit in asthma and the population is not selected for type-2 inflammation; with about 62 per arm and an SD near 380 mL the highest dose needs roughly 140 mL over placebo to reach significance.

sonnet.r: An oral JAK1 inhibitor in an unselected exacerbation-prone asthma population with about 62 per arm needs roughly a 125 mL FEV1 gain over placebo to reach significance, which is a large effect for this mechanism.

haiku.r: With about 62 patients per arm and a likely effect near 60 mL, the 24-week FEV1 difference probably falls short of significance; lung-function gains from a JAK1 inhibitor in asthma are unproven.

carbon.r: Systemic JAK1 inhibition may produce smaller bronchodilator FEV1 gains than biologics like dupilumab or tezepelumab, leaving ~62 patients per arm underpowered for modest effects.

sol.r: JAK1 inhibition may produce only a modest FEV1 gain after optimized ICS-LABA, below what roughly 62 patients per arm can establish.

trials.t: A Study of Tobemstomig + Nab-Paclitaxel Compared With Pembrolizumab + Nab-Paclitaxel in Participants With Previously Untreated, PD-L1-Positive, Locally-Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival (time to disease progression or death from any cause), followed up to about 24 months

fable.r: Adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 has not clearly beaten PD-1 alone outside melanoma, and with 83 patients a hazard ratio near 0.6 would be needed for significance against an active pembrolizumab control.

opus.r: A PD-1/LAG-3 bispecific must beat an active pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel arm on PFS in only 83 patients; tobemstomig showed no advantage over pembrolizumab in other phase 2 head-to-head studies and Roche has deprioritised it.

sonnet.r: A PD-1/LAG-3 bispecific against pembrolizumab on the same chemotherapy backbone needs an implausibly large PFS gain to be significant in 83 patients, and the program appears deprioritized.

haiku.r: A LAG-3 add-on to pembrolizumab in only 83 patients needs a hazard ratio near 0.6 to reach significance, and most such add-ons have not clearly beaten pembrolizumab.

carbon.r: Demonstrating statistically significant PFS superiority of PD-1xLAG-3 bispecific tobemstomig over active pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel with only 83 patients requires an unrealistically large hazard ratio reduction.

sol.r: An 83-patient trial needs a large incremental PFS benefit over pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy, whereas adding LAG3 blockade may provide only modest improvement.

trials.t: Trial of Two Adagrasib Dosing Regimens in NSCLC With KRAS G12C Mutation (KRYSTAL 21)
trials.c: Advanced Cancer; Metastatic Cancer; Malignant Neoplasm of Lung
trials.ep: Objective Response Rate (ORR) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST 1.1).

fable.r: A fully enrolled post-marketing dose-comparison study that should complete normally; BMS tends to post results close to the 12-month mark, which falls after the 31 Aug 2027 read date.

opus.r: A dose-optimisation study tied to the adagrasib accelerated approval; BMS will run it to completion, with results posting probably near the 12-month deadline in late 2027.

sonnet.r: Descriptive dose-regimen comparison with data collection essentially complete at registered primary completion; BMS usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting by the August 2027 read date is unlikely to be more than a minority outcome.

haiku.r: No efficacy goal, so the risks are operational: results posting by August 2027 is close to even, and a substantive change to the descriptive ORR primary is unlikely.

carbon.r: KRYSTAL-21 is an FDA post-marketing dose-optimization trial that has finished recruitment with registered completion in late 2026, so it should finish cleanly and post results near the 12-month window.

sol.r: This fully enrolled, sponsor-backed dose-optimization study should usually finish rather than stop, although registry posting may wait until close to its reporting deadline.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Daily OM-85 in Young Children With Recurrent Wheezing
trials.c: Recurrent Wheezing; Wheezing Lower Respiratory Illness
trials.ep: Rate of wheezing/asthma-like episodes (WEs) during the 6-month treatment period

fable.r: Earlier positive OM-85 wheeze data come from small single-centre trials; in a rigorous multinational trial the true reduction may be nearer 15-20% than 38%, which 148 children per arm cannot reliably detect.

opus.r: Older small trials of OM-85 showed ~35-40% fewer wheezing episodes, but modern multicentre trials of bacterial lysates usually show smaller effects; with overdispersed episode counts in 296 children, a 20% reduction gives under 50% power.

sonnet.r: Bacterial lysate effects on wheezing are modest and inconsistent; with about 150 per arm a rate ratio around 0.8 to 0.85 would not reach significance.

haiku.r: The 296-child, 6-month rate ratio needs roughly a 20 percent cut in episodes to reach significance, and OM-85 effects in young wheezers have been modest and inconsistent.

carbon.r: Multicenter western pediatric wheezing cohorts with controller use and high vaccination rates may experience a smaller episode reduction from oral bacterial lysates than earlier single-center studies.

sol.r: The wheezing reduction suggested by small earlier studies may shrink under rigorous multicenter testing with contemporary controller therapy and substantial spontaneous improvement.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of SPH4336 in Combination With Endocrine Therapy in the Treatment of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer
trials.c: Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Objective response rate per RECIST 1.1, assessed over approximately 3 years

fable.r: Continuing CDK4/6 inhibition after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor has given at best a modest benefit (postMONARCH HR 0.73; PACE and PALMIRA negative), and the trial lists both ORR and PFS as primary outcomes.

opus.r: CDK4/6 rechallenge after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor gives modest ORR gains (about 5-10 points), which 127 per arm barely detects, and both ORR and PFS primaries must be met.

sonnet.r: Both ORR and PFS are listed as primaries and must both be met; ORR after prior CDK4/6 inhibitor is low in both arms, so a significant ORR gap is hard to show, and PFS data are likely not mature by mid-2027.

haiku.r: Two co-primaries, ORR and PFS, must both be significant in the same arm, and an add-on to endocrine therapy after CDK4/6 failure is likely to show only a modest ORR gain.

carbon.r: Continuing CDK4/6 inhibition after progression on prior CDK4/6 therapy has produced mixed results across agents, and dual ORR/PFS primary endpoints raise the bar for success.

sol.r: Acquired resistance after CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy may leave too little incremental activity to demonstrate both a response-rate advantage and longer PFS.

trials.t: LSALT Peptide for Prevention or Attenuation of Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Cardiac Surgery
trials.ep: Percentage of patients with acute kidney injury (KDIGO criteria) within 7 days after on-pump cardiac surgery

fable.r: Nearly every drug tested to prevent cardiac-surgery AKI has failed in controlled trials, and with 120 per arm LSALT would need an absolute reduction of about 12 points on a noisy creatinine and urine-output endpoint.

opus.r: Pharmacological prevention of cardiac-surgery AKI has a long record of failures, and LSALT peptide has no human AKI efficacy data; a 120-per-arm trial needs about a 15-point absolute reduction to be significant.

sonnet.r: A small phase 2 of a novel peptide on a hard endpoint (any KDIGO AKI incl. urine output) in an enriched population; the incidence in placebo is high and the drug needs about a 40 percent relative reduction to be significant.

haiku.r: A 5-day IV peptide must cut the roughly 40 percent AKI rate by about 12 points to be significant at 120 per arm, and early-phase kidney-protection drugs have mostly failed to do that.

carbon.r: Cardiac surgery-associated AKI involves multifactorial ischemia, hemolysis, and hemodynamic injury where single-pathway DPEP-1 inhibition with LSALT peptide has unproven clinical efficacy.

sol.r: Blocking inflammatory leukocyte recruitment may not reduce heterogeneous perioperative AKI enough to show superiority with 120 patients per arm.
