trials.t: A Study of an Intermittent ADT Approach With Apalutamide Monotherapy in Participants With mCSPC
trials.ep: Radiographic progression-free survival from randomization (after 6 months of apalutamide plus ADT with PSA <0.2 ng/mL), assessed at 18 months

fable.r: Both primaries must be met: non-inferior 18-month rPFS, with few events and an unstated margin, and a diary-based percent change in hot-flash score that depends on how quickly testosterone recovers after ADT is stopped.

opus.r: The hot-flash co-primary should be clearly met, but non-inferiority on 18-month rPFS rests on few events in good-prognosis PSA responders, so a wide confidence interval could cross the margin even with no true difference.

sonnet.r: Both primaries must be met: rPFS non-inferiority within an unknown margin and a hot-flash benefit; the hot-flash benefit is near-certain, but non-inferiority on rPFS with few events and an unstated margin carries real risk.

haiku.r: Dropping ADT in the intermittent arm can let 18-month rPFS fall beyond the unstated non-inferiority margin, and the rate gap must stay inside it.

carbon.r: With high 18-month rPFS rates in deep PSA responders and only a subset of enrolled patients randomized at Cycle 7, random variation could breach the non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: Deep PSA responders should retain good short-term disease control, but fewer randomized patients than enrolled and an unstated non-inferiority margin could prevent a conclusive result.

trials.t: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of Oral Minoxidil 1 mg in Female Androgenetic Alopecia
trials.ep: Change in target-area non-vellus hair count from baseline to week 24

fable.r: 1 mg is a low dose; if its gain over placebo is nearer 6 than 10 hairs/cm2 the 1% significance level is at risk, and the trial also wants oral minoxidil to match topical 2% within an unstated margin.

opus.r: Superiority over placebo is very likely with 208 versus 104 patients, but 24 weeks is short for minoxidil, the strict 0.01 level and any co-primary non-inferiority test against topical 2% minoxidil add risk.

sonnet.r: The 0.01 significance level and the placebo response in hair counts make a small true effect hard to confirm; the non-inferiority comparison to topical 2% minoxidil may also be required and has no stated margin.

haiku.r: The primary is a descriptive hair-count analysis and the trial's own hypothesis is ambiguous between superiority to placebo and non-inferiority to topical 2 percent, so the sponsor may not report the primary objective as met.

carbon.r: If the trial requires formal non-inferiority against active 2% topical minoxidil under double-dummy clinical supervision, high topical adherence could narrow oral minoxidil's margin.

sol.r: Oral minoxidil is likely to beat placebo, but the active-comparator non-inferiority requirement and its unstated margin remain important uncertainties.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Inavolisib in Combination With Phesgo Versus Placebo in Combination With Phesgo in Participants With PIK3CA-Mutated HER2-Positive Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival on maintenance therapy after first-line induction, followed up to about 40 months

fable.r: Adding a PI3K-alpha inhibitor to pertuzumab/trastuzumab adds hyperglycaemia, diarrhoea and stomatitis over a long maintenance period, which can erode dose intensity; a result by mid-2027 could also be an early stop for slow accrual.

opus.r: PI3K blockade may add less in HER2-driven disease than in HR+/HER2- (INAVO120), and long maintenance with inavolisib toxicity (hyperglycaemia, diarrhoea, stomatitis) could erode dose intensity in a modest 230-patient trial.

sonnet.r: Inavolisib has proven PFS benefit in PIK3CA-mutated HR+ disease, but PI3K inhibition with HER2 therapy is unproven (alpelisib EPIK-B2 was stopped), and PIK3CA-mutant HER2+ maintenance PFS may only be modestly improved.

haiku.r: Main risk is a PFS gain too small for 230 patients: at a true HR near 0.65 with about 140 events, power is modest, and the registered 2026-12 completion date may slip past mid-2027.

carbon.r: Induction responders receiving Phesgo plus optional endocrine therapy may achieve longer control PFS than historical CLEOPATRA PIK3CA-mutant estimates, slowing event accrual and attenuating hazard ratios.

sol.r: PIK3CA targeting may not add enough to dual HER2 blockade to reproduce the large inavolisib benefit seen in endocrine-resistant HER2-negative disease.

trials.t: A Study to Compare Efficacy, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics and Safety of CT-P53 and Ocrevus in Patients With Relapsing-remitting Multiple Sclerosis
trials.ep: Ocrelizumab AUC in the PK group, and the number of new gadolinium-enhancing T1 lesions up to week 24 in the main group

fable.r: Equivalence must be shown several times over (two PK AUC windows in patients against both EU and US Ocrevus, plus near-zero lesion counts), so a variance-driven miss on any one comparison is the main way to fail.

opus.r: Biosimilars rarely fail; the residual risk is a PK geometric-mean ratio CI or the ratio of near-zero GdE lesion counts falling outside the protocol margins through chance or a manufacturing difference.

sonnet.r: The trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026 against a Feb 2027 registered completion, so the date will probably slip and topline is more likely H2 2027; Celltrion biosimilar equivalence trials almost always succeed.

haiku.r: Main risk is a lesion-count equivalence test that is underpowered, because new GdE lesions are rare on modern ocrelizumab, so the count-ratio interval may be too wide to show equivalence even if the drug matches.

carbon.r: Near-complete suppression of new T1 Gd-enhancing MRI lesions by anti-CD20 therapy yields very low event counts, creating ratio variability despite comparable PK and B-cell depletion.

sol.r: Near-complete lesion suppression by ocrelizumab can leave sparse MRI counts, making efficacy equivalence less certain than straightforward PK comparability.

trials.t: Afimkibart (RO7790121) for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Active Crohn's Disease
trials.ep: Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAE), Serious Adverse Events (SAE) and AE Leading to Discontinuation

fable.r: A 21-patient safety study inherited from Telavant with a year-end placeholder date; it will most likely close around then or be pushed a few months, with results posted about a year after completion.

opus.r: Enrolment stopped at 21 after Roche moved afimkibart into phase 3, so the study is likely closed around end-2026 as completed or terminated, with results posting due only after the read date.

sonnet.r: Small Roche phase 2 (21 patients) with a safety primary and a registered end of 2026; Roche usually keeps or updates dates promptly, and results posting typically comes closer to the one-year deadline.

haiku.r: Closed-to-enrolment Phase 2 safety-primary study with 21 enrolled. Main uncertainties are whether Roche revises the 2026-12-31 completion date past 2027-03-31 and whether results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov within a year of completion.

carbon.r: With enrollment closed at 21 participants and registered completion at year-end 2026, the trial is likely winding down on schedule ahead of Roche's broader Phase 3 afimkibart Crohn's program.

sol.r: The very small enrolled cohort and safety-only primary suggest curtailed recruitment followed by safety follow-up, with some risk of administrative termination or another completion-date revision.

trials.t: Disitamab Vedotin With Pembrolizumab vs Chemotherapy in Previously Untreated Urothelial Cancer Expressing HER2
trials.sp: Seagen, a wholly owned subsidiary of Pfizer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review, from randomization to progression or death, about 3 years

fable.r: PFS should be won comfortably, so the realistic way to miss is the second primary: overall survival may be immature or short of its interim boundary when PFS is first reported in a trial of only 412 patients.

opus.r: PFS should be met, but OS counts as a co-primary here and may not cross its interim boundary at the first readout, since post-progression enfortumab vedotin in the chemotherapy arm dilutes the OS difference in a global population.

sonnet.r: Strong precedent for an ADC plus PD-1 over platinum chemo, but OS is a co-primary and may be immature at the first analysis, and HER2 IHC 1+ patients may benefit less.

haiku.r: Main risk is the wrong population: HER2 IHC 1+ patients are a large share and may benefit less than IHC 2+/3+ patients, diluting the PFS hazard ratio, and both PFS and OS must reach superiority.

carbon.r: While PFS superiority is highly likely, meeting both PFS and OS co-primary endpoints by mid-2027 faces risk from immature OS events and post-progression enfortumab vedotin or checkpoint inhibitor crossover.

sol.r: A substantial PFS benefit is plausible, but the second primary OS endpoint may remain immature or be diluted by effective subsequent therapies at the first disclosure.

trials.t: Study of ALTO-300 in MDD
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 6 in MADRS total score in a pre-defined patient subgroup, ALTO-300 added to an ongoing antidepressant.

fable.r: Agomelatine's edge over placebo is small (around 2 MADRS points) and the EEG biomarker was derived from open-label data, so the enriched subgroup may not separate enough from a high US placebo response.

opus.r: Agomelatine has small antidepressant effects and little adjunctive evidence, and a biomarker-defined subgroup primary in an adjunctive MDD trial with high placebo response leaves little room to separate.

sonnet.r: Adjunctive MDD trials have large placebo responses and Alto's biomarker-enriched programme has missed before (ALTO-100 phase 2b); the subgroup is small, so power is limited.

haiku.r: Main risk is underpowering: a biomarker subgroup of roughly 80 patients per arm gives under 50 percent power for a 2-point MADRS difference, and the high adjunctive placebo response erodes any gain.

carbon.r: Large placebo improvements in US multicenter adjunctive MDD trials and modest effect sizes of agomelatine risk overwhelming EEG biomarker enrichment in a reduced subgroup sample.

sol.r: The pre-defined biomarker subgroup may not reproduce exploratory enrichment, leaving agomelatine's modest average activity unable to separate from a substantial adjunctive-placebo response.

trials.t: Determine Effectiveness of Anifrolumab In SYstemic Sclerosis (DAISY)
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with revised CRISS-25 response at week 52

fable.r: Anifrolumab reached phase 3 in systemic sclerosis with no randomized phase 2, and placebo patients on background mycophenolate often improve enough to reach CRISS-25, leaving little room for a modest drug effect.

opus.r: Type I IFN blockade has no randomized efficacy data in SSc, and background mycophenolate drives placebo improvement in a demanding multi-domain composite, so a difference of about 11 points with 157 per arm may not be reached.

sonnet.r: Systemic sclerosis phase 3 trials have a poor record and anifrolumab's phase 2 did not clearly separate on skin score; placebo CRISS response is also substantial.

haiku.r: Main risk is a weak drug effect on a composite responder endpoint in a population with high placebo variability, since the response needs gains across skin, lung, function and patient measures together.

carbon.r: Permitted background mycophenolate and immunosuppressants stabilize skin and lung disease in placebo patients, historically blunting biologic treatment differences in Phase 3 systemic sclerosis trials.

sol.r: Background immunosuppression and spontaneous skin improvement may produce many placebo CRISS-25 responders, leaving too little incremental benefit from interferon blockade.

trials.t: A Clinical Study of SI-B001 Combined With Docetaxel in the Treatment of Non-small Cell Lung Adenocarcinoma and Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma
trials.c: Non-small Cell Lung Adenocarcinoma; Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Lung
trials.ep: Overall survival from randomization to death from any cause, followed up to about 24 months

fable.r: An EGFR x HER3 antibody added to docetaxel is unlikely to move overall survival much in unselected post-immunotherapy NSCLC, where nearly every docetaxel combination or replacement has failed on survival.

opus.r: A naked EGFRxHER3 bispecific added to docetaxel in EGFR-wild-type NSCLC after immunochemotherapy is likely to give only a modest OS gain, and both OS and BICR-PFS must reach significance.

sonnet.r: A naked EGFR x HER3 bispecific added to docetaxel must beat docetaxel on both OS and PFS (co-primary); post-IO NSCLC docetaxel add-on and replacement strategies have mostly failed to improve OS.

haiku.r: Main risk is a modest added benefit over docetaxel alone, since the docetaxel backbone is shared by both arms and the OS primary needs a clear hazard reduction at 589 patients.

carbon.r: Unconjugated EGFRxHER3 bispecific blockade added to docetaxel may modestly improve PFS and ORR without achieving statistically significant overall survival superiority required across co-primary endpoints.

sol.r: Dual EGFR/HER3 inhibition may improve tumour control without producing a sufficiently large survival gain in an unselected post-immunotherapy population.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Deucravacitinib in Adults With Active Sjögren's Syndrome
trials.ep: Change from baseline in ESSDAI (EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index) score at week 52.

fable.r: With no phase 2 in Sjogren's, TYK2 inhibition may add only about a point over a placebo arm that typically improves 4 to 5 ESSDAI points by week 52.

opus.r: Without phase 2 data in Sjogren's, TYK2 inhibition may give at most a 1-point ESSDAI benefit, which a large placebo improvement and between-patient variability can easily mask.

sonnet.r: ESSDAI trials in Sjogren's carry large placebo improvement in recently diagnosed, highly active patients, leaving only a modest placebo-adjusted effect to detect.

haiku.r: Main risk is a placebo-adjusted ESSDAI change below about 1 point, since placebo change in Sjogren trials is large and drug effects have been small; the trial is well powered for an effect of 1.5 or more.

carbon.r: Large placebo ESSDAI declines over 52 weeks and absence of dedicated Phase 2 Sjögren's efficacy data for deucravacitinib create substantial risk of insufficient separation despite strong IFN biology.

sol.r: TYK2 blockade may not add enough to substantial placebo ESSDAI improvement, while effects on glandular damage and patient-reported symptoms are less established than its lupus activity.

trials.t: Study of Tinengotinib VS. Physician's Choice a Treatment of Subjects With FGFR-altered in Cholangiocarcinoma
trials.ep: Part B: progression-free survival by BICR per RECIST v1.1, from randomization to first documented progression or death.

fable.r: Part B is small with a 2:1 split, so if the true hazard ratio is nearer 0.7 than 0.55 against chemotherapy in a slow-growing FGFR2-fusion population, the BICR PFS analysis may not reach significance.

opus.r: Resistance to a prior FGFR inhibitor is heterogeneous (off-target bypass as well as kinase-domain mutations), so tinengotinib's phase 1/2 activity may not hold across a broader randomized Part B population.

sonnet.r: Part B is small and event-driven; a true effect is likely against poor chemotherapy outcomes after FGFR inhibitor failure, but few events and an uncertain dose selection add variance.

haiku.r: Main risk is underpowering: 67 control patients and about 160 PFS events leave a narrow margin, and the Part B dose chosen in Part A adds uncertainty about the experimental arm.

carbon.r: Heterogeneous non-FGFR2 bypass resistance mechanisms (such as RAS/MAPK alterations) after prior FGFR inhibition and modest Part B sample size could dilute tinengotinib's PFS advantage.

sol.r: Only part of the 200-patient enrolment contributes to the selected-dose comparison, so heterogeneous post-FGFR-inhibitor resistance could leave insufficient statistical precision.

trials.t: Ischemic and Bleeding Outcomes After Angiolite Stent Implantation and an Abbreviated Dual Antiplatelet Therapy
trials.ep: Target lesion failure at 1 year, Angiolite sirolimus-eluting stent versus Xience everolimus-eluting stent, across both antiplatelet regimens

fable.r: The stent non-inferiority test should pass, but the paired bleeding superiority test for 1-month DAPT has only about 100 events and a control arm in which many patients will stop DAPT early anyway.

opus.r: With a 1-year TLF rate near 5%, a tight absolute non-inferiority margin or higher-than-expected event rates in an all-comer population could leave the upper confidence bound above the margin even with equivalent stents.

sonnet.r: Both stent non-inferiority on target lesion failure and superiority of 1-month DAPT on bleeding are primaries; the second is the more fragile, and the margin is unknown.

haiku.r: Main risk is the bleeding co-primary: superiority of 1-month over 12-month DAPT on BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding needs a clear gap, and with roughly 30 to 50 events per arm it may fall short even if stent non-inferiority holds.

carbon.r: Because both factorial primary endpoints must succeed, lower-than-expected BARC 2, 3, or 5 bleeding rates or open-label DAPT non-adherence could leave the 1-month vs 12-month bleeding comparison underpowered.

sol.r: Similar stent performance is likely, but a low target-lesion-failure event count or a tight non-inferiority margin could defeat that comparison even if abbreviated DAPT reduces bleeding.

trials.t: ELAPR002f Injectable Gel in the Treatment of Atrophic Acne Scars
trials.ep: Share of participants with at least 1-grade improvement on both cheeks on the Allergan Acne Scar Improvement Scale (ASIS), baseline to Day 181

fable.r: Saline injected with a needle three times has a real subcision effect, so if the control response on the blinded 5-grade scale is high the 39-patient saline arm leaves limited power.

opus.r: Intradermal saline injections themselves produce visible scar improvement from needle trauma and assessor optimism, so the saline responder rate could be high enough to shrink the gap on a stringent both-cheeks responder definition.

sonnet.r: A saline intradermal active control that also gets three injection sessions can produce a sizeable 1-grade response on both cheeks, which could narrow the margin versus a filler-like gel in 118 vs 39 patients.

haiku.r: A space-filling gel should produce a large ASIS gain, but the saline active control with intradermal needling may respond well and narrow the gap; the two-cheek responder rule also adds stringency.

carbon.r: Repeated intradermal saline injections induce mechanical subcision and dermal remodeling that can elevate bilateral 1-grade ASIS responder rates in the small 39-patient control arm.

sol.r: Saline injections can themselves improve scar appearance, and the gel's incremental effect must persist to Day 181 and produce improvement on both cheeks.

trials.t: A Study of Comparing Overall Improvement of Patients With Spondyloarthritis Treated With Jitongning Tablets and Placebo
trials.ep: Proportion of participants achieving ASAS20 improvement at week 8

fable.r: A herbal tablet may add too little over a sizeable placebo response on the largely subjective ASAS20 at only 8 weeks in patients washed out of NSAIDs.

opus.r: A herbal tablet has no proven anti-inflammatory potency in axial spondyloarthritis, and after an NSAID washout the placebo arm may still post 25-35% ASAS20 at week 8, leaving a small difference.

sonnet.r: Placebo ASAS20 response at week 8 after NSAID washout can be 30% or higher; a TCM tablet needs a 12+ point margin with 204 per arm, though such domestic phase 3 trials are usually reported as positive.

haiku.r: A modest herbal effect over eight weeks against a high placebo ASAS20 response, with 204 per arm, leaves the trial near its power limit; the enrolment is also slow, so the timeline is likely to slip.

carbon.r: After NSAID washout, subjective ASAS20 symptom regression to the mean in the placebo arm may narrow the 8-week treatment effect of an oral herbal formulation.

sol.r: The tablets may provide symptomatic relief without enough incremental anti-inflammatory activity to separate from a substantial placebo response on ASAS20.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy of Durvalumab Plus Tremelimumab in Combination With Chemotherapy Compared With Pembrolizumab in Combination With Chemotherapy in Metastatic NSCLC Patients With Non-squamous Histology Who Have Mutations and/or Co-mutations in STK11, KEAP1, or KRAS
trials.ep: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival (RECIST 1.1 progression or death) in randomized participants

fable.r: With about 100 patients and under 80 PFS events, only a hazard ratio near 0.63 or better would be significant, and the record frames PFS as an estimate, not a tested hypothesis.

opus.r: The tremelimumab benefit in STK11/KEAP1/KRAS-mutant disease comes from exploratory POSEIDON subgroups, mostly on OS, and against an active pembrolizumab-chemo control a 100-patient trial needs a PFS HR near 0.6 to reach significance.

sonnet.r: A 103-patient phase IIb with roughly 75-80 PFS events needs an HR near 0.6 to reach p<0.05; the likely true effect of durvalumab plus tremelimumab over pembrolizumab with chemotherapy is HR 0.7-0.85.

haiku.r: With about 100 randomized patients and roughly 70 PFS events, a hazard ratio significant at 0.05 needs to be near 0.6, a larger gain than an added CTLA-4 arm is likely to give in this genotype.

carbon.r: With only 103 randomized patients against an active pembrolizumab-chemotherapy standard and multiple registered PFS primary measures, only a large hazard ratio improvement could achieve statistical significance.

sol.r: A modest CTLA-4 benefit over an effective pembrolizumab–chemotherapy regimen is unlikely to achieve conventional significance with approximately 100 patients.

trials.t: IN10018 in Combination With Pegylated Liposomal Doxorubicin (PLD) vs. Placebo in Combination With PLD for the Treatment of Platinum-resistant Recurrent Ovarian Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent central review (follow-up up to 2 years)

fable.r: The single-arm phase 1b signal (response near 50%, PFS about 6 months) may shrink under blinded randomization and central review, leaving a hazard ratio short of the roughly 0.65 needed.

opus.r: The FAK-inhibitor add-on effect rests on single-arm phase 1b data; if the true PFS gain over PLD is modest, about 115 events with 2:1 allocation may not reach significance by BICR.

sonnet.r: A FAK inhibitor added to PLD in a double-blind randomized phase 2 with about 130 BICR PFS events needs HR near 0.7 or better; the earlier single-arm signal may overstate the benefit over PLD alone.

haiku.r: A FAK inhibitor added to PLD in platinum-resistant disease may add only a modest PFS gain, and about 140 events in a 2:1 phase 2 need a hazard ratio near 0.71 to reach significance.

carbon.r: Promising single-arm FAK inhibitor plus PLD activity in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer often attenuates under blinded central review against a randomized PLD control arm.

sol.r: The main risk is that encouraging early combination activity reflects patient selection rather than a sufficiently large randomized benefit from FAK inhibition.

trials.t: A Phase III Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Anifrolumab in Adults With Chronic and/or Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: CLASI-70 response (at least 70% reduction from baseline in CLASI-A score) at Week 24

fable.r: Cutaneous lupus trials can show a high placebo response on background therapy, and scarring discoid lesions may not clear enough for a 70% CLASI-A reduction by week 24.

opus.r: CLE placebo arms can improve with background topicals and seasonal variation, and scarring discoid lesions respond slowly, which could compress the CLASI-70 difference at week 24.

sonnet.r: Chronic discoid CLE is less interferon-driven than SLE skin disease, so the CLASI-70 gap at week 24 could be smaller than the 15-25 points seen with CLASI-50 in SLE; with 170 per arm a gap under 10 points would be borderline.

haiku.r: CLASI-70 is a stringent responder threshold at week 24, and the skin response to a drug validated in SLE is untested in refractory CLE, so a weaker-than-hoped response is the most likely failure route.

carbon.r: The stringent CLASI-70 responder threshold at Week 24 may be harder to reach in fibrotic or scarred chronic discoid lupus lesions despite clear biological activity.

sol.r: A stringent CLASI-70 threshold in chronic, antimalarial-refractory lesions could yield fewer responders than the earlier SLE skin data imply.

trials.t: Study of Tilpisertib Fosmecarbil in Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with clinical response per modified Mayo Clinic Score at week 12

fable.r: TPL2 inhibition has no clinical proof of concept in ulcerative colitis and the earlier compound's phase 2 was stopped, so the effect in advanced-therapy failures may be too small for arms of about 40.

opus.r: TPL2 inhibition is unvalidated in UC; the earlier tilpisertib molecule needed a prodrug reformulation, and in an advanced-therapy-refractory population with roughly 44 patients per dose arm a moderate effect would miss significance.

sonnet.r: A novel TPL2/COT mechanism in advanced-therapy-experienced UC, with only about 55-60 patients in the top-dose arm, needs a 15+ point gap in clinical response versus a placebo rate near 25-30%.

haiku.r: The highest-dose arm is probably smaller than the 88 planned, and a phase 2 in advanced-therapy-experienced UC needs about 12 to 15 points of separation at week 12 to reach significance, which is a large gap for this population.

carbon.r: Oral TPL2 (MAP3K8) inhibition lacks prior clinical proof of efficacy in ulcerative colitis and faces redundant inflammatory pathways in advanced-therapy-experienced patients.

sol.r: Clinical response is permissive, but an unvalidated TPL2 mechanism may add little in a heavily pretreated population once patients are split among doses.

trials.t: Study of Organ Perfusion in Heart Transplantation in Children
trials.ep: adverse event reporting

fable.r: Paediatric heart transplants are rare in Germany, so the 15-patient target at three sites will probably slip past the registered date; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by the read date is very unlikely.

opus.r: Pediatric heart transplants are rare and enrolment across three German centres is slow, so the registered January 2027 completion will probably slip or recruitment will continue past March 2027.

sonnet.r: Small 15-patient pediatric heart transplant study in only 3 German centres; pediatric heart transplants are rare, enrolment has been slow since 2023, and a safety-only primary outcome from a small German sponsor makes late completion likely and CT.gov results unlikely.

haiku.r: Fifteen children across three German centres, all waiting for a first transplant, will make enrolment slow, so the January 2027 completion date will probably slip past May 2027 while the trial is still recruiting.

carbon.r: Slow donor organ availability in pediatric heart transplantation across three German centers makes enrollment delays beyond the registered January 2027 primary completion date likely.

sol.r: Recruitment will probably extend because eligible pediatric heart transplants are uncommon and donor procurement and recipient eligibility impose additional constraints.

trials.t: MDMA-Assisted CBCT for PTSD vs CBCT RCT
trials.ep: Change in CAPS-5 total severity score from baseline to 3-month follow-up in the participant with PTSD

fable.r: A single-site pilot with perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm, compared against an active couple therapy, has limited power to show a CAPS-5 difference of 6-7 points.

opus.r: A single-site feasibility pilot with perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm against an active conjoint therapy may not test CAPS-5 formally or reach significance even with a real 10-point effect.

sonnet.r: A single-site pilot with perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm, SD of CAPS-5 change near 14, and primary outcomes that are mostly feasibility and safety, so significance on CAPS-5 is uncertain and the 'primary objective met' wording is ambiguous.

haiku.r: A 60-person single-site pilot needs a CAPS-5 gap of about 8 points to reach significance, and the sample is too small to show that size reliably; the trial also reads more as feasibility than as a superiority test.

carbon.r: The registry lists feasibility, safety, and appropriateness questionnaires alongside CAPS-5 as primary outcomes in a small dyadic sample compared against an already effective CBCT control.

sol.r: CBCT is an effective active comparator, and enrollment may represent only about 15 PTSD patients per arm, leaving little power for MDMA's incremental benefit.

trials.t: Trial of Efficacy and Safety of NS-229 Versus Placebo in Patients With Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis
trials.c: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis; Churg-Strauss Syndrome
trials.ep: Proportion of patients in remission at week 28, defined as BVAS = 0 and prednisolone/prednisone dose of 4 mg/day or less.

fable.r: With about 22 patients per arm, significance needs a remission gap of roughly 35 points, which only a large, so far unproven, effect of JAK1 inhibition in EGPA would deliver.

opus.r: With about 22 patients per arm, a strict single-timepoint remission (BVAS 0, prednisolone <=4 mg) and a placebo arm partly on background mepolizumab/benralizumab, a JAK1 effect would need to exceed roughly 25-30 points to reach p<0.05.

sonnet.r: About 22 patients per arm and a strict endpoint (BVAS 0 with prednisolone 4 mg or less) mean NS-229 needs roughly a 35-point gain to reach p<0.05; a phase 2 novel oral agent in EGPA on top of steroids and biologics will probably fall short.

haiku.r: Only about 45 patients, split roughly 23 to 22, against a strict composite remission endpoint (BVAS 0 plus a steroid taper to 4 mg or less) leaves little power for a clear superiority result in a phase 2.

carbon.r: With only 45 EGPA patients and optional background anti-IL-5 therapy, detecting statistically significant steroid-sparing remission at p<0.05 requires an unusually large effect from JAK1 inhibition.

sol.r: With only 45 patients, conventional significance requires a very large remission difference, while background anti-IL5 therapy and steroid tapering make control response unpredictable.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Patidegib Gel 2% for Preventing Basal Cell Carcinomas on the Face of Adults With Gorlin Syndrome
trials.ep: Number of new basal cell carcinomas on the face per participant over 12 months, assessed by the central photo review board

fable.r: The trial repeats a post hoc winning subgroup of a failed phase 3; if the true reduction in new facial BCCs is nearer 30% than 50%, 113 patients with overdispersed counts will not reach significance.

opus.r: Topical patidegib may not deliver enough hedgehog inhibition in the skin; the earlier 2% gel phase 3 missed overall, and this trial rests on a post hoc PTCH1-mutation subgroup whose effect may shrink on replication.

sonnet.r: The earlier phase 3 of patidegib 2% gel in Gorlin syndrome missed its primary endpoint, and this trial rests on a post-hoc high-burden subgroup; topical hedgehog inhibition may be too weak to cut new BCC counts significantly at 12 months.

haiku.r: A topical gel applied to the face has to reach many small skin tumours at useful levels, and the count endpoint needs a sizeable relative cut in new lesions to reach significance in 113 patients.

carbon.r: Limited dermal penetration of topical patidegib 2% gel and inter-patient overdispersion in new BCC lesion counts contributed to an earlier Phase 3 miss in Gorlin syndrome.

sol.r: Strong Hedgehog biology may not overcome limited topical efficacy, and enrichment based on an earlier favorable subgroup may not reproduce the hoped-for prevention benefit.

trials.t: A Study to Test if a Fixed-Dose Combination of Fluticasone Propionate/Albuterol Sulfate is Effective in Preventing Asthma Exacerbations
trials.sp: Teva Branded Pharmaceutical Products R&D LLC
trials.ep: Time to first severe clinical asthma exacerbation during the event-driven double-blind treatment period (minimum 24 weeks, up to 42 months)

fable.r: If as-needed fluticasone through the dry powder device delivers less anti-inflammatory benefit than budesonide did in MANDALA, the hazard ratio could drift toward 0.85-0.9 and miss significance.

opus.r: As-needed fluticasone propionate via a dry-powder inhaler (including children) may deliver less anti-inflammatory effect per rescue use than budesonide-albuterol did in MANDALA, shrinking the hazard ratio toward 0.85 or above.

sonnet.r: As-needed ICS plus albuterol rescue has cut severe exacerbations by about 25-30% in MANDALA and BATURA; a fluticasone/albuterol analogue at high dose in a large event-driven trial should replicate, with some risk from a different ICS or a pediatric mix.

haiku.r: The control arm gets albuterol alone, a weak comparator, so adding a high-dose inhaled steroid should cut severe exacerbations clearly; the main risk is a smaller-than-expected effect in an event-driven trial of 924 per arm.

carbon.r: High adherence to background inhaled controller therapy could lower severe exacerbation rates or attenuate the relative rescue benefit, while hierarchical gating through the low-dose arm could affect secondary testing.

sol.r: Improved controller adherence and intensive follow-up could suppress exacerbations in the albuterol arm and erode the incremental benefit of rescue fluticasone.

trials.t: Phase II Study of Artesunate Ointment for the Treatment of Vulvar High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions (Vulvar HSIL, VIN2/3)
trials.c: Vulvar Diseases; HPV Infection; Vulvar HSIL
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with complete histologic response of vulvar HSIL at week 18.

fable.r: With 18 versus 9 patients, artesunate needs about 7 of 18 complete histologic responses against none on placebo; a real but moderate effect would miss, and a single placebo regression raises the bar further.

opus.r: With 18 vs 9 patients, Fisher's exact test needs about 8 of 18 complete histologic responses against 0 of 9 on placebo for p<0.05; a plausible 20-35% complete response rate on topical artesunate falls short.

sonnet.r: With only 18 vs 9 patients, a significant difference needs about 50% histologic complete response against near 0% on placebo; the topical artesunate effect from earlier small studies is likely smaller and placebo response in vulvar HSIL is non-zero.

haiku.r: With 18 patients on drug and 9 on placebo, only a very large difference in complete histologic response can reach significance, and biopsy-based regression is noisy.

carbon.r: With only 18 experimental and 9 placebo patients, two-sided p<0.05 requires an unusually large difference in complete histologic response.

sol.r: With only nine placebo patients, even moderate artesunate activity may not produce a statistically convincing difference in complete histologic clearance.

trials.t: A Clinical Trial to Assess the Safety and PK of OMN6 in HABP or VABP Caused by Acinetobacter Baumannii Complex
trials.c: Hospital-acquired Bacterial Pneumonia; Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pneumonia
trials.ep: To assess the safety of a single-day treatment with OMN6 vs. matching placebo when coadministered with a background therapy of meropenem and colistin

fable.r: Likely to run late: enrolling 54 patients with rapid-test-positive Acinetobacter HABP/VABP in about ten months at 15 sites is ambitious for a small sponsor; results posting by August 2027 is very unlikely.

opus.r: Enrolling 54 patients with Acinetobacter HABP/VABP in Greece and Israel within about 10 months of a May 2026 start is ambitious; the March 2027 primary completion will probably slip.

sonnet.r: Phase 2a in Acinetobacter HABP/VABP started May 2026 with sequential cohorts; this rare, critically ill population is slow to enrol, so the March 2027 primary completion likely slips past June 2027; a small company will not post results by Aug 2027.

haiku.r: Recruiting ventilated and hospital-acquired pneumonia patients in only two countries means slow enrolment, so the March 2027 completion date will probably slip past late June 2027 unless the record is updated.

carbon.r: Recruiting ventilated pneumonia patients with rapid-test confirmed Acinetobacter baumannii and strict organ-function exclusions is notoriously slow, making delays past June 2027 highly likely.

sol.r: Sequential dosing and a narrowly eligible critically ill population make recruitment delay more likely than completion on the ambitious March schedule.

trials.t: Study to Investigate Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Zibotentan/Dapagliflozin Compared to Dapagliflozin in Participants With Chronic Kidney Disease and High Proteinuria (ZENITH High Proteinuria)
trials.c: Chronic Kidney Disease With High Proteinuria
trials.ep: Change in eGFR from baseline to Month 24

fable.r: Change in eGFR at month 24 includes any acute haemodynamic dip from the endothelin antagonist, so a roughly 30% albuminuria reduction may translate into only about 1 mL/min/1.73 m2, close to what the trial can detect.

opus.r: Total eGFR change at 24 months mixes any acute hemodynamic dip with the chronic benefit; endothelin antagonists slow decline modestly (about 1 mL/min/yr), so the 24-month difference may be only 1-1.5 units against an SE near 0.5.

sonnet.r: Zibotentan adds a UACR reduction of about 30-35% over dapagliflozin, but an endothelin antagonist's acute eGFR dip offsets the chronic slope benefit at month 24, so the net eGFR difference may be about 1 mL/min, near the edge of detectability.

haiku.r: The dapagliflozin control already slows eGFR decline, so the added endothelin blocker must add a measurable eGFR gain over two years; fluid retention from the endothelin class could also blunt the kidney signal.

carbon.r: Acute hemodynamic eGFR dip from zibotentan may partially offset chronic slope preservation at Month 24 on top of background RAASi and dapagliflozin.

sol.r: An acute hemodynamic eGFR reduction and effective dapagliflozin background therapy may obscure a modest chronic kidney-protective benefit at month 24.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate Efficacy and Safety of TOUR006 in Participants 18 to 80 Years of Age With Thyroid Eye Disease
trials.sp: Tourmaline Bio, Inc., a Novartis Company
trials.ep: Share with proptosis response (≥2 mm reduction in study eye, no ≥2 mm worsening in fellow eye, no rescue) at Week 20

fable.r: IL-6 blockade mainly calms inflammation; its proptosis effect looks smaller than that of IGF-1R antibodies, and with about 26 patients per arm the trial needs a gain of roughly 25 points or more over placebo.

opus.r: IL-6 blockade mainly calms orbital inflammation; its effect on proptosis (the primary) is likely smaller than IGF-1R inhibition, and about 26 patients per arm cannot reliably detect a 20-25 point difference.

sonnet.r: Anti-IL-6 acts mainly on inflammation (CAS) rather than proptosis; a 2 mm proptosis response at week 20 may be modest vs IGF-1R drugs, and with about 26 per arm the effect must reach about 30 points over placebo to be significant.

haiku.r: Only about 26 patients per arm in a three-arm phase 2b, and the proptosis response needs a 2 mm drop with no rescue, so a clear superiority result at week 20 depends on a large effect.

carbon.r: IL-6 blockade reduces orbital inflammation (CAS) in thyroid eye disease, but its ability to achieve >=2 mm proptosis reduction at Week 20 is much weaker than IGF-1R inhibition.

sol.r: IL-6 inhibition may suppress inflammatory activity without reversing proptosis sufficiently for a small week-20 study.

trials.t: Study of Lenacapavir and Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate (F/TDF) in Prevention of HIV in Cisgender Women in the United States (HPTN 102)
trials.ep: Pharmacokinetic (PK) Parameter: Ctrough for Lenacapavir (LEN) at the End of Week 26

fable.r: Should run to plan as an open-label PK and safety study of an approved product; the main uncertainty is whether results are posted by the end of August 2027, about a year after primary completion.

opus.r: Gilead's PURPOSE 3 hit primary completion in July 2026 with lenacapavir PrEP already approved, so results are due on ClinicalTrials.gov by July 2027 with no reason to delay; Gilead usually posts on time.

sonnet.r: Gilead PrEP phase 2 with primary completion July 2026 is already fully enrolled; Gilead usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline (July 2027), so posting by Aug 2027 is more likely than not, and the PK, safety and acceptability outcomes are unlikely to change.

haiku.r: A completed, US-only Gilead study whose registered primary completion passed in July 2026, so results posting is due under federal rules and Gilead usually meets that clock.

carbon.r: Active, not recruiting HPTN/Gilead Phase 2 PrEP study whose July 2026 primary completion has passed; ongoing follow-up to January 2028 delays registry results posting.

sol.r: Completed enrollment and apparently completed primary follow-up favor continued extension follow-up and results posting around the one-year reporting deadline.

trials.t: Study of Lenacapavir and Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate (F/TDF) for Prevention of HIV in People Who Inject Drugs (HPTN 103)
trials.ep: Pharmacokinetic (PK) Parameter: Ctrough for Lenacapavir (LEN): LEN Plasma concentration at the End of the Dosing Interval (Week 26)

fable.r: Past primary completion and likely to finish as planned; results fall due around late July 2027, so posting by 31 August 2027 is somewhat better than even odds.

opus.r: PK/safety phase 2 run by Gilead with HPTN; follow-up past primary completion (July 2026) is routine, so stopping is very unlikely and results posting by the one-year deadline (July 2027) is likely given Gilead's posting record.

sonnet.r: Gilead-sponsored phase 2 PK/safety study with primary completion registered July 2026; the record is in follow-up with no efficacy goal. Gilead usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline (about July 2027), so posting by 31 Aug 2027 is roughly a coin flip.

haiku.r: Phase 2 PK and safety study of 181 people at nine US sites; primary completion passed in July 2026 with the record still active, so it will likely run to plan and the open question is when results are posted.

carbon.r: Active, not recruiting Gilead/HPTN/NIH Phase 2 study with all primary outcomes assessed through Week 52+30 days (completed July 2026), giving a solid chance of timely posting.

sol.r: The established cohort and mature lenacapavir program favor continuation, although retention in people who inject drugs can complicate final data cleaning.

trials.t: Global Trial in APG2575 for Patients With CLL/SLL
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by independent review committee per iwCLL guidelines, assessed at 12 months

fable.r: Patients stable on a BTK inhibitor progress slowly, so few PFS events will have accrued by mid-2027; an early look could be immature or show no clear separation yet, and added toxicity could offset early benefit.

opus.r: Patients already on BTKi for at least a year progress slowly when BTKi is simply continued, so PFS events accrue slowly and the trial may need long follow-up before a significant difference can be shown.

sonnet.r: If an early readout exists it is most likely an event-driven interim; the risk is too few PFS events in patients who are stable on a BTK inhibitor, so the hazard ratio is imprecise even if the combination works.

haiku.r: Adding a BCL-2 inhibitor to a BTK inhibitor may give a smaller PFS gain than hoped over a control that keeps the BTKi, and an open-label trial in mixed previously treated CLL may read only modestly.

carbon.r: Patients stable on BTKi monotherapy for >=12 months without overt progression may have low 12-month progression rates, delaying PFS events or narrowing early separation.

sol.r: Patients already maintained on a BTK inhibitor for at least a year may progress slowly, leaving too few early PFS events to demonstrate the benefit of adding lisaftoclax.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of Oral NXC-736 in Adult Participants With Moderate and Severe Alopecia Areata
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in SALT (Severity of Alopecia Tool) score at week 12

fable.r: No clinical proof of the mechanism in alopecia areata and a 12-week endpoint that is early even for JAK inhibitors; a small trial needs a difference of about 14 points in percent SALT change.

opus.r: Unproven oral agent in alopecia areata tested over only 12 weeks with about 36 patients per arm; even JAK inhibitors show modest SALT change at week 12, so a significant separation from placebo is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Small phase 2a with an unproven oral mechanism in alopecia areata and only 12 weeks of treatment, short for hair regrowth; the placebo arm is noisy, so a significant difference needs a large effect.

haiku.r: A 73-patient phase 2a split 37 and 36 at an undisclosed dose; the week-12 effect against placebo is the main uncertainty, and a trial this small may still reach significance if the drug works as the class suggests.

carbon.r: S1P receptor modulation (NXC736) lacks clinical proof-of-concept for rapid hair regrowth by Week 12 compared to JAK inhibitors in alopecia areata.

sol.r: An unproven treatment may not generate enough consistent hair regrowth within 12 weeks to separate from variable placebo changes.

trials.t: Study to Assess the Efficacy & Safety of KHK4951 in Patients With Diabetic Macular Edema
trials.ep: Proportion of participants losing 15 or more ETDRS letters of best corrected visual acuity from baseline through week 36

fable.r: Loss of 15 or more letters is rare when aflibercept is available, so eye drops can at best match the comparator on this endpoint; statistical superiority is very unlikely.

opus.r: Aflibercept rarely lets patients lose 15 or more letters (about 2-4%), so an eye drop cannot be shown superior on vision loss; at best it shows comparable rates, which is not superiority.

sonnet.r: The primary counts the share losing 15 or more letters, a rare event in both arms over 36 weeks, so superiority of eye drops over aflibercept injection is very unlikely and any statement would probably be descriptive.

haiku.r: Eye drops against an intravitreal anti-VEGF standard in about 185 eyes: the drug is probably less potent, so a few more eyes may lose 15 letters, and a superiority test on a loss outcome is very unlikely to read in its favour.

carbon.r: Intravitreal aflibercept is a highly effective active control (<3% lose >=15 letters), making superiority—or even narrow non-inferiority—extremely hard for topical VEGFR drops.

sol.r: Aflibercept already prevents most large visual-acuity losses, leaving very little room for eye drops to demonstrate superiority on this endpoint.

trials.t: ARTEMIS - A Research Study to Look at How Ziltivekimab Works Compared to Placebo in People With a Heart Attack
trials.ep: Time to first 3-point MACE (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke), up to 25 months

fable.r: Acute MI patients not selected on hsCRP and treated with modern therapy may gain only about a 10% relative reduction in MACE, less than the roughly 12% the trial needs to observe; colchicine and other post-MI strategies have recently been neutral.

opus.r: Anti-inflammatory therapy after acute MI has mixed results (CANTOS positive, CLEAR SYNERGY colchicine null); an IL-6 effect around HR 0.85-0.9 could miss significance even with about 1000 events.

sonnet.r: An IL-6 inhibitor needs roughly a 12 percent or larger relative risk reduction to reach significance with about 850 events; CANTOS-size effects (HR 0.85) give only marginal power while colchicine post-MI trials were mixed.

haiku.r: The result depends on whether IL-6 blockade cuts recurrent events by about 15 percent, as canakinumab did; a smaller true effect would miss significance even with 10,000 patients.

carbon.r: Acute post-MI recurrent events include stent thrombosis and non-inflammatory mechanisms, where IL-6 blockade lacks proven MACE reduction despiteCANTOS IL-1beta precedent.

sol.r: Broad early post-MI enrollment may dilute a benefit confined to persistent inflammatory risk despite strong IL-6 biomarker suppression.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability and Drug Levels of BMS-986435/MYK-224 in Participants With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
trials.ep: Incidence of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs)

fable.r: Fully enrolled BMS phase 2a with about 24 weeks of follow-up and a completion date weeks away; it should close on schedule, with registry results following roughly a year after completion.

opus.r: 24-week safety/PK phase 2a by BMS, no longer recruiting, with primary completion December 2026; it should complete on schedule, and results may be posted near the one-year deadline, after the read date.

sonnet.r: BMS phase 2a safety/PK study that is active and not recruiting with primary completion December 2026. BMS tends to keep dates or update them modestly, and results are usually posted near the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Phase 2a safety and PK study of 227 patients with HFpEF at 86 sites in 11 countries, with primary completion in December 2026; it will likely report in 2027, and posting timing is the main open question.

carbon.r: Enrollment is complete with primary completion registered for December 2026, making timely completion likely with low risk of termination.

sol.r: Completed recruitment and short follow-up favor timely completion, while registry results posting will probably lag until nearer the one-year reporting deadline.

trials.t: SC1011 Twice Daily vs Placebo in Patients Diagnosed With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF)
trials.ep: Adjusted annual rate of decline in forced vital capacity (FVC, mL) over 52 weeks

fable.r: About 105 patients per arm at most (fewer if several doses were randomized) gives modest power for a pirfenidone-sized FVC benefit, and slow recruitment of a placebo-only IPF trial in China adds dropout and timing risk.

opus.r: A pirfenidone-like agent in about 100 patients per arm needs a reduction in FVC decline of at least 60 mL/year to reach significance; the effect may be smaller or diluted by the interim dose selection.

sonnet.r: About 100 patients per arm gives a standard error near 35 mL/year for the FVC slope difference, so a pirfenidone-like effect of 70-100 mL/year is borderline, and dose selection at an interim adds uncertainty.

haiku.r: A single-site Chinese phase 2/3 with about 105 patients per arm and a dose chosen at a week-26 interim; chance noise in the FVC difference is roughly 25 mL/year, so a true effect near 80 mL/year is needed for significance.

carbon.r: Splitting 210 patients across dose-selection arms may leave modest statistical power if FVC variability is high or the selected dose offers less than 90 mL/year slowing.

sol.r: A plausible antifibrotic effect may be insufficient for significance with only 210 participants, particularly if dose selection reduces the effective comparison size.

trials.t: A Study to Assess Efficacy and Safety of KarXT for the Treatment of Psychosis Associated With Alzheimer's Disease (ADEPT-2)
trials.sp: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb company
trials.ep: Change from baseline to end of treatment (up to week 14) in NPI-C Hallucinations and Delusions score (range 0-45)

fable.r: Placebo response in dementia-related psychosis over 12 weeks is large and variable across 150+ sites, so a real but small KarXT effect (d about 0.2) could fall short of significance, especially if tolerability limits dosing in the elderly.

opus.r: Placebo response in dementia-related psychosis trials is large and variable, and elderly patients may not tolerate doses giving the muscarinic effect seen in schizophrenia; a modest drug-placebo gap of about 1-1.5 NPI-C points could be lost in noise.

sonnet.r: Placebo response on NPI-C hallucinations and delusions is large in dementia psychosis, and tolerability (nausea, vomiting, falls) in frail elderly may drive dropouts; the 250 per arm design is otherwise well powered for a 2-point difference.

haiku.r: Placebo response on the NPI-C hallucinations and delusions scale is large in dementia trials, and a moderate drug effect over 14 weeks may not reach significance.

carbon.r: Large caregiver-mediated placebo improvements on neuropsychiatric scales over 14 weeks and cholinergic/gastrointestinal dropouts in frail elderly patients risk attenuating treatment separation.

sol.r: Large caregiver- and clinician-rated placebo improvements could obscure a modest muscarinic benefit in fluctuating Alzheimer's psychosis.

trials.t: Phase 3, Multi-center, Prospective, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo- Controlled Study to Evaluate the Effectiveness and Safety of ZP5-9676 for the Treatment of Soil Transmitted Helminthiasis (STH)
trials.ep: Hookworm cure rate at the Day 14 test-of-cure visit

fable.r: Single-dose benzimidazoles other than albendazole cure only a minority of hookworm and Trichuris infections, so with about 57 evaluable hookworm cases per arm and a primary covering each species, one species could miss significance.

opus.r: If ZP5-9676 is a new benzimidazole, its single-dose hookworm efficacy is unproven in humans; a cure rate only modestly above placebo would be the main threat, though even 40% versus ~12% would be significant with ~114 evaluable hookworm cases.

sonnet.r: Placebo cure of hookworm is near zero, so a working anthelmintic wins easily; the risk is that the primary covers three species and only hookworm is sized (114 evaluable), so Ascaris or Trichuris comparisons could be underpowered.

haiku.r: A single anthelmintic dose usually clears hookworm far better than placebo; the risks are a shortfall in heavy infections and the strict day-14 cure definition.

carbon.r: If the trial requires co-primary statistical significance across all three helminth species including Trichuris trichiura, lower benzimidazole cure rates in trichuriasis could prevent full primary success.

sol.r: Whipworm cure efficacy is the weakest link because the registered primary objective covers all three helminth infections, not hookworm alone.

trials.t: UCMSCs as Treatment for Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (Stroke Neuroncell-EX)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Barthel Index score at 12 months after infusion in acute ischemic stroke

fable.r: Eighty patients cannot detect the small functional gain, if any, that intravenous stem cells add to large and variable spontaneous recovery, and both Barthel Index and mRS must be met.

opus.r: With 40 patients per arm, a 12-month Barthel Index difference needs about 11 points to reach significance and the mRS co-primary must also be met; placebo-controlled IV cell-therapy stroke trials (MASTERS, TREASURE) have not shown efficacy.

sonnet.r: With 80 patients, a single site and a large natural recovery in the placebo arm, only a sizeable Barthel gain would reach significance; co-primary mRS and multiple time points add chance and reporting-bias noise.

haiku.r: With 40 patients per arm, a 12-month Barthel difference needs about 11 points to reach significance, which a cell therapy of this kind rarely shows; the record also suggests the 12-month follow-up will run past the scoring deadline.

carbon.r: With only 80 patients total, broad symptom-onset eligibility up to 4 weeks, and two co-primary functional scales (BI and mRS), the study is severely underpowered for realistic stem cell effects.

sol.r: Cell therapy has not established a reproducible functional benefit after stroke, and both disability co-primary outcomes must succeed in a small heterogeneous sample.

trials.t: A Study of Repotrectinib Versus Crizotinib in Participants With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (TKI)-naïve ROS1-positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) (TRIDENT-3)
trials.ep: BICR-assessed progression-free survival per RECIST v1.1, up to approximately 41 months

fable.r: Crizotinib is unusually durable in ROS1 disease (median PFS up to about 19-20 months in some series), so with only about 100 events a strong control arm could leave the hazard ratio short of significance.

opus.r: Crizotinib could do better than expected by BICR, or too few PFS events could accrue in a 190-patient trial with long PFS, but repotrectinib's 35.7-month TKI-naive PFS leaves a wide margin.

sonnet.r: TRIDENT-1 median PFS in TKI-naive ROS1+ NSCLC was 35.7 months against about 16-20 months for crizotinib; a crizotinib arm that outperforms history or immature follow-up are the only realistic threats.

haiku.r: Repotrectinib has strong single-arm activity in ROS1 and crizotinib PFS in TKI-naive patients is near 19 months, so a clear PFS gain is likely; the risk is a hazard ratio closer to 0.7 in 190 patients.

carbon.r: Crizotinib occasionally achieves nearly 19-20 months median PFS in selected ROS1-positive cohorts, which could delay event accrual or narrow the hazard ratio in a 190-patient trial.

sol.r: Crizotinib may deliver longer centrally assessed PFS than historical estimates, narrowing the advantage in this relatively small randomized comparison.

trials.t: Beamion LUNG-2: A Study to Test Whether Zongertinib (BI 1810631) Helps People With Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer With HER2 Mutations Compared With Standard Treatment
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1 in first-line HER2-mutant non-squamous NSCLC

fable.r: Failure would most likely need pembrolizumab-chemotherapy to perform far better in HER2-mutant disease than the 6-8 months seen in retrospective series, combined with early censoring in an open-label design.

opus.r: Pembrolizumab-chemotherapy could outperform its modest historical PFS in HER2-mutant NSCLC and narrow the gap, though zongertinib's high first-line response rate makes failure unlikely.

sonnet.r: Zongertinib has about 75% ORR in HER2-mutant NSCLC against chemo-immunotherapy PFS near 6 months; failure would need a surprisingly durable control arm or immature data.

haiku.r: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy is a strong control, but HER2 tyrosine kinase inhibitors have shown high response rates, so the likely outcome is a clear PFS win; the risk is a modest hazard ratio.

carbon.r: First-line platinum-pemetrexed plus pembrolizumab with pemetrexed maintenance can yield 8.5 to 9.5 months median PFS, narrowing separation if first-line zongertinib durability falls short of 13 months.

sol.r: A stronger-than-expected chemo-immunotherapy control could reduce the PFS advantage suggested by nonrandomized zongertinib cohorts.

trials.t: A Trial to Learn if the Combination of Fianlimab, Cemiplimab, and Chemotherapy is Safe and Works Better Than the Combination of Cemiplimab and Chemotherapy in Adult Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer That Can be Treated With Surgery
trials.ep: Pathological complete response in resected tumor after neoadjuvant treatment, by blinded independent pathology review (up to 24 months)

fable.r: LAG-3 blockade has added little to PD-1 plus chemotherapy in lung cancer, and a phase 2 with under 100 patients per arm needs a pCR gain of about 15 points over an active cemiplimab-chemotherapy control.

opus.r: LAG-3 blockade has added little in NSCLC so far, and a ~195-patient phase 2 needs roughly a 10-12 point pCR gain over a ~20% chemo-immunotherapy control to reach significance.

sonnet.r: LAG-3 add-on to PD-1 plus chemotherapy has a poor track record in lung cancer, and a 98 versus 97 phase 2 can only show a significant pCR gap if the true effect is large, which is unlikely.

haiku.r: Adding a LAG-3 antibody to cemiplimab plus chemotherapy is expected to add a few points of pCR, not the 12 or more needed for significance with about 100 patients per arm.

carbon.r: With roughly 98 patients per arm against an active cemiplimab-chemotherapy control achieving ~21% pCR, detecting a realistic 6-9 percentage point incremental pCR gain at two-sided alpha 0.05 is underpowered.

sol.r: Adding LAG-3 blockade may provide only a small pCR increment over an already effective PD-1-plus-chemotherapy regimen.

trials.t: A 52-Week Study to Learn About the Safety and Effects of Ritlecitinib in Participants With Nonsegmental Vitiligo
trials.ep: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), and adverse events (AEs) leading to discontinuation

fable.r: Fully enrolled 52-week extension whose participants rolled over on a fixed schedule from the parent study; it should complete on time, with results posted about a year after completion.

opus.r: Pfizer's long-term extension is fully enrolled with a fixed 52-week treatment, so it should complete close to its March 2027 date; results posting before August 2027 is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Pfizer-run 52-week extension that is fully enrolled with a registered primary completion of Mar 2027; slippage of more than 90 days is uncommon and results usually post closer to 12 months after completion.

haiku.r: A long-term safety extension with a March 2027 registered completion; the main risks are a later completion date than registered and results posted only after the read date.

carbon.r: As an active, non-recruiting 52-week rollover extension from a completed parent study, Tranquillo LTE should finish near its March 2027 target without major amendments.

sol.r: This fully enrolled extension should largely follow its fixed 52-week schedule, with results posting more likely after the August registry read date.

trials.t: M108 Plus CAPOX Versus Placebo Plus CAPOX as First-line Treatment for Claudin (CLDN) 18.2-Positive, HER2-Negative, PD-L1 CPS<5, Locally Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction (GEJ) Adenocarcinoma.
trials.c: Locally Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic Gastric Cancer; Locally Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic Gastroesophageal Junction (GEJ) Adenocarcinoma
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by independent review committee per RECIST 1.1, up to 24 months

fable.r: If CLDN18.2 positivity is defined more broadly than in the zolbetuximab trials, the benefit may be diluted in low expressers and the PFS hazard ratio could drift toward 0.85 and miss significance.

opus.r: M108's benefit could be smaller than zolbetuximab's if the CLDN18.2 cutoff is broad and low expressers are enrolled, diluting the PFS hazard ratio.

sonnet.r: Naked CLDN18.2 antibodies add roughly 25-30% PFS risk reduction to chemotherapy (zolbetuximab HR 0.69-0.75), so an unproven antibody of this class could land on either side of significance; the CPS<5 restriction is helpful.

haiku.r: A CLDN18.2 antibody added to CAPOX has the precedent of zolbetuximab's PFS gain, so a hazard ratio near 0.7 is expected; the risk is a weaker effect in a single-country trial of 486 patients.

carbon.r: Inclusion of lower CLDN18.2 expression cutoffs or higher gastroesophageal junction proportions alongside early on-target gastrointestinal toxicity discontinuations could dilute the PFS benefit.

sol.r: M108 may not reproduce the class's modest PFS benefit, particularly if its unspecified CLDN18.2 threshold includes tumors with lower target expression.

trials.t: A Trial to Learn if Fianlimab and Cemiplimab Are Safe and Work Better Than Anti-PD1 Alone in Adult Participants With Resectable Stage 3 or 4 Melanoma
trials.ep: Pathological complete response rate at surgery after peri-operative treatment, assessed by blinded independent pathological review (up to 1 year)

fable.r: The LAG-3 add-on may raise pCR by only 10-15 points over cemiplimab alone, as with response rates in metastatic melanoma, and about 75 patients per arm cannot reliably detect that.

opus.r: LAG-3 blockade adds only a modest increment over PD-1 alone (RELATIVITY-047 HR 0.75), and with about 75 patients per arm a pCR gain under ~18 points is unlikely to reach two-sided significance.

sonnet.r: Adding the LAG-3 antibody fianlimab to cemiplimab may raise pCR, but with about 75 patients per arm a gain under roughly 15 points will not reach p<0.05, and LAG-3 add-on benefit over anti-PD1 has been inconsistent.

haiku.r: About 75 patients per arm is too few to reliably show a modest pCR gap from adding LAG-3 blockade to anti-PD-1, so a real but small benefit could still read as not significant.

carbon.r: Adding fianlimab to cemiplimab may yield a smaller incremental pCR gain over anti-PD-1 monotherapy than expected in an unselected resectable stage III/IV population of 151 patients.

sol.r: With roughly 75 patients per arm, a modest incremental pCR benefit over active PD-1 treatment could miss significance despite genuine combination activity.

trials.t: A Study of KC1036 Versus Investigator's Choice of Chemotherapy in Patients With Advanced Esophageal Cancer
trials.ep: Overall survival from randomization to death from any cause, up to about 24 months

fable.r: An anti-angiogenic multi-kinase inhibitor may improve response and PFS without a clear survival gain over active third-line chemotherapy, as happened with anlotinib in ESCC.

opus.r: Multi-target VEGFR/AXL TKIs in ESCC have improved PFS against placebo but have not shown convincing OS gains, and beating active chemotherapy on OS in heavily pretreated patients with post-progression crossover to other agents is a high bar.

sonnet.r: An oral multi-target kinase inhibitor in post-PD-1, 2+ line ESCC must show an OS benefit over irinotecan/docetaxel/S-1; earlier TKIs in this setting showed modest, often non-significant OS gains. Results are also unlikely to be public by mid-2027.

haiku.r: The drug mechanism and earlier data are not in the record, so a moderate overall-survival benefit is assumed, and an event-driven endpoint with recruitment still open at launch makes a June 2027 readout uncertain.

carbon.r: Active salvage chemotherapy (irinotecan, docetaxel, or S-1) and post-progression crossover therapies may attenuate any overall survival advantage from multi-kinase VEGFR2/AXL inhibition.

sol.r: A cytostatic antiangiogenic effect may improve response or PFS without extending overall survival against salvage chemotherapy.

trials.t: Proof of Concept Study of Vaginal AZU-101 in Vulvovaginal Atrophy in Postmenopausal Women
trials.ep: Number of Participants Who Had Any Serious Adverse Events or Any Treatment Emergent Adverse Events With Severity Greater Than "Moderate" as measured by CTCAE v4.0

fable.r: Single-site, sequential-cohort study from a small biotech that started about 2.5 years after registration; finishing up to 90 women by December 2026 looks optimistic, so the primary completion date will probably slip.

opus.r: Small biotech phase 2a with sequential dose cohorts at a single site, started July 2026 and aiming to finish 90 participants by December 2026; slippage and an unrefreshed record are both likely, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

sonnet.r: A small single-site proof-of-concept study by a private biotech with sequential dose cohorts, a 6-month registered primary window and a recent start; the dates will probably slip, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Single-site phase 2 with dose cohorts that wait on the first cohort; the registered December 2026 primary completion is only six months after start, so a slip is likely and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

carbon.r: Sequential dose-cohort escalation across three vaginal AZU-101 doses at a single US site starting July 2026 makes minor enrollment delays past December 2026 likely, though termination risk is low.

sol.r: Short dosing permits rapid follow-up, but sequential dose cohorts and restrictive, biopsy-heavy recruitment at one site make the six-month enrollment target fragile.

trials.t: Artesunate Ointment for the Treatment of Anal HSIL in HIV-negative Participants
trials.c: Anal High-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion; Anal HSIL; Anal HPV Infection
trials.ep: Histopathologic complete or partial response of intra-anal HSIL by week 18, after four 5-day ointment cycles

fable.r: Only 48 patients randomized 2:1, with spontaneous regression and a loose partial-response definition likely to inflate the placebo rate, so even a real effect may miss significance.

opus.r: With 32 vs 16 patients, only a difference of roughly 35 points or more would reach significance, and placebo arms in anal HSIL can show sizeable regression (biopsy removal of small lesions, spontaneous clearance, and partial responses counted).

sonnet.r: With 32 vs 16 patients, a true gap near 25 points gives under 50% power, and placebo response in biopsy-defined anal HSIL (spontaneous regression) is substantial.

haiku.r: With 32 patients on drug and 16 on placebo, a significant histologic response needs a gap of roughly 30 points, and placebo regression is common, so a clear win is unlikely even if the ointment is partly active.

carbon.r: With only 48 patients randomized 2:1 (32 experimental vs 16 placebo) and spontaneous anal HSIL regression around 20-25%, statistical power at two-sided alpha 0.05 is modest.

sol.r: The 32-versus-16 allocation requires a large response difference, while spontaneous regression, biopsy effects and histologic variability can generate substantial placebo response.

trials.t: ASKB589 in Combination With CAPOX and PD-1 Inhibitor in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic GC/GEJ Adenocarcinoma
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by independent review committee (RECIST 1.1) or death, up to about 24 months

fable.r: The added benefit of a CLDN18.2 antibody on top of chemotherapy plus PD-1 blockade may be smaller than zolbetuximab's benefit over chemotherapy alone, especially in a broader CLDN18.2-positive population.

opus.r: Anti-CLDN18.2 antibodies have only been proven on top of chemotherapy alone; their incremental PFS benefit on a PD-1 plus chemotherapy backbone is untested, and a broader CLDN18.2 cutoff could dilute the effect.

sonnet.r: Anti-CLDN18.2 antibodies add PFS benefit to chemotherapy (zolbetuximab HR about 0.69-0.75), but the PD-1 backbone raises the control arm and may shrink the incremental gain; 780 patients still give good power for HR near 0.75.

haiku.r: An add-on to a strong PD-1 plus CAPOX control often gives a PFS hazard ratio near 0.7 to 0.8, and an IRC-assessed PFS readout has to land before June 2027 to be scored.

carbon.r: On-target CLDN18.2 gastrointestinal toxicities (nausea, vomiting, hypoalbuminemia) layered onto CAPOX plus tislelizumab could increase early treatment discontinuations and dose reductions, diluting PFS benefit.

sol.r: CLDN18.2 targeting has randomized validation, but its incremental benefit may shrink when both arms receive active PD-1 plus CAPOX, while added gastrointestinal toxicity can reduce treatment exposure.

trials.t: Oral Tafenoquine Plus Standard of Care Versus Placebo Plus Standard of Care for Babesiosis
trials.ep: Time to sustained clinical resolution of babesiosis symptoms (first self-reported 7 symptom-free days), Day 1 to Day 90

fable.r: At most 33 patients and a noisy self-reported symptom endpoint dominated by lingering fatigue leave the trial with little power, even if tafenoquine speeds parasite clearance.

opus.r: With about 33 patients and a patient-reported symptom-resolution endpoint dominated by lingering fatigue, a significant hazard ratio would need a very large benefit over standard atovaquone plus azithromycin in low-risk patients.

sonnet.r: About 33 patients on atovaquone plus azithromycin, which already works in low-risk hospitalized babesiosis, leave little room for tafenoquine to speed symptom resolution measurably, and the sample is far too small to detect a modest hazard ratio.

haiku.r: With 33 hospitalized patients and roughly 28 expected events, a significant gain in time to sustained resolution needs a large effect, and enrolment was still open at launch so a readout by June 2027 is uncertain.

carbon.r: Enrolling only 33 low-relapse-risk patients already receiving effective atovaquone-azithromycin leaves severe underpowering to detect faster complete resolution across 11 non-specific symptoms.

sol.r: Only about 26 recovery events are likely, and persistent nonspecific fatigue can obscure a parasiticidal benefit on an endpoint requiring seven days free of every symptom.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Povorcitinib in Participants With Moderate to Severe Hidradenitis Suppurativa
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)

fable.r: Extension study with closed enrolment should finish on schedule around December 2026; results are likely to be posted near the 12-month deadline, after the read date.

opus.r: Large-sponsor long-term extension with enrolment closed and a completion date consistent with the parent studies' timeline; likely to finish near the registered date, with results posting probably near the 12-month deadline after the read date.

sonnet.r: A large Incyte long-term extension with enrolment complete and a registered end of December 2026; sponsor-managed record, modest chance the end date is extended, and results are likely posted only near the 12-month deadline.

haiku.r: A long-term extension of a large sponsor's phase 3 program that may keep dosing patients and move its completion date, while results posting may land after August 2027.

carbon.r: As an active, non-recruiting fixed-duration 56-week extension of completed STOP-HS phase 3 trials, primary completion should occur near schedule around December 2026 with minimal stopping or amendment risk.

sol.r: Enrollment is closed and fixed-duration extension follow-up makes on-time completion likely; registry results may lag the safety database lock by most of a year.

trials.t: A Study on the Safety, Reactogenicity, and Immune Response to the GVGH iNTS-GMMA Vaccine Against Invasive Nontyphoidal Salmonella in Adults, Children, and Infants
trials.ep: Number of adult participants 18-50 years of age with solicited administration site events

fable.r: Completed GSK vaccine study; results are due about August 2027 and public posting may fall just before or just after the 31 August 2027 read date.

opus.r: Completed GSK vaccine study; GSK reliably submits results within about 12 months of primary completion (August 2026), so posting by end of August 2027 is likely, though QC review can push it past the read date.

sonnet.r: A completed GSK phase 2 vaccine study; GSK normally posts results close to the 12-month deadline after primary completion (August 2026), and a completed trial rarely changes primary outcomes.

haiku.r: A completed phase 2a vaccine study in Ghana whose results posting is due about a year after its August 2026 primary completion; GSK usually posts on time, though the deadline falls near the read date.

carbon.r: Because this GSK vaccine phase 2a trial is already completed as of August 2026, termination is virtually impossible and timely ClinicalTrials.gov results posting within 12 months by August 2027 is highly likely.

sol.r: Already completed, this sponsor-led vaccine study is very unlikely to stop or change primary outcomes; results posting near the one-year completion anniversary is likely.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of BR1019A and BR1019B Combination Therapy
trials.ep: Change from baseline in mean sitting systolic blood pressure at week 12, triple combination versus the same combination without BR1019A.

fable.r: Both co-primaries must be met; the likeliest miss is the HbA1c comparison, if baseline HbA1c is low or arms are smaller than assumed, leaving the 12-week difference short of significance.

opus.r: Both co-primaries must be met; the antihypertensive component should clearly beat placebo on SBP, so the residual risk is mainly the HbA1c comparison or a high placebo/regression effect in a 12-week office-BP trial.

sonnet.r: Add-on factorial design against matched placebo, where the component's known blood-pressure or HbA1c effect should easily win at n about 92 per arm; the main risks are the second co-primary (HbA1c) and a low placebo-arm baseline.

haiku.r: A third agent added to a two-drug combination usually lowers systolic pressure by only a few mmHg, and both co-primary endpoints must be met, so a 92-per-arm trial may miss significance.

carbon.r: Meeting both co-primary endpoints requires simultaneous Week 12 superiority on both systolic blood pressure and HbA1c, creating modest compound risk from washout variability or adherence.

sol.r: Attenuated component separation after washout or run-in could undermine either co-primary: a large comparator BP fall or a small incremental HbA1c reduction would prevent overall success.

trials.t: DV Combined With Cadonilimab in Subjects With HER2-expressing Gastric Cancer and Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma After Progression on First-line Therapy
trials.ep: Phase II: objective response rate per RECIST 1.1, assessed up to approximately 2 years.

fable.r: With about 30 patients per arm and no clear formal hypothesis in phase II, the response-rate gap over paclitaxel may not reach, or not be reported as reaching, statistical significance.

opus.r: The phase II part has about 30 patients per arm and may be analysed descriptively; even a 25-point ORR gain is borderline significant at that size, and the record also lists phase III PFS and OS as primary outcomes that cannot be met by mid-2027.

sonnet.r: A HER2 ADC plus a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific should out-respond second-line paclitaxel (ORR about 15%), but 30 patients per arm give wide uncertainty and the HER2 IHC 1+ cases may respond poorly.

haiku.r: With about 30 patients per arm, the response gap must exceed roughly 25 points to reach significance, and the registry shows recruitment still open at launch.

carbon.r: With only 90 patients registered across three phase II arms and phase III PFS/OS co-primaries also listed, an early phase II readout may be descriptive or underpowered rather than formally meeting all registered primary hypotheses.

sol.r: Thirty patients per arm, heterogeneous HER2 expression and unrestricted prior PD-1 treatment could leave the ORR difference short of a formal win despite visible activity.

trials.t: A Study on the Safety of TAK-279 and Whether it Can Reduce Inflammation in the Bowel of Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease
trials.ep: Endoscopic response at Week 12: SES-CD decrease over 50% from baseline (isolated ileal disease: SES-CD <=4 or at least 2-point reduction)

fable.r: TYK2 inhibition has not yet shown efficacy in Crohn's disease (deucravacitinib failed in LATTICE-CD), so zasocitinib may not reach an endoscopic effect large enough to be significant with about 67 patients per arm.

opus.r: Selective TYK2 inhibition has already failed in IBD (deucravacitinib LATTICE-CD and LATTICE-UC); zasocitinib's higher exposure may help, but week-12 endoscopic response with 67 per arm needs roughly a 20-point gain over placebo.
