opus.r: A TKI implant dosed every 6 months could lose a few letters against aflibercept every 8 weeks in partly loaded naive eyes; if the mean deficit approaches the likely 4.5-letter margin, non-inferiority fails, though rescue rules and loading doses limit this.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority of a 6-monthly axitinib implant against aflibercept 2 mg needs near-equal week-48 vision; durable agents have usually met the margin, but a small loss in a 4 to 5 letter margin is the main risk.

haiku.r: Non-inferiority to aflibercept is likely for a sustained axitinib implant, but a letter loss beyond the margin is the main way it fails; the record does not state the margin.

carbon.r: If sustained axitinib release from the bioresorbable hydrogel implant wanes before scheduled redosing, breakthrough exudation could cause BCVA loss exceeding the non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: Insufficient durability between implant administrations could permit recurrent exudation and enough irreversible vision loss to miss the non-inferiority margin.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Solriktug in Adult Participants With Asthma
trials.ep: Change from baseline in blood eosinophil count, averaged over weeks 8 to 12

fable.r: About 36 patients per arm and highly variable eosinophil counts in a population not clearly selected for eosinophilia; a noisy placebo arm or descriptive-only reporting could leave the primary unconfirmed.

opus.r: Anti-TSLP antibodies reliably lower blood eosinophils, so the main risks are the small arms (about 36 each) in an unselected asthma population with modest baseline counts, and a private sponsor reporting only descriptive reductions without a stated test.

sonnet.r: A biologic that blocks the upstream cytokine pathway should cut blood eosinophils sharply even in 36 per arm; the main risk is a press release that gives no statement on the primary comparison.

haiku.r: A 36-per-arm eosinophil study can show a clear drop if the drug works at a top dose, but a modest pharmacodynamic effect would be missed at this size; any one of the three doses meeting the objective also counts.

carbon.r: Because baseline blood eosinophil elevation was not required at screening, lower baseline eosinophil counts across ~36-patient arms could increase relative variance.

sol.r: Without explicit eosinophil enrichment, variable baseline counts and only about 36 patients per arm could obscure an otherwise credible anti-TSLP pharmacodynamic effect.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Solrikitug in Participants With COPD (ZION)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in blood eosinophil count through week 12

fable.r: Arms of about 60 and skewed eosinophil counts with regression to the mean in an eosinophil-enriched placebo group; failure would more likely come from noise or vague reporting than from lack of pharmacology.

opus.r: Eosinophil lowering by an anti-TSLP antibody in COPD selected for high eosinophils is near certain; the residual risk is noise in about 60 patients per arm and reporting without a formal statistical statement.

sonnet.r: Eosinophil lowering in an eosinophil-enriched COPD population should be large and significant at the high dose; the risk is the report form (percent change, or no formal statement) rather than the biology.

haiku.r: The 61-per-arm design has good power for an eosinophil drop of about 90 cells, so the risk is that the high dose suppresses eosinophils less in COPD than in asthma.

carbon.r: If solrikitug has suboptimal pharmacokinetics or neutralising immunogenicity in COPD patients, pharmacodynamic suppression of blood eosinophils through week 12 could be attenuated.

sol.r: The main primary-endpoint risk is shallower-than-expected eosinophil suppression against regression to the mean, while a successful biomarker result may still produce little lung-function benefit.

trials.t: A Prospective Pivotal Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Avastin® Bevacizumab (BEV) With or Without Microbubble-mediated Focused Ultrasound (FUS-MB) Using NaviFUS System in Recurrent Glioblastoma Multiforme Patients
trials.c: Glioblastoma Multiforme; Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma Multiforme, Adult
trials.ep: Progression-free survival rate at 6 months from randomization (PFS-6, RANO criteria)

fable.r: Sixteen patients per arm cannot show a significant PFS-6 gain unless the difference is around 40 points, and opening the blood-brain barrier adds uncertain benefit to bevacizumab, which acts on tumour vessels.

opus.r: With 16 patients per arm, a significant PFS-6 difference needs an absolute gain of roughly 45 points, far beyond what focused-ultrasound BBB opening with bevacizumab plausibly delivers, since bevacizumab penetration is not the main limit in rGBM.

sonnet.r: Only 16 patients per arm: PFS-6 would need a difference of roughly 40 points to reach p<0.05, and the study is still recruiting, so it is unlikely to report by mid-2027.

haiku.r: With 16 patients per arm the 6-month progression-free comparison can only reach significance with a very large gap, so a claimed benefit would more likely be non-significant or descriptive.

carbon.r: With only 16 patients per arm, achieving two-sided p<0.05 on 6-month progression-free survival against an active bevacizumab control requires an unrealistically large >40 percentage-point gain.

sol.r: Sixteen patients per arm require an unusually large PFS-6 gain, and bevacizumab's vascular target weakens the premise that increased brain penetration alone will improve tumor control.

trials.t: A Study Comparing BL-B01D1 With Topotecan in Patients With Recurrent Small Cell Lung Cancer(PANKU-Lung03)
trials.ep: Overall survival, from randomization to death from any cause (follow-up up to about 24 months)

fable.r: Topotecan patients may live longer than history suggests through later lines, and BL-B01D1's marked haematological toxicity and shorter responses in platinum-resistant disease could shrink the survival gain below significance.

opus.r: Topoisomerase-I ADCs show high response rates in SCLC, but heavy myelosuppression and post-progression therapies could dilute the OS gain over topotecan; an OS effect smaller than response data suggest is the main way this fails.

sonnet.r: EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC against topotecan in second-line SCLC after PD-1 and platinum has shown high response rates in phase 2 and topotecan control survival is short; with 722 patients the OS comparison is well powered.

haiku.r: Post-PD-1 small cell lung cancer after platinum failure is a weak setting for topotecan, so a positive overall survival hazard ratio is likely, but an antibody-drug conjugate benefit can be modest and the margin is thin.

carbon.r: Subsequent systemic therapies after progression in Chinese thoracic oncology centers could prolong control-arm survival and attenuate the overall survival hazard ratio despite superior PFS.

sol.r: An ADC response advantage may yield only a short progression delay and be offset by marrow toxicity or subsequent therapy, leaving overall survival insufficiently improved.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Frexalimab, Brivekimig, or Rilzabrutinib in Participants Aged 16 to 75 Years With Primary Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis or Minimal Change Disease
trials.c: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis; Glomerulonephritis Minimal Lesion
trials.ep: Percent reduction in urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) from baseline to Week 12

fable.r: About 14-21 patients per arm with a highly variable proteinuria endpoint means only a large (roughly 35% relative) UPCR reduction would reach significance, and CD40L blockade has no proven effect in FSGS or MCD.

opus.r: Roughly 14 patients per active arm in an exploratory phase 2a umbrella; a significant week-12 UPCR difference needs a very large effect, and Sanofi may report descriptively without a formal test.

sonnet.r: About 14 patients per arm with highly variable percent UPCR change gives low power; an anti-CD40L effect in steroid-responsive MCD/FSGS is plausible but placebo also drifts down, and slow rare-disease recruitment pushes any readout past mid-2027.

haiku.r: Only 14 patients per arm on a 12-week percent UPCR change with a between-patient SD near 35 points: significance needs a gap of about 26 points, so a modest frexalimab effect would be missed.

carbon.r: With roughly 14 patients per arm and high patient-to-patient variability in UPCR, this exploratory 12-week Phase 2a umbrella trial is underpowered for formal statistical significance unless one agent has a dramatic anti-proteinuric effect.

sol.r: Very small matched cohorts and variable proteinuria make a statistically convincing week-12 difference difficult despite enrichment for previous immunosuppressive responsiveness.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Effect of Bimekizumab on Gene Expression Biomarkers in Study Participants With Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis
trials.c: Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis; Psoriatic Arthritis
trials.ep: Change from Baseline in composite gene expression score using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in lesional skin at Week 48

fable.r: Fully enrolled open-label biomarker study with a fixed week-48 biopsy endpoint; it should complete on schedule in March 2027, with results posted about a year later, after the read date.

opus.r: Enrolment is closed and the 48-week single-arm biomarker endpoint is fixed; UCB usually keeps dates close, so a modest slip is the main operational risk and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Open-label single-arm biomarker study, fully enrolled (active, not recruiting); the week-48 biopsy readout is date-driven so little slippage, but UCB usually posts results only many months after primary completion and study completion is March 2028.

haiku.r: Main schedule risk is the biomarker analysis of skin biopsies after the March 2027 primary completion, which could push the registry date; results posting for this US-site trial often lags the one-year deadline.

carbon.r: Because enrollment is already complete and the primary endpoint is assessed at a fixed 48-week visit, primary completion should occur near schedule in March 2027, with results posted after full study completion in 2028.

sol.r: Closed enrollment and an established treatment favor completion, with week-48 biopsy collection and biomarker processing posing the main operational uncertainties.

trials.t: The Phase III Clinical Study of Herombopag for the Treatment of Thrombocytopenia in Chronic Liver Disease Patients Undergoing Elective Invasive Surgery
trials.c: Thrombocytopenia in Chronic Liver Disease Patients Undergoing Elective Invasive Surgery
trials.ep: Part B: share of patients with platelet count ≥50×10^9/L and rise ≥20×10^9/L from baseline within 24 hours before surgery, without platelet transfusion or rescue

fable.r: Failure would need the Part A dose to give a much smaller platelet rise than avatrombopag or lusutrombopag, for example in Child-Pugh B or very low baseline counts; placebo response on this endpoint is near zero.

opus.r: Oral TPO-receptor agonists reliably raise platelets before procedures while placebo rarely reaches >=50 with a >=20 rise; the main residual risk is an operational or reporting issue (Part A/B split shrinking arms) rather than efficacy.

sonnet.r: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists reliably beat placebo on pre-procedure platelet response in this setting; the main uncertainty is whether and when Hengrui publishes, not efficacy.

haiku.r: The composite needs platelets of at least 50 and a rise of 20 within 24 hours before surgery with no rescue, so surgery timing and rescue use can cut responders; the effect should be large enough that the readout itself is the main risk.

carbon.r: Oral TPO-receptor agonists reliably raise platelet counts above 50x10^9/L before procedures against minimal spontaneous placebo responses, leaving mainly operational or reporting risk.

sol.r: The main residual risk is an inadequate platelet rise within the short presurgical window because of dose selection or variable exposure in liver disease.

trials.t: A Clinical Study Comparing SG301 Plus Pomalidomide and Dexamethasone to Placebo Plus Pomalidomide and Dexamethasone in Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma Patients
trials.ep: Progression-free survival in the randomized Stage 2 part

fable.r: SG301 may be a weaker anti-CD38 antibody than daratumumab or isatuximab, and inclusion of CD38-exposed patients could dilute the PFS benefit over pomalidomide-dexamethasone.

opus.r: Anti-CD38 plus Pd is a proven doublet-to-triplet gain, but Chinese patients with prior daratumumab exposure (only primary refractoriness is excluded) could blunt the benefit, and a novel anti-CD38 may be less potent than daratumumab or isatuximab.

sonnet.r: Adding an anti-CD38-type antibody to pomalidomide-dexamethasone has repeatedly cut progression risk by about 40 percent; the larger risk is timing, since a recruiting trial from a small sponsor is unlikely to read out PFS by mid-2027.

haiku.r: The risk is that SG301 adds too little to pomalidomide and dexamethasone; a control median near 4.5 months leaves room for a clear hazard ratio, but a modest mechanism gain would be missed at about 220 events.

carbon.r: Although anti-CD38 therapy added to pomalidomide-dexamethasone is well validated, slower-than-planned accrual or lower event rates in second-line patients could reduce PFS maturity or attenuate hazard ratios.

sol.r: SG301 may not reproduce the durability of established CD38 antibodies, particularly in participants previously exposed to that class.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of PJ009 in Patients With Short Bowel Syndrome Requiring Parenteral Nutrition
trials.ep: Percentage of patients with at least 20% reduction from baseline in weekly parenteral nutrition/IV volume at weeks 20 to 24

fable.r: With about 36 patients per arm, a placebo responder rate of 30-40% from protocol-driven weaning could leave a real 25-30 point teduglutide-like effect short of significance.

opus.r: With about 36 patients per arm, a teduglutide-sized gain (~30 points) gives only ~70-80% power, and placebo responder rates rise when PN is actively weaned during the double-blind period.

sonnet.r: A daily GLP-2 analog should beat placebo on PN reduction as teduglutide did, but with 36 per arm and a 20 percent responder threshold the margin for a significant result is modest.

haiku.r: Seventy-two patients split across two arms leaves a wide spread on a responder rate with placebo near 27 percent; the sample, more than the drug class, is the main risk.

carbon.r: Intensive fluid optimization and weaning protocols in small short bowel syndrome trials can inflate placebo responder rates to 30-40%, narrowing separation with 72 patients.

sol.r: PN optimization and continued intestinal adaptation may produce more placebo responders than a 72-patient study can comfortably accommodate.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety Study of Povorcitinib in Participants With Prurigo Nodularis (STOP-PN1)
trials.ep: Share of patients with both ≥4-point Itch NRS improvement and IGA-CPG-S 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement at week 24

fable.r: The strict composite (itch response plus near-clear nodules at week 24) with dropouts counted as non-responders is the only plausible way a strongly antipruritic JAK1 inhibitor misses.

opus.r: The composite requires both a 4-point itch response and near-clear nodules at week 24; lesion clearance lags itch relief, so the absolute composite gain could be smaller than expected, though sample size gives ample power.

sonnet.r: The composite of itch NRS4 plus IGA success at week 24 is strict and the phase 2 itch effect was modest, but about 115-175 patients per arm gives good power if the JAK1 inhibitor effect holds.

haiku.r: The single composite needs both a 4-point itch drop and a two-grade IGA improvement at week 24, so lesion clearance lagging behind itch could cost responders; the effect should still be large for this drug class.

carbon.r: Requiring complete or near-complete nodule clearance (IGA 0/1) alongside itch relief at week 24 is much stricter than itch reduction alone if chronic fibrotic nodules remodel slowly.

sol.r: The composite could disappoint if rapid itch relief does not translate into sufficient nodule clearance by week 24.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety Study of Povorcitinib in Participants With Prurigo Nodularis (STOP-PN2)
trials.ep: Share of patients with both ≥4-point Itch NRS improvement and IGA-CPG-S 0/1 with ≥2-grade improvement at week 24

fable.r: The strict composite (itch response plus near-clear nodules at week 24) with dropouts counted as non-responders is the only plausible way a strongly antipruritic JAK1 inhibitor misses.

opus.r: The composite of itch NRS4 plus IGA-CPG-S 0/1 at week 24 is demanding because nodule clearance lags itch relief; a regional mix including Japan could raise placebo response, but power remains high.

sonnet.r: Twin of STOP-PN1: the strict itch-plus-lesion composite at week 24 and a modest phase 2 itch effect are the main risks, but the trial is well powered if the JAK1 inhibitor effect holds.

haiku.r: The composite needs both itch and lesion criteria at week 24, so a lagging lesion response could cost responders. The sister trial shares the design, so one readout likely reads across to the other.

carbon.r: Achieving the strict composite of >=4-point itch reduction plus IGA 0/1 lesion clearance by week 24 can lag behind rapid JAK1-mediated antipruritic benefit in patients with dense fibrotic nodules.

sol.r: Insufficient lesion clearance among patients with severe baseline nodules is the likeliest way that strong itch efficacy fails the composite primary endpoint.

trials.t: FDA018-ADC vs Investigator's Choice Chemotherapy to Treat Locally Advanced, Recurrent or Metastatic Triple-negative Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by BICR (RECIST 1.1), up to 24 months

fable.r: PFS is likely positive; the risk is that the dual primary with OS is immature or not significant when PFS is reported, or that FDA018 is less active than other Trop2 ADCs.

opus.r: PFS is very likely positive, but OS is a dual primary; if the first report has immature OS without significance, the round's all-primaries rule could score the trial as not met.

sonnet.r: A TROP2 ADC should clearly beat single-agent chemotherapy on PFS, but the OS co-primary must also be met and may be immature at the first announcement.

haiku.r: The main risk is that the new ADC gives a smaller gain than the sacituzumab precedent in a similar post-taxane setting, leaving a hazard ratio above 0.7 that 350 patients might not separate from chemotherapy.

carbon.r: If the protocol requires both PFS and OS as strict co-primary endpoints rather than split-alpha dual primaries, immature OS or post-progression crossover at initial readout could delay or prevent meeting OS.

sol.r: An ADC may improve PFS yet fail the separately required OS objective because of subsequent therapy, toxicity or insufficient death-event maturity.

trials.t: Clinical Trial of Protective Efficacy of Quadrivalent Recombinant Norovirus Vaccine (Pichia Pastoris)
trials.sp: Anhui Zhifei Longcom Biologic Pharmacy Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Incidence of acute gastroenteritis caused by vaccine-genotype norovirus (GI.1, GII.3, GII.4, GII.17), from 7 days after the third dose through about 2 years

fable.r: VLP norovirus vaccines have not yet protected young children (HIL-214 failed in infants); antigenic drift in GII.4 and GII.17 and weak blocking-antibody responses could leave efficacy too low.

opus.r: Injectable VLP norovirus vaccines have not proven protective in young children (HIL-214 failed in infants), immunity is strain-specific and short-lived, and genotype shifts (GII.17, GII.4 variants) may cut efficacy.

sonnet.r: Norovirus VLP efficacy in young children is unproven (a bivalent infant vaccine failed in phase 2b), and the primary depends on enough PCR-confirmed cases of four specific genotypes over two years.

haiku.r: Norovirus vaccines have often given only partial protection against a subset of genotypes, so the main risk is vaccine efficacy against these four genotypes falling well below the 55 to 60 percent this 3300-per-arm design needs.

carbon.r: Intramuscular VLP norovirus vaccines elicit limited gut mucosal immunity in unprimed infants—who form 45% of enrollment and contribute most gastroenteritis cases—and face antigenic drift and possible strict lower-bound VE criteria.

sol.r: Strong antibody responses may not confer durable clinical protection, particularly in infants who are likely to contribute most endpoint cases.

trials.t: A Study of Bupivacaine Liposome Injection in the Treatment of Pain After Thoracoscopic Surgery
trials.ep: Area under the curve of pain intensity during exercise or cough over 0-72 hours after paravertebral block

fable.r: Plain bupivacaine plus rescue analgesia may leave little room for a significant 72-hour pain AUC difference with about 24-32 patients per arm.

opus.r: Plain bupivacaine paravertebral block already gives strong early analgesia, and small dose arms (~24 patients) after thoracoscopy, with multimodal rescue analgesia, often leave liposomal-vs-plain differences non-significant.

sonnet.r: A dose-finding phase 2 with about 24 patients per arm and an active bupivacaine control makes superiority on 72-hour pain AUC uncertain, though the longer duration of liposomal bupivacaine favours it.

haiku.r: A dose-finding design with perhaps 20 to 30 patients per arm leaves a wide spread on a 72-hour pain AUC, so a real but modest liposome advantage over plain bupivacaine could be missed.

carbon.r: Beating an active bupivacaine hydrochloride paravertebral block plus multimodal postoperative rescue analgesia on 72-hour pain AUC with roughly 24-32 patients per dose arm is statistically challenging.

sol.r: An effective conventional bupivacaine block plus rescue analgesia may leave too little incremental pain reduction for small dose-finding cohorts to establish superiority.

trials.t: MEN1703 (SEL24) to Treat Relapsed or Refractory Aggressive B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (JASPIS-01)
trials.ep: Part 1: Incidence and severity of adverse events (AE)

fable.r: Still recruiting two months before the registered primary completion, with 178 planned patients and an optional randomized part 3, so the date will almost certainly slip; a cash-constrained, partner-funded sponsor adds some risk of an early stop.

opus.r: Small-biotech multi-part phase 2 still recruiting toward 178 patients with a December 2026 primary completion date that looks unrealistic; date extension is likely and a funding-driven stop is a real possibility.

sonnet.r: Small-company phase 2 with a safety run-in, enrichment and an optional randomized part; 178 patients and a registered end of Dec 2026 will not be reached, so the trial will still be recruiting after March 2027 and will not have posted results.

haiku.r: Recruiting in a slow refractory-lymphoma phase 2 against an end-2026 completion date, so the registry will likely show a late completion; the main operational risks are suspension by a small sponsor and a reshaped Part 3.

carbon.r: Still recruiting 178 lymphoma patients across three sequential/parallel parts two months before its registered December 2026 primary completion makes a substantial timeline delay very likely.

sol.r: Sequential dose selection, an optional randomized expansion and 12-month assessments make the December 2026 completion target ambitious while recruitment continues.

trials.t: A Clinical Study to Evaluate DNTH103 in Adults With Multifocal Motor Neuropathy
trials.ep: Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) and Treatment Emergent Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the primary safety window is only 17 weeks, so primary completion close to the registered December 2026 date is likely, while results posting on the registry by August 2027 is unlikely for a small sponsor.

opus.r: Fully enrolled 46-patient phase 2 with a 17-week primary period; topline guided for around end-2026, so the primary completion date should hold and posting by August 2027 is unlikely for a small biotech.

sonnet.r: Rare-disease phase 2 with a 17-week safety primary, enrollment closed, and registered primary completion Dec 2026; small biotech is unlikely to post results by Aug 2027 and a modest chance the date slips.

haiku.r: A small active, not-recruiting Phase 2 whose single safety primary is unlikely to change; the operational question is whether the December 2026 completion date slips past March 2027 in the registry.

carbon.r: Because enrollment of 46 patients is already complete in October 2026 and the primary safety window is 17 weeks, primary completion should occur near schedule.

sol.r: Completed recruitment and a 17-week primary assessment support near-term primary completion, although the long-term extension and registry results posting will likely continue later.

trials.t: Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of AMOR-1 as a Treatment for Hypocalcemia Associated With Hypoparathyroidism in Adults
trials.ep: Percentage achieving composite at week 14: at least 50% cut in oral calcium dose, albumin-adjusted serum calcium 8.0-10.0 mg/dL, no vitamin D increase

fable.r: Failure would most likely come from serum calcium falling below 8.0 mg/dL on half the elemental calcium, forcing dose increases so that too few AMOR-1 patients keep the 50% reduction.

opus.r: The composite needs serum calcium of 8.0-10.0 mg/dL on half the elemental calcium without raising active vitamin D; if amorphous calcium does not fully compensate, many AMOR-1 patients will be titrated up or fall below range, shrinking the responder rate.

sonnet.r: AMOR-1 gets half the elemental calcium, so serum calcium may drift out of 8.0-10.0 mg/dL at week 14, but the control arm cannot reach a 50% dose cut, so even a modest responder rate beats it.

haiku.r: The composite needs a 50 percent calcium cut, serum calcium in range and no vitamin D rise, and the control arm keeps its full dose so it almost cannot respond; the risk is that few AMOR-1 patients meet all three elements.

carbon.r: If amorphous calcium carbonate fails to achieve nearly double fractional absorption in hypoparathyroid patients, a 50% elemental calcium cut will cause hypocalcemia or require calcitriol rescues.

sol.r: The composite structurally favors the half-dose replacement arm, but greater absorption must still be sufficient to maintain calcium without increasing vitamin D.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About the Investigational Medicine Called PF-06821497 (Mevrometostat) in Men With mCRPC Who Were Previously Treated With Abiraterone Acetate for Prostate Cancer (MEVPRO-1).
trials.ep: Radiographic progression-free survival by blinded independent central review (RECIST 1.1 soft tissue, PCWG3 bone) or death, up to about 2 years

fable.r: The only real route to failure is a physician's-choice arm doing better than expected because of docetaxel, and I believe a positive primary result has already been announced.

opus.r: The randomized phase 1 signal (HR about 0.5 vs enzalutamide) came from roughly 80 patients and will likely shrink; a control arm that includes docetaxel is stronger than enzalutamide alone, so the true HR may sit near 0.75-0.8.

sonnet.r: The phase 1 hazard ratio near 0.4 came from small numbers and is likely optimistic, and a pooled control that includes docetaxel is somewhat stronger than enzalutamide alone, but a 600-patient trial still has high power at a realistic HR near 0.65.

haiku.r: The add-on effect of mevrometostat over enzalutamide after abiraterone may be too small to reach significance, even though a hazard ratio near 0.7 is plausible in 600 patients.

carbon.r: Allowing docetaxel chemotherapy in the physician's-choice control arm raises control rPFS relative to the Phase 1/2 enzalutamide-only comparator, attenuating the hazard ratio.

sol.r: The encouraging randomized expansion used enzalutamide alone as control; inclusion of docetaxel could materially reduce the phase 3 advantage.

trials.t: 4-Week, Multi-center Dose-Ranging Study for the IBS-C in Pts. 6 to <12 Yrs
trials.ep: Change from baseline in average weekly spontaneous bowel movement (SBM) frequency at week 4

fable.r: With about 10 patients on the top dose and about 12 on pooled placebo, the study cannot support a formal significant result on weekly stool frequency.

opus.r: Pediatric dose-escalation study with about 10 patients per dose cohort and only 12 pooled placebo patients; results will likely be descriptive, and any test would have very low power against a sizable pediatric placebo response.

sonnet.r: The top-dose cohort has about 10 children against 12 pooled placebo, and this is a dose-ranging safety study without a formal hypothesis, so a descriptive report or a non-significant test is the likely outcome even with a real effect.

haiku.r: Ten highest-dose patients against twelve pooled placebo patients in a dose-escalation design make a significant result hard to reach, so an underpowered test is the most likely failure.

carbon.r: Sequential cohorts of only 10 active patients per dose versus 12 pooled placebo patients provide low statistical power to detect a typical 1.2–1.5 weekly SBM difference.

sol.r: Tenapanor should increase stool frequency, but ten children per dose and a small placebo pool leave substantial uncertainty around formal superiority.

trials.t: A Phase 2a/b Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Subcutaneous Amlitelimab in Adults With Nonresponsive Celiac Disease
trials.ep: Change in duodenal villus height to crypt depth ratio (Vh:Cd) from baseline to week 28

fable.r: OX40L blockade is untested in celiac disease and may not protect the mucosa from gluten-driven injury enough to show against a modest, noisy placebo decline.

opus.r: Simulated inadvertent gluten exposure may cause only modest mucosal damage in placebo patients over 28 weeks, leaving little Vh:Cd decline to prevent; with about 38 per arm and noisy biopsy morphometry, a real but small protective effect may miss significance.

sonnet.r: OX40L blockade has no proven mucosal effect in celiac disease; it must blunt the gluten-induced fall in Vh:Cd against a noisy biopsy endpoint with about 38 patients per arm, and most celiac phase 2 programs have failed.

haiku.r: A small six-arm histology trial in non-responsive coeliac disease; the Vh:Cd change is noisy and the drug's effect on the mucosa is unproven, so no significant difference is the likely outcome.

carbon.r: OX40L blockade lacks prior clinical proof-of-concept for preventing gluten-induced duodenal villous atrophy, where intraepithelial IL-15 and innate pathways also drive mucosal damage.

sol.r: OX40L blockade may not adequately suppress established gluten-specific immune responses, and small challenge cohorts make modest histologic protection difficult to establish.

trials.t: A Study of Obexelimab in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.ep: Share of patients achieving a BICLA (BILAG-Based Composite Lupus Assessment) response at week 24

fable.r: B-cell inhibition without depletion may give only a modest BICLA gain over a placebo response near 35% in 24 weeks, short of the roughly 14 points needed with 95 patients per arm.

opus.r: Non-depleting B-cell inhibition gave only a non-significant trend in an earlier SLE phase 2, and BICLA placebo responses near 35% mean the trial needs a roughly 14-point gain to reach significance with 95 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: SLE placebo BICLA response runs high at 30-45% and the effect of a non-depleting CD19/FcgRIIb antibody is unproven in lupus, so a difference under about 15 points would miss significance with 95 per arm.

haiku.r: A phase 2 SLE BICLA trial with 95 per arm and a typically high placebo response; the most likely failure is a drug effect too weak to clear significance at this size.

carbon.r: Background lupus immunosuppressants and steroids produce substantial Week 24 BICLA placebo response rates (~35%), requiring ~14 percentage points of separation with 95 patients per arm.

sol.r: Earlier obexelimab data suggested activity without a secure primary-endpoint win; a modest BICLA increment may be insufficient in 190 patients receiving background therapy.

trials.t: Phase 3 Study of Adjunctive Treatment With Seltorexant in Adult and Elderly Participants With Major Depressive Disorder and Insomnia Symptoms
trials.ep: Part 1: change from baseline in MADRS total score at Day 43

fable.r: A true effect near 2 MADRS points leaves the trial exposed to a high placebo response across many sites in Latin America and Eastern Europe.

opus.r: Seltorexant's adjunctive antidepressant effect is small (about 2-3 MADRS points), so placebo-response variability across 16 mostly ex-US countries could erase significance; a required Part 2 relapse result would also come late.

sonnet.r: The expected 2-3 point MADRS advantage is small relative to a placebo change near 10 points, earlier phase 3 results were not uniformly significant, and the second primary (relapse in Part 2) must also be met.

haiku.r: Adjunctive MDD trials have a high placebo response, and a 20 mg effect of about two MADRS points is at the edge of detectability, so a strong placebo response is the most likely failure.

carbon.r: Global 205-site antidepressant trials risk elevated placebo MADRS improvement (~13–15 points) that can compress a 2-to-3 point adjunctive treatment difference.

sol.r: Acute MADRS improvement is credible, but success across both registered primary outcomes additionally requires a convincing and timely relapse-prevention analysis.

trials.t: "A Study of a Deuterated Psilocin Analog (CYB003) in Humans With Major Depressive Disorder"
trials.ep: Change from baseline in MADRS total score at day 42 (end of treatment)

fable.r: The large phase 2 effect may shrink in a 45-site phase 3, as it did for psilocybin in COMP005, especially with patients staying on serotonergic antidepressants.

opus.r: Psychological support plus high expectancy can drive large placebo MADRS drops in a US-only psychedelic trial; if the placebo arm improves 12+ points, the margin over CYB003 could narrow to a non-significant 3-4 points.

sonnet.r: Adjunctive MDD trials carry large placebo response with psychological support; the psychedelic effect (partial unblinding helps) must still exceed about 2.7 MADRS points with 110 per arm, which phase 2 and psilocybin phase 3 data suggest is likely.

haiku.r: Psychedelic trials carry a strong expectancy-driven placebo response that can compress a modest MADRS difference at day 42, which is the most likely reason this would fail.

carbon.r: Concomitant background SSRI receptor downregulation and structured psychological support across 45 sites can shrink Phase 3 effect sizes compared with small Phase 2 cohorts.

sol.r: The large early CYB003 signal may shrink as psychological-support effects, expectancy and variable site-level placebo responses scale up in phase 3.

trials.t: A Study With CIT-013 in RA Patients
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 6 in DAS28-CRP

fable.r: NET inhibition is unproven in RA and may not move DAS28-CRP within 6 weeks by the 0.65 points that 24 patients per arm can detect.

opus.r: An unvalidated NET-targeting mechanism tested over only 6 weeks in about 24 patients per arm on background csDMARDs; placebo DAS28-CRP drops of 0.7-1.0 points leave little room for a modest effect to reach significance.

sonnet.r: A novel anti-NETosis antibody tested for only 6 weeks in about 24 patients per arm needs a difference of roughly 0.6 DAS28 points to reach significance, and placebo response in csDMARD-background RA is sizeable.

haiku.r: Phase 2a with about 24 patients per arm and three dose levels splits the sample, so a significant week-6 DAS28-CRP difference is unlikely even if the high dose is active; sponsor disclosure timing is also uncertain.

carbon.r: Six weeks and 24 patients per arm give limited time and power for an upstream NETosis-clearing antibody to separate on DAS28-CRP against short-term placebo regression.

sol.r: Neutralizing NET-associated targets may not rapidly improve established synovitis enough to separate from placebo in approximately 24 patients per dose.

trials.t: A Study of Neoadjuvant Dostarlimab Plus Capecitabine Plus Oxaliplatin (CAPEOX) Vs CAPEOX With Previously Untreated T4N0 or Stage III Mismatch Repair Proficient (MMRp)/Microsatellite Stable (MSS) Colon Cancer
trials.ep: Major pathological response (at most 10% residual viable tumour in resected specimen, local assessment) after neoadjuvant therapy, up to about 18 weeks

fable.r: PD-1 blockade has limited activity in MMR-proficient colon cancer, so the gain in major pathological response over CAPEOX alone may be too small for a 120-patient phase 2 to show.

opus.r: PD-1 blockade adds little in MMRp/MSS colon cancer; with 60 per arm, a plausible 5-10 point gain in major pathological response over neoadjuvant CAPEOX is unlikely to reach two-sided significance.

sonnet.r: PD-1 blockade adds modest activity to chemotherapy in MSS colon cancer, and with 60 patients per arm only a difference near 20 points would reach p<0.05.

haiku.r: PD-1 blockade adds little in MSS colon cancer, and with 60 per arm a significant mPR gain needs about 13 points; the trial was still recruiting at launch, so results will likely come after mid-2027.

carbon.r: Anti-PD-1 monotherapy added to fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin chemotherapy has historically shown modest incremental pathological response in mismatch-repair-proficient/MSS colon cancer, making a statistically significant lift hard to achieve in 120 patients.

sol.r: Most MSS/pMMR colon cancers resist PD-1 blockade, so the pathological-response gain may be smaller than this 120-patient study can establish.

trials.t: Studying Solriamfetol Modulation of TAAR-1, Dopamine, and Norepinephrine in Shift Work Disorder (SUSTAIN)
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in mean sleep latency on the Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT)

fable.r: The wake-promoting effect on MWT is very likely, but the second primary outcome (CGI-S of sleepiness on the night shift) has a large placebo response in shift workers and must be met by the same dose.

opus.r: Both co-primaries must succeed for one dose; the CGI-S co-primary in a heterogeneous shift-worker population with high placebo response, plus night-time MWT variability and dropouts, is the weaker link despite solriamfetol's large wake-promoting effect.

sonnet.r: Solriamfetol robustly lifts MWT latency in other sleepiness disorders, so the MWT should win, but both MWT and CGI-S must be met and placebo response or night-shift measurement noise could sink one.

haiku.r: Solriamfetol 300 mg should lengthen MWT latency with 173 per arm, but the CGI-S co-primary must also be met and placebo response in shift-work sleepiness is high; enrolment was still open at launch against a December 2026 completion.

carbon.r: Both co-primary endpoints—objective MWT sleep latency and subjective night-shift CGI-S—must achieve statistical significance in the same dose arm, exposing the subjective global scale to higher placebo variability.

sol.r: The objective wakefulness effect should be robust, but the co-primary CGI-S endpoint may be diluted by placebo improvement and variable night-shift schedules.

trials.t: A Double Blind Study Performed to Evaluate the Efficacy and the Safety of EscharEx in Debridement of VLU (VALUE)
trials.ep: Complete debridement of the venous leg ulcer, clinically (visually) assessed after each application, within up to 2 weeks

fable.r: Complete debridement should be met easily, but the second primary outcome, time to complete wound closure over 12 weeks, showed only a trend in phase 2 and the trial has limited power for it.

opus.r: Complete debridement should clearly beat gel vehicle, but the record lists time to complete wound closure within 12 weeks as a second primary; showing faster closure versus vehicle with about 108 per arm is uncertain and both must succeed.

sonnet.r: Complete debridement should be met given phase 2 data, but wound closure is a co-primary that a product applied for only up to 8 days may not move enough, and both must succeed.

haiku.r: Complete debridement within 2 weeks is a large, likely separable endpoint with 108 per arm, but the second co-primary (time to wound closure) must also be met, and recruitment was still open at launch.

carbon.r: While EscharEx strongly outperforms gel vehicle on 2-week enzymatic debridement, meeting a second co-primary outcome on 12-week wound closure is difficult because post-debridement venous ulcer healing depends heavily on compression and vascular status.

sol.r: A substantial debridement benefit is likely, but faster removal of slough may not establish the protocol-required wound-closure result within 12 weeks.

trials.t: A Trial of HRS-8427 in the Treatment of Adults With Complicated Urinary Tract Infection, Including Acute Pyelonephritis
trials.c: Complicated Urinary Tract Infection(cUTI), Including Acute Pyelonephritis(AP)
trials.ep: Share of patients with composite microbiological eradication and clinical response at test of cure (7 days after end of treatment, day 14 to 21)

fable.r: If the unstated non-inferiority margin is 10 points, the roughly 400 microbiologically evaluable patients leave little room for chance variation unless HRS-8427 is truly better than imipenem.

opus.r: As a non-inferiority comparison with imipenem-cilastatin, failure needs HRS-8427's composite cure to fall more than the margin (likely 10 points) below control, which is uncommon for new beta-lactams in cUTI.

sonnet.r: A new siderophore-type cephalosporin versus imipenem in cUTI usually clears a 10-point non-inferiority margin, so the main risk is a strong imipenem arm or resistant isolates in China.

haiku.r: A composite cure endpoint against imipenem-cilastatin with about 290 per arm is likely non-inferior if the margin is standard; the margin is not in the record, and Chinese sponsors often disclose results later.

carbon.r: Resistant or complicated uropathogens with structural urinary tract abnormalities could increase microbiological relapse after treatment cessation and narrow the margin against imipenem-cilastatin.

sol.r: Insufficient microbiological eradication against the enrolled resistant pathogens could push the confidence bound beyond the non-inferiority margin.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of KN057 Prophylaxis in Patients With Haemophilia A or B Without Inhibitors
trials.c: Hemophilia A Without Inhibitor; Hemophilia B Without Inhibitor
trials.ep: Annualized rate of treated spontaneous and traumatic bleeds from week 1 to week 26, KN057 prophylaxis vs on-demand treatment (Part A)

fable.r: The efficacy contrast against on-demand treatment is very large for this class; the residual risk is a thrombotic safety signal or hold, as seen with other anti-TFPI antibodies, disrupting the trial.

opus.r: Anti-TFPI prophylaxis versus on-demand treatment gives very large bleed reductions; the only realistic threats are thrombotic events forcing a dosing pause, as happened with concizumab, or heavy dropout in a small Part A.

sonnet.r: Prophylaxis with an anti-TFPI agent versus on-demand treatment cuts treated bleeds by 70-90% in earlier trials, so success is near certain; the open question is when Alphamab discloses it.

haiku.r: Prophylaxis with an anti-TFPI agent should cut treated bleeds by most of the on-demand rate; the risks are the 21-patient control arm, the uncontrolled Part B co-primary, and disclosure timing.

carbon.r: Anti-TFPI agents carry a class risk of procoagulant overcorrection, D-dimer elevation, or thromboembolic events that could cause treatment discontinuations or impact Part B non-inferiority.

sol.r: Anti-TFPI prophylaxis should greatly reduce on-demand bleeding, with thrombosis-related interruption a greater threat than inadequate Part A efficacy.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Recombinant Human FGF21-Fc Fusion Protein for Injection (TQA2225/AP025) in Adult Subjects With Non-alcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH)
trials.sp: Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Group Nanjing Shunxin Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: NASH resolution (ballooning 0, inflammation 0-1, >=2-point NAS reduction) without worsening of fibrosis on liver biopsy at week 48

fable.r: With about 40 patients per arm and missing week-48 biopsies counted as failures, only a difference above roughly 20 points reaches significance, and the potency of this FGF21 analogue is unproven.

opus.r: FGF21 analogues reliably improve NASH resolution, but potency varies by construct (pegbelfermin underwhelmed); with about 40 per arm a less potent Fc-FGF21 or a high placebo response could miss significance.

sonnet.r: FGF21 analogs have shown large histologic effects, but about 40 patients per arm with a biopsy endpoint is small and the trial is slow, so a readout before mid-2027 is very unlikely.

haiku.r: A China-only phase 2 with 40 per arm has limited power for a biopsy responder endpoint, and it was still recruiting at launch, so a week-48 histology readout is unlikely before mid-2027.

carbon.r: With roughly 40 patients per arm and biopsy reader variability plus missing week-48 paired biopsies, a true histological benefit could still miss statistical significance.

sol.r: Despite strong FGF21 class evidence, approximately 40 patients per arm leave biopsy-based success vulnerable to sampling variation, placebo response and missing biopsies.

trials.t: Allogenic Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells for the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in WOMAC total score (0-96, higher is worse) at 48 weeks after the first injection

fable.r: Hyaluronate injections bring a large improvement in WOMAC on their own, leaving a small margin for the cells, and the MRI cartilage outcome at 24 weeks must also be met.

opus.r: Against active hyaluronate rather than saline, MSC injections in knee OA have shown only small WOMAC differences, and the MRI cartilage co-primary at 24 weeks must also succeed, a bar few cell therapies have cleared.

sonnet.r: Both WOMAC at 48 weeks and MRI cartilage must be met; the cartilage co-primary and a sizeable hyaluronate response are the main hurdles, and no readout is likely before mid-2027.

haiku.r: Cell therapy against an active hyaluronate comparator with 260 per arm may show a modest WOMAC gain, but the trial was still recruiting at launch against a December 2026 completion, so a 2027 public result is unlikely.

carbon.r: Achieving statistical superiority over active intra-articular sodium hyaluronate on both 48-week WOMAC symptoms and 24-week quantitative MRI cartilage structure is historically very challenging in knee osteoarthritis.

sol.r: A modest symptomatic benefit may be detectable, but convincing cartilage improvement on the co-primary MRI assessment after only 24 weeks is much less likely.

trials.t: Vebreltinib Plus PLB1004 as the First-line Therapy for Patients With EGFRm+/MET+ Locally Advanced or Metastatic NSCLC.
trials.ep: The objective response rate of the tumor (ORR)

fable.r: The trial was still recruiting at its registered primary completion date, so it will most likely run on with a late record update and no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.

opus.r: China-only phase 2 still recruiting past its registered October 2026 primary completion; expect the dates to be pushed back rather than termination, no ClinicalTrials.gov results posting, and little change to the ORR primary.

sonnet.r: A single-site Chinese phase 2 with ORR as the only primary, still recruiting past its registered completion; it will probably run on quietly, with little chance of posted results or a stop by August 2027.

haiku.r: Single-sponsor randomised phase 2 in China still recruiting at launch with a passed completion date; expect a late registry update and slow posting of results.

carbon.r: Biomarker-selected first-line EGFRm+/MET-overexpressing (IHC 3+) NSCLC requires dual-biomarker screening that slows enrollment, while Chinese Phase 2 oncology sponsors rarely post results directly on ClinicalTrials.gov soon after primary completion.

sol.r: Biomarker-selected enrollment is likely to prolong recruitment, but ongoing development is more likely than termination and early registry results posting is unlikely.

trials.t: A Trial Evaluating Efficacy of AGA2118 in PostMenopausal Women wIth Low Bone MasS (ARTEMIS)
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline to month 12 in lumbar spine bone mineral density

fable.r: A bone-density gain over placebo is close to certain for a sclerostin-blocking antibody; the residual risk is a topline that only calls the data positive without a statement on the primary endpoint.

opus.r: Sclerostin-pathway antibodies reliably raise spine BMD by 10%+ in a year against a flat placebo; the only realistic failure is an unexpectedly weak or poorly tolerated highest-dose regimen.

sonnet.r: A dual sclerostin/DKK1 bispecific at its highest regimen should raise lumbar spine BMD far above placebo; the main uncertainty is the dose actually tested and whether and when Angitia reports.

haiku.r: With 54 per arm and a clear anabolic bone effect expected at month 12, the lumbar spine signal should be strong, and the main risk is that the highest regimen gives a smaller gain than hoped.

carbon.r: Dual Wnt pathway disinhibition via sclerostin and DKK1 blockade could trigger injection-site reactions, anti-drug antibodies, or cardiovascular safety signals rather than fail on bone mineral density efficacy.

sol.r: With a sensitive lumbar-spine BMD endpoint and multiple active regimens, unexpected tolerability problems are more likely to prevent success than inadequate statistical power.

trials.t: A Study of SHJ002 Sterile Ophthalmic Solution for Myopia Control
trials.ep: Change in cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction from baseline to final visit (up to 52 weeks)

fable.r: Atropine is an effective comparator, so an unproven antisense eye drop would need a clear advantage in refraction change to show superiority in 140 children; comparable efficacy is the likelier report.

opus.r: Atropine is an active, proven myopia-control comparator; a first-in-class antisense eye drop with no controlled human efficacy data is unlikely to beat it on refraction change with 70 children per arm.

sonnet.r: The comparator is active atropine, which already slows myopia, and a 140-patient exploratory phase 2 is unlikely to show a significant superiority difference in spherical equivalent against it.

haiku.r: Atropine is a proven active comparator, so with about 70 per arm a superiority win on cycloplegic spherical equivalent needs a large gain that a phase 2 antisense drop is unlikely to show.

carbon.r: Topical antisense oligonucleotide eye drops face formidable corneal and scleral penetration barriers in human eyes, making statistical superiority (or tight non-inferiority) against active atropine control unlikely in 140 children.

sol.r: An unvalidated topical antisense therapy must outperform atropine, with uncertain delivery to relevant ocular tissues and substantial age-dependent variability.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate JCXH-105, an srRNA-based Herpes Zoster Vaccine
trials.ep: Percentage of participants with at least 2-fold increase in gE-specific CD4+ T cells (2+ activation markers) at day 89 versus baseline

fable.r: Shingrix with AS01 gives CD4+ T-cell response rates above 90%, so superiority is out of reach; success depends on the sponsor having a non-inferiority objective and saying it was met, not just calling the data positive.

opus.r: Shingrix produces a CD4+ T-cell response in roughly 90% of recipients, leaving almost no room for a statistically superior response rate; the trial is mainly a safety comparison with no stated efficacy hypothesis.

sonnet.r: Shingrix already produces a near-ceiling gE-specific CD4+ response rate, so superiority of an srRNA vaccine on this responder rate is very unlikely; a comparability message is the realistic best case.

haiku.r: Shingrix is a very strong comparator on CD4 response, and at about 233 per arm the test needs a gap of roughly 12 points to reach significance, so a clear superiority win is less likely than a comparable-response result.

carbon.r: Shingrix induces gE-specific CD4+ T-cell responses in roughly 90% of older adults, leaving minimal headroom for superiority and making descriptive reporting without a formal primary hypothesis likely.

sol.r: Shingrix leaves little headroom on a binary CD4 responder endpoint, so stronger response magnitude from srRNA might not translate into a significantly higher response rate.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate KarXT as a Treatment for Psychosis Associated With Alzheimer's Disease (ADEPT-4)
trials.sp: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb company
trials.ep: Change from baseline in NPI-C Hallucinations plus Delusions (NPI-C: H+D) score at week 14

fable.r: Placebo improvement in dementia-psychosis trials is large and site quality across 296 sites is uneven, so a modest KarXT effect at the lower dose used in the elderly may not separate on NPI-C H+D.

opus.r: Dementia-related psychosis trials have large placebo responses and noisy clinician ratings, so a real but modest muscarinic effect of about 2 points can be swamped; tolerability-limited dosing in frail elderly adds risk.

sonnet.r: Placebo response in Alzheimer's psychosis trials is large, and the elderly tolerate the cholinergic side effects of KarXT worse, so a mean difference of about 1.5 points may fall just short of significance.

haiku.r: ADEPT-4 is still recruiting at the snapshot with a registered completion date that must move, so the readout will likely be late, and the main risk to success is a large placebo response on NPI-C in Alzheimer psychosis.

carbon.r: Large placebo improvements and caregiver-mediated regression to the mean on NPI-C hallucinations and delusions scores frequently attenuate drug-placebo separation in Alzheimer's psychosis trials.

sol.r: Placebo and caregiver-contact effects in dementia psychosis may erase a modest muscarinic benefit, while gastrointestinal intolerance can reduce treatment exposure.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Induction Therapy With Afimkibart (Also Known as RO7790121) in Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.c: Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Clinical remission at Week 12 by modified Mayo score (mMS ≤2, stool frequency ≤1, rectal bleeding 0, endoscopic subscore ≤1)

fable.r: A miss would need a far smaller effect than the three phase 2 anti-TL1A trials showed, for example from the earlier week-12 read or loss of exposure to anti-drug antibodies.

opus.r: Anti-TL1A antibodies have shown 20-25 point placebo-adjusted remission gains in phase 2; failure would need the phase 3 effect to shrink drastically against a placebo rate near 9%, which is unlikely with ~175 per arm.

sonnet.r: Anti-TL1A antibodies showed large clinical remission gains over placebo in phase 2 UC, so the week-12 induction primary should be met; residual risk is a higher placebo rate or a lower effective dose.

haiku.r: A large expected week 12 gap against a low placebo remission rate makes a win very likely, and the residual risks are the unstated dose and whether Roche releases the topline before June 2027.

carbon.r: Higher-than-expected Week 12 placebo clinical remission in conventional-therapy-failure patients is the main residual risk to statistical separation.

sol.r: The main failure scenario is a smaller-than-expected induction effect in advanced-therapy-experienced patients, rather than an intrinsically insensitive remission endpoint.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Afimkibart (Also Known as RO7790121) for Induction and Maintenance Therapy in Participants With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.c: Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants in clinical remission (modified Mayo score ≤2 with stool, bleeding and endoscopic subscore criteria) at Week 12

fable.r: Both week 12 and week 52 remission must be met; the added risk is loss of response over a year of treat-through dosing, for example from anti-drug antibodies, on top of the induction risk.

opus.r: Both week-12 and week-52 remission must be met; the class effect is large and treat-through placebo remission at week 52 is usually below 10%, so failure needs a much weaker drug than phase 2 suggested.

sonnet.r: Both co-primaries (week 12 and week 52 remission) must be met; week 12 is very likely, and week 52 in the treat-through design adds some risk, but anti-TL1A effects look durable.

haiku.r: Both week 12 and week 52 clinical remission must be met by the same arm, so the week 52 treat-through readout is the main point of failure, and a slip past June 2027 is plausible.

carbon.r: Meeting the trial objective requires achieving statistical significance on both Week 12 and Week 52 clinical remission co-primary endpoints in a treat-through design.

sol.r: Both induction and maintenance remission must succeed; unexpectedly weak induction or loss of sustained benefit would defeat the joint objective.

trials.t: Once Daily Versus Twice Daily Budesonide Orodispersible Tablets for Induction of Remission in EoE
trials.ep: Proportion of patients in histological remission of eosinophilic esophagitis at the end of 6 weeks of treatment

fable.r: If the margin is 10 points, 154 per arm gives only about 80% power with truly equal arms, and a small real deficit for once-daily dosing would cut that to about half.

opus.r: The same 2 mg daily dose given once rather than twice may lose some mucosal contact time and histological effect; with a remission rate near 90% and ~154 per arm, a 3-5 point deficit could push the lower bound past a 10-point margin.

sonnet.r: Same total daily dose given once rather than twice may slightly lower mucosal contact; non-inferiority succeeds unless the once-daily regimen loses more than the unstated margin, with remission rates near 90% leaving little room.

haiku.r: The non-inferiority test with about 154 per arm and no stated margin makes a clean pass uncertain, and a small private sponsor may say little before the deadline.

carbon.r: Once-daily 2 mg topical budesonide provides fewer episodes of esophageal mucosal contact than twice-daily 1 mg dosing, risking a lower histological remission rate that misses the non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: A single daily mucosal exposure may lose enough histologic efficacy to cross the protocol's non-inferiority margin despite an identical total daily dose.

trials.t: A Study of Eltrekibart and Mirikizumab in Adult Patients With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants in clinical remission at week 12

fable.r: Unproven mechanism in ulcerative colitis with small arms; enrolment of 143 across 207 sites suggests the adaptive study did not expand, so monotherapy likely shows little gain over placebo.

opus.r: Blocking neutrophil-recruiting CXC chemokines is unproven in UC, and with about 48 per arm only a remission gain of 15+ points would reach significance as monotherapy; the combination with mirikizumab, not monotherapy, is the more likely winner.

sonnet.r: An anti-ELR+ chemokine antibody given alone has uncertain efficacy in UC and the dose-ranging arms are small, so a significant monotherapy-versus-placebo remission difference is unlikely.

haiku.r: A phase 2 with about 48 per arm needs a very large gap to reach significance, so the main risk is an underpowered test, and Lilly may say little publicly before the 2027 congresses.

carbon.r: Neutralizing ELR+ CXC chemokines alone may be insufficient to induce mucosal healing and Week 12 clinical remission in ulcerative colitis, especially given small per-arm sample sizes.

sol.r: Neutrophil-chemokine blockade may add too little UC remission efficacy, and the small adaptive study has limited ability to distinguish a modest monotherapy effect from chance.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study of AK112 Plus AK117 Versus Pembrolizumab in Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (R/M HNSCC)
trials.c: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
trials.ep: Overall survival from randomization to death from any cause, up to about 2 years

fable.r: Higher response and PFS may not carry through to survival against pembrolizumab, as in LEAP-010, and the CD47 component may add toxicity without much benefit.

opus.r: OS is a hard endpoint against pembrolizumab, which has a durable tail in PD-L1+ HNSCC; the anti-CD47 component has no proven OS benefit in solid tumours and VEGF blockade has not improved OS in HNSCC before.

sonnet.r: Pembrolizumab in CPS>=1 first-line HNSCC is a strong control (median OS about 12-14 months), and an OS primary needs many events; a report by mid-2027 would likely be an interim that Akeso only announces if positive.

haiku.r: The pembrolizumab control is strong in this population and the CD47 add-on has failed in earlier trials, so the bispecific has to carry an overall survival gain largely on its own.

carbon.r: Beating first-line pembrolizumab on overall survival in PD-L1-positive HNSCC has repeatedly failed for both VEGF-pathway combinations (LEAP-010) and CD47 inhibitors (ASPEN-03).

sol.r: Better tumor control from VEGF and CD47 blockade may not translate into longer survival, particularly if bleeding, anemia or treatment discontinuation offset efficacy.

trials.t: Safety and Pharmacodynamic Effects of BIIB122 in Participants With LRRK2-Associated Parkinson's Disease (LRRK2-PD)
trials.ep: Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) with BIIB122 compared with placebo over the 12-week double-blind period

fable.r: Small phase 2a already closed to recruitment should finish its 12-week blinded period on time; the main risk is early termination of the extension if the BIIB122 programme is ended after LUMA.

opus.r: Enrolment is complete and the 12-week double-blind period should end on schedule; results posting is not due until about a year after primary completion, and the OLE continues to 2028.

sonnet.r: Small 12-week safety and pharmacodynamic phase 2a, already fully enrolled with an OLE; primary completion in March 2027 should hold, and Denali/Biogen rarely post results within five months of completion.

haiku.r: A large developer with a current record and a safety-only primary makes lateness and termination unlikely; the main uncertainty is whether results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027.

carbon.r: With enrollment of 50 LRRK2-PD patients already completed by October 2026 and a short 12-week double-blind primary safety period, the study should finish its primary phase on time unless external BIIB122 program decisions intervene during the open-label extension.

sol.r: Recruitment is closed and blinded exposure is only 12 weeks, making near-schedule completion likely, although decisions about the larger BIIB122 program could drive an early stop.

trials.t: A Study of E2814 With Concurrent Lecanemab Treatment in Participants With Early Alzheimer's Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline in CSF MTBR-tau-243 at 6 months in early Alzheimer's disease on concurrent lecanemab

fable.r: The CSF MTBR-tau243 assay may capture antibody-bound tau or move on lecanemab alone, blunting the dose-response, and Eisai may report late or only in general terms.

opus.r: Lecanemab itself lowers CSF MTBR-tau243, so the incremental reduction from an anti-MTBR antibody could be smaller than expected and a dose-response test in roughly 105 patients across several arms may lack power.

sonnet.r: A target-engagement biomarker should move clearly with the highest E2814 dose, so the main risk is a small sample with several dose arms and assay variance, or a dose-response test that is not strictly significant.

haiku.r: The CSF biomarker may move too little or too unevenly at six months in about 52 patients per arm, and the assay unit and dose arms are not stated, so a significant dose response is uncertain.

carbon.r: While E2814 strongly reduces free CSF MTBR-tau-243, multi-dose group splitting in 105 patients or reporting descriptive biomarker trends without a formal primary test poses the main residual risk.

sol.r: A small dose-ranging study may not demonstrate the required incremental six-month CSF dose response on top of active lecanemab, even if E2814 engages tau.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Safety and Efficacy of MEDI0618 Compared to Placebo in Adult Participants With Episodic Migraine
trials.ep: Change from the 4-week baseline in mean monthly migraine headache days across the 12-week treatment period

fable.r: PAR2 blockade has no prior clinical evidence in migraine prevention, so the most likely failure is simply too little effect on monthly migraine days.

opus.r: PACAP-pathway blockade is less validated than CGRP: an anti-PAC1 receptor antibody failed, and only one anti-PACAP ligand antibody has shown about a 2-day benefit, so the effect may be too small in a hard-to-treat population.

sonnet.r: MEDI0618 (PAR2 antibody) has a novel, unproven migraine mechanism, tested in patients who have failed two or more preventives, where effects over placebo are small and placebo response is sizeable.

haiku.r: Anti-CGRP mechanisms have shown reproducible migraine-day reductions over placebo, so 155 patients per arm should detect a moderate effect; the risk is a smaller effect for this subcutaneous agent or dilution by the aCGRP-naive and inadequate-responder cohorts.

carbon.r: PAR2 blockade with MEDI0618 is an unvalidated clinical mechanism in human migraine prevention, and many preclinical meningeal pain targets fail to translate into clinical headache reduction.

sol.r: PAR2 blockade lacks established preventive efficacy in humans, and averaging the whole treatment period may dilute a modest or slow-onset effect against a substantial placebo response.

trials.t: Evaluation of the Safety and Efficacy of Treatment w/High Dose Melphalan Given Directly Into the Liver Followed by Treatment w/Approved Cancer Treatment or Approved Cancer Treatment Alone in Patients w/ Metastatic Colorectal Cancer w/Liver Dominant Disease
trials.ep: Hepatic progression-free survival: time from randomization to first hepatic disease progression, assessed over 24 months

fable.r: About 60 hepatic progression events with 2:1 allocation need an observed HR near 0.6 or better; melphalan is not an established colorectal drug and systemic therapy is delayed about 3 months in the experimental arm.

opus.r: Only 90 patients randomised 2:1 with about 30 controls; even a real hepatic PFS benefit may miss significance, and any readout by mid-2027 would be an immature early look.

sonnet.r: Only about 90 patients with a 2:1 split and few hepatic progression events, so a real local-control benefit may still miss significance; the 6-month hepatic PFS of the control is also uncertain.

haiku.r: With about 30 control patients and roughly 65 hepatic progression events, a hazard ratio of 0.6 sits near the edge of detection, so a significant result needs a larger effect than the design assumes.

carbon.r: With 2:1 randomization across 90 patients and an active SUNLIGHT control arm, modest sample size and hematologic toxicity delaying systemic consolidation may limit power for hepatic PFS.

sol.r: Refractory colorectal metastases may not respond sufficiently to regional melphalan to beat an effective systemic doublet, particularly with only 30 control patients.

trials.t: This Study Will Evaluate the Effectiveness of NTX-001, a Surgical Nerve Repair Product When Used in People With Upper Extremity Nerve Lacerations.
trials.c: Peripheral Nerve Injury Upper Limb; Peripheral Nerve Injury (PNI)
trials.ep: Mean Michigan Hand Questionnaire two-domain score (activities of daily living and pain) at week 24

fable.r: The two-domain MHQ endpoint was chosen after a small phase 2, so the true effect is probably smaller than assumed, and 98 patients only detect a standardised difference near 0.6; most direct repairs recover well by week 24.

opus.r: A patient-reported hand function and pain score at 24 weeks is noisy and driven by many factors besides axonal fusion; with 49 per arm a modest PEG-fusion benefit is unlikely to reach significance.

sonnet.r: A patient-reported two-domain composite at week 24 in just 98 patients is noisy, and standard repair also recovers well; a PEG-fusion benefit on function may not separate from control at 24 weeks.

haiku.r: With 49 patients per arm and a patient-reported composite score, a superiority result needs a difference that the trial may not show, and the registry still shows estimated completion dates.

carbon.r: Substantial patient-to-patient heterogeneity in nerve transection level, mixed versus sensory nerve involvement, and functional recovery over 24 weeks creates high variance for a 98-patient surgical trial.

sol.r: Variation in injury location, associated tissue damage and spontaneous recovery could overwhelm a treatment effect in a 98-patient trial using a subjective functional composite.

trials.t: A Study of TX000045 in Patients With Pulmonary Hypertension Secondary to Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (the APEX Study)
trials.c: Pulmonary Hypertension; Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 24 in pulmonary vascular resistance by right heart catheterization, in participants with combined pre- and post-capillary PH

fable.r: The chronic placebo-controlled trough effect on PVR may be much smaller than the acute fall after one IV dose; the CpcPH primary subset is only part of 191 patients, and relaxin-class drugs have disappointed in heart failure.

opus.r: The primary analysis is limited to the CpcPH subgroup, roughly 45-50 patients per arm, and PVR change by catheterisation is variable; an effect under about 0.7 Wood units could miss significance.

sonnet.r: The primary analysis is limited to the combined pre- and post-capillary subgroup, roughly 30 to 40 per arm, so only a sizeable PVR reduction would reach significance; the relaxin mechanism has not been proven in this population.

haiku.r: The primary analysis is limited to the combined pre- and post-capillary subgroup, so about 40 to 50 patients per arm drive a noisy catheter-measured PVR, and a modest relaxin-class effect may not clear significance.

carbon.r: Chronic RXFP1 agonism over 24 weeks may show attenuated hemodynamic durability compared with acute Phase 1b catheterization effects, and restricting the primary analysis to the CpcPH subgroup reduces sample size.

sol.r: The encouraging acute relaxin-mediated hemodynamic effect may attenuate with chronic treatment or fail to reproduce against placebo in the smaller CpcPH analysis population.

trials.t: A Study of AK104 in Subjects With Unresectable Locally Advanced NSCLC
trials.ep: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival (RECIST 1.1 progression or death) after chemoradiotherapy, up to 3 years

fable.r: Sugemalimab is an active PD-L1 comparator; adding CTLA-4 blockade to PD-1 has not clearly improved outcomes in NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598; BTCRC LUN16-081 consolidation) and may add pneumonitis-related discontinuation after chemoradiotherapy.

opus.r: Adding CTLA-4 blockade to PD-(L)1 consolidation after chemoradiotherapy has not improved PFS before (nivolumab plus ipilimumab in BTCRC LUN 16-081), so cadonilimab may not beat an active PD-L1 comparator.

sonnet.r: Sugemalimab is itself an effective consolidation drug (median PFS about 10 months by investigator), so showing superiority needs a clear added benefit from CTLA-4 co-blockade; the hazard ratio may land near 0.8.

haiku.r: Sugemalimab consolidation in this setting sets a strong progression-free survival benchmark, so cadonilimab has to show a clear gain over an active PD-L1 control, and the 560-patient trial gives moderate power.

carbon.r: Sugemalimab is an established active PD-L1 consolidation standard after chemoradiotherapy, and adding CTLA-4 blockade via cadonilimab increases pneumonitis and treatment discontinuations that may offset incremental efficacy.

sol.r: Sugemalimab already provides effective consolidation, and adding CTLA-4 activity may yield insufficient incremental PFS benefit while increasing post-radiation immune toxicity.

trials.t: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of VX-993 for Pain Associated With Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
trials.ep: Change from baseline in weekly average of daily pain intensity on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) at Week 12

fable.r: NaV1.8 inhibitors have matched but not beaten pregabalin (VX-548 phase 2), so a comparison with the active control would fail; if the primary is within-group change it is easily met, but Vertex may not frame a deprioritised drug that way.

opus.r: Pregabalin is an effective active comparator in DPN pain; NaV1.8 inhibition (suzetrigine) only matched pregabalin in a similar phase 2, and VX-993 already failed in acute pain, so superiority over pregabalin is very unlikely.

sonnet.r: VX-993 missed efficacy in its acute pain phase 2, and beating pregabalin on NPRS (rather than just placebo) is a stringent test for a NaV1.8 inhibitor in a noisy phase 2 of about 100 per arm.

haiku.r: The investigational agent has to beat pregabalin, a moderately effective active control, by about 0.6 points at week 12, which is a high bar.

carbon.r: Without a pure placebo arm or if tested directly against active pregabalin, an oral NaV1.8 inhibitor is unlikely to demonstrate statistically significant superiority over pregabalin on Week 12 NPRS pain reduction.

sol.r: Pain reduction from baseline is likely, but chronic neuropathic analgesia may be modest and insufficiently differentiated from pregabalin to justify advancing another Nav1.8 inhibitor.

trials.t: A Study to Learn How PF-06821497 (Mevrometostat) Works in Men With Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer.
trials.ep: Radiographic progression-free survival by blinded central review (RECIST 1.1 soft tissue, PCWG3 bone) or death, over about 3 years

fable.r: Enzalutamide alone controls ARSi-naive disease for 18 months or more, so the added effect of EZH2 inhibition may be smaller than in post-abiraterone disease, and the rPFS analysis may be immature.

opus.r: In ARSi-naive disease enzalutamide alone is very effective (rPFS about 20 months), so EZH2 inhibition may add less than in the post-abiraterone setting where the randomized signal was seen.

sonnet.r: Enzalutamide in ARSi-naive mCRPC is a strong control (rPFS about 20 months or more), so the EZH2 add-on must deliver a hazard ratio near 0.75 or better to reach significance.

haiku.r: An EZH2 inhibitor added to enzalutamide has to show a clear radiographic progression gain on top of an active androgen receptor inhibitor, and that is the most likely point of failure.

carbon.r: First-line ARSi-naive mCRPC patients achieve roughly 20 months median rPFS on enzalutamide alone, and added gastrointestinal and hematologic toxicity from mevrometostat may limit treatment duration before AR resistance emerges.

sol.r: Enzalutamide can provide prolonged disease control in ARSi-naive mCRPC, potentially diluting the combination's incremental benefit and delaying the required event count.

trials.t: FK-PC101 as Adjuvant Therapy for Men With High-Risk Prostate Cancer
trials.c: Prostate Cancer (Adenocarcinoma); Prostate CA; Prostate Cancers
trials.ep: Disease-free survival (local, distant or PSA biochemical recurrence, or death) over about 22 months after randomization

fable.r: About 100 patients and roughly 30 DFS events can only detect a very large effect; cancer vaccines have a poor record in prostate cancer, and an early public statement would more likely call interim data encouraging than report a met primary.

opus.r: Autologous whole-cell cancer vaccines have repeatedly failed to change recurrence in prostate cancer, and with about 100 patients and perhaps 25 DFS events only a very large effect would be significant.

sonnet.r: About 100 patients and perhaps 20 to 25 DFS events leave little power for a personalised vaccine effect, and enrolment is still open, so a report by mid-2027 is unlikely and would probably be an interim.

haiku.r: Fifty patients per arm with few DFS events in a 3-site, slowly recruiting adjuvant trial gives little power to show a benefit over observation.

carbon.r: Whole-cell prostate cancer vaccines have consistently failed to prevent recurrence in randomized trials, and requiring undetectable PSA at two months post-prostatectomy leaves very few DFS events within 22 months.

sol.r: The vaccine lacks convincing randomized evidence of preventing biochemical recurrence, and approximately 30 events would require an exceptionally large treatment effect.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate Sonrotoclax Combined With Zanubrutinib Versus Zanubrutinib Alone in Participants With Previously Untreated Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
trials.ep: Best complete response or complete response with incomplete marrow recovery (CR/CRi) rate by independent review (iwCLL 2018) at month 16

fable.r: The main risk is formal: CR/CRi needs marrow-confirmed remission within 16 months by independent review and the arms are small; if the analysis is descriptive, the sponsor may not state a met hypothesis.

opus.r: IRC-assessed CR/CRi needs marrow confirmation, so missing biopsies or a strict month-16 window could cap the combination's CR rate; the gap over zanubrutinib alone should still be large.

sonnet.r: Month-16 IRC-assessed CR/CRi may be too early for the combination to separate fully, but BTK-inhibitor monotherapy gives few CRs by then and Bcl-2 plus BTK combinations clearly raise CR/CRi.

haiku.r: With 47 patients per arm the trial has adequate power only if the BCL2 add-on lifts CR/CRi by about 25 points; a smaller true gain would miss significance.

carbon.r: As a Phase 2 contribution-of-components study supporting registration, the main risk is descriptive reporting without a formal primary hypothesis p-value or conservative independent review lymph node criteria at Month 16.

sol.r: Failure would most likely reflect fewer or later marrow-confirmed complete responses than early combination data suggest, rather than an absence of antileukemic activity.

trials.t: Evaluation of Sonelokimab in Patients With Active Psoriatic Arthritis and Anti-TNFα Inadequate Response
trials.ep: Proportion of participants achieving ACR50 response at week 16

fable.r: Efficacy risk is low; the main threat is an inflated placebo ACR50 response, as placebo response hurt sonelokimab's VELA-2 hidradenitis trial, or a weaker response in TNF-experienced patients.

opus.r: IL-17A/F blockade reliably beats placebo on ACR50 in TNF-IR PsA; the only plausible failure is sonelokimab underperforming as it did versus expectations in HS, which still would likely leave a significant gap over a ~9% placebo rate.

sonnet.r: IL-17A/F nanobody has strong ARGO phase 2 PsA data; the main risk is a lower effect in TNF-IR patients or an unusually strong placebo response, neither likely to erase a 25+ point gap.

haiku.r: With 150 per arm and a placebo ACR50 near 10 percent, the main risk is a smaller drug effect in anti-TNF-experienced patients than phase 2 suggested.
