carbon.r: Unexpectedly elevated placebo ACR50 responses across global sites represent the main statistical risk, although dual IL-17A/F inhibition has consistently shown large treatment margins in TNF-IR psoriatic arthritis.

sol.r: Unexpected placebo inflation is the principal threat to an otherwise well-supported dual-IL-17 mechanism with a large anticipated ACR50 difference.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called Rimegepant in Women When Used for Intermittent Prevention of Menstrual Migraine
trials.ep: Mean change from observation period in migraine days per 5-day perimenstrual period, averaged across 5 double-blind treatment cycles

fable.r: Rimegepant's preventive effect is modest (0.8 days per month over placebo with every-other-day dosing) and perimenstrual attacks are hard to treat; a high placebo response over five cycles could shrink the difference.

opus.r: Menstrual migraine trials have large placebo responses on a short 5-day window with few migraine days at baseline, so a modest gepant effect (about 0.3 days per period) could be lost in noise.

sonnet.r: Gepant prevention effects are modest and placebo response in a 5-day window is large; 241 per arm and averaging over five cycles give good power only if the effect is at least about 0.25 migraine days.

haiku.r: Placebo response in menstrual migraine prevention is large, so a modest intermittent-dosing benefit of about a third of a migraine day per perimenstrual period may be hard to show.

carbon.r: Cycle-to-cycle variability in menstrual onset prediction can misalign short perimenstrual dosing with actual menses, diluting the measured reduction in migraine days within the narrow 5-day window.

sol.r: A large observation-to-treatment placebo improvement could erase a modest incremental benefit in hormonally triggered attacks that can be unusually difficult to prevent.

trials.t: A Phase II Study of Zuberitamab Injection in Patients With Primary Membranous Nephropathy
trials.ep: Proportion of patients achieving overall response in urinary protein/creatinine ratio at week 76

fable.r: If cyclosporine is continued to week 76 instead of being stopped at about 12 months as in MENTOR, its responders do not relapse and 45 patients per arm cannot separate the arms.

opus.r: With about 45 patients per arm, a 15-20 point gain in remission over cyclosporine at week 76 has only about even odds of reaching p<0.05, and the exploratory phase 2 may not formally test superiority at all.

sonnet.r: With 45 per arm a 20-point gap in response is borderline significant, and a cyclosporine arm held to week 76 could respond better than expected.

haiku.r: Forty-five patients per arm against cyclosporine gives power only for a large response gap, and an undefined response measure and single-site reporting add timing and form risk.

carbon.r: With roughly 45 patients per arm in an exploratory Phase 2 design, prolonged cyclosporine maintenance or higher-than-expected control remission at week 76 could leave the study underpowered for formal superiority.

sol.r: The expected advantage depends heavily on cyclosporine withdrawal; continued cyclosporine or unusually durable control-arm remissions could eliminate superiority in this small trial.

trials.t: A Master Protocol for Orforglipron in Participants With Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity or Overweight
trials.ep: Change from baseline in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at Week 52, study GZ01 (participants not using PAP)

fable.r: Orforglipron's weight loss is about half tirzepatide's, so the AHI effect could be smaller than expected, though it would have to fall below about 5 events/h to miss significance.

opus.r: Weight loss drives AHI reduction; orforglipron gives roughly 9-11% placebo-adjusted weight loss, which should still reduce AHI by about 10-15 events/h, far beyond what 178 per arm needs to detect.

sonnet.r: Orforglipron produces about 10% weight loss at one year and AHI falls with weight, so a placebo-adjusted reduction near 10 events/hour with 178 per arm is very likely significant.

haiku.r: The risk is that an oral GLP-1 with about 12 percent weight loss lowers AHI less than injectable tirzepatide, although 178 per arm would still detect a modest effect.

carbon.r: Higher gastrointestinal adverse event discontinuations or hepatic safety signals with oral small-molecule GLP-1 therapy could attenuate treatment-regimen weight loss and AHI reduction in one of the two master-protocol substudies.

sol.r: Orforglipron should improve AHI through weight loss, but less weight loss than tirzepatide and heterogeneous airway anatomy could attenuate the sleep-apnea benefit.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Efgartigimod PH20 SC in Adults With Systemic Sclerosis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in modified Rodnan Skin Score (mRSS) at week 24

fable.r: FcRn blockade has no proven effect on skin fibrosis, and with 58 vs 29 patients the observed mRSS difference must exceed about 3 points against a placebo arm that usually improves on background therapy.

opus.r: SSc autoantibodies are not clearly pathogenic, so IgG lowering by FcRn blockade may not soften skin; mRSS also improves spontaneously on placebo, and 58 vs 29 patients cannot detect a small difference.

sonnet.r: FcRn blockade removes IgG but the causal role of autoantibodies in skin fibrosis is unproven; a 58 vs 29 trial with a large placebo response in early disease detects only a sizeable effect on mRSS.

haiku.r: A modest skin-score effect in an 87-patient trial with only 29 placebo patients is unlikely to separate from the spread of mRSS change.

carbon.r: Lowering circulating IgG autoantibodies via FcRn blockade may not reverse established TGF-beta- and fibroblast-driven dermal fibrosis rapidly enough to separate on mRSS by week 24.

sol.r: Lowering circulating IgG may not reverse established skin fibrosis, while spontaneous improvement and background treatment can shrink the mRSS contrast at only 24 weeks.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Efficacy and Safety Study of GAL-101, 2% Ophthalmic Solution in Non-foveal Geographic Atrophy Secondary to Non-neovascular AMD
trials.ep: Annual rate of growth in geographic atrophy lesion area on fundus autofluorescence, baseline to last on-treatment visit (48 to 96 weeks)

fable.r: A topical amyloid-beta modulator has no prior evidence of slowing geographic atrophy, and 55 eyes per arm can detect only a slowing of a third or more.

opus.r: A topical amyloid-aggregation inhibitor must reach the retina at active levels to slow GA; eye-drop and oral approaches have consistently failed here, and 55 per arm detects only a large effect on lesion growth.

sonnet.r: An eye-drop with indirect anti-amyloid mechanism must slow GA growth by about 20% in only 55 per arm; even approved injectable complement inhibitors achieve 15 to 20% reductions.

haiku.r: With 55 eyes per arm and a widely varying placebo growth rate, a true benefit of about 0.3 mm2 per year would be hard to detect.

carbon.r: Topical ophthalmic drops rarely achieve therapeutic posterior-segment retina exposure, and amyloid-beta targeting has previously failed to slow geographic atrophy progression in clinical trials.

sol.r: Neither topical posterior-segment delivery nor amyloid-oligomer targeting has established clinical efficacy in GA, and this trial may miss a modest slowing of lesion growth.

trials.t: A Phase 3, Placebo-Controlled Study to Investigate LP352 in Children and Adults With Dravet Syndrome (DS)
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in countable motor seizure frequency during the treatment period (up to 15 weeks)

fable.r: The phase 2 signal in Dravet syndrome rested on a handful of patients, so the true effect of selective 5-HT2C agonism may be well below fenfluramine's and too small for about 50 per arm.

opus.r: Selective 5-HT2C agonism may capture less of fenfluramine's anti-seizure effect than PACIFIC's small Dravet subset suggested; a weaker drug plus a variable placebo response could leave the difference non-significant with about 48 per arm.

sonnet.r: 5-HT2C agonism (like fenfluramine) is validated in Dravet and bexicaserin gave about 50% median seizure reduction in phase 1b/2, but 48 per arm and a placebo response near -10 to -15% leave some chance of a miss.

haiku.r: Placebo seizure reduction in Dravet trials is often large and variable, so a 96-patient trial may miss a moderate drug effect despite a plausible mechanism.

carbon.r: Heavy pretreatment or refractoriness to prior serotonergic therapy (fenfluramine) in contemporary Dravet syndrome cohorts could blunt LP352's effect size relative to earlier trials.

sol.r: PACIFIC's Dravet subgroup was very small, so a disease-specific effect below the broader DEE signal could leave this modest phase 3 underpowered.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of SP-8203 (Otaplimastat) in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke Receiving Thrombolytic Standard of Care
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with modified Rankin Scale score 0-1 at Day 90

fable.r: Neuroprotectants added to thrombolysis have repeatedly failed in phase 3, and otaplimastat's phase 2 showed no efficacy signal that would support the roughly 10-point gain the trial is powered for.

opus.r: Neuroprotectants added to reperfusion have almost uniformly failed in phase 3 stroke trials, and otaplimastat's phase 2 showed safety but no clear efficacy signal, so a true effect of a few points on mRS 0-1 is unlikely to be detected.

sonnet.r: A multipotent MMP-inhibiting neuroprotectant added to thrombolysis in a trial sized for a roughly 10-point mRS 0-1 gain; neuroprotectants have almost always failed phase 3, and enrolment of 852 in Korea will probably run past March 2027.

haiku.r: Neuroprotectants have repeatedly failed on 90-day mRS, and 426 per arm only detects about a 10-point gain, so a small or null effect on top of alteplase is the likely outcome; enrolment at two sites makes a slip past the March 2027 completion likely.

carbon.r: Acute ischemic stroke neuroprotectants co-administered with thrombolysis have consistently failed to translate small Phase 2 signals into statistically significant Day 90 mRS improvements in Phase 3.

sol.r: Acute-stroke neuroprotection has repeatedly failed to add durable functional benefit to reperfusion, and the earlier otaplimastat signal may overstate its true effect.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of HSK31858 in Participants With Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis
trials.ep: Annualized rate of pulmonary exacerbations over 52 weeks in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis

fable.r: The phase 2 effect (exacerbations roughly halved) will probably regress toward the 20% reduction seen with brensocatib in ASPEN, which would leave about 220 patients per arm underpowered.

opus.r: DPP1 inhibition gave only about a 20% exacerbation-rate reduction in ASPEN with 1,700 patients; with 669 patients and overdispersed exacerbation counts, a similar effect would leave power near 60-70%, so a modest true effect could miss significance.

sonnet.r: DPP1 inhibition is validated by brensocatib, but its exacerbation benefit was modest (rate ratio about 0.8), so a 669-patient trial has only moderate power if HSK31858 is similar or a bit weaker, or the Chinese placebo rate is low.

haiku.r: A rate ratio near 0.8 is about what a DPP1 inhibitor achieved in ASPEN, but 669 patients give power of only about 40 to 50 percent at 0.05, so an underpowered miss is the main risk; a public readout by mid-2027 is likely if the trial closed in late 2026.

carbon.r: A lower-than-expected on-trial pulmonary exacerbation rate in the placebo arm could compress absolute event counts and attenuate the Phase 2 rate ratio toward unity.

sol.r: A class-consistent but only 15-20% exacerbation reduction could be insufficient at this sample size, particularly if on-study exacerbations fall well below historical rates.

trials.t: A Study of Retatrutide (LY3437943) Compared to Tirzepatide (LY3298176) in Adults Who Have Obesity
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 80

fable.r: Tirzepatide at maximum dose already gives about 21% weight loss, and higher adverse-event discontinuation on retatrutide narrows the gap under the treatment-regimen estimand, though probably not enough to lose superiority.

opus.r: Retatrutide's weight loss clearly exceeds tirzepatide's in cross-trial data, so the main threat is higher retatrutide discontinuation for GI events or excess weight loss diluting the treatment-regimen difference; even so the trial is heavily powered.

sonnet.r: Retatrutide has shown about 28% weight loss at 68 weeks against roughly 21% for tirzepatide at similar duration, so superiority is very likely; the risk is high retatrutide dropout from adverse events, or a lower retatrutide dose, narrowing the gap.

haiku.r: Retatrutide's weight-loss effect looks well above tirzepatide's, so superiority at week 80 with 400 per arm is very likely; the risks are a lower retatrutide dose or an undisclosed tirzepatide dose, and Lilly usually reports topline quickly after completion.

carbon.r: Higher gastrointestinal or dysesthesia-related treatment discontinuations on retatrutide relative to tirzepatide could narrow the treatment-regimen estimand weight-loss advantage.

sol.r: Maximally tolerated tirzepatide produces very large weight loss, so a smaller incremental glucagon benefit or more retatrutide discontinuations could erase superiority.

trials.t: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial on Efficacy and Safety of Fluticasone Propionate/Albuterol Sulfate Combination in Participants 12 Years and Older With Asthma
trials.sp: Teva Branded Pharmaceutical Products R&D LLC
trials.ep: Baseline-adjusted FEV1 area under the effect curve 0-6 hours post-dose, over 4 weeks (Day 1 and Week 4)

fable.r: Showing the fluticasone contribution on trough FEV1 against albuterol alone after only 4 weeks is the weaker of the two required comparisons.

opus.r: The AUEC primary is near-certain given the albuterol component, but if the trial's hypothesis requires trough FEV1 superiority over the albuterol-alone arm after only 4 weeks, the fluticasone contribution (about 100 mL) could fall short of significance with about 160 per arm.

sonnet.r: Both co-primaries must be met: albuterol's 6-hour bronchodilation is near certain to show, but trough FEV1 after only 4 weeks depends on the inhaled steroid effect against the albuterol-only arm and is the weaker comparison.

haiku.r: Two co-primary hypotheses must both succeed in the same arm and the trough FEV1 comparator is not stated, so the combined hypothesis is the main risk; the AUEC gain should be clear at 162 per arm, but a 4-week trough gain is small.

carbon.r: Meeting FDA combination-rule co-primary endpoints requires trough FEV1 superiority of Fp/ABS over albuterol monotherapy at just 4 weeks, which has tighter statistical margin than acute bronchodilation.

sol.r: Success likely requires demonstrating the steroid component's trough-FEV1 contribution against albuterol, not merely the easier combination-versus-placebo AUEC contrast.

trials.t: A Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of TachoSil and Surgicel Original as an Adjunct to Control Mild to Moderate Soft Tissue Bleeding During Surgery
trials.ep: Hemostatic success at the target bleeding site within 3 minutes after application of study intervention

fable.r: In mild soft-tissue bleeding with firm pressure, plain Surgicel may reach 70% or more hemostasis at 3 minutes, leaving too small a gap for 58 patients per arm.

opus.r: For mild (VIBe 1) soft-tissue bleeding, oxidized cellulose already achieves hemostasis within 3 minutes in most patients, so the margin left for TachoSil may be too small for 58 patients per arm to show significance.

sonnet.r: Only 58 per arm and an open-label design; a fibrin-coated patch should achieve faster hemostasis than oxidized cellulose, but a smaller true gap or a strong Surgicel arm at 3 minutes would leave the trial short of significance.

haiku.r: At 58 per arm the 3-minute success gap must be about 18 points to reach significance, and a plausible 12-point advantage makes an underpowered miss the main risk; enrolment was still open at launch, so the registered December 2026 completion may slip.

carbon.r: Predominance of mild Grade 1 bleeding sites could elevate 3-minute hemostasis rates with Surgicel Original above 65%, compressing the treatment difference in a 116-patient sample.

sol.r: Surgicel plus three minutes of firm pressure may already control most mild bleeding, leaving too little separation for superiority in 116 patients.

trials.t: A Phase III Study in Subjects With Primary Open Angle Glaucoma or Ocular Hypertension in China
trials.ep: Change from baseline in mean diurnal intraocular pressure at Week 4

fable.r: Omidenepag lowers IOP about 0.6 mmHg less than latanoprost, so a slightly larger gap or a wide interval in the Chinese cohort could breach a 1.5 mmHg non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: Omidenepag lowers IOP slightly less than latanoprost (about 0.6 mmHg in AYAME, upper CI 1.26 against a 1.5 margin), so a slightly larger gap in Chinese patients could push the upper confidence bound past the non-inferiority margin.

sonnet.r: A bridging non-inferiority comparison with latanoprost; omidenepag was non-inferior to latanoprost in Japanese phase 3 (AYAME), so success is likely, but a 115-per-arm study could miss the margin if the Chinese effect is smaller, and results may not be made public soon.

haiku.r: The record does not state the design; if it is non-inferiority against latanoprost, a difference near zero should pass, but if it is superiority the drug is unlikely to win, and the main risk is a weaker IOP effect than latanoprost.

carbon.r: Latanoprost lowers intraocular pressure by roughly 0.4 to 0.6 mmHg more than omidenepag isopropyl on average, leaving limited buffer below a standard 1.5 mmHg non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: Latanoprost generally lowers IOP slightly more than omidenepag, so a narrow non-inferiority margin could defeat an otherwise effective bridging study.

trials.t: Efficacy & Safety Study of Relugolix in Women With Heavy Menstrual Bleeding Associated With Uterine Fibroids
trials.ep: Share of women with menstrual blood loss <80 mL and ≥50% reduction from baseline over the final 35 days of 12-week double-blind treatment.

fable.r: Efficacy risk is minimal; failure would come from missing or poorly collected alkaline hematin samples in the last 35 days, counted as non-response, in a small single-site trial.

opus.r: The relugolix responder effect in LIBERTY was more than 50 points, so failure would need an implausibly high placebo response or major dropout in this small 80-vs-40 trial.

sonnet.r: Relugolix with add-back gave about 72% responders against 15 to 19% on placebo in LIBERTY, so a 2:1 trial of 120 should be clearly positive; the main uncertainty is whether Qilu makes the result public by mid-2027.

haiku.r: Relugolix combination therapy's responder effect is large in LIBERTY, so a 65-point gap should pass easily at 80 versus 40 women; the risks are a one-site trial with small arms and a thin or slow public statement by mid-2027.

carbon.r: Because relugolix 40 mg rapidly and profoundly suppresses menstrual bleeding relative to placebo, failure would likely arise only from operational issues, alkaline hematin collection dropouts, or incomplete topline reporting.

sol.r: Relugolix should strongly suppress bleeding, leaving hormonal tolerability and incomplete final-cycle blood-loss collections as the principal residual risks with the unusual listed add-back regimen.

trials.t: A Phase IIb Study of 610 in Participants With Severe Eosinophilic Asthma
trials.ep: Change from baseline in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at week 52

fable.r: Anti-IL-5 antibodies improve FEV1 modestly and FEV1 at week 52 is noisy; with about 75 per arm a true gain near 100-130 mL would often miss significance.

opus.r: Anti-IL-5 antibodies improve pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by only about 100-160 mL with an SD near 400 mL, so about 75 patients per arm gives roughly 40-60% power per dose, and placebo improvement at week 52 can shrink the difference.

sonnet.r: Anti-IL-5 antibodies raise FEV1 by only about 100 mL, and with roughly 75 patients per arm the 52-week FEV1 comparison is underpowered; two dose groups give some extra chance that one reaches significance.

haiku.r: A 75-per-arm FEV1 trial needs a gain near 95 mL for significance at week 52, and anti-IL-5 gains in asthma have been modest, so an underpowered miss is the main risk; a single-site Chinese readout by June 2027 is uncertain.

carbon.r: Anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibodies typically improve pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by only 100 to 140 mL over placebo with large inter-patient spirometric variability (~380 mL SD), making N=75 per arm modestly powered.

sol.r: Anti-IL-5 treatment can substantially reduce exacerbations while producing only a small, noisy FEV1 improvement, making the week-52 lung-function primary vulnerable.

trials.t: Study Evaluating AZD7798 for Treatment in Crohn's Disease Patients With an Ileostomy
trials.ep: Number of participants with adverse events

fable.r: Induction is complete and only open-label maintenance remains, so a stop is unlikely; posting by August 2027 hinges on AstraZeneca submitting within a year of primary completion.

opus.r: AstraZeneca phase 2 closed at 24 patients with induction done; open-label maintenance runs to Sept 2027, so it likely continues unless AZD7798 is deprioritised, and results posting falls right around the 12-month mark.

sonnet.r: Small AstraZeneca phase 2 (24 of about 30 planned) with safety-only primaries and a 40-week open-label extension; primary completion Aug 2026 puts the 12-month results deadline just before the read date, so posting by 31 Aug 2027 is possible but not likely.

haiku.r: Small safety-only phase 2 (24 enrolled) with twelve safety primaries; the uncertainties are whether results post soon after the study completion date and whether the twelve primary measures get edited.

carbon.r: This small 24-patient Phase 2 ileostomy Crohn's study is already active, not recruiting past its August 2026 primary completion date, but lacks US sites and runs open-label maintenance until September 2027, delaying ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.

sol.r: Enrollment appears complete and the induction safety assessment should already be finished, while open-label maintenance and follow-up continue into 2027.

trials.t: A Study to Learn More About the Effects and Safety of Felzartamab Infusions in Adults With Kidney Transplants Who Have Antibody-Mediated Rejection (AMR)
trials.ep: Percentage of participants with biopsy-proven histologic resolution of antibody-mediated rejection at week 24 (Part A)

fable.r: The phase 2 effect came from 22 patients and may shrink in a broader, multi-centre population with more chronic damage and central biopsy reading.

opus.r: Biopsy sampling variability and regression to the mean can produce spontaneous histologic resolution on placebo (20% in phase 2), shrinking the margin, especially if central Banff reading is strict and many patients have chronic active lesions.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 showed a very large effect on AMR resolution, so failure would most likely come from a heavier chronic-active, scarred late-AMR mix and a higher placebo resolution rate than in the small phase 2.

haiku.r: Biopsy-based histologic resolution at week 24 is a slow, noisy endpoint in late AMR where placebo rarely resolves; a real plasma-cell effect should still show a clear gap at 66 per arm.

carbon.r: Multicenter Phase 3 replication across 56 global sites with Banff 2022 central biopsy scoring and refractory chronic active AMR patients could attenuate the dramatic histologic resolution rate observed in Phase 2.

sol.r: The principal risk is that the striking small phase 2 biopsy benefit shrinks substantially in a larger, more heterogeneous transplant population.

trials.t: A Study to Compare Pharmacokinetics, Efficacy, Safety, and Immunogenicity of MB12 (Proposed Pembrolizumab Biosimilar) to Keytruda® in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (BENITO Study)
trials.c: Non Squamous Non Small Cell Lung Cancer
trials.ep: PK bioequivalence (AUC from 0 to 504 hours between cycles 1 and 2; AUC at steady state between cycles 7 and 8) and objective response rate up to week 24

fable.r: All of several equivalence tests must pass; steady-state AUC after attrition and three-way comparison with EU and US Keytruda leave little slack if exposure differs by 8-10%.

opus.r: A small real PK difference versus one of the reference products (EU or US Keytruda), or a chance ORR difference that lands outside the equivalence margin, is the most plausible way this biosimilar study fails.

sonnet.r: Biosimilar pembrolizumab trials usually meet PK and ORR equivalence at n=726, but two primaries and a three-way PK comparison against EU and US reference leave some risk of missing a margin.

haiku.r: Two co-primary equivalence outcomes must both pass: the PK ratio inside 80-125 percent and an ORR difference within a margin the record does not state. Both usually pass in biosimilar pembrolizumab trials this size, so the risk is one miss.

carbon.r: Demonstrating co-primary equivalence on both cycle-level PK AUC ratios and 24-week objective response rate exposes the trial to random ORR variation across arms pushing confidence bounds slightly outside equivalence margins.

sol.r: The main residual risk is a PK or response-rate confidence interval crossing an equivalence boundary, particularly after attrition before steady-state sampling.

trials.t: A Study on the Safety of an Investigational Chickenpox Vaccine, When Given to Healthy Children, 12 to 15 Months of Age
trials.ep: Percentage of participants reporting each solicited administration site events

fable.r: Record still listed recruiting a month before a completion date that needs six months of follow-up, so a slip past February 2027 is about as likely as not; posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

opus.r: Still recruiting in late Oct 2026 with 181-day safety follow-up, so the registered Nov 2026 completion cannot hold and should move to mid-2027; GSK updates records and usually posts results about a year after completion.

sonnet.r: The record still said recruiting in Oct 2026 although the registered completion (Nov 2026) is 181 days after the last dose, so the last vaccination and the date must move later; GSK posts results typically within about a year of completion.

haiku.r: Safety-only vaccine study with eight safety primaries, still recruiting at launch against a November 2026 completion date; the uncertainties are whether the registry date slips past February 2027 and whether results post in time.

carbon.r: Because the trial remained in recruiting status in late October 2026 while primary safety outcomes require 181 days of post-dose follow-up, primary completion will almost certainly slip more than 90 days past November 2026.

sol.r: The established vaccine sponsor and single-dose design favor completion, but six-month safety follow-up makes continued recruitment the main source of delay.

trials.t: A Study of Lianxiaxiaopi Granules in the Treatment of Postprandial Distress Syndrome
trials.ep: Postprandial distress syndrome responder rate: response (≥50% reduction in fullness and early satiety) in more than half of weeks, over 8 weeks

fable.r: Placebo response in functional dyspepsia is high and variable, and a herbal formula with a 10-point true gain would miss significance about half the time.

opus.r: Placebo response in functional dyspepsia is high (often 30-40%), so an herbal granule with a modest true effect may not separate at 171 per arm.

sonnet.r: Functional dyspepsia placebo response is high and the stringent weekly 50% reduction in two symptoms may narrow the gap, but Chinese TCM phase 3 trials with 171 per arm usually report a positive primary.

haiku.r: Placebo response in functional dyspepsia is high, and a responder endpoint needing response in more than half of the weeks is sensitive to it; the trial was still recruiting past its registered completion date.

carbon.r: Rome IV postprandial distress syndrome trials exhibit substantial and variable placebo response rates (often 30% to 40% over 8 weeks), which can compress the treatment difference on subjective diary symptom responder endpoints.

sol.r: A substantial placebo response in symptom diaries could erase a modest herbal-treatment effect despite the moderately sized phase 3 sample.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of VGR-R01 Gene Therapy in Patients With Bietti Crystalline Dystrophy
trials.c: Bietti Crystalline Dystrophy; Inherited Retinal Diseases
trials.ep: Proportion of subjects with a BCVA change from baseline in the study eye by ETDRS at week 52 (response threshold not specified)

fable.r: Only 30 treated and 15 untreated patients; a responder rate under about 30% in treated eyes, or one or two control responders, would leave the comparison non-significant.

opus.r: With only 15 untreated controls and an undefined BCVA response threshold, a modest gene-therapy gain in visual acuity could miss significance even if real.

sonnet.r: The responder threshold is not defined in the record; with an untreated control that declines slowly, a gene therapy effect is likely to be large, but a strict threshold or n=45 could dilute it.

haiku.r: With 30 treated eyes against 15 untreated controls and an unstated responder threshold, the comparison is small and the choice of threshold can swing the result either way.

carbon.r: Achieving a binary ETDRS visual acuity responder threshold at 52 weeks in a degenerative RPE dystrophy like Bietti crystalline dystrophy is challenging with only 30 treated and 15 untreated control patients.

sol.r: Gene replacement may preserve surviving retina without producing a sufficiently large one-year BCVA improvement in patients with advanced, heterogeneous photoreceptor loss.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of Upadacitinib in Combination With Topical Corticosteroids in Children From 2 to Less Than 12 Years of Age in Japan With Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Percentage of children achieving EASI 75 (at least 75% reduction from baseline in EASI) at week 12

fable.r: Only a high placebo response to topical corticosteroids in a small Japanese paediatric sample could erode the expected gap of about 45 points.

opus.r: Placebo plus topical corticosteroids can reach 25-35% EASI-75 in well-managed Japanese children, but even then the upadacitinib effect should remain large enough with about 50 per arm.

sonnet.r: Upadacitinib has a very large EASI 75 effect with TCS in adolescents and adults; only a small sample (about 50 per arm) or an unexpectedly strong placebo+TCS response could threaten significance.

haiku.r: Upadacitinib has a large, replicated EASI-75 effect in older patients; the main way to miss is an unusually high placebo-plus-steroid response in a small Japanese pediatric sample of about 99.

carbon.r: Diligent background topical corticosteroid use in Japanese pediatric dermatology clinics could elevate placebo EASI 75 response, though upadacitinib's large effect size makes missing significance unlikely.

sol.r: Intensive topical corticosteroid use in young children could raise placebo EASI-75 response enough to narrow an otherwise substantial upadacitinib advantage.

trials.t: Tissue Repair Gel in Venous Leg Ulcers in AU/US
trials.c: Venous Leg Ulcer; Venous Ulcer; Venous Stasis Ulcer
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with complete closure of the target venous leg ulcer at or before the Week 16 end-of-treatment visit

fable.r: Venous ulcers of 2-12 cm2 under good compression often close on standard care alone, and topical agents with promising phase 2 data (e.g. HP802-247) have repeatedly failed to beat vehicle in phase 3.

opus.r: Topical wound-healing agents added to compression rarely beat standard care in phase 3, because good compression already closes 35-50% of ulcers by week 16 and the add-on effect is small.

sonnet.r: Venous leg ulcer drug trials often fail to beat compression-based standard care; a 10-point gain is needed with 156 per arm, and standard care alone is not truly blinded.

haiku.r: A gel added to standard care has to lift complete closure at 16 weeks well above a compression-based control; small-company wound-gel trials often miss, and slow enrollment could push results past the window.

carbon.r: Topical TR987 showed modest Phase 2 complete-closure effects in venous leg ulcers, and variable healing under compression standard of care makes an 11-point superiority threshold hard to clear.

sol.r: Compression and frequent wound care may produce enough control-arm healing to erase the statistical advantage of a modest adjunctive gel effect.

trials.t: A Clinical Study of TQC2731 Injection in Patients With Moderate to Severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
trials.sp: Shanghai Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Technology Development Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Annualized rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations over the 24-week treatment period

fable.r: A 24-week trial of 258 patients yields only about 110-120 exacerbations, too few to show at two-sided 0.05 the 15-30% rate reduction that anti-TSLP has achieved in COPD (tezepelumab, COURSE).

opus.r: About 100-130 exacerbations over 24 weeks give little power for the 15-30% reduction anti-TSLP achieved in COPD; tezepelumab's COURSE missed with a 17% reduction over 52 weeks.

sonnet.r: A 24-week exacerbation endpoint with 129 per arm yields only about 50 events per arm, so a plausible 25-35% reduction from an anti-TSLP type antibody is unlikely to reach significance.

haiku.r: At 129 per arm and about 105 expected events, a rate ratio near 0.65 is only borderline significant, so a modest true effect or a high placebo event rate on triple therapy could miss.

carbon.r: Without baseline blood eosinophil enrichment, 258 patients followed for only 24 weeks accrue too few COPD exacerbations to reliably detect the modest ~15-20% overall class reduction seen with anti-TSLP therapy.

sol.r: A 24-week exacerbation study on optimized inhaled therapy may observe too few, overdispersed events to establish a modest biologic effect without clear type-2 enrichment.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of ENN0403 in Subjects With DME
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Central Retinal Thickness (CRT) at week 12

fable.r: Already completed in August 2026; a small China-only two-dose study that will most likely stay as it is on the registry without posted results.

opus.r: Small Chinese sponsor's two-dose oral phase 2 in DME is already completed; status should stay completed, and posting of results on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely without US sites.

sonnet.r: Completed two-dose phase 2 from a Chinese sponsor with a single stable primary outcome; no US registration obligation makes results posting unlikely.

haiku.r: Completed single-primary phase 2 with no control arm; the uncertainties are whether this small sponsor posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov and whether the primary is edited after completion.

carbon.r: This small China-only Phase 2 DME dose-ranging trial is already marked completed on the registry, making subsequent termination or primary outcome amendment unlikely and near-term ClinicalTrials.gov results posting uncommon.

sol.r: The study is already listed as completed, making a subsequent stop or substantive endpoint change unlikely, while results posting remains uncertain for this small China-only trial.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of AP306 at Fixed Doses in Dialysis Participants With Hyperphosphatemia
trials.c: Hyperphosphatemia; Chronic Kidney Disease Requiring Chronic Dialysis; End Stage Renal Disease on Dialysis
trials.ep: Change in serum phosphate from baseline to end of 8-week treatment (or before rescue therapy or drug interruption)

fable.r: With only about 24 patients per arm and six regimens sharing the alpha, a noisy placebo arm or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis is the main way a clearly active phosphate-lowering drug could miss.

opus.r: Only about 24 patients per arm over 8 weeks; phosphate change is noisy (SD ~1.4 mg/dL) and regression to the mean after binder washout lowers placebo too, so a real ~1 mg/dL effect can still miss significance.

sonnet.r: Only about 24 patients per arm and six doses; an unexpectedly weak gut-restricted phosphate transporter inhibitor effect or a large placebo response could leave the top dose short of significance.

haiku.r: Only 24 patients per arm, a wide spread of phosphate in dialysis, and a 7-arm design make a significant result at 125 mg TID less certain than the mechanism suggests; the drug's dose-response is the other open question.

carbon.r: Splitting 168 dialysis patients across seven arms (~24 per arm) introduces small-sample variability, multi-arm multiplicity, and potential GI-driven dropouts at higher TID doses.

sol.r: Small per-dose groups, multiplicity and variable phosphate levels could obscure a genuine dose response, especially if gastrointestinal intolerance reduces high-dose exposure.

trials.t: A Study of BGM0504 in Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes Patients Only Through Diet and Exercise
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 32.

fable.r: Efficacy failure against placebo is implausible for a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist; the residual risk is a disclosure that calls the trial positive without stating the primary endpoint result, or an unexpected conduct problem.

opus.r: Failure is very unlikely; the only plausible route is an unusually large placebo response in a Chinese monotherapy population combined with high dropout, which would shrink but almost certainly not erase a ~1.9-point HbA1c gap.

sonnet.r: A GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist against placebo in drug-naive type 2 diabetes with baseline HbA1c 7.5-11% should win by a wide margin; the only real risk is an unexpectedly weak molecule or odd handling of the analysis.

haiku.r: Around 69 patients per arm and a GLP-1-class effect of roughly 1.5 to 2 HbA1c points make superiority very likely; the open risk is a weaker-than-expected 10 mg dose response.

carbon.r: Dual GIP/GLP-1 agonism has overwhelming glycemic efficacy against placebo, leaving gastrointestinal intolerability or a brief top-line disclosure omitting formal endpoint details as the only minor risks.

sol.r: Glycemic superiority over placebo is highly likely; failure would most plausibly follow poor tolerability, differential discontinuation or an unfavorable rescue-treatment estimand.

trials.t: A Study of BGM0504 in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 32.

fable.r: Semaglutide is a potent comparator; if the protocol's primary hypothesis is superiority rather than non-inferiority, a smaller-than-expected HbA1c gap in an open-label trial is the way this could miss.

opus.r: Semaglutide 1 mg is a strong comparator (~1.8-1.9 point HbA1c drop in Chinese patients); non-inferiority is very likely, but if the trial's actual primary hypothesis is superiority, a 10 mg dose may not separate significantly.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority against semaglutide is likely if BGM0504 10 mg behaves like tirzepatide; failure would need the molecule to fall clearly short of semaglutide, which the margin of probably 0.3 points would catch.

haiku.r: Non-inferiority to an active GLP-1 comparator with an unstated margin; the risk is that 10 mg BGM0504 trails semaglutide by more than a margin of about 0.4 points, or that a superiority test misses.

carbon.r: Semaglutide produces robust ~1.6-1.8% HbA1c reductions in Chinese T2DM patients, which could narrow separation if the trial requires superiority rather than standard non-inferiority.

sol.r: Semaglutide is a potent comparator, so an unexpectedly strong control response or a superiority rather than non-inferiority requirement could defeat a modest BGM0504 advantage.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate LP352 in Children and Adults With Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies (DEE)
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in countable motor seizure frequency during the treatment period (up to 15 weeks)

fable.r: The phase 2 signal came from 52 patients with nine on placebo; in a broad LGS and other-DEE population the true effect may shrink towards fenfluramine's modest LGS benefit while placebo response rises in a 17-country trial.

opus.r: A selective 5-HT2C agonist may not reproduce fenfluramine's multi-receptor efficacy in a heterogeneous DEE population; the small, partly unblinded-feeling PACIFIC effect could shrink substantially in a 367-patient phase 3 with a sizeable placebo response.

sonnet.r: A broad mixed DEE population with LGS and other syndromes, plus an unknown dose, could dilute the large effect seen in the small phase 2; otherwise the sample is large and the mechanism clinically precedented.

haiku.r: Seizure-count endpoints in DEE carry a heavy placebo response; the main risk is a placebo-adjusted effect below about 10 points, which the 367-patient sample would not reliably detect.

carbon.r: Global 116-site caregiver seizure-diary studies across heterogeneous DEE syndromes risk elevated placebo seizure reductions and noisy baseline counts that compress treatment separation.

sol.r: The small phase 2 signal may shrink when extended to younger patients and diverse DEE syndromes, particularly with greater placebo response or titration-related withdrawals.

trials.t: A Single-Dose Study to Evaluate Safety and Efficacy of CS-1103 in Participants Receiving a Single Dose of Methamphetamine
trials.c: Methamphetamine Intoxication; Methamphetamine Disorders; Methamphetamine Abuse
trials.ep: Number of participants with CS-1103-related adverse events (AEs) assessed by physical examinations

fable.r: Single-site dose-escalation study still recruiting on its registered completion date, so it will finish late and results are unlikely to be posted before late 2027.

opus.r: A single-site NIDA-funded inpatient dose-escalation study that is still recruiting past its registered completion date; it will most likely simply run late, with dates pushed out rather than results posted by August 2027.

sonnet.r: Single-site, 40-participant phase 2 single-dose safety/PK study with safety primaries; still recruiting at its registered primary completion date, so dates likely slip, results are unlikely to be posted soon, and the vague primary outcomes could be tidied.

haiku.r: Single-site, 40-person phase 2 safety study whose primary completion date had already passed at launch while the record still said recruiting; it most likely finishes and reports, and record lag is the main operational uncertainty.

carbon.r: Still recruiting on its registered October 2026 primary completion date, this single-site NIDA inpatient IV methamphetamine challenge study will likely finish in 2027 with low chance of posting results before August 2027.

sol.r: The short single-site design should finish, although screening medically suitable methamphetamine users can delay enrollment and registry results posting may lag completion.

trials.t: Ascending Doses of Crofelemer Powder for Oral Solution in Pediatric Microvillus Inclusion Disease (MVID)
trials.c: Microvillus Inclusion Disease; Congenital Disorders; Rare Diseases
trials.ep: Safety and Tolerability

fable.r: Six-patient crossover study with enrolment closed should finish close to schedule, with the sponsor's finances the main threat and results posting unlikely before late 2027.

opus.r: An ultra-rare pediatric crossover study with 32 weeks of blinded dose escalation; with only 6 patients the timeline depends on a few individuals, and the small sponsor updates the record irregularly, so slippage past March 2027 is plausible.

sonnet.r: Six-patient ultra-rare pediatric study with safety primaries, run by a small cash-constrained sponsor; recruitment is closed but follow-up and the extension phase may push the registry date, and results posting within the window is unlikely.

haiku.r: Six-patient rare-disease study with a 32-week double-blind period and an optional 48-week extension; the registered December 2026 completion is likely to slip, so lateness is the main operational risk.

carbon.r: With all ~6 ultra-rare pediatric MVID participants already enrolled by October 2026, the 32-week crossover period should mostly finish near schedule, though clinical fragility could cause minor delays.

sol.r: A closed six-patient cohort is likely to finish, but medically fragile children, long crossover and extension follow-up, and small-sponsor resources can push completion beyond the current date.

trials.t: A Study to Test Whether BI 771716 Helps People With an Advanced Form of Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) Called Geographic Atrophy
trials.ep: Annual growth rate (slope) of square-root-transformed geographic atrophy area on fundus autofluorescence in the study eye, baseline to Week 56

fable.r: The comparator is an approved, active drug: beating pegcetacoplan on lesion growth with about 67 eyes per arm would need a far larger effect than any geographic atrophy therapy has shown.

opus.r: Beating an active complement inhibitor that already slows GA growth ~20% would need a further large effect; with ~67 eyes per arm over 56 weeks, superiority over pegcetacoplan is very hard even for an active drug.

sonnet.r: Pegcetacoplan already slows GA growth by about 20%; with about 67 per arm, a new complement inhibitor would need to be clearly better than it to reach significance on a 56-week slope.

haiku.r: Superiority over an approved active comparator with about 67 patients per arm needs a clear edge in GA growth; the main risk is that BI 771716 is only about as good as pegcetacoplan.

carbon.r: Beating FDA-approved pegcetacoplan—which already slows geographic atrophy growth by ~18-22%—with only ~67 patients per arm requires roughly a 40% total lesion-growth reduction rarely achieved in GA.

sol.r: The active complement-inhibitor control already slows lesion growth, so this small phase 2 trial may not establish an additional anatomical benefit, let alone improve vision.

trials.t: Study of Novel Treatment Combination Therapies in Participants With Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Regardless of PD-L1 Expression Status; Substudy-01
trials.c: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
trials.ep: Objective response rate (complete or partial response, RECIST v1.1, investigator-assessed), assessed up to 36 months

fable.r: Only 39 patients were enrolled (about 20 per arm), so neither ORR nor PFS can reach significance, and anti-TIGIT antibodies including domvanalimab have added little to PD-1 blockade in randomized trials.

opus.r: With about 20 patients per arm, significance on both ORR and PFS is nearly impossible, and anti-TIGIT add-on effects to PD-1 plus chemotherapy have repeatedly failed in phase 3, so the experimental arm is unlikely to separate at all.

sonnet.r: Anti-TIGIT add-ons have failed to beat anti-PD-1 alone repeatedly (including gastric STAR-221); with 39 patients and two co-primaries that both must favour domvanalimab, a clear win is very unlikely.

haiku.r: With 39 patients and two co-primary outcomes (ORR and PFS) that must both favour the four-drug arm, significance needs a large gap in a very small sample; the anti-TIGIT class has also had weak phase 3 results.

carbon.r: With only 39 enrolled patients split across two arms and co-primary endpoints of ORR and PFS, the substudy lacks statistical power to demonstrate formal superiority for adding anti-TIGIT domvanalimab.

sol.r: With only 39 patients, a modest incremental TIGIT benefit is unlikely to establish superiority on both ORR and PFS against an active PD-1 plus chemotherapy control.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Study of CAL101 in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in forced vital capacity (FVC) at week 28

fable.r: S100A4 neutralization has no clinical proof of concept in IPF, and most novel mechanisms fail to slow FVC decline in 150-patient, 28-week trials, especially on top of background antifibrotics.

opus.r: A first-in-class anti-S100A8/A9 antibody in IPF has no clinical proof of mechanism; most novel IPF mechanisms fail in phase 2, and with background antifibrotics shrinking placebo decline, a 28-week trial of 150 patients needs a ~60 mL effect.

sonnet.r: Most novel-mechanism IPF phase 2 trials with about 75 patients per arm fail to show a significant FVC benefit at 28 weeks; the monthly IV antibody effect size is unknown and FVC is a noisy endpoint.

haiku.r: A significant gain over placebo needs roughly 45 to 50 mL in FVC at 28 weeks against a noisy measure, which few novel IPF mechanisms show at phase 2; the main risk is a real benefit that is smaller than that.

carbon.r: Novel antifibrotic mechanisms like S100A4 neutralization lack prior clinical proof-of-concept in IPF, where most Phase 2 candidates fail to slow FVC decline on top of standard antifibrotics.

sol.r: Novel S100A4 inhibition may not produce enough additional antifibrotic activity to separate from placebo on noisy 28-week FVC measurements.

trials.t: A Study on the Immune Response and Safety of an Investigational Chickenpox Vaccine When Given to Healthy Children 12 to 15 Months of Age
trials.ep: Anti-VZV gE IgG seroresponse and geometric mean concentration at day 43: consistency of three lots, and the pooled lots against Varivax

fable.r: Four co-primary immunogenicity objectives must all succeed; variation in potency between live-virus lots, or a lower rate of reaching the 300 mIU/mL seroresponse threshold than Varivax, is the main way to miss.

opus.r: All objectives must succeed: three-lot GMC consistency plus seroresponse and GMC non-inferiority against Varivax; a live attenuated vaccine with somewhat lower gE antibody response than Varivax could miss one GMC margin.

sonnet.r: All four primary immunogenicity criteria (three-lot consistency and non-inferiority to Varivax on seroresponse and GMC) must pass; the likeliest miss is a GMC ratio against Varivax or one lot pair falling outside the margin.

haiku.r: Equivalence on three lot ratios and on seroresponse against Varivax is likely with near-ceiling seroresponse; the main risk is one lot-to-lot ratio falling outside the protocol margin.

carbon.r: Meeting four simultaneous co-primary immunogenicity criteria across three vaccine lots and against Varivax creates multiplicity risk if GMC ratios or seroresponse margins drift slightly.

sol.r: Residual manufacturing-lot or assay variability could push one required comparison outside its protocol margin despite similar overall immune responses.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of a New Formulation of Cabotegravir Long-Acting Administered Intramuscularly in a 4-month Dosing Interval (Q4M)
trials.ep: CAB trough concentrations for target of 1.05 microgram per milliliter (μg/mL) for men and 1.39 μg/mL for women

fable.r: Fully enrolled PK study of a registrational four-monthly cabotegravir formulation that has passed primary completion; stopping is unlikely, and GSK/ViiV usually post results near the 12-month deadline, which falls just after the read date.

opus.r: Single-arm PK bridging study of the registrational Q4M cabotegravir formulation; ViiV runs such studies to completion and usually posts close to the 12-month deadline, which falls just after the read date.

sonnet.r: Single-arm ViiV PK study, already past registered primary completion and active not recruiting. Primary window runs to Month 25, so the date may be revised; ViiV usually posts results only near the 12-month deadline and a stop is unlikely.

haiku.r: Already active and not recruiting Phase 2 PK study, so the realistic risks are a late results posting and a reworded PK primary rather than a failure to run.

carbon.r: With recruitment finished and primary completion registered for September 2026, this ongoing ViiV Phase 2b PK study should remain active into follow-up and post primary results near the 1-year FDAAA deadline.

sol.r: Completed recruitment and established cabotegravir safety favor continued PK follow-up, while the long extension makes early registry posting less certain.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Empasiprubart Versus IVIg in Adults With Multifocal Motor Neuropathy
trials.ep: Change from baseline in grip strength (4-week average) in the most affected hand at week 24

fable.r: The comparator is IVIg in patients selected as IVIg responders on stable maintenance, so empasiprubart must beat an effective active treatment on grip strength rather than a placebo.

opus.r: Superiority against active IVIg maintenance in IVIg-responsive patients is a high bar; with 77 per arm the trial needs empasiprubart to improve grip strength clearly beyond the IVIg-maintained baseline, not just preserve it.

sonnet.r: Patients are already stable on optimised maintenance IVIg, so beating it on grip strength is hard; the likely outcome is comparable efficacy rather than clear superiority.

haiku.r: IVIg is a proven maintenance therapy in MMN, so beating it on grip strength is the hard part, and 77 patients per arm limits power for a modest effect.

carbon.r: Control patients remain on an already effective maintenance IVIg regimen, leaving limited room for empasiprubart to show superior grip strength if superiority rather than non-inferiority is required.

sol.r: Patients are selected for established IVIg responsiveness, so maintaining effective IVIg is a much harder comparator than withdrawing it or giving placebo.

trials.t: A Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate HLX43 in Patients With Locally Advanced or Metastatic HCC Failed or Intolerance to Standard Therapy
trials.ep: ORR

fable.r: Open-label three-dose randomized phase 2 from a Chinese sponsor; likely to finish enrolment late but run to completion, with results reported at congresses and not on ClinicalTrials.gov.

opus.r: Open-label single-site Chinese dose-optimisation study of a priority ADC; likely to keep running past its stale completion date, with little chance of CT.gov posting.

sonnet.r: Single-site Chinese open-label phase 2 dose-exploration trial from Henlius, with descriptive ORR and PFS primaries. Henlius rarely posts phase 2 results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and the trial is still recruiting, so the dates will probably slip. A stop is unlikely, though HCC could be deprioritised behind other HLX43 indications.

haiku.r: Single-site Chinese dose-finding study still recruiting past its registered completion date, so the risks are slippage, a stop, or no posting on ClinicalTrials.gov.

carbon.r: Still recruiting at its October 2026 registered primary completion date, this China-only Phase 2 ADC dose-exploration study is unlikely to post tabular results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027.

sol.r: Dose optimization is likely to continue, but recruitment near the projected completion date and longer PFS follow-up make prompt structured registry results unlikely.

trials.t: A Dose Finding Study With an Anti-TSLP Antibody (GSK5784283) in Adults Aged 18 to 75 Years of Age With Uncontrolled Asthma
trials.ep: Part A: change from baseline in fraction of exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) at Week 26

fable.r: TSLP blockade reliably lowers FeNO, so the main risk is the endpoint: a week 26 reading at the end of a long dosing interval may have waned, or the first public statement may not address the primary endpoint.

opus.r: Anti-TSLP reliably lowers FeNO, so the main risk is that the first public statement is a pipeline note calling the data positive without a formal primary-endpoint result, or that the posted analysis lacks a significance test.

sonnet.r: TSLP blockade reliably lowers FeNO, so the biomarker primary should be met. The main risk is that disclosure is only called positive without a statement on the primary endpoint, or that the model-based dose analysis is reported differently.

haiku.r: The highest dose arm is a fraction of a multi-arm dose-finding design, so a modest placebo-adjusted FeNO fall could miss significance.

carbon.r: If Part A results are only summarized qualitatively in pipeline updates before full study completion in September 2027, a primary readout could fall short of formal reporting criteria.

sol.r: Insufficient sustained exposure through week 26 could weaken late FeNO suppression despite a validated target and stronger effects at earlier visits.

trials.t: Randomised Clinical Trial to Investigate Efficacy and Safety of Benralizumab 30 mg SC as an add-on Therapy in Uncontrolled Eosinophilic Asthma Patients Treated With Medium-dose ICS-LABA Compared to Conventional Escalation to High-dose ICS-LABA Treatment
trials.ep: Annualized rate of asthma exacerbations from baseline through Week 48

fable.r: With 130 patients and roughly 85 exacerbations, the trial has about 50% power for a 40% rate reduction, and escalation to high-dose ICS-LABA gives the control arm some benefit of its own.

opus.r: With 130 patients over 48 weeks only about 80-90 exacerbations are expected; a realistic rate ratio near 0.6 against an active high-dose ICS comparator gives well under 60% power for a negative-binomial test.

sonnet.r: Only 65 patients per arm against an active control (step-up to high-dose ICS-LABA) with an eosinophil floor of 150, so a plausible rate ratio of about 0.65 gives only modest power.

haiku.r: Escalating to high-dose ICS-LABA is a strong comparator, and 65 patients per arm limits power for a rate ratio around 0.6 to 0.7.

carbon.r: Completing with only 130 patients across 86 sites leaves the trial modestly powered (~45-50%) to detect exacerbation rate superiority against active escalation to high-dose ICS-LABA, especially including patients with eosinophils 150-299 cells/uL.

sol.r: Benralizumab is active, but 130 patients may generate too few exacerbations after adherence improves and the control arm escalates to high-dose ICS-LABA.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy, and Safety of QL2107 Plus Chemo and Compare With Keytruda in Participants With IV nqNSCLC
trials.ep: Objective response rate within 24 weeks by independent review (RECIST 1.1)

fable.r: Equivalence on 24-week ORR with 808 patients is well powered; a miss would most likely come from a chance imbalance in response rates or assessment noise near the margin.

opus.r: Biosimilar equivalence on ORR with about 400 per arm is usually well powered; failure would come from chance imbalance or a real quality difference shifting the ratio outside the margin.

sonnet.r: Large 808-patient biosimilar equivalence trial with ORR around 50 percent is well powered for usual margins. The main risk is a chance miss of the ORR margin or a stricter protocol margin, and results are also unlikely to be public by mid-2027.

haiku.r: A pembrolizumab biosimilar ORR equivalence study with 808 patients is usually designed to pass, so the main risks are delay in an ongoing single-site study and a late public statement.

carbon.r: With 808 randomized patients, true biosimilar equivalence failure is rare, leaving chance IRC response imbalance or incomplete primary-endpoint phrasing in initial disclosures as the main risks.

sol.r: The main residual risk is a biosimilar comparability problem or chance ORR imbalance crossing the undisclosed equivalence margins, rather than failure of pembrolizumab activity.

trials.t: A Trial of Setmelanotide in Patients With Congenital Hypothalamic Obesity (Sub-study of NCT05774756)
trials.c: Hypothalamic Obesity; Multiple Pituitary Hormone Deficiency Genetic Form; Septo-Optic Dysplasia
trials.ep: Mean percent change from baseline in BMI after 26 weeks on a therapeutic regimen

fable.r: Congenital hypothalamic obesity is aetiologically mixed, and some patients' weight gain may not be driven by impaired MC4R-pathway signalling, which would dilute the large effect seen in acquired disease in a 39-patient trial.

opus.r: Congenital hypothalamic obesity (SOD, ONH, PSIS) is a different mechanism from acquired injury; if the MC4R pathway deficit is less central, setmelanotide's effect could be smaller than in TRANSCEND, and 39 patients leave little room.

sonnet.r: Congenital hypothalamic obesity may respond less than acquired hypothalamic obesity, and with 39 patients including growing children an attenuated effect or high variance could miss significance.

haiku.r: This 39-patient sub-study has a large expected BMI effect, so its main risk is sample size and timing rather than the drug.

carbon.r: Congenital hypothalamic-pituitary malformations are genetically and anatomically more heterogeneous than surgical hypothalamic injury, which could dilute mean BMI response if non-melanocortin defects are enrolled.

sol.r: Congenital hypothalamic and pituitary disorders are heterogeneous; some patients may lack the preserved MC4R circuitry needed to reproduce the acquired-obesity response.

trials.t: A Pivotal Phase II Clinical Trial of Utidelone Injection Plus Capecitabine in HER2-negative Breast Cancer Patients With Brain Metastases
trials.c: HER2-negative Breast Cancer Patients With Brain Metastases
trials.ep: Intracranial Objective Response Rate (IC-ORR) evaluated by investigator according to RECIST 1.1 criteria.

fable.r: A 120-patient US trial in HER2-negative breast cancer with measurable brain metastases, run by a small sponsor at 12 sites and still recruiting three months before its registered January 2027 primary completion with a 12-month response window, will very likely slip well past the 90-day margin.

opus.r: Small US single-arm two-stage study by a small sponsor, still recruiting 120 brain-metastasis patients at 12 sites in late 2026; very likely to run past its January 2027 primary completion date.

sonnet.r: Small biotech single-arm two-stage pivotal phase 2 enrolling 120 brain-metastases patients at 12 US sites, with a 12-month IC-ORR window. The registered completion of January 2027 looks unrealistic, so the date will probably slip. Some risk of sponsor stop or primary tweaks after the stage 1 review.

haiku.r: A single-arm US pivotal Phase 2 still recruiting past its January 2027 primary completion date, so the realistic risks are delay and a stop, not failure to run.

carbon.r: Because the trial was still recruiting 120 US brain-metastasis patients in late October 2026 with a 12-month primary endpoint, primary completion will almost certainly slip past April 2027.

sol.r: Recruiting 120 patients with measurable brain metastases across a small US network makes the January 2027 primary completion target ambitious, particularly with staged enrollment.

trials.t: AK112 or Placebo Plus Nab-Paclitaxel as First-line Treatment in Inoperable Locally Advanced/ Metastatic Triple-negative Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival assessed by independent radiologic review committee, up to about 2 years

fable.r: PFS should be won comfortably given VEGF plus PD-1 blockade on a taxane, so the likeliest route to a not-met label is the second primary outcome, overall survival, being immature or unproven when PFS is reported.

opus.r: PFS benefit is likely, but OS is a second primary endpoint that will be immature by mid-2027; under the co-primary rule a PFS-only announcement may not count as meeting all primary outcomes.

sonnet.r: PFS is very likely positive, but OS is a co-primary and will be immature at the PFS analysis, so the sponsor may not be able to say all primary objectives were met by the deadline.

haiku.r: The co-primary overall survival must also be significant and reported by June 2027, which is unlikely even if PFS works.

carbon.r: Although ivonescimab plus nab-paclitaxel has a high likelihood of significantly prolonging PFS, overall survival is listed as a second primary outcome and will likely remain immature at initial PFS readout.

sol.r: PFS is likely to improve, but both registered primaries must succeed under the round's rules, and OS may be immature or insufficiently separated at the first readout.

trials.t: A Study to Test Different Doses of BI 1584862 in People With a Distinct Form of Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) Called Geographic Atrophy
trials.ep: Slope of growth in square-root-transformed geographic atrophy area on fundus autofluorescence over up to 50 weeks in the study eye

fable.r: A new mechanism tested with about 37 patients per arm can reach significance only with a growth reduction of roughly 25-30%, which is larger than the approved complement inhibitors achieve.

opus.r: Novel GA mechanisms mostly fail in phase 2, and even approved complement inhibitors slow square-root growth by only about 0.05 mm/yr, which about 37 patients per arm over 50 weeks cannot reliably detect.

sonnet.r: Geographic atrophy phase 2 programmes have a poor hit rate, particularly for novel mechanisms, and about 38 patients per dose group over 50 weeks gives limited power unless the effect is 20 to 25 percent or more.

haiku.r: A Phase 2 dose-finding study with about 37 to 38 per arm, so a modest slowing of GA growth at the highest dose may not reach significance.

carbon.r: Non-complement oral/systemic candidates in geographic atrophy have historically failed to slow lesion growth, and ~38 patients per arm requires a ~25% slope reduction to achieve statistical significance.

sol.r: Established GA therapies produce modest anatomical slowing; an unproven agent with roughly 38 patients per dose may not produce a sufficiently large, consistent effect over 50 weeks.

trials.t: A Study Evaluating NPT 2042 Versus Placebo in Subjects Aged 16-75 Years With Genetic Generalized Epilepsy (GGE) and Absence Seizures
trials.ep: Within-subject percent change in EEG absence seizure frequency from treatment-period baseline, NPT 2042 vs placebo, over crossover periods up to 12 weeks

fable.r: Fourteen crossover subjects split over two doses, with highly variable EEG seizure counts, leave little power, and the registered primary is descriptive (mean and median differences) with no stated test.

opus.r: Unvalidated new compound in a 14-subject crossover split across two doses; EEG spike-wave counts are noisy, and an exploratory study reporting mean and median differences may give no formal test of the primary.

sonnet.r: Only 14 subjects in a single-centre crossover with EEG-counted absence seizures, which vary a lot between 72-hour recordings; a real T-type-like effect could show, but chance noise is large and the higher-dose subset may be small.

haiku.r: Small single-centre crossover of 14 patients with an EEG-based primary; power is thin and the sponsor may report only in a press release or abstract.

carbon.r: With only 14 crossover participants split across two doses at a single center, substantial day-to-day variability in ambulatory EEG spike-wave burst counts limits statistical power unless the drug effect is very large.

sol.r: Only 14 crossover participants, potentially divided between two doses, leave substantial uncertainty from heterogeneous and fluctuating EEG seizure counts.

trials.t: Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of CMG190303 in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Dyslipidemia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24, dapagliflozin/rosuvastatin combination versus rosuvastatin monotherapy

fable.r: Both comparisons test well-established effects, so a miss would most likely come from an imprecise HbA1c comparison with about 80 patients per arm and a low baseline HbA1c among patients entering on dual therapy.

opus.r: Both co-primaries compare the combination against the component that lacks the active ingredient (dapagliflozin for HbA1c, rosuvastatin for LDL-C), so each should succeed; the remaining risk is execution or reporting.

sonnet.r: Add-on dapagliflozin lowers HbA1c about 0.5-0.8 points over rosuvastatin alone and rosuvastatin cuts LDL-C about 40-50% over dapagliflozin; the factorial FDC design is very likely to win both co-primaries. Residual risk is a recruitment-driven delay or no public report.

haiku.r: Well-powered add-on versus rosuvastatin; main unknowns are the fixed-dose combination dose and whether the sponsor announces by June 2027.

carbon.r: Both dapagliflozin on HbA1c and rosuvastatin on LDL-C have overwhelming statistical power (>99%), leaving incomplete primary-endpoint detail in initial Korean corporate disclosures as the main residual risk.

sol.r: Both components have well-established, complementary effects; an unexpected formulation, exposure or trial-conduct problem is more plausible than failure of their underlying pharmacology.

trials.t: A Phase 2a Multicenter Clinical Trial of TB006 in Participants With Parkinson's Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 28 in Parkinson's disease rating scale total score (assumed MDS-UPDRS) in early Parkinson's disease

fable.r: An anti-galectin-3 antibody has no demonstrated effect on Parkinson's motor scores, and 31 patients per arm over 28 weeks cannot detect anything short of a large symptomatic effect.

opus.r: An anti-galectin-3 antibody with no validated mechanism in PD, tested over only 28 weeks in 62 levodopa-treated early-PD patients, where MDS-UPDRS change is small and noisy.

sonnet.r: A 62-patient, 28-week study of an antibody in early Parkinson's on levodopa has little power for the MDS-UPDRS (SE about 2.3 points), and no disease-modifying PD drug has shown a clear symptomatic gain of that size in a trial this size.

haiku.r: Early-PD phase 2a with 31 per arm; the efficacy primary is likely underpowered, and a public statement by June 2027 is plausible after the November 2026 completion.

carbon.r: Anti-galectin-3 antibody therapy lacks strong clinical validation in levodopa-treated early Parkinson's disease, and 31 patients per arm over 28 weeks is underpowered for plausible disease-modifying effects.

sol.r: Galectin-3 targeting lacks established clinical efficacy in Parkinson's disease, and 28 weeks may reveal little benefit beyond variable placebo and levodopa-related changes.

trials.t: A Phase III Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of GZR18 Injection in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Poor Blood Glucose Control by Diet and Exercise
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 44

fable.r: A GLP-1 receptor agonist against placebo in drug-naive patients almost cannot miss on HbA1c, so the residual risk is a result reported only as positive without an explicit statement on the primary endpoint.

opus.r: A full-dose long-acting GLP-1 agonist against placebo in drug-naive T2D almost always gives a large, significant HbA1c difference; failure would need a trial-conduct or reporting problem.

sonnet.r: A potent long-acting GLP-1 agonist against placebo in drug-naive Chinese T2DM at 44 weeks should lower HbA1c by well over a point more than placebo; failure would need an unusual design or analysis problem.

haiku.r: GLP-1-class drug versus placebo in a well-powered phase 3; the main uncertainty is when the sponsor publishes the topline, not whether it wins.

carbon.r: Biweekly GLP-1 receptor agonist GZR18 produces large HbA1c reductions (~1.6-2.0%) versus placebo with near-certain statistical power, leaving non-detailed headline reporting as the main residual risk.

sol.r: A potent GLP-1 agonist should readily beat placebo on HbA1c; unexpectedly poor gastrointestinal tolerability, treatment discontinuation or missing-data handling is the principal residual risk.

trials.t: A Phase III Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of GZR18 Injection in Adult Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c (%) at week 44

fable.r: Semaglutide 1 mg already lowers HbA1c by nearly 2 points, so if the primary hypothesis is superiority rather than non-inferiority, an advantage of about 0.2 points over a strong comparator may not reach significance.

opus.r: Semaglutide 1 mg is a strong comparator (about -1.8 HbA1c points in Chinese patients); superiority needs a clear dose advantage, though the trial's own hypothesis is probably non-inferiority first, which is very likely met.

sonnet.r: The head-to-head against semaglutide most likely meets non-inferiority, but if it is strictly a superiority test the margin over semaglutide is small (about 0.2-0.3 points) and could fall short.

haiku.r: Active-controlled against semaglutide with 550 per arm; success depends on a small edge over semaglutide, and the design (superiority or non-inferiority) is unstated in the record.

carbon.r: Semaglutide achieves robust ~1.7% HbA1c reductions in Chinese T2DM patients, so meeting superiority—if required rather than standard non-inferiority—depends on higher-dose GZR18 maintaining its Phase 2 edge.

sol.r: Semaglutide is a potent comparator, so a modest glycemic advantage could miss superiority; success is substantially more likely if the protocol's objective is non-inferiority.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Effectiveness and Safety of Pacritinib in Patients With VEXAS Syndrome (PAXIS)
trials.ep: Overall response rate (partial clinical response or better at any time) during the double-blind treatment period, up to week 24

fable.r: The first public result will probably be the phase 2a part with about 26 patients per arm, where only a very large response difference reaches significance, and pacritinib has no prior controlled data in VEXAS.

opus.r: Phase 2a compares only about 26 patients per arm, and the full 2a+2b analysis is unlikely by mid-2027. A placebo arm counting response at any time during GC taper can be high, so significance is fragile.

sonnet.r: The 2a stage has only about 26 per arm, response requires a clear GC taper, and an any-time responder endpoint admits placebo responders; a genuine JAK-driven effect could still separate, but the margin for significance is thin.

haiku.r: Responder endpoint with 52 per arm and dose not stated; phase 2b is still recruiting, so the primary result is unlikely to be public before June 2027.

carbon.r: Older, frail VEXAS patients have high rates of cytopenias, infections, and gastrointestinal intolerance to pacritinib that could cause early treatment discontinuations and attenuate response rates.

sol.r: Retrospective activity of other JAK inhibitors may not translate fully to pacritinib, and transient partial responses during glucocorticoid taper could narrow the placebo-adjusted difference.

trials.t: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of TQC2938 in Patients With Moderate to Severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
trials.sp: Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Group Nanjing Shunxin Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Annualized rate of moderate-to-severe acute exacerbations of COPD over 24 weeks

fable.r: A 24-week exacerbation endpoint in 256 patients yields only about 100 events, so even a class-typical 15-25% rate reduction would not reach significance.

opus.r: With about 128 per arm, a 24-week window and around 100 exacerbations, a realistic 20-30% rate reduction is often not significant; phase 2 trials of TSLP and IL-33 biologics in COPD have missed similar endpoints.

sonnet.r: Only about 110 exacerbations are expected in 24 weeks across 256 patients, so even a 25-30% true rate reduction is detected less than a third of the time; the population is not enriched by eosinophils or type 2 markers.

haiku.r: Exacerbation-rate primary over 24 weeks with few events expected, so power is modest; the primary completes March 2027, which leaves little time for a public statement before June.

carbon.r: Anti-ST2/IL-33 biologics yield modest (~10-20%) COPD exacerbation reductions in populations including current smokers, which 256 patients followed for only 24 weeks is underpowered to detect.

sol.r: A 24-week exacerbation endpoint in 256 patients may yield too few events to distinguish a typical 20–30% biologic effect, especially without clearly established inflammatory enrichment.

trials.t: Investigating an mRNA CAR T-cell Therapy, Known as Descartes-08, as a Potential Approach to Treat Myasthenia Gravis
trials.ep: Proportion of patients who are MG-ADL responders at Month 4 (responder threshold not defined in the record)

fable.r: Phase 2b evidence rests on about 26 evaluable patients and a different scale; with 64 per arm the trial needs roughly a 17-point gap in MG-ADL responders, and placebo response after leukapheresis and six infusions could reach 45-50%.

opus.r: MG-ADL responder rates on placebo at a single time point are often 30-45%, and the phase 2b effect came from a small sample; a 64-per-arm trial needs a 20-25 point difference to reach significance.

sonnet.r: Phase 2b showed a large responder gap (about 70% vs 25%), but it was a 36-patient study and phase 3 effects shrink; with 64 per arm a placebo rate near 35% would need a gap of 20 points to be significant.

haiku.r: Responder endpoint in 64 per arm with an undefined threshold; placebo responses are high in myasthenia, so a large gap is needed for a clear positive.

carbon.r: A higher-than-expected placebo MG-ADL response rate across 34 international sites alongside typical Phase 3 effect shrinkage could erode power in a 128-patient trial.

sol.r: The small phase 2 signal may shrink in a larger blinded responder analysis, particularly if improvement on placebo and background therapy is substantial.

trials.t: Study on the Efficacy and Safety of QLM1016 in Schizophrenia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at week 6

fable.r: The record names no margin; if the sponsor's hypothesis is superiority over aripiprazole rather than non-inferiority, an active comparator with a roughly 30-point PANSS fall leaves almost no room to win.

opus.r: Aripiprazole is an effective active comparator; if the trial's hypothesis is superiority, a new 3-6 mg antipsychotic is unlikely to beat it by a significant PANSS margin, whereas a non-inferiority design (usual for Chinese registration trials) would very likely succeed.

sonnet.r: The 3-6 mg QLM1016 arm is compared with active aripiprazole; if the design is superiority over a good active comparator it likely fails, but a Chinese active-controlled trial is usually a non-inferiority design that would pass.

haiku.r: Aripiprazole is a well-established comparator, so QLM1016 must beat it on PANSS by a clear margin to reach significance with 201 per arm; a small gap is the most likely way this fails.

carbon.r: Therapeutic-dose aripiprazole oral film (10-20 mg) produces robust 6-week PANSS reductions, leaving virtually no margin if superiority is required or risking a miss if QLM1016 is slightly weaker.

sol.r: Aripiprazole should produce substantial symptom improvement; QLM1016 may not separate from it if superiority rather than non-inferiority is required.

trials.t: Trial of JMKX003142 in Participants With Rapidly Progressive Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
trials.ep: Percentage change in total kidney volume (TKV) from baseline to week 52

fable.r: Arms may be as small as 45 if two doses share the 135 patients, MRI kidney volume change is noisy over one year, and aquaretic dropouts thin the data; the V2-antagonist mechanism is inferred, not stated.

opus.r: If JMKX003142 is a vasopressin V2 antagonist (thirst and diuretic exclusions suggest an aquaretic), a tolvaptan-like TKV effect should be detectable; failure would come from insufficient potency or dose, or dilution by aquaresis-driven dropouts in a 52-week trial of ~67 per arm.
