sonnet.r: With 135 patients and a TKV percent-change SD near 8, a vasopressin V2-type effect of about 3 points gives only around 55 percent power, and MRI measurement noise adds more.

haiku.r: A 135-patient phase 2 with a fixed 52-week TKV endpoint has limited power for a modest slowing effect, and TKV variance between patients is high, so a non-significant result is the most likely failure.

carbon.r: Splitting 135 patients across multiple Phase 2 dose groups with ~7.5% SD in 52-week TKV growth and elevated aquaretic-type dropouts could limit power.

sol.r: JMKX003142 may not reproduce meaningful suppression of cyst growth at a tolerable exposure; the record supplies no drug-specific efficacy evidence.

trials.t: A Study of ONO-2020 in Patients With Agitation Associated With Alzheimer's Disease Dementia
trials.c: Agitation Associated With Alzheimer's Disease Dementia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Cohen-Mansfield Agitation Inventory (CMAI) total score at week 12

fable.r: A novel epigenetic mechanism with no prior agitation data must beat a sizeable placebo fall with only about 45 patients per arm, which needs an effect at least as large as brexpiprazole's.

opus.r: ONO-2020 is a novel non-antipsychotic mechanism with no prior agitation efficacy data; with 45 patients per arm and a substantial placebo response on CMAI in inpatients, a significant difference requires an effect larger than brexpiprazole's.

sonnet.r: A 45-per-arm phase 2a in agitation with a novel mechanism and the usual large placebo response in hospitalised patients has little power to show a CMAI difference.

haiku.r: A 45-per-arm phase 2a on a placebo-responsive agitation scale: the gap needed to show significance at week 12 is larger than the probable drug effect, so an underpowered null is the most likely outcome.

carbon.r: With only 45 hospitalized patients per arm and large inpatient placebo improvements on CMAI, the Phase 2a trial is underpowered unless ONO-2020 has an unusually large effect.

sol.r: A modest agitation effect may not separate from placebo with only about 45 patients per arm, despite inpatient stabilization and standardized observation.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Icotrokinra (JNJ-77242113) in Biologic-experienced and Biologic-naive Participants With Active Psoriatic Arthritis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving ACR20 response at Week 16

fable.r: Icotrokinra has no dedicated PsA phase 2; an oral peptide with low systemic exposure could act less in joints than in skin, though with 750 patients only a gap under about 8 points would miss.

opus.r: Icotrokinra has no published PsA phase 2; if the oral IL-23R peptide gives less joint efficacy than injectable IL-23 blockers, ACR20 separation could shrink, though 375 per arm leaves ample power even for a 10-point gap.

sonnet.r: Icotrokinra showed a 28-point ACR20 gain at week 16 in the phase 2 ANTHEM-PsA trial, and 375 per arm gives overwhelming power; the only plausible miss is a dilution from biologic-experienced patients.

haiku.r: The main risk is a high placebo ACR20 response at week 16, which would shrink the gap, though an oral IL-23 pathway drug with a strong psoriasis record should clear the bar comfortably.

carbon.r: The only plausible efficacy risk is lower oral peptide exposure in synovial tissue than skin, though massive sample size (N=750) still provides overwhelming statistical power.

sol.r: Strong skin efficacy may overstate joint efficacy, particularly after biologic failure and with the relatively low CRP entry threshold.

trials.t: A Study of TAK-360 in Adults With Idiopathic Hypersomnia
trials.ep: Number of Participants With at Least One Treatment-emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)

fable.r: Takeda's phase 2 was still recruiting a month before its registered completion, so a slip of a few months is likely; a stop is unlikely unless an orexin-class safety signal appears, and results posting before August 2027 would be early for Takeda.

opus.r: Still recruiting a month before its registered primary completion, so the 8-week dose-finding study will likely finish in early-to-mid 2027; Takeda keeps records current and posts results near the 12-month deadline.

sonnet.r: A safety-primary phase 2 dose-finding study in rare idiopathic hypersomnia that is still recruiting a month before the registered completion, so a slip beyond February 2027 is close to a coin flip; Takeda usually posts results within about a year.

haiku.r: Recruiting at launch against a November 2026 primary completion for a 96-patient dose-finding study across 29 sites, so a slip past February 2027 is about as likely as not; a stop is unlikely for a Takeda phase 2.

carbon.r: Recruiting 96 patients with rare idiopathic hypersomnia across 29 sites while still open in late October 2026 makes a >90-day slip past November 2026 primary completion likely.

sol.r: Short follow-up and a well-resourced sponsor favor completion, but rare-disease recruitment and adaptive dose cohorts could push the November target into 2027.

trials.t: A Study of SC0062 Capsule for the Treatment of IgA Nephropathy with Proteinuria
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) at week 36

fable.r: Failure would need a much smaller proteinuria effect than phase 2, for instance if the 10 mg dose is used and performs at the low end, since 360 patients give ample power for a 25% relative reduction.

opus.r: Selective endothelin-A antagonism reliably lowers proteinuria in IgAN (atrasentan about -36% vs placebo); failure would need SC0062 10 mg to be much less potent than in phase 2 or fluid-retention dropouts to dilute the effect.

sonnet.r: Endothelin A antagonists reliably cut proteinuria by 35-45 percent in IgAN, so the 36-week primary should be met in 360 patients; the main uncertainty is whether the result is announced by June 2027.

haiku.r: The main risk is a smaller proteinuria effect at 10 mg on top of maximal RAAS blockade and SGLT2 inhibition, though this drug class usually clears that bar; a late readout also leaves little time for a 2027 filing.

carbon.r: Endothelin A receptor blockade can induce fluid retention or hemodilution, though BNP gating and SC0062's high ETA selectivity make missing 36-week UPCR unlikely.

sol.r: SC0062 may add too little sustained proteinuria reduction on optimized RAAS/SGLT2 therapy, particularly if fluid retention limits dosing.

trials.t: Study on the Efficacy and Safety of HRS-7535 in Patients With Mild Decrease in Ejection Fraction/Preserved Ejection Fraction Heart Failure and Obesity
trials.c: Adults With Heart Failure, Mild Decrease in Ejection Fraction/Preserved Ejection Fraction, and Obesity
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in body weight at week 36

fable.r: Weight loss with an oral GLP-1 agonist is close to certain; the residual risk is GI intolerance and dropouts in older heart-failure patients blunting the treatment-policy estimate.

opus.r: An oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist over 36 weeks should clearly separate on weight; the main residual risk is GI-driven discontinuation and missing data diluting a treatment-policy estimate in an older HFpEF population.

sonnet.r: An oral GLP-1 agonist over 36 weeks in 225 patients should clearly beat placebo on weight; the risk is a low dose arm or limited weight loss in HFpEF, not significance.

haiku.r: The main risk is a modest weight loss at the tested dose, since oral agents often trail injectables, though a 6 point difference at week 36 is still well within reach for 113 per arm.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance or heart-rate increases from small-molecule oral GLP-1 receptor agonism in older HFpEF patients could raise treatment discontinuations and attenuate ITT weight loss.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance and HF-related treatment interruptions could dilute weight loss despite a highly responsive GLP-1-based primary endpoint.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Ruxolitinib Cream in Children and Adolescents (6 to <18 Years Old) With Moderate Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Share of patients achieving EASI75 (at least 75% improvement in EASI from baseline) at week 8 of the vehicle-controlled period

fable.r: Only an unusually high vehicle response in a small paediatric sample could erase a gap that has been about 40-50 points in every earlier ruxolitinib cream trial.

opus.r: Ruxolitinib cream has shown large EASI75 gains in every vehicle-controlled AD trial; the only plausible failure is an unusually high vehicle response in a small (~80 per arm) moderate-AD sample.

sonnet.r: Ruxolitinib cream beat vehicle by about 30 points on EASI75 in earlier TRuE-AD trials, so 80 per arm is enough; the only real risk is a high vehicle response in a moderate-AD paediatric cohort.

haiku.r: Risk is low; the main way this fails is an unusually high vehicle response in the younger children, which would shrink the gap at week 8.

carbon.r: Frequent emollient-like vehicle cream application in pediatric moderate atopic dermatitis across 93 sites could inflate vehicle EASI75 response, though expected drug separation remains very large.

sol.r: Requiring prior TCS/TCI failure may select more treatment-resistant disease than earlier ruxolitinib cream studies.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of KBP-336 in Obese Individuals with Osteoarthritis
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to day 183

fable.r: Both primaries must be met; WOMAC pain at 6 months is the weak one, since weight-loss-driven pain relief builds slowly and placebo response in knee OA trials is large.

opus.r: Both primaries must be met; weight loss is likely, but a 6-month WOMAC pain co-primary faces a large placebo response and only modest weight-mediated pain relief at that point, unlike semaglutide's 68-week STEP 9 result.

sonnet.r: The weight primary is near certain for an amylin-type agonist, but the co-primary WOMAC pain endpoint must also be met and knee OA pain trials carry large placebo responses.

haiku.r: Two co-primary outcomes must both be met; the WOMAC pain change is the weaker link, since weight loss effects on knee pain over 183 days are modest, so success hinges on both.

carbon.r: Meeting both co-primary endpoints requires statistically significant WOMAC knee pain improvement at just 26 weeks against large osteoarthritis placebo analgesia across multiple Phase 2 dose arms.

sol.r: A substantial placebo-associated improvement in WOMAC pain may prevent the same dose from meeting both co-primary endpoints, even if weight loss is clear.

trials.t: Study of the Safety and Immunogenicity of Catch-up Vaccination With a 21-valent Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine (PCV21) in Healthy Infants, Toddlers, Children, and Adolescents
trials.ep: Number of participants reporting immediate adverse events (AEs)

fable.r: Enrollment is closed and the longest follow-up ends about December 2026, so the trial should finish on time; posting within nine months of completion is unlikely for an unlicensed Sanofi vaccine.

opus.r: Enrolment is closed and the registered primary completion is close, so the trial should finish near schedule; Sanofi posts results near the 12-month deadline, which falls after the read date.

sonnet.r: A fully enrolled Sanofi vaccine safety and immunogenicity trial with a firm completion date, descriptive immunogenicity outcomes and a standard posting cadence of around a year after primary completion.

haiku.r: Active, not recruiting with a December 2026 completion; the safety-heavy primary list is likely to be tidied near close, and a slip past March 2027 is possible but not the expected path.

carbon.r: With enrollment already completed across 38 experienced sites and fixed follow-up windows, this Sanofi pediatric catch-up vaccine study is likely to finish close to its December 2026 target without substantive protocol changes.

sol.r: Enrollment is closed and follow-up is bounded, making near-schedule completion likely, but registry results may wait until the usual one-year reporting window.

trials.t: A Trial of HRS-8427 in the Treatment of Adults With Bacterial Pneumonia
trials.c: Hospital-acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP); Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pneumonia (VABP)
trials.ep: All-cause mortality rate (share of patients who died from any cause) from first dose of study drug through Day 14

fable.r: With 60 patients per arm and only a few deaths expected by day 14, the trial cannot show a mortality advantage over meropenem; the readout will most likely be descriptive.

opus.r: With 60 patients per arm and a Day-14 mortality near 10-12%, no plausible antibiotic effect could show significant superiority on mortality against meropenem; the phase 2 is likely descriptive.

sonnet.r: With about 60 patients per arm and Day-14 mortality near 12%, a superiority win over meropenem is very unlikely; any claim would rest on comparability.

haiku.r: About 60 patients per arm cannot show a significant Day-14 mortality difference unless the drug effect is very large, and phase 2 antibiotic trials rarely show that.

carbon.r: With only 60 patients per arm against active meropenem, the study cannot realistically show superiority on Day-14 mortality and may report descriptive Phase 2 results without a formal non-inferiority test.

sol.r: With only about 60 patients per arm, broadly similar antibiotic efficacy is unlikely to produce significant Day-14 mortality superiority.

trials.t: A Study of Navenibart in Participants With Hereditary Angioedema
trials.ep: Time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (attack rate) during the 6-month treatment period, Day 1 to Day 181

fable.r: The mechanism is validated and the expected effect is large, so a miss would most likely come from a conduct or analysis problem, or from exposure waning late in a six-monthly arm, rather than from lack of efficacy.

opus.r: Plasma kallikrein blockade is validated (lanadelumab, garadacimab); the only realistic risk is that the extended Q3M/Q6M dosing loses coverage late in the interval, but even a 60% reduction would be significant here.

sonnet.r: Plasma kallikrein-class prophylaxis effects in HAE are large against placebo; the main risk is an unexpectedly weak low dose arm or high placebo response, not the primary.

haiku.r: The main risk is a dose or regimen that falls short, since the phase 3 dose is not stated, although prophylactic HAE antibodies have cut attack rates by roughly 80 to 90 percent.

carbon.r: Unexpected immunogenicity, hypersensitivity, or treatment discontinuations are the main residual risks given the thoroughly validated mechanism of plasma kallikrein inhibition in hereditary angioedema.

sol.r: The main residual efficacy risk is waning protection late in an extended dosing interval rather than failure of kallikrein inhibition itself.

trials.t: Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of 4-MUST Tablets in Chronic Cholecystitis and Biliary Dyskinesia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in upper-abdominal pain/discomfort severity on 0-100 mm VAS at day 29

fable.r: Functional biliary pain responds strongly to placebo over four weeks, and with 75-100 patients per arm split across doses a true difference under about 8 mm on the VAS could miss significance.

opus.r: Functional upper-abdominal pain responds strongly to placebo over four weeks, so a modest choleretic/spasmolytic effect may not separate on VAS.

sonnet.r: Functional biliary and dyspeptic pain shows large placebo responses on VAS; a modest dose effect may not separate from placebo at 100 per arm.

haiku.r: With about 100 patients per arm and a large placebo response, a modest drug edge of about 6 mm leaves the design close to the edge of significance.

carbon.r: Substantial placebo improvement on subjective abdominal pain VAS scores over 4 weeks in functional biliary disorders could narrow between-group separation despite multiple tested doses.

sol.r: Substantial placebo improvement and regression to the mean in a mixed biliary-symptom population could erase a modest analgesic benefit.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Effectiveness of ALKS 2680 in Subjects With Idiopathic Hypersomnia
trials.ep: Change in Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score from baseline to week 8

fable.r: About 30 patients per dose arm and a sizeable placebo fall in ESS leave limited power if the placebo-adjusted effect at the top dose is nearer 2.5 than 4 points, as the narcolepsy type 2 data suggest it could be.

opus.r: Idiopathic hypersomnia patients have intact orexin signalling, so an orexin-2 agonist may give a smaller ESS benefit than in narcolepsy, and a 30-patient-per-arm design leaves little margin.

sonnet.r: Orexin-2 agonist should lower ESS at the top dose; with only about 30 patients per arm and a noisy self-rated scale the margin is not huge.

haiku.r: Idiopathic hypersomnia is heterogeneous and pitolisant missed its primary endpoint in it, so a sleepiness gain under about 2.5 points would not reach significance.

carbon.r: Because patients with idiopathic hypersomnia have normal endogenous orexin signaling, wake-promoting effects on 8-week ESS could be smaller than those seen in orexin-deficient narcolepsy type 1.

sol.r: Acute wake promotion may translate less consistently into sustained subjective benefit in heterogeneous IH than in orexin-deficient narcolepsy.

trials.t: Study to Assess Adverse Events and Change in Disease Activity When Oral ABBV-932 is Added to Antidepressant Therapies in Adult Participants With Generalized Anxiety Disorder
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAM-A) total score at week 6

fable.r: Placebo added to ongoing antidepressants typically yields 8-10 HAM-A points of improvement in six weeks, leaving little room for an adjunctive D3/D2 partial agonist whose class has repeatedly failed in GAD.

opus.r: Adjunctive GAD trials have large placebo-plus-antidepressant HAM-A responses (around 10 points in 6 weeks), which swamp modest add-on effects; many adjunct trials have failed.

sonnet.r: Adjunctive psychiatric phase 2 trials often miss on HAM-A because of high placebo response and a modest drug-placebo gap.

haiku.r: A high placebo response in adjunctive GAD trials means the drug's HAM-A advantage over placebo may be too small to show at six weeks.

carbon.r: Large, variable placebo responses across 52 US psychiatric sites commonly obscure modest adjunctive anxiolytic drug effects on 6-week HAM-A scores.

sol.r: A large adjunctive-treatment placebo response could overwhelm a modest drug effect across numerous U.S. sites.

trials.t: Phase 3 Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of AR882 in Gout Patients (AR882-301)
trials.ep: Share of patients with serum urate below 6 mg/dL at Month 6

fable.r: Efficacy risk is negligible for a potent URAT1 inhibitor on a urate threshold endpoint; a miss would need a conduct or data problem, or very heavy dropout counted as non-response.

opus.r: A potent URAT1 inhibitor against placebo cannot plausibly miss on serum urate; the only risk is heavy dropout from gout flares counted as non-response, which would shrink but not erase the difference.

sonnet.r: A potent URAT1 inhibitor against placebo on serum urate below 6 mg/dL is near-certain to win; the only uncertainty is the size of the gap.

haiku.r: Failure needs both doses to miss a very large urate effect, so the residual risk is trial-level noise at month six or a measurement problem.

carbon.r: Only unexpected renal safety signals or extreme treatment discontinuations could threaten Month-6 serum urate superiority given potent URAT1 inhibition against a near-zero placebo response.

sol.r: Strong urate lowering should readily beat placebo; unexpectedly high discontinuation or renal tolerability problems are the main threats.

trials.t: Comparative PK, PD, Efficacy, and Safety Assessment of the Proposed Ocrelizumab Biosimilar CYB704 and Ocrevus in Participants With Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis
trials.ep: Ocrelizumab AUC (weeks 1 to 3 and weeks 3 to 25)

fable.r: A miss would come from a real exposure difference between CYB704 and one of the two reference products, or from high between-patient PK variability in a parallel-group patient study with several AUC comparisons.

opus.r: Three-arm PK similarity with about 60 patients per arm across two AUC intervals; higher-than-expected between-patient variability or a small manufacturing difference could push a 90% CI outside the margin.

sonnet.r: Biosimilar PK equivalence in patients usually succeeds; risk is AUC variability and the need to hit margins versus both EU and US reference.

haiku.r: Failure would come from an AUC ratio outside the protocol margins in one of the two windows, a problem rare in well-matched biosimilar programs.

carbon.r: Demonstrating simultaneous pharmacokinetic bioequivalence across two AUC windows against both US- and EU-sourced Ocrevus in 183 MS patients carries modest multiplicity and inter-patient variability risk.

sol.r: Unexpected PK variability or a small systematic exposure difference could prevent all required product and interval comparisons from meeting equivalence margins.

trials.t: A Study in Adult Participants With EoE to Evaluate Vonoprazan 20 mg Compared to Placebo After 12 Weeks and to Evaluate Vonoprazan 20 mg Up to 24 Weeks
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with peak esophageal intraepithelial eosinophil count below 15 eos/hpf at Week 12

fable.r: If most enrolled patients are prior PPI non-responders, vonoprazan's histologic response could fall to 15-20%, too little to separate from placebo with 47 patients per arm.

opus.r: If enrolled patients were largely prior PPI non-responders, acid suppression with vonoprazan may induce histologic remission in few of them, shrinking the gap to placebo.

sonnet.r: Histologic response to acid suppression in EoE is about 40-50% against single-digit placebo, so only a weak P-CAB effect would sink it.

haiku.r: Vonoprazan may not lift histologic response as far as PPIs do in EoE, and a response gap under about 25 points would fail the test in a 95-patient trial.

carbon.r: Inclusion of adult EoE participants with prior proton-pump inhibitor non-response could limit histologic remission rates achievable through potassium-competitive acid blockade.

sol.r: If most participants already have acid-suppression-refractory EoE, stronger acid control may yield too few histologic responders.

trials.t: HS-20089 for Injection in Patients With Platinum-Resistant Recurrent Epithelial Ovarian Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review committee per RECIST 1.1

fable.r: In an unselected platinum-resistant population B7-H4 expression varies, and if responses are short-lived the PFS gain over chemotherapy could be too small; the open-label design also adds censoring noise in the BIRC assessment.

opus.r: B7-H4 is not used to select patients, so if responses concentrate in high expressers the unselected PFS benefit could fall short, though chemotherapy controls in platinum-resistant disease are weak.

sonnet.r: A Topo1-payload ADC against single-agent chemo in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer is likely to win on PFS; the real uncertainty is whether any result is public by mid-2027.

haiku.r: The main risk is a progression-or-death hazard ratio near 0.8 or higher, which would leave the 468-patient trial short of significance.

carbon.r: Enrolling platinum-resistant ovarian cancer patients without prospective B7-H4 expression selection could dilute the progression-free survival benefit of HS-20089 against weekly paclitaxel and other chemotherapies.

sol.r: Early ADC response signals may overstate benefit in an unselected phase 3 population, particularly if toxicity reduces sustained exposure.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety Study of Ixoberogene Soroparvovec (Ixo-vec) in Participants With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
trials.c: Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD); Wet AMD
trials.ep: Mean change from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity (ETDRS letters), averaged over Weeks 52 and 56

fable.r: Non-inferiority fails if Ixo-vec eyes lose a few letters versus fixed q8w aflibercept, from waning expression, delayed rescue, or inflammation and steroid-related cataract, pushing the confidence bound past the margin with only about 155 patients per arm.

opus.r: A single Ixo-vec dose plus as-needed aflibercept may trail fixed q8w aflibercept by one to two letters, especially in treatment-naive eyes, and with about 155 per arm the lower confidence bound can cross an unstated margin of roughly 4 to 5 letters.

sonnet.r: A single Ixo-vec injection must stay within the non-inferiority margin of aflibercept on BCVA; phase 2 LUNA supports this, but the margin is unstated and the gene therapy could fall slightly short.

haiku.r: Gene-therapy expression may fall short of the aflibercept gain across a mixed population, and rescue injections could blur the mean. Timing risk is modest; a public statement is likely around Q2 2027.

carbon.r: Intraocular inflammation or delayed transgene expression after single-dose intravitreal AAV.7m8 gene therapy could lower mean BCVA enough to miss the non-inferiority margin against regular aflibercept.

sol.r: Variable transgene expression and delayed rescue could cost several BCVA letters versus regularly dosed aflibercept, eroding the non-inferiority margin.

trials.t: A Study to Identify an Optimal Dose of QCZ484 in Mild to Moderate Hypertensive Patients
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Month 3 in mean 24-hour systolic blood pressure measured by ambulatory blood pressure monitoring

fable.r: AGT silencing should lower 24-h SBP by 10 mmHg or more versus saline, so the main way to miss is disclosure: Novartis may only flag a positive phase 2 readout in a pipeline update without stating the primary endpoint before a congress presentation.

opus.r: Only failure path is QCZ484 knocking down angiotensinogen less than zilebesiran or the highest-dose arm being small enough that a modest drop in 24-hour ABPM misses significance.

sonnet.r: Highest dose of a six-monthly RAAS-pathway agent versus saline should clearly lower 24-hour SBP; failure would need an unexpectedly weak molecule or high placebo response.

haiku.r: The highest dose must lower 24-hour SBP clearly below placebo in a dose-finding trial with one top dose. The class effect is plausible, but ABPM noise and a single-dose ceiling leave real risk.

carbon.r: Subcutaneous QCZ484 given every 6 months could exhibit weaker or less durable pharmacodynamic knockdown and blood pressure lowering at Month 3 than competing long-acting antihypertensives.

sol.r: QCZ484-specific potency is not established in the record; inadequate sustained target suppression could leave a smaller-than-expected month-3 ambulatory BP reduction.

trials.t: Evaluation of Maridebart Cafraglutide in Adult Participants Without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Have Obesity or Are Overweight
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 72

fable.r: Failure is very unlikely; the residual risk is GI intolerance and dropouts shrinking the treatment-policy estimate, not loss of superiority over placebo at week 72.

opus.r: Superiority over placebo is near certain with about 1,900 per arm; the only realistic threat is GI-driven discontinuation diluting the treatment-policy estimate, which affects the size of the effect, not significance.

sonnet.r: Efficacy failure is very unlikely given phase 2 weight loss of 16-20 percent at 52 weeks; the only real risk is tolerability-driven dropout shrinking the treatment-regimen effect.

haiku.r: Superiority on percent weight loss is near-certain if the trial reads out. The open issues are when the sponsor makes the public statement and whether it files by year end.

carbon.r: High gastrointestinal adverse event rates or an unexpected safety signal could attenuate treatment-regimen weight loss or cause regulatory delay, though missing statistical superiority is extremely unlikely.

sol.r: The expected weight effect is far larger than the statistical threshold; unexpectedly poor gastrointestinal tolerability or a major safety signal is the credible route to failure.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Maridebart Cafraglutide in Adult Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Have Obesity or Are Overweight
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 72 in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight

fable.r: Failure is very unlikely; the residual risk is GI intolerance and dropouts shrinking the treatment-policy estimate in people with diabetes, not loss of superiority over placebo at week 72.

opus.r: With about 550 per arm, superiority on weight is near certain; GI-related discontinuation could shrink the treatment-policy effect but not remove significance.

sonnet.r: Weight loss in type 2 diabetes is smaller than without diabetes but still large; success is near certain and the uncertainty is the size of the placebo-adjusted effect.

haiku.r: Superiority on percent weight loss in adults with type 2 diabetes is very likely when reported. The main uncertainty is whether the sponsor announces this trial separately before June 2027 or bundles it with MARITIME-1.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal tolerability issues during dose escalation could elevate treatment discontinuation, although statistical superiority over placebo in N=1,105 is near-certain.

sol.r: Diabetes attenuates expected weight loss but should not threaten superiority; tolerability-related discontinuation or an unexpected safety issue is the larger residual risk.

trials.t: A Study of AL2846 Capsule Versus Placebo in the Treatment of Advanced Radioiodine-Refractory Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma
trials.sp: Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Progression-free survival assessed by independent review committee (progression or death), from randomization over up to 34 months

fable.r: The risk is that AL2846 has weaker anti-angiogenic activity than cabozantinib after prior VEGFR TKIs, or that a small 144-patient trial with crossover and early censoring gives an imprecise hazard ratio; a readout by mid-2027 is itself unlikely as the trial is still recruiting.

opus.r: Placebo PFS after VEGFR TKI failure is about 2 months, so any active multikinase/MET inhibitor should separate; failure needs AL2846 to have little activity in TKI-refractory disease.

sonnet.r: Placebo-controlled trial after VEGFR TKI failure, where placebo PFS is very short and TKI effects are large; failure would come only from a small sample or atypical control performance.

haiku.r: A 144-patient trial in a refractory population with a short placebo PFS. A hazard ratio near 0.5 would clear significance, but slow enrolment pushes the readout and any public statement late.

carbon.r: Cross-resistance after prior VEGFR TKI therapy such as anlotinib or lenvatinib could attenuate AL2846's progression-free survival benefit compared with historical cabozantinib benchmarks.

sol.r: The key uncertainty is whether AL2846 retains enough activity after VEGFR-TKI progression; cross-resistance could turn a large expected PFS advantage into an underpowered modest effect.

trials.t: A Study of IBI362 in Subjects With HFpEF or HFmrEF Combined With Obesity
trials.c: Obesity; Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFPEF); Heart Failure With Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 36 in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS)

fable.r: With about 47 patients per arm, a true KCCQ-CSS gain of 5 to 7 points (SD near 19) is significant less than half the time, and both primaries (KCCQ-CSS and weight) must be met by the same dose.

opus.r: With about 47 per arm and KCCQ-CSS change SD near 17-19, a true 7-point gain gives only about 50% power per dose; weight is sure to be met, so the KCCQ co-primary decides.

sonnet.r: Weight co-primary is near certain, but the KCCQ-CSS co-primary with about 47 per arm and SD near 18 points has only about even odds of significance despite a plausible 6-8 point benefit.

haiku.r: Two co-primary endpoints with about 47 patients per arm: the KCCQ-CSS gain must be significant as well as the weight loss. The power is thin for a KCCQ effect of roughly 6 points.

carbon.r: With only about 47 participants per arm and high patient-to-patient variability in KCCQ-CSS scores, a true 7-to-8-point symptom improvement could miss statistical significance alongside the co-primary weight endpoint.

sol.r: Weight loss should be clear, but only 47 patients per arm and a variable KCCQ response make the symptom co-primary the likely bottleneck.

trials.t: Efficacy Anda Safety of Etoricoxib With Betamethasone for the Treatment of Acute Gout Arthritis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in affected-joint pain on a 4-point Likert scale at day 8 (also assessed days 2 and 5)

fable.r: Etoricoxib alone resolves most gout flare pain within days, leaving little room for added betamethasone to show a significant difference in 72 patients, especially by day 8.

opus.r: A coarse 4-point pain scale in a 72-patient trial leaves little room: by day 8 most attacks resolve on etoricoxib alone, so any steroid benefit shows only at day 2, if at all.

sonnet.r: Etoricoxib alone is already very effective in acute gout, so adding betamethasone must show an incremental pain benefit on a coarse 4-point scale in only about 36 patients per arm.

haiku.r: A 72-patient single-site trial on a 4-point pain scale. The steroid add-on should cut pain early, but a day-8 difference is less certain, and the results may never be publicised.

carbon.r: Full-dose etoricoxib monotherapy resolves acute gout pain rapidly over 8 days, creating a strong active control and floor effect that makes demonstrating added benefit from betamethasone in 72 patients difficult.

sol.r: Adding a corticosteroid may accelerate early relief, but etoricoxib and natural flare resolution leave little pain or swelling to improve by day 8.

trials.t: 53-Week Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Intra-articular Injections of TPX-100 With Mild to Severe Tibio-Femoral Osteoarthritis of the Knee
trials.ep: Toxicity Reaction (CTC 5.0 standard）

fable.r: Enrollment is complete and follow-up is a fixed 53 weeks, so the trial should finish near March 2027; a small private sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.

opus.r: Fully enrolled small-sponsor phase 2 with 53-week follow-up; likely to finish near its March 2027 date, with results posting and record updates lagging.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 safety-primary study with enrolment closed and primary completion in March 2027; a small sponsor adds some risk of delay, funding stops and slow results posting.

haiku.r: Safety-only primary outcome. The trial is likely to run close to plan, and the main risk is a registry date slip rather than a stop.

carbon.r: Having already completed enrollment well ahead of its March 2027 53-week primary completion date across 33 US sites, this Phase 2 intra-articular knee osteoarthritis trial is on track to finish on schedule.

sol.r: Completed recruitment and a four-week injection course favor completion, but the small sponsor and unusually safety-only primary listing leave meaningful delay and amendment risk.

trials.t: Randomized Controlled Trial of Remote Symptoms Monitoring With Resilience PRO Compared to Care As Usual Only
trials.ep: Health-related quality of life on the EORTC QLQ-C30 (global health status/QoL score, 0-100) at 3 months

fable.r: The benefit of remote symptom monitoring on QLQ-C30 at 3 months is small (about 2 to 3 points), and a mixed-stage population on any systemic therapy may dilute it below what the trial was powered to detect.

opus.r: ePRO monitoring effects on global QoL at 3 months are small (a few points) and diluted by usual-care symptom management in French and German centres and by missing questionnaires, so even 1,458 patients may not show significance.

sonnet.r: Remote symptom monitoring shifts global quality of life only modestly at 3 months across a heterogeneous cancer population, and effects of 2 points on QLQ-C30 are near the detection limit.

haiku.r: A gain of about two QLQ-C30 points at 3 months is a small effect for a symptom-alert app, so the trial sits close to significance. Timing also matters, since enrolment was still open at launch.

carbon.r: Routine oncology care across French and German academic centers may already address symptoms proactively, diluting the incremental 3-month quality-of-life gain from app-based ePRO alerts.

sol.r: Remote monitoring probably adds only a few QoL points over modern supportive care; heterogeneous cancers and incomplete questionnaires could dilute that advantage.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy of Remibrutinib Compared to Dupilumab at Early Timepoints in Adults With Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria Inadequately Controlled by Second Generation H1-antihistamines
trials.ep: Absolute change from baseline in weekly Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7, range 0-42) at week 4

fable.r: Dupilumab acts slowly in CSU, so the only real risk is an unexpectedly strong early response in the dupilumab arm (loading dose, active-comparator expectancy) narrowing the week 4 gap.

opus.r: Dupilumab with a 600 mg loading dose may act faster in CSU than its slow week-24 curves suggest, narrowing the week-4 gap below what 205 per arm can detect.

sonnet.r: Remibrutinib's rapid onset versus dupilumab's slower rise should favour remibrutinib at week 4, but the margin is moderate and dupilumab's loading dose narrows it.

haiku.r: Remibrutinib should act faster than dupilumab, whose loading dose gives an early gain, so a superiority win at week 4 is close to even. The trial should read out near the sponsor's 2027 timeline.

carbon.r: A faster-than-expected early UAS7 response in the dupilumab loading-dose arm plus double-dummy placebo response could narrow the Week 4 treatment difference.

sol.r: The bet is on faster onset rather than superior long-term efficacy; a stronger week-4 dupilumab response would narrow remibrutinib's expected advantage.

trials.t: A Double-blind Study Evaluating the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Zorevunersen in Patients With Dravet Syndrome
trials.ep: Change from baseline in major motor seizure frequency (daily seizure diary) at week 28

fable.r: The large seizure reductions seen in small open-label phase 1/2a cohorts may shrink against a sham intrathecal control with its own placebo response, leaving the week-28 difference too small to reach significance.

opus.r: Phase 1/2a seizure reductions were open-label on top of multiple ASMs; against a sham procedure the true week-28 effect of a slowly building Nav1.1 upregulation could be smaller than the open-label signal suggested.

sonnet.r: Large sham-controlled phase 3 of a disease-modifying ASO with a big phase 2 signal; the main way to fail is a strong sham response or a smaller effect than the open-label data suggested.

haiku.r: Main failure path is a drug effect smaller than the open-label Phase 1/2 signal suggested; 85 per arm gives good power only for a moderate effect.

carbon.r: Repeated sham lumbar puncture procedures and intensive clinical follow-up could inflate sham-arm seizure reductions on caregiver diaries.

sol.r: The large open-label seizure reductions may shrink substantially under sham control in patients already receiving modern multidrug therapy.

trials.t: An Interventional Study of Infigratinib in Children With Hypochondroplasia
trials.ep: Change from baseline (BL) in Annualized Height Velocity (AHV; cm/year)

fable.r: The record covers only the open-label phase 2 part and still shows enrolling by invitation three months before its date; slow enrolment or adding the phase 3 part to this record would push primary completion later.

opus.r: The open-label phase 2 portion (24 children rolled over from ACCEL) runs to its 26-week AHV readout, but the record also covers a placebo-controlled phase 3 portion that will likely extend dates and enrollment.

sonnet.r: The record is a combined phase 2/3 with a 26-week primary but still 'enrolling by invitation', so the January 2027 completion date is likely to slip or be rewritten when the placebo-controlled phase 3 part is added.

haiku.r: Enrolling by invitation from an existing cohort; the risk is that the Phase 3 part or data cleaning pushes primary completion past May 2027. Results posting by August 2027 is possible but not the default.

carbon.r: Because the trial is still enrolling by invitation in late October 2026 and requires at least 26 weeks of follow-up plus a planned Phase 3 double-blind portion, registry primary completion is likely to slip past May 2027.

sol.r: The small invitation-only cohort is feasible, but transition from dose finding into the randomized phase 3 portion is likely to extend completion and alter the endpoint schedule.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety Study of QLM3003 Ointment in Participants With Mild or Moderate Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving at least 75% improvement in EASI from baseline (EASI-75) at week 8

fable.r: Vehicle response in mild disease could be high and the molecule's potency is not well documented publicly, but a topical JAK inhibitor rarely misses EASI-75 against vehicle with 120 patients per arm.

opus.r: QLM3003's mechanism and phase 2 data are not public; if it behaves like a weak PDE4-type topical, an emollient ointment vehicle with a 20-25% EASI-75 rate could leave a gap too small to separate.

sonnet.r: Vehicle response in mild-to-moderate topical AD trials is high (EASI-75 of 15-30% at week 8), which is the main threat to an otherwise well-powered 120-per-arm phase 3 of a topical with a presumably positive phase 2.

haiku.r: Two-arm responder trial; the main risk is a weaker topical effect than hoped, since placebo responses in mild to moderate AD vary and no Phase 2 data are in the record.

carbon.r: Frequent twice-daily application of emollient ointment vehicle in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis can raise placebo EASI-75 rates and compress the active drug's treatment margin.

sol.r: Without a clearly established drug-specific efficacy signal, a smaller-than-expected incremental benefit over an effective ointment vehicle is the principal risk.

trials.t: A Study of ONO-2020 in Participants With Mild to Moderate Alzheimer's Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 26 in ADAS-cog 12 score

fable.r: A novel epigenetic regulator added to standard symptomatic therapy is unlikely to move ADAS-cog 12 within 26 weeks; almost every add-on mechanism tested this way has failed on cognition.

opus.r: A first-in-class oral epigenetic regulator with only phase 1 data must beat placebo on ADAS-cog12 within 26 weeks, when placebo decline is only 1-2 points and most novel AD mechanisms have shown no cognitive separation.

sonnet.r: Novel epigenetic mechanism in a 26-week phase 2 of about 87 per arm; the odds of a significant ADAS-cog 12 benefit are low, as with most symptomatic AD phase 2 programs.

haiku.r: Cognitive primary at 26 weeks in mild to moderate AD; most such Phase 2 trials miss, and I expect an effect near zero at 87 per arm, so the risk is a weak or absent drug effect.

carbon.r: Novel small-molecule epigenetic regulators have low historical probability of demonstrating clinically and statistically significant ADAS-cog 12 improvements over 26 weeks in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.

sol.r: A novel epigenetic intervention may not produce a sufficiently large cognitive benefit over 26 weeks to overcome ADAS-cog variability and dose multiplicity.

trials.t: A Study Comparing IBI362 vs Semaglutide in Chinese Overweight or Obese Adults With Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Fatty Liver Disease （MAFLD）
trials.c: Overweight; Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Fatty Liver Disease (MAFLD)
trials.ep: Percentage change in body weight from baseline at Week 48

fable.r: Semaglutide 2.4 mg could do better than expected in this lower-BMI fatty-liver population while mazdutide 9 mg underdelivers because of titration time and diabetic participants, narrowing the gap on weight.

opus.r: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a strong comparator for both weight and liver fat; the liver-fat co-primary could show a smaller-than-expected gap, and open-label dropout could dilute differences, though both risks look small.

sonnet.r: Mazdutide 9 mg should beat semaglutide 2.4 mg on weight and probably on liver fat; the residual risk is that the liver-fat co-primary or an open-label tolerability effect fails to separate.

haiku.r: Superiority on body weight is very likely given the dose gap; the main risk is the MRI-PDFF co-primary failing in the same arm, so p_met stays below 0.8.

carbon.r: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a potent active comparator, so higher-than-expected weight loss in the control arm or gastrointestinal dose holds on mazdutide 9 mg could narrow the weight-loss difference.

sol.r: Semaglutide may remove enough liver fat to narrow the MRI-PDFF difference, jeopardizing the liver-fat co-primary despite a clear weight advantage.

trials.t: A Study to Assess Safety and Tolerability of PCRX-201 in Subjects With Painful Osteoarthritis of the Knee
trials.ep: Incidence (number and percent) of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) for PCRX-201 Dose A and Dose B versus placebo from Week 1 through Week 52

fable.r: Part B is still recruiting and the primary safety window runs 52 weeks per subject, so the November 2026 primary completion date cannot hold for the whole study and should move to late 2027 or beyond.

opus.r: Part B (90 patients) depends on process-2 drug and is still recruiting with a 52-week safety primary, so the November 2026 primary completion date cannot hold and will be pushed into 2027-2028.

sonnet.r: Part B enrollment depends on process-2 drug supply and the status is still recruiting in Oct 2026, so a November 2026 primary completion on a 52-week safety endpoint will almost certainly be pushed far beyond February 2027.

haiku.r: Still recruiting with a Part B that depends on a second manufacturing process, so the registered November 2026 primary completion is likely to slip well past February 2027.

carbon.r: The trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 and requires 52 weeks of post-injection safety follow-up plus Part B manufacturing availability, making primary completion before March 2027 virtually impossible.

sol.r: Recruiting status near the planned completion date conflicts with the required 52-week follow-up, and Part B additionally depends on availability of a second manufacturing process.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Weekly Doses of GLM101 in Participants With PMM2-CDG
trials.ep: Change from baseline in International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS) total score at week 24 (Part A)

fable.r: Open-label ICARS gains may partly reflect practice and placebo effects, and with about 25 patients per arm only an advantage of roughly 4-5 points or more over placebo reaches significance.

opus.r: With 25 per arm and a noisy 24-week ICARS change in a slowly progressive, heterogeneous disease, only a ~4-point difference is detectable, larger than a metabolic-substrate therapy is likely to produce in six months.

sonnet.r: A 50-patient rare-disease trial on ICARS with a placebo response and heterogeneous ages is underpowered for the modest improvement seen in open-label data of a first-in-class replacement therapy.

haiku.r: Small trial (25 per arm) with a noisy ICARS endpoint; a moderate ataxia effect is hard to detect reliably, so the risk is that the trial cannot show a real but modest effect.

carbon.r: With only 50 patients across heterogeneous pediatric and adult PMM2-CDG severities, rater variability and developmental or practice improvements on ICARS in the placebo arm may obscure a modest central nervous system effect.

sol.r: Improving systemic glycosylation may not reverse established cerebellar dysfunction enough to separate from placebo on ICARS within 24 weeks.

trials.t: A Trial of the Efficacy and Safety of SEP-363856 in Acutely Psychotic Participants With Schizophrenia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at week 6

fable.r: Ulotaront's true advantage over placebo looks like 2-4 PANSS points from DIAMOND 1 and 2, below the roughly 4.5-point difference this trial needs for significance, and placebo response in acute trials stays high.

opus.r: Both DIAMOND phase 3 trials failed because placebo PANSS improvements of 14-19 points matched ulotaront; stricter enrolment may help but a 3-5 point true effect leaves this trial near coin-flip power.

sonnet.r: Ulotaront missed in two earlier phase 3 acute schizophrenia trials because of large placebo responses and small drug-placebo gaps; this repeat at 75/100 mg with enriched entry criteria is still more likely to fail than succeed.

haiku.r: Earlier Phase 3 trials of ulotaront in acute schizophrenia did not show a clear PANSS advantage, so the main risk is a drug effect too small to separate from a high placebo response, even with 179 per arm.

carbon.r: Large inpatient placebo responses across 73 US and Japanese sites could replicate the placebo inflation that caused ulotaront to miss its primary endpoint in DIAMOND 1 and DIAMOND 2.

sol.r: Ulotaront has already missed two phase 3 primary endpoints, and a substantial inpatient placebo response could again erase its modest PANSS advantage.

trials.t: An Open-label Study of Lutetium (177Lu) Vipivotide Tetraxetan (AAA617) in Combination With ARPI Versus AAA617 in PSMA Positive First-line mCRPC
trials.ep: Safety: Number of participants with adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)

fable.r: Novartis closed the study early after 7 participants; the open questions are whether the record ends as terminated or completed and how soon the small safety dataset is posted.

opus.r: The study was closed out early with only 7 of the planned patients and its completion date has passed, so the record will likely be closed as terminated (or completed under the amended protocol) with Novartis posting safety results around the one-year deadline.

sonnet.r: A seven-patient phase 2 closed out early by Novartis; the status may be flipped to terminated, and Novartis posts results to ClinicalTrials.gov reliably within about a year.

haiku.r: Closed early with seven enrolled, so the record will likely move to terminated; results posting follows the Novartis timetable, due by about October 2027.

carbon.r: As stated in the registry description, enrollment was closed early at 7 randomized patients with study completion set for October 2026, leading to either a Completed or Terminated final registry status and timely safety results posting.

sol.r: The record explicitly describes early closure after only seven randomized participants, making a formal termination update much more likely than renewed enrollment.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Trial in Healthy Adult Participants of the Recombinant MVA-BN-WEV Vaccine
trials.ep: Optimal dose of MVA-BN-WEV vaccine in adult participants in terms of immunogenicity based on eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV)- and Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV)-specific humoral immune responses to the MVA-BN-WEV vaccination.

fable.r: Fully enrolled vaccine trial with a fixed visit schedule and US defence co-funding; it should complete near the registered date, with results posted later than August 2027.

opus.r: Enrollment is complete and the booster-response primary falls in early 2027, so the US-government-funded trial should finish close to schedule, with results posted only after the one-year window.

sonnet.r: A fully enrolled, not-recruiting vaccine phase 2 whose fixed vaccination schedule should reach its February 2027 primary completion; results posting normally follows many months later.

haiku.r: Enrolment complete and the trial in follow-up, so the February 2027 primary completion should hold; results posting falls due in early 2028, after the read date.

carbon.r: Enrollment of all 411 healthy volunteers is already complete across 9 US sites with fixed vaccination intervals, so primary data collection should conclude close to February 2027.

sol.r: Completed enrollment and a well-established vaccine platform favor routine completion, with booster scheduling and specialized antibody testing the main potential sources of delay.

trials.t: A Study of TQB3473 Tablets Compared to Placebo in the Treatment of Adult Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia
trials.sp: Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Durable platelet response: platelet count at least 50x10^9/L at 4 or more of 6 visits during weeks 14-24, without rescue

fable.r: If TQB3473 is only as active as fostamatinib (durable response under 20%), dropouts and a small placebo arm could leave the difference short of significance, though this is unlikely.

opus.r: Placebo durable response in refractory chronic ITP is near zero, so the only real risk is that TQB3473 gives a weak durable response at the dose chosen.

sonnet.r: Syk inhibitor in refractory chronic ITP with platelets <30; placebo durable response is near zero, so only a clearly weaker-than-class effect would fail.

haiku.r: Placebo durable response is low in this relapsed ITP population, so the effect size and whether the sponsor shows it at 4 of 6 visits decide the result; the record gives no mechanism or dose detail.

carbon.r: TQB3473 could show lower sustained platelet responses in heavily pretreated chronic ITP than seen with peer SYK inhibitors, though near-zero placebo durable response preserves high statistical power.

sol.r: Placebo durable responses should be uncommon, but insufficient compound-specific activity could leave TQB3473 below the response advantage demonstrated by successful oral ITP therapies.

trials.t: To Evaluate the Efficacy of Three Times Weekly (TIW) Vadadustat Compared to Standard of Care ESA in Patients With Anemia of CKD Receiving In-Center Hemodialysis
trials.ep: Change in hemoglobin from baseline to the mean of weeks 20 to 24

fable.r: Three-times-weekly vadadustat tends to give lower hemoglobin than ESA, and a gap near 0.5 g/dL would push the confidence bound past a -0.75 g/dL non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: Vadadustat usually leaves hemoglobin a little lower than ESA, and three-times-weekly dosing may lose some potency, so the lower confidence bound could cross a non-inferiority margin; a true superiority test would almost surely fail.

sonnet.r: If the hypothesis is non-inferiority against Mircera (likely, margin around -0.75 g/dL) it should be met easily; if it is truly superiority, TIW vadadustat will not beat an ESA on hemoglobin.

haiku.r: Completed trial where the main uncertainty is the hypothesis: the card says superiority, but a hemoglobin comparison against an ESA is usually non-inferiority and the record gives no margin. Superiority on 353 patients is unlikely to be significant.

carbon.r: Three-times-weekly vadadustat may achieve slightly lower hemoglobin maintenance than daily dosing or standard ESA, or fail if tested for superiority rather than non-inferiority.

sol.r: Three-times-weekly exposure may maintain hemoglobin less reliably than titrated ESA; success is much likelier under non-inferiority than superiority.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Tobevibart + Elebsiran in Chronic HDV Infection
trials.ep: HDV RNA below LLOQ/target not detected plus ALT normalization, at Week 48 (immediate treatment) vs Week 12 (delayed treatment)

fable.r: Failure would need the composite response to collapse because ALT normalization lags behind viral suppression, which phase 2 data make very unlikely against a near-zero control.

opus.r: The control arm is untreated at week 12 and will have almost no responders, so failure would need the strict undetectable-plus-ALT-normal response at week 48 to fall far below phase 2 levels.

sonnet.r: Delayed-treatment control at week 12 should show about 0% composite response, so failure would require an unexpectedly weak combination effect at week 48.

haiku.r: The immediate arm is read at week 48 and the delayed arm at week 12 before it is treated, so the comparison is favourable. The risk is the composite with ALT normalization and how the sponsor words the result.

carbon.r: The stringent requirement for Target Not Detected HDV RNA combined with ALT normalization at Week 48 could yield lower response rates in cirrhotic patients, though untreated Week 12 control response is near zero.

sol.r: The target-not-detected plus normal-ALT composite is stricter than broader virologic-response definitions and could yield fewer responders than expected.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of Crofelemer in Adult Patients With Short Bowel Syndrome and Intestinal Failure (SBS-IF) Without Colon-in-continuity (CIC)
trials.c: Short Bowel Syndrome; Malabsorption Syndromes; Short Gut Syndrome
trials.ep: Change from baseline in weekly parenteral support volume (parenteral nutrition with or without IV fluids) at 24 weeks

fable.r: Six patients per arm cannot show a significant difference in parenteral support volume unless the effect is very large and consistent.

opus.r: With about six patients per arm and two efficacy primaries (PS volume and stool volume) that would both need significance, a formal win is very unlikely even if crofelemer reduces losses somewhat.

sonnet.r: Six patients per arm cannot reliably show a significant change in parenteral support volume; the primary set also includes descriptive safety outcomes and a sponsor claim of success is unlikely.

haiku.r: Six patients per arm at the highest dose cannot give a reliable superiority test on parenteral support volume. A small sponsor would likely call a numerical trend encouraging rather than state a significant primary result.

carbon.r: With only 6 patients per arm and multiple safety and preliminary efficacy primary outcomes, the study is severely underpowered to achieve formal statistical significance.

sol.r: Only six patients per arm must establish benefit on both parenteral-support and stool-volume primaries despite substantial anatomical and fluid-management variability.

trials.t: Study of New Antiandrogenic Progestogen + Low-dose Estrogen for Moderate Acne Vulgaris
trials.c: Acne Vulgaris; Acne Vulgaris on the Face
trials.ep: Change from baseline in inflammatory acne lesion count at cycle 6 (week 24)

fable.r: All three co-primary endpoints must be met and any statement by mid-2027 would have to come from an interim analysis or an early stop, given the trial only began in August 2026.

opus.r: Placebo plus standard skincare cuts lesion counts substantially in acne trials, and all three co-primaries (inflammatory count, total count, ISGA 0/1) must be significant, with the ISGA success-rate endpoint the most fragile.

sonnet.r: Three co-primaries must all succeed; the ISGA 0/1 responder endpoint is the least powered and placebo response in acne is large.

haiku.r: The three co-primary outcomes must all be met, and the ISGA 0 or 1 outcome is the hardest. The drug is a reduced-estrogen variant of an established combination, so its effect may be close to placebo plus a modest gain.

carbon.r: Standard skincare and placebo lesion regression could narrow the difference on the strict ISGA 0/1 co-primary endpoint, though antiandrogenic cyproterone plus ethinyl estradiol has robust established efficacy.

sol.r: Lesion counts should improve, but the clear/almost-clear ISGA co-primary could fail despite statistically significant count reductions.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of IBI302 inSubjects With Diabetic Macular Edema（DME）
trials.sp: Innovent Biologics Technology Limited (Shanghai R&D Center)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity (ETDRS letters) at Week 16

fable.r: Faricimab produces near-maximal visual gains by week 16, leaving no room for superiority and making success depend on a pre-specified non-inferiority objective in a small trial.

opus.r: Faricimab after four monthly loading doses already gives about 9-10 letters by week 16, so a bispecific VEGF/complement drug is very unlikely to show statistically superior vision gains in 50 vs 50 patients.

sonnet.r: A 50-patient arm versus faricimab is underpowered to show BCVA superiority at week 16; the realistic outcome is parity, which only counts if the sponsor frames it as met.

haiku.r: Fifty patients per arm can only show a superiority difference of about six letters or more, which a comparator as strong as faricimab makes unlikely. Whether the trial passes depends on whether the sponsor states a non-inferiority hypothesis.

carbon.r: Faricimab produces ~10-11 ETDRS letters of gain during Week 16 loading in DME, leaving minimal headroom for IBI302 to show superiority or reliably clear a tight non-inferiority margin with 50 patients per arm.

sol.r: Faricimab should produce substantial early visual improvement, leaving little room for IBI302 to demonstrate superiority in approximately 50 patients per dose.

trials.t: Safety of a Single, Intravitreal Injection of 6.0M jCell (Famzeretcel) in Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP)
trials.ep: Safety of Intravitreal Injection of 6.0M jCell

fable.r: Enrolment is complete and follow-up is six months, so the trial should finish near the registered date, with registry results posted later than August 2027.

opus.r: Single-injection safety trial, fully enrolled, with a 6-month endpoint; it should complete around end-2026, but a small cell-therapy sponsor could slow follow-up or results posting.

sonnet.r: Enrolment appears complete with a 6-month safety endpoint due around December 2026, so only modest slippage is expected; jCyte is a private company unlikely to post results by August 2027.

haiku.r: Small private sponsor with a registry completion date of December 2026 that has not been updated; a six-month safety study of 31 patients is likely to finish near the registry date, but posting results by August 2027 is unlikely.

carbon.r: With enrollment already completed for 31 participants and a single-injection 6-month safety follow-up targeting December 2026 completion, the trial is likely to finish on schedule with low attrition.

sol.r: The small, already-enrolled cohort and six-month follow-up favor completion near schedule, although full registry results may lag sponsor disclosure.

trials.t: A Study of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) Compared With Placebo in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Obesity or Overweight
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 40

fable.r: Only if insulin dose reductions offset the glycaemic benefit, as partly happened with liraglutide, would the HbA1c difference shrink, and even then the sample is large enough to detect about 0.2 points.

opus.r: Insulin optimization in the placebo arm and insulin down-titration on tirzepatide (to avoid hypoglycemia) could shrink the HbA1c gap in type 1 diabetes, though about 450 per arm leaves a large safety margin.

sonnet.r: Tirzepatide lowers HbA1c and weight robustly; failure would need an unexpectedly strong placebo response from intensified diabetes care or heavy dropout from GI adverse events.

haiku.r: With about 450 per arm, superiority on HbA1c is very likely if the drug works as in type 2 diabetes. The real uncertainty is the size of the effect in type 1 diabetes, where incretin add-ons give smaller reductions.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance, hypoglycemia, or ketosis could increase treatment discontinuations or prompt aggressive insulin down-titration that slightly attenuates HbA1c lowering, though statistical power remains overwhelming.

sol.r: Insulin optimization and CGM-guided care may compress the HbA1c difference even if tirzepatide produces substantial weight loss.

trials.t: A Study of Carmustine With and Without Ethanol in Subjects With Lymphoma
trials.ep: Evaluation of infusion-related toxicities

fable.r: Recruitment of 49 transplant patients at four sites was still open five months before the registered completion date, so a delay beyond 90 days is about as likely as not.

opus.r: Small 4-site phase 2 still recruiting with a 30-day post-transplant safety endpoint; the remaining enrollment by early 2027 is tight for a small sponsor, so completion may slip.

sonnet.r: A 49-patient, 4-site BEAM-transplant trial from a small sponsor is likely to recruit slowly, so primary completion should slip past mid-2027; early termination is a modest risk and results will not be posted by August 2027.

haiku.r: Recruiting at four sites with a March 2027 completion date, so slippage past June 2027 is likely; the small US sponsor carries a real termination risk and results posting is unlikely this year.

carbon.r: Enrolling 49 autologous transplant lymphoma patients across four US centers may slightly overrun the March 2027 target, though the brief 30-day post-transplant follow-up limits major delays.

sol.r: Short post-transplant observation limits follow-up delay, but recruitment through only four sites could push completion beyond the planned date.

trials.t: Phase 3 Study of Human TH-SC01 Cell Injection for Treating Perianal Fistulas in Patients With Crohn's Disease
trials.ep: Combined remission at week 24: all treated external openings clinically remitted and no collections over 2 cm on central blinded MRI

fable.r: Fistula curettage and internal-opening closure in the saline arm give combined remission near 35-45%, which erased the cell-therapy effect in ADMIRE-CD II.

opus.r: Curettage, seton removal and closure with saline give combined remission rates of 35-45% in control arms, which wiped out the stem-cell effect in ADMIRE-CD II.

sonnet.r: Placebo combined remission in perianal Crohn's fistula trials is high (about 35%) and the ADMIRE-CD II repeat of darvadstrocel failed, so a cell therapy margin is fragile.

haiku.r: The combined endpoint needs all openings closed and no MRI collection over 2 cm, which is strict and where a miss would come from. Darvadstrocel's phase 3 gain over placebo supports the mechanism.

carbon.r: Surgical fistula conditioning and saline injection yielded high placebo combined remission (~34-46%) in prior mesenchymal stem cell Phase 3 trials, risking an insufficient treatment delta.

sol.r: Fistula preparation, closure procedures and background Crohn's therapy can generate high saline-arm remission, as demonstrated by the failed confirmatory darvadstrocel trial.

trials.t: A Study to Test Whether Vicadrostat in Combination With Empagliflozin Helps People With Chronic Kidney Disease
trials.ep: Absolute change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (mL/min/1.73m2) from baseline to Week 14 and week 16

fable.r: Trial is already completed; the only live question is whether Boehringer's results clear registry QC within about 12.5 months of the August 2026 completion.

opus.r: Completed Boehringer phase 2 with a short 16-week design; the main uncertainty is whether results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov before the 31 Aug 2027 read date, about 12.5 months after primary completion.

sonnet.r: The trial is already completed (primary completion 14 Aug 2026), so stopping is very unlikely and the primary outcome should stay as registered. Boehringer Ingelheim usually posts results near the 12-month deadline, which falls about two weeks before the read date, so posting is roughly a coin flip.

haiku.r: Completed phase 2 with no efficacy goal; the main uncertainty is whether results reach the registry within the year after primary completion.

carbon.r: The trial is already marked completed on ClinicalTrials.gov, and Boehringer Ingelheim reliably posts results within one year of completion.

sol.r: The trial is already completed, making operational failure unlikely; routine results posting near the one-year completion anniversary is the principal remaining milestone.

trials.t: Focused Orticumab Research for Treating Inflammation in Coronary Arteries
trials.c: Acute Coronary Syndromes; Coronary Arterial Disease (CAD); Inflammation
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in mean coronary Fat Attenuation Index (FAI) score across RCA, LAD and LCX at 24 weeks

fable.r: Mechanism is unproven: the same anti-oxidised LDL antibody did not reduce vascular inflammation on FDG-PET in GLACIER, and the FAI signal rests on a small exploratory analysis in psoriasis.

opus.r: The rationale rests on a post hoc signal of reduced coronary FAI in high-inflammation psoriasis patients; an anti-oxLDL antibody may not move a noisy perivascular imaging score significantly within 24 weeks in 120 per arm.

sonnet.r: An anti-oxLDL antibody has an unproven effect on pericoronary fat inflammation within 24 weeks on top of statins. FAI measurement noise is large and regression to the mean affects both arms, so a clean placebo-adjusted difference is uncertain.

haiku.r: FAI is a noisy CCTA-derived marker and a 24-week change in a 240-patient trial is small, so a null imaging result is the likeliest failure; the record still shows recruiting at launch, which pushes readout later.

carbon.r: Orticumab previously missed an FDG-PET arterial inflammation endpoint and relies here on replicating an exploratory CCTA FAI subgroup signal against regression to the mean.

sol.r: The encouraging earlier coronary-imaging signal may not replicate in a larger, controlled post-MI population despite enrichment for elevated baseline inflammation.

trials.t: A Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Sibeprenlimab Administered Subcutaneously in Participants With Sjögren's
trials.ep: Change from baseline in ESSDAI score (0-123, higher is worse) at Week 28

fable.r: With about 41 per arm the trial needs an observed ESSDAI difference near 2 points, more than the roughly 1.5 points I expect from APRIL-only blockade.

opus.r: APRIL-only blockade spares BAFF, the main driver of B-cell activity in Sjogren's, and ESSDAI trials show large placebo responses; with about 40 per arm, a modest 1-2 point difference is unlikely to reach significance.

sonnet.r: With about 41 patients per arm and a large placebo response on ESSDAI, a 2-point true effect gives only about 50% power. APRIL blockade lowers IgG, which mechanically helps the ESSDAI biological domain, but systemic activity in an IgG-high population is still small.

haiku.r: Phase 2 ESSDAI trials in Sjogren's often miss, and 83 patients give a wide spread on a 28-week change, so the size of the drug effect is the main uncertainty; the record shows active, not recruiting, pointing to a mid-2027 readout.

carbon.r: With roughly 41 patients per arm and substantial placebo regression on ESSDAI, the proof-of-concept study is underpowered for moderate treatment effects of selective APRIL blockade.

sol.r: A modest ESSDAI effect from selective APRIL blockade could be obscured by substantial placebo improvement and between-patient variation in only about 40 participants per arm.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Clinical Study of SHR-A1912 Combined With R-GemOx Versus R-GemOx in Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma
trials.ep: Complete response rate, assessed up to 1 year after the first dose of the last enrolled patient

fable.r: A complete response gain is very likely, but overall survival is also registered as primary and will be immature, so a report by mid-2027 may not count as the full primary objective met.

opus.r: CRR is likely to improve, as with polatuzumab-R-GemOx, but OS is a second primary outcome that will be immature at any 2027 readout, and the round requires all primary outcomes met.

sonnet.r: CRR should clearly favour the anti-CD79b ADC, as pola-R-GemOx did, but overall survival is a co-primary with a 5-year frame and is unlikely to be mature or reported as met in any early statement. Under the co-primary rule that is the main way this fails.

haiku.r: Both co-primary endpoints must be met by the same arm, and overall survival cannot mature by mid-2027, so a clean positive public statement by June is unlikely; the complete-response difference itself looks achievable at 141 per arm.

carbon.r: Although anti-CD79b ADC addition to R-GemOx strongly boosts complete response, overall survival is listed alongside CRR as a primary outcome and could be immature or co-primary.

sol.r: A convincing complete-response advantage may emerge before the co-primary overall-survival endpoint is mature or statistically significant, preventing an all-primary-endpoints success.

trials.t: Study of BLU-808 in Chronic Inducible Urticaria (CIndU) and Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (CSU)
trials.c: Chronic Inducible Urticaria; Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria
trials.ep: Part A and Part B: Number of Participants with Treatment-emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)

fable.r: Enrolment is closed with a 16-week safety primary, so completion near the registered date is likely; results are not due until about a year later, and a sponsor portfolio decision is the main stop risk.

opus.r: Fully enrolled 16-week safety study now under Sanofi after the Blueprint acquisition; likely to complete on or near schedule, with results posting near the 12-month deadline in late 2027.

sonnet.r: Safety-primary phase 2 with enrolment closed and primary completion set for end of 2026. Sanofi, which now owns the asset, will likely keep it running to completion; a date slip beyond March 2027 is possible, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Safety-only phase 2 with a completion date of 31 December 2026; the main question is whether results reach the registry by the read date, since the sponsor has until about December 2027 to post.

carbon.r: With enrollment already completed by October 2026 and a 16-week safety follow-up, primary completion should occur near schedule without substantive outcome amendments.

sol.r: Completed recruitment and a 16-week primary assessment favor timely completion; early registry posting is less certain than completion because the usual reporting anniversary falls after the read date.

trials.t: A Study of IBI362 in Participants With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH)
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with MASH resolution and no worsening of fibrosis on liver histology at Week 60

fable.r: Failure would need an unusually high placebo resolution rate or many missing week-60 biopsies in arms of only about 60 patients.

opus.r: GLP-1/glucagon co-agonists produce large MASH-resolution effects; failure would need an unusually high placebo histology response or biopsy-reading noise in about 60 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Incretin-glucagon agonists give large MASH resolution rates, but central pathology reads and a 60-week window can lift placebo response. With about 60 per arm the effect still very likely reaches significance, so the main risk is a higher placebo rate than expected.

haiku.r: Histologic resolution is read from paired biopsies at week 60 in a single-country trial of about 60 per arm, so reader variability could blur the result, but the incretin-class effect on MASH resolution is large enough that a miss is unlikely.

carbon.r: Paired Week 60 liver biopsies suffer from histological reader variability and non-responder imputation if participants drop out before repeat biopsy.

sol.r: Biopsy variability, missing week-60 biopsies and gastrointestinal-treatment discontinuations are more plausible threats than absence of a meaningful metabolic effect.

trials.t: A Study of IPN10200 for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia in Adults
trials.ep: Change from baseline in TWSTRS total score (0-85) at Week 4 after a single injection session

fable.r: A first dose-finding study in cervical dystonia may use doses too low for a full effect, and arms of about 44 leave limited power if the gain is under 5 TWSTRS points.

opus.r: Botulinum toxins reliably beat placebo on TWSTRS at week 4, so the risk is that this engineered long-acting toxin is under-dosed in a first dose-finding study in cervical dystonia.

sonnet.r: Botulinum-toxin-class agents nearly always beat placebo on TWSTRS at week 4 in cervical dystonia. The risk is that the new toxin's highest dose is under-dosed or less potent than expected, and blinded data are probably not read out before late 2027.

haiku.r: Forty-four patients per arm against a placebo response of a few TWSTRS points at week 4 leaves a real chance of missing significance, and the dose of the highest arm is not stated; recruitment still open at launch suggests the readout may slip past June 2027.

carbon.r: Conservative Phase 2 dosing of the engineered chimeric neurotoxin corabotase to minimize dysphagia risk could yield sub-optimal cervical muscle denervation at Week 4.

sol.r: The principal efficacy risk is selecting doses with insufficient early muscle-relaxant activity; proving prolonged duration is harder but is not the week-4 primary objective.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Effects of Zibotentan/Dapagliflozin Combination Compared to Dapagliflozin Alone in Adult Participants With Chronic Kidney Disease and High Proteinuria
trials.c: Chronic Kidney Disease With High Proteinuria
trials.ep: Change from baseline in log-transformed urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) at week 12

fable.r: The low zibotentan dose in the fixed combination gives a moderate UACR effect, and with noisy UACR and 112 per arm an unlucky sample could miss significance.

opus.r: Endothelin antagonism on top of SGLT2i has a well-replicated albuminuria-lowering effect; failure would need an unexpectedly small effect in this high-proteinuria regional population.

sonnet.r: Zibotentan added to dapagliflozin lowered UACR by about 30% beyond dapagliflozin alone in the phase 2b ZENITH trial, and 112 per arm gives high power. Failure would need a much smaller effect in this Russian-only population.

haiku.r: Dapagliflozin alone already lowers albuminuria substantially, so the added zibotentan effect has to clear a high bar; the endothelin mechanism is well established for albuminuria, and the 12-week endpoint is short enough to report well before the June 2027 deadline.

carbon.r: With zibotentan's additive albuminuria reduction on top of dapagliflozin already proven in ZENITH-CKD, operational execution or ERA fluid-retention dropouts pose the main residual risk.

sol.r: Endothelin-antagonist fluid retention could cause discontinuations and attenuate an otherwise well-supported albuminuria effect, especially in patients with advanced proteinuric CKD.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Bemdaneprocel in Adults Who Have Parkinson's Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 78 in PD diary ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia (hours per 16-hour waking day)

fable.r: Sham surgery produces large, durable placebo responses on diary endpoints, as in earlier transplant and gene therapy trials; before 2028 the only possible result is an early stop.

opus.r: Sham-surgery placebo responses in Parkinson's cell and gene therapy trials have repeatedly erased open-label gains, and diary ON-time is noisy with only 34 sham patients; no readout is possible before 2028.

sonnet.r: A sham-surgery-controlled cell therapy trial with an 18-month patient-diary endpoint faces a large placebo response, as sham-controlled PD gene and cell therapy trials have shown. Phase 1 was open-label, and the cell dose is unproven for efficacy. Results before mid-2027 are very unlikely.
