haiku.r: The 2:1 allocation of 102 patients leaves the sham-controlled ON-time comparison underpowered for a modest diary gain, and sham responses on diaries can be large; the 78-week endpoint is still enrolling at launch, so the registered March 2027 completion cannot hold.

carbon.r: Sham neurosurgery produces large, durable placebo ON-time gains in Parkinson's trials, and any result reported by mid-2027 despite ongoing 2026 recruitment risks reflecting an early stop.

sol.r: Ongoing recruitment is difficult to reconcile with a March 2027 week-78 completion; an unusually early announcement is more likely to concern stopping or an interim assessment than definitive primary success.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Two Dosing Regimens of Subcutaneous Nivolumab in Combination With Intravenous Ipilimumab and Chemotherapy in Participants With Previously Untreated Metastatic or Recurrent Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
trials.ep: Maximum observed serum concentration (Cmax) of subcutaneous Nivolumab in serum

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the PK primaries are read by week 18, so the February 2027 date should hold; BMS rarely posts results months ahead of the 12-month due date.

opus.r: Fully enrolled 76-patient PK study of subcutaneous nivolumab; week-18 trough sampling should finish near the registered February 2027 date, with results posted on the registry only about a year after that.

sonnet.r: Active, not recruiting phase 2 PK study with short Cmax/AUC windows and a Cycle 7 trough, so the Feb 2027 primary completion should hold; BMS usually posts results near the 12-month deadline and the study runs to late 2028.

haiku.r: Primary completion is 5 Feb 2027 and the record is already active, not recruiting, so the main path to lateness is a later date update; results posting is possible within the FDAAA window but probably lands after August 2027.

carbon.r: Enrollment is already closed as of October 2026 and the longest primary PK assessment is at Week 18, aligning closely with the February 2027 primary completion date.

sol.r: Closed recruitment, short pharmacokinetic follow-up and an established treatment backbone favor completion on schedule, while registry posting is more likely after the August 2027 read date.

trials.t: Placebo-Controlled Trial of IFx-Hu2.0 Followed By Pembrolizumab In Checkpoint Inhibitor Naïve Participants With Advanced Or Metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma
trials.c: Advanced Or Metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma
trials.ep: Confirmed objective response rate (complete or partial response, BICR, RECIST 1.1), first at 12 weeks, with analysis at about 24 weeks

fable.r: Pembrolizumab alone already yields responses in about half of patients, so 59 per arm needs a 20-25 point ORR gain from an intralesional agent supported only by a small uncontrolled phase 1b.

opus.r: First-line pembrolizumab already gives roughly 45-55% confirmed responses in Merkel cell carcinoma, so with 59 patients per arm a single-lesion intralesional injection must add about 18 points to reach significance, which is unlikely for an unproven innate-immune plasmid.

sonnet.r: Pembrolizumab alone gives roughly 40-55% ORR in checkpoint-naive MCC, leaving little room; with 59 per arm a difference of about 18 points is needed for significance and an add-on injection effect is likely smaller.

haiku.r: With 59 patients per arm, a superiority test needs a gain of roughly 19 points over a pembrolizumab control near 45 percent, so a real but modest IFx-Hu2.0 effect would likely miss significance.

carbon.r: Pembrolizumab monotherapy already achieves roughly 50% confirmed objective response rates in checkpoint-naive Merkel cell carcinoma, leaving limited headroom for a single-lesion intralesional adjunct to demonstrate statistically significant superiority in 118 patients.

sol.r: Pembrolizumab already produces durable responses in roughly half of untreated advanced MCC patients, so a modest priming effect may not separate with only 59 patients per arm.

trials.t: AK112 and Chemotherapy in First-line Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent central review, followed up to about 3 years

fable.r: Bevacizumab already supplies VEGF blockade in the control arm, so the gain must come from PD-1 blockade in mostly MSS colorectal cancer, where add-on benefit has been modest (HR about 0.8) and 560 patients may not suffice.

opus.r: Ivonescimab's VEGF arm only matches bevacizumab, so the trial depends on PD-1 blockade adding PFS benefit in a mostly microsatellite-stable colorectal population, where CheckMate 9X8 failed and only AtezoTRIBE succeeded.

sonnet.r: Bevacizumab already blocks VEGF and MSS colorectal cancer is largely PD-1 insensitive, so the PD-1 arm of ivonescimab may add only a modest PFS gain, near the HR of about 0.8 needed for significance with roughly 340 events.

haiku.r: Bevacizumab with chemotherapy is a strong first-line control in colorectal cancer and PD-1 blockade adds little in microsatellite-stable disease, so the PFS gain must come from the bispecific's own VEGF activity.

carbon.r: About 95% of unselected metastatic colorectal cancers are microsatellite-stable tumors where adding PD-1 blockade to chemotherapy plus VEGF inhibition has yielded modest or non-significant progression-free survival gains in prior randomized trials.

sol.r: Most metastatic colorectal cancers are relatively resistant to checkpoint blockade, so replacing bevacizumab with a PD-1/VEGF bispecific may add less benefit than its lung-cancer results suggest.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of KarXT for the Treatment of Manic Episodes in Bipolar-I Disorder
trials.c: Bipolar-I Disorder With Mania or Mania With Mixed Features
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) total score at Week 3

fable.r: No prior mania data: a muscarinic agonist may be less antimanic than D2 blockers, and a week of titration inside a 3-week trial plus high placebo response could shrink the YMRS difference below the roughly 2.7 points needed.

opus.r: A muscarinic agonist has no proven antimanic effect, and KarXT's titration and GI side effects may blunt separation within a 3-week inpatient trial where placebo arms often improve 10 or more YMRS points.

sonnet.r: Muscarinic M1/M4 agonism has no proven antimanic effect and lacks direct D2 blockade, the mechanism behind all approved acute mania drugs, so the drug may separate from placebo less than in schizophrenia.

haiku.r: Placebo responses in acute mania trials are large within three weeks, so a KarXT gain of only two to three YMRS points would be needed to reach significance, and a strong placebo response could absorb it.

carbon.r: Cholinergic gastrointestinal adverse events during rapid inpatient titration and high inpatient placebo improvement on YMRS could attenuate the week-3 treatment difference.

sol.r: Robust antipsychotic efficacy does not establish a clinically meaningful antimanic effect, and inpatient placebo improvement could erase a modest signal.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of KarXT for the Treatment of Manic Episodes in Bipolar-I Disorder (BALSAM-2)
trials.c: Bipolar Disorder Type I With Mania or Mania With Mixed Features
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) total score at Week 3

fable.r: Untested mechanism in mania: muscarinic agonism may calm mania less than D2 blockade, titration takes a third of the 3-week window, and placebo response at sites in India, China and eastern Europe could be large.

opus.r: Multinational inpatient mania trials with sites in India, China and Eastern Europe often show placebo YMRS drops above 10 points, which can swamp a modest effect from a non-dopamine-blocking drug titrated over the first week.

sonnet.r: Muscarinic M1/M4 agonism has no proven antimanic effect and lacks direct D2 blockade, the mechanism behind all approved acute mania drugs, so the drug may separate from placebo less than in schizophrenia.

haiku.r: Placebo responses in acute mania trials are large within three weeks, so a KarXT gain of only two to three YMRS points would be needed to reach significance, and a strong placebo response could absorb it.

carbon.r: Broad multinational enrollment across 85 sites in 11 countries increases inter-rater noise and inpatient placebo response on the YMRS, which can dilute week-3 separation.

sol.r: KarXT may improve psychotic symptoms without producing enough additional improvement in core mania to overcome substantial inpatient placebo response.

trials.t: A Study to Compare Pharmacokinetics, Efficacy and Safety of Subcutaneous CT-P44 and Darzalex Faspro in Combination With Lenalidomide and Dexamethasone in Patients With Refractory or Relapsed Multiple Myeloma
trials.ep: PK equivalence: daratumumab AUC over weeks 0 to 1 and weeks 8 to 10

fable.r: High between-patient variability of subcutaneous daratumumab exposure in myeloma, with two AUC windows that must both fall inside the equivalence margins, is the main way a true biosimilar could miss.

opus.r: Biosimilar PK equivalence usually holds; the residual risk is a formulation difference (e.g. the hyaluronidase co-formulation or absorption) pushing an AUC ratio interval outside the margin.

sonnet.r: Both AUC ratios must fall within the equivalence margins; daratumumab SC exposure is variable (target-mediated disposition) so imbalance in tumour burden between arms is the main risk, though about 236 per arm gives ample precision.

haiku.r: Equivalence within the protocol window is likely for a biosimilar of a well-characterized product, so the main risk is a single-site, small-sample AUC ratio falling outside the margins at one of the two time windows.

carbon.r: Target-mediated drug disposition and inter-patient myeloma tumor burden variability could widen confidence intervals around subcutaneous daratumumab AUC ratios at early and late sampling windows.

sol.r: Subcutaneous absorption variability or a small formulation-related exposure shift could push one of the two AUC confidence intervals outside the protocol's equivalence bounds.

trials.t: A Study of TAK-360 in Adults With Narcolepsy Without Cataplexy (NT2)
trials.ep: Number of Participants With at Least One Treatment-emergent Adverse Event (TEAE)

fable.r: Recruitment of narcolepsy type 2 patients is slow and the record still recruits a month before its completion date, so a slip of several months is likely; termination or outcome changes are unlikely.

opus.r: Still recruiting a month before its registered November 2026 completion date, so Takeda will likely push primary completion into 2027; results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Recruiting a 88-patient narcolepsy type 2 dose-finding trial right at its planned Nov 2026 primary completion suggests a possible slip of a few months; Takeda posts results relatively promptly but usually 9-12 months after completion.

haiku.r: The record still reads recruiting with a November 2026 completion date, so a later completion date is the more likely registry change; results posting by August 2027 is uncertain for a Takeda phase 2 study.

carbon.r: Because this adaptive 52-site narcolepsy type 2 trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 just ahead of its November 2026 target date and includes up to 15 weeks of follow-up, primary completion will likely slip by more than 90 days.

sol.r: This small multinational safety-led study should finish, but NT2 diagnostic screening and adaptive dose selection could delay completion.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate D-0502 in Subjects With ER+ Her2- Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival assessed by Independent Review Committee, from enrollment up to 2 years

fable.r: Benefit of oral SERDs over fulvestrant is concentrated in ESR1-mutated tumours; in an all-comer second-line Chinese population the blended hazard ratio may land near 0.85 and miss significance.

opus.r: Oral SERDs beat fulvestrant in all-comers only when ESR1-mutant tumours drive the effect; this Chinese population is largely ESR1 wild-type and partly CDK4/6-naive, so an all-patient PFS benefit is likely too small.

sonnet.r: Oral SERDs versus fulvestrant mostly win only in ESR1-mutant disease; in an unselected population the PFS gain is modest (HR about 0.8), which with about 400 events is close to the significance threshold.

haiku.r: Fulvestrant is a modest control in endocrine-pretreated disease, so an oral SERD can plausibly reach a hazard ratio near 0.6, but a smaller effect or a population with prior CDK4/6 exposure could blunt the gain.

carbon.r: Enrolling all-comer ER-positive/HER2-negative patients without restricting or co-primary gating on ESR1 mutations dilutes oral SERD superiority over fulvestrant.

sol.r: An advantage over fulvestrant may be concentrated in ESR1-mutant disease, while this all-comer population includes patients likely to respond well to fulvestrant.

trials.t: A Study of 2 Doses of Remigromig (EYE103) Compared With Ranibizumab (0.5 mg) in Participants With DME
trials.ep: Change from baseline in ETDRS best-corrected visual acuity (letters) at Week 52

fable.r: A first-in-class Wnt agonist must match monthly ranibizumab on vision; if barrier restoration alone dries the macula less completely than VEGF blockade, the BCVA difference will breach the non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: If remigromig's VEGF blockade is weaker than ranibizumab's at matched monthly dosing, a BCVA deficit of 2-3 letters could break a 4-letter non-inferiority margin; otherwise non-inferiority with ~350 per arm is very likely.

sonnet.r: A novel Wnt-pathway antibody must match monthly ranibizumab on BCVA within the margin; failure would need EYE103 to be clearly less effective than a potent monthly anti-VEGF, which phase 2 did not suggest.

haiku.r: The primary is non-inferiority against ranibizumab with a margin the record does not state, so the risk is a remigromig gain that trails ranibizumab by more than a typical 4 letter margin, most likely through weaker durability at week 52.

carbon.r: Monthly ranibizumab 0.5 mg reliably produces over 10 ETDRS letters of visual gain in DME, posing a tough benchmark for a Wnt-agonist monotherapy that does not directly neutralize VEGF.

sol.r: Early Wnt-pathway results may not translate into vision gains maintained for a year against monthly ranibizumab, particularly without direct VEGF inhibition.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Ruxolitinib Cream in Participants With Hidradenitis Suppurativa (TRuE-HS2)
trials.ep: Proportion achieving HiSCR75 (at least 75% reduction in abscess and inflammatory nodule count, no increase in abscesses or draining tunnels) at week 16

fable.r: Vehicle response is high and variable in mild HS with few lesions, and a topical may not reach deep nodules, so the HiSCR75 gap could shrink well below the 29 points seen in the small phase 2.

opus.r: In mild HS with as few as 4 lesions, a 75% count drop can happen by chance or with emollient vehicle, so a high vehicle HiSCR75 rate could shrink the gap below significance, as happened in one of the two prurigo nodularis trials of the same cream.

sonnet.r: A topical JAK inhibitor must reduce deep inflammatory nodules and abscesses by 75% over vehicle in 16 weeks; topical HS therapies have historically had little effect and vehicle response in mild disease with low lesion counts is substantial.

haiku.r: Topical ruxolitinib must cut abscess and nodule counts by 75 percent in 16 weeks in mild to moderate HS, a high bar for a cream against a vehicle near 18 percent, so the main risk is a true effect too small to clear significance.

carbon.r: Spontaneous fluctuation of superficial inflammatory nodules in mild-to-moderate HS without draining tunnels can elevate vehicle HiSCR75 response rates at week 16.

sol.r: Spontaneous lesion-count fluctuations and a high vehicle response in mild HS could shrink the HiSCR75 difference despite topical JAK activity.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate Efficacy and Safety of Brivekimig in Participants With Crohn's Disease
trials.ep: Proportion achieving endoscopic response (centrally read SES-CD decrease >50% from baseline) at week 16

fable.r: With about 33 patients per arm, a true 15-20 point endoscopic response gain over placebo has only around even odds of reaching significance, especially if many patients previously failed anti-TNF.

opus.r: About 33 patients per arm in a mixed conventional- and advanced-therapy-experienced CD population gives roughly 50-65% power even for a 20-25 point gain in centrally read endoscopic response.

sonnet.r: About 33 per arm in a dose-ranging phase 2; a real TNF-driven effect is plausible but power for the high dose versus placebo is only moderate, and the sponsor may not state significance.

haiku.r: About 33 patients per arm in a dose-ranging phase 2; a dual TNF and IL-23 agent should beat placebo on endoscopic response, but the gap at the highest dose must clear a small-sample threshold.

carbon.r: With roughly 33 patients per arm, sampling variation in placebo endoscopic response or a high share of anti-TNF-refractory enrollees could keep a clinically meaningful benefit short of statistical significance.

sol.r: With only about 33 patients per arm, a few placebo endoscopic responses or nonresponders on active treatment could erase significance despite clinically useful activity.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Ruxolitinib Cream in Participants With Hidradenitis Suppurativa (TRuE-HS1)
trials.ep: Proportion achieving HiSCR75 (at least 75% reduction in abscess and inflammatory nodule count, no increase in abscesses or draining tunnels) at week 16

fable.r: Mild HS with low lesion counts fluctuates spontaneously, so vehicle HiSCR75 could run high (vehicle response sank TRuE-PN2); the phase 2 signal came from 69 patients with uneven dropout and may shrink under non-responder imputation.

opus.r: In mild-moderate HS with low AN counts (as few as 4), small fluctuations give a high vehicle HiSCR75 rate, which can shrink a topical drug's margin.

sonnet.r: Mild-moderate HS with few nodules gives a high vehicle HiSCR75 response, and a topical JAK1/2 cream may not reach deep nodules, so the gap may be under the roughly 9-10 points needed.

haiku.r: Topical drug in mild to moderate HS, where vehicle responses are substantial and penetration into deep nodules is limited, so the HiSCR75 gap may be modest.

carbon.r: Spontaneous lesion wax-and-wane in mild-to-moderate tunnel-free hidradenitis suppurativa can inflate the vehicle cream HiSCR75 response rate and compress the treatment difference.

sol.r: Topical JAK inhibition may not suppress deep follicular inflammation enough to separate from a substantial vehicle response on the stringent HiSCR75 threshold.

trials.t: A Long-Term Study of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Obesity or Overweight
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 40

fable.r: Insulin is cut when tirzepatide starts and titrated to target in both arms, which can shrink the HbA1c difference toward the 0.2 points seen with liraglutide; even so the trial is powered to detect that.

opus.r: In type 1 diabetes, insulin dose reductions to avoid hypoglycaemia can absorb much of an incretin's glucose effect, as with liraglutide in ADJUNCT ONE, leaving a small HbA1c difference.

sonnet.r: Tirzepatide's glycemic and weight effects are large; a 0.5-0.7 point HbA1c gap against placebo with 230 per arm is far beyond the detection threshold, so the only real uncertainty is timing of disclosure.

haiku.r: Large, well-powered add-on trial; the main risk is weaker glucose lowering in T1D than in T2D, where incretin drugs have shown smaller HbA1c gains.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance, hypoglycemia during insulin titration, or ketosis in type 1 diabetes could elevate treatment discontinuations and attenuate on-treatment glycemic gains.

sol.r: Insulin optimization and automated delivery could absorb much of the incremental HbA1c benefit even if tirzepatide produces substantial weight loss and insulin-dose reductions.

trials.t: A Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of ALG-000184 Compared With Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate in Untreated HBeAg-Positive and HBeAg- Negative Adult Subjects With Chronic Hepatitis B (B-SUPREME)
trials.ep: Proportion of HBeAg-positive patients with HBV DNA below LLOQ (10 IU/mL, target detected or not detected) at Week 48

fable.r: TDF is a strong comparator and each HBeAg stratum has only about 50 to 60 patients per arm, so a 20-point advantage at the 10 IU/mL cut-off may miss significance, and both strata must succeed.

opus.r: TDF already suppresses HBV DNA in many patients by week 48, and superiority must hold in both HBeAg-positive and HBeAg-negative parts with about 50 per arm each.

sonnet.r: Both parts' primaries must be met; TDF suppresses HBeAg-negative patients near ceiling, so superiority there with about 50 per arm is hard, and no formal hypothesis or margin is stated.

haiku.r: Monotherapy must match TDF on undetectable HBV DNA at week 48 in HBeAg-positive patients, and both co-primary endpoints must be met by the same arm, a high bar at 50 per arm.

carbon.r: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate already achieves high 48-week HBV DNA suppression, especially in HBeAg-negative patients, making superiority across both co-primary cohorts difficult with 50 patients per arm.

sol.r: Both study parts must succeed, and high TDF suppression in HBeAg-negative patients could leave too little separation on the target-not-detected endpoint for the available sample.

trials.t: Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of PA5108 Ocular Implants in Primary Open Angle Glaucoma or Ocular Hypertension
trials.ep: Change in mean diurnal intraocular pressure in the study eye from baseline to week 12.

fable.r: Latanoprost drops lower diurnal IOP by about 7 mmHg, which intracameral prostaglandin implants have at best matched; with 25 per arm neither superiority nor a tight non-inferiority margin is within reach.

opus.r: Daily latanoprost drops are the gold-standard IOP lowerer; a sustained-release latanoprost implant is unlikely to beat it with 25 eyes per arm, and the trial likely aims at comparability, not superiority.

sonnet.r: Latanoprost drops already lower diurnal IOP about 7-8 mmHg; a sustained-release implant is likely comparable rather than superior, and the design hypothesis is not stated.

haiku.r: Latanoprost is a strong IOP-lowering control and at about 25 patients per arm the high-dose implant needs a clear superiority gap; the realistic risk is that it only matches latanoprost.

carbon.r: Daily topical latanoprost 0.005% produces ~7 mmHg diurnal IOP reduction, leaving minimal room for an intracameral latanoprost implant to prove statistical superiority or tight non-inferiority with 25 patients per arm.

sol.r: Sustained prostaglandin delivery should lower IOP, but demonstrating superiority to effective latanoprost drops with about 25 patients per arm is substantially harder than matching their effect.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy Evaluation of GC101 Gene Therapy Via Intrathecal (IT) Injectionin the Treatment of Patients With Type 2 Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) - Phase III
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Hammersmith Functional Motor Scale Expanded (HFMSE) total score at Week 52

fable.r: Controls stay on effective nusinersen, so the gap to gene therapy may be only 1 to 2 HFMSE points, below what 25 patients per arm can detect.

opus.r: Continued nusinersen keeps pretreated type 2 SMA patients stable or slightly improving, so switching to intrathecal gene therapy may add only about 1 HFMSE point, too little to detect with 25 per arm.

sonnet.r: Open-label with 25 per arm in stable, nusinersen-pretreated type 2 SMA; a gain of about 2 HFMSE points over continued nusinersen is plausible but near the detection limit given an SD near 4-5.

haiku.r: Only 25 per arm in a switch design where the control keeps nusinersen; the gain over continued treatment must clear a noisy small-sample threshold, and the trial was still recruiting at launch.

carbon.r: Switching treatment-experienced Type 2 SMA patients from ongoing maintenance nusinersen to intrathecal AAV9 gene therapy leaves a modest incremental motor gain over active standard-of-care control in only 50 patients.

sol.r: Children already benefiting from nusinersen may gain too little additional motor function after SMN gene transfer to establish superiority in a 50-patient trial.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Different Targeted Therapies for Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving ACR50 response at week 12

fable.r: IL-1 inhibition is a weak mechanism in rheumatoid arthritis and the population is biologic-refractory; a 9-point ACR50 gain would not be significant with about 30 to 45 patients per arm.

opus.r: IL-1 blockade has historically had modest efficacy in RA, and in a biologic-refractory population with about 30 per arm a 10-15 point ACR50 gain would not reach significance.

sonnet.r: IL-1alpha/beta blockade has historically weak RA efficacy and 30 per arm needs roughly 30% versus 10% ACR50 for significance in a b/tsDMARD-experienced population.

haiku.r: IL-1 blockade alone tends to give modest RA responses, and about 30 patients per arm makes a monotherapy ACR50 gap over placebo hard to show significantly.

carbon.r: IL-1 blockade has historically shown modest efficacy in rheumatoid arthritis, and 30 patients per arm in biologic-experienced patients provides limited power unless CD40 co-blockade drives a large ACR50 jump.

sol.r: IL-1 blockade may provide insufficient ACR50 improvement in biologic-exposed RA, and the small individual substudies leave little protection against a modest treatment effect.

trials.t: A Phase III Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of HRS9531 Injection in Subjects With Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and Obesity
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at week 52, in patients not on PAP therapy

fable.r: Percent change in AHI is highly variable and only about 70 patients per arm are enrolled; a lower-BMI Chinese population with more anatomical apnea could blunt the weight-loss effect.

opus.r: Percent change in AHI is noisy and skewed, and a sizeable placebo response could shrink the gap, though a GLP-1/GIP agonist producing large weight loss should still clearly separate.

sonnet.r: A dual GLP-1/GIP agonist with large weight loss should cut AHI strongly, as tirzepatide did in SURMOUNT-OSA; the main uncertainty is whether anything is disclosed before mid-2027.

haiku.r: Weight-driven AHI gains from an incretin agent should be large, so the bigger risk is timing: the trial was still recruiting at launch, and a 52-week endpoint cannot read out by June 2027.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal adverse events or loss to follow-up before Week 52 polysomnography could modestly dilute treatment-regimen estimand effects, though class efficacy in obesity-related OSA is very large.

sol.r: OSA in a relatively lower-BMI Chinese population may be less weight-responsive than in SURMOUNT-OSA, while percent AHI change is noisy.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Brivekimig in Adult Participants With Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Proportion achieving clinical remission by modified Mayo Score (0-2, with stool frequency 0-1, rectal bleeding 0, endoscopy 0-1) at week 16

fable.r: With about 35 patients per arm, a 15-point remission gain over placebo is only borderline significant, and prior advanced-therapy failures may blunt a TNF-based drug.

opus.r: With about 35 per arm, a 15-20 point gain in modified Mayo remission gives roughly 50-60% power, and advanced-therapy-experienced patients dilute the anti-TNF component's effect.

sonnet.r: Strict mMS clinical remission with about 35 per arm needs a gap near 20 points; the population includes advanced-therapy-experienced patients where TNF blockade works less well.

haiku.r: With about 35 patients per arm, a clinical-remission gap of about 15 to 17 points is needed for significance, so a real but moderate effect at the highest dose could still miss.

carbon.r: With roughly 35 participants per arm in a mixed advanced-therapy-naive and advanced-therapy-experienced ulcerative colitis population, even an active biologic effect of 15-18 percentage points can miss statistical significance.

sol.r: Even a clinically meaningful remission advantage may not reach significance with roughly 35 patients per arm, particularly if prior advanced-therapy exposure reduces response.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called PF-07275315 in People With Moderate-To-Severe Asthma
trials.ep: Change from baseline in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at Week 12

fable.r: About 50 to 60 patients per arm and an FEV1 SD near 400 mL leave moderate power for a 150 mL effect, and a population not selected for type 2 inflammation may dilute it.

opus.r: Dose-ranging phase 2 with roughly 60-85 patients per arm; a tezepelumab-like FEV1 gain of about 120 mL against a between-patient SD near 380 mL gives only around 50% power per dose, and an early public statement is more likely a pipeline discontinuation than a positive readout.

sonnet.r: Dose-ranging phase 2 with 252 patients over several arms leaves about 50-60 per arm, so even a dupilumab-like 140-200 mL FEV1 gain on top of ICS-LABA has only modest power at the highest dose.

haiku.r: Placebo-adjusted FEV1 gains from add-on asthma drugs are modest, so the highest dose may miss significance; the 252-patient study may not be disclosed by June 2027 unless the result is material.

carbon.r: Improved inhalational controller adherence during clinical trial monitoring in bronchodilator-responsive asthma patients frequently produces large placebo FEV1 gains that increase variance and narrow treatment separation.

sol.r: Absence of a type-2 biomarker entry threshold may dilute lung-function benefit, while improved background-inhaler adherence can produce substantial placebo improvement.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Parallel-group Phase 2 Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of XH-S004 Tablets in Patients With Non-cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis
trials.sp: Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical Industrial Development Co. Ltd.
trials.ep: Time to first pulmonary exacerbation (EMBARC definition) over the 24-week treatment period

fable.r: Only about 55 first exacerbations are expected per dose-versus-placebo comparison, so a true hazard ratio near 0.6 would reach two-sided 0.05 only about half the time.

opus.r: About 78 patients per arm and roughly 50-60 first exacerbations in the 40 mg versus placebo comparison over 24 weeks; even a WILLOW-sized hazard ratio near 0.6 is borderline for significance, and ASPEN showed the class effect on time to first exacerbation can be closer to 0.8.

sonnet.r: With roughly 75-80 patients per arm and about 70-80 exacerbations overall in 24 weeks, a time-to-first-exacerbation primary has limited power unless the DPP1 inhibitor matches brensocatib's WILLOW effect.

haiku.r: Seventy-eight patients per arm give under 50 percent power at a hazard ratio near 0.65, so a significant result is far from assured; Chinese phase 2 results often surface at congresses after June 2027.

carbon.r: A lower-than-expected 24-week exacerbation event rate in the 78-patient placebo group could leave fewer than 55 events per pairwise comparison, reducing power for a ~0.62 hazard ratio.

sol.r: A moderate DPP1-class reduction in exacerbation risk may be real but insufficiently large for significance with only about 60–65 first events in each active-placebo comparison.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Rilzabrutinib in Adult Participants With Graves' Disease
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in FT4 levels

fable.r: Small open-label Sanofi phase 2 needing actively hyperthyroid Graves' patients for 16 weeks; it was still recruiting about 15 weeks before the registered completion date, so some slippage is likely, and Sanofi usually posts results about a year after completion.

opus.r: Small open-label Sanofi phase 2 still recruiting in late 2026 with a February 2027 completion date for a 16-week endpoint; Graves' patients are hard to recruit off standard antithyroid drugs, so the date will likely slip, while termination is possible but unlikely.

sonnet.r: Open-label, single-arm-per-dose phase 2 of 30 patients that is still recruiting in late 2026 against a February 2027 primary completion; Sanofi usually posts results a year after completion, so a posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Small open-label Sanofi study still recruiting at launch against a February 2027 primary completion; a slip past mid-May 2027 is about even, and posted results by August 2027 are unlikely.

carbon.r: Recruiting 30 active Graves' disease patients including an active orbitopathy subset across 24 sites makes a moderate enrollment slip past May 2027 plausible.

sol.r: The small enrollment target and broad site network favor completion, but identifying eligible patients with active Graves' disease could push recruitment beyond the planned date.

trials.t: A Clinical Study to Investigate the Effect of Oral Neflamapimod on Motor Recovery After Acute Ischaemic Stroke
trials.c: Moderate to Severe Acute Ischaemic Stroke; Ischaemic Stroke
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in Fugl-Meyer motor score (upper plus lower extremity, 0-100)

fable.r: Only 45 patients enrolled against three primary outcomes; with a between-patient SD near 17 Fugl-Meyer points the trial can only detect a gain of 10 points or more, and nothing suggests neflamapimod is that strong.

opus.r: Only 45 patients (about 22 per arm) with three co-primary motor outcomes that must all be significant; spontaneous recovery after stroke is large and variable (SD about 14 Fugl-Meyer points), so a p38-alpha inhibitor would need an implausibly large effect.

sonnet.r: About 45 patients in total, large spontaneous motor recovery in the first weeks after stroke, and three motor primary endpoints that all need to be met leave very little chance of a clean win.

haiku.r: Three co-primary superiority tests in about 22 patients per arm, all of which must win, make a positive result very unlikely; the trial is complete, so the open question is whether the sponsor or its collaborator discloses topline by June 2027.

carbon.r: With only 45 enrolled patients, large spontaneous motor recovery variance, and three listed primary outcomes, the trial is severely underpowered unless the true drug effect is unusually large.

sol.r: Large spontaneous motor recovery and substantial patient heterogeneity make it difficult for this small trial to demonstrate concordant benefits across all three primary outcomes.

trials.t: Tibulizumab Skin Healing and Inflammation Evaluation for Lasting Defense
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in abscess and inflammatory nodule (AN) count at Week 16

fable.r: Placebo AN-count reductions in recent HS trials run 25-35% or more; with about 82 per arm, an IL-17A-level effect of roughly 18 points sits only just above the 16 points needed for significance.

opus.r: HS trials have high and variable placebo responses (AN count often falls 25-35% on placebo), and IL-17A blockade alone gives modest separation; with about 82 per arm and a skewed percent-change endpoint (SD near 60%), a placebo-adjusted gain under 15 points would miss.

sonnet.r: Tibulizumab is a BAFF/IL-17A bispecific; IL-17A blockade works in HS, but placebo response in AN count is large and the bispecific's IL-17A potency at the tested doses is uncertain.

haiku.r: Two doses are tested and either meeting the objective counts, which lifts the odds; the risk is that both doses are weaker than the IL-17A and BAFF mechanism suggests, or that the placebo abscess response is high.

carbon.r: Anti-IL-17A/BAFF blockade could show weaker tissue penetration or dose response than dual IL-17A/F inhibition amidst high placebo variability in hidradenitis suppurativa lesion counts.

sol.r: IL-17A blockade is validated in HS, but tibulizumab may not deliver enough additional lesion reduction to overcome variable placebo improvement and dose-comparison multiplicity.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Phase III Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HRS9531 Injection in Subjects With Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and Obesity Who Are on Positive Airway Pressure Ventilation (PAP) Therapy
trials.c: Subjects With Moderate-to-severe OSA and Obesity Who Are on PAP Therapy
trials.ep: Change from baseline in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at week 52, in patients on PAP therapy

fable.r: The effect should be large, so the residual risk is 70 per arm with noisy polysomnography AHI and missing week-52 studies after PAP withdrawal; timing of any public result is the bigger uncertainty.

opus.r: GLP-1/GIP agonism robustly lowers AHI via weight loss; the realistic failure route is heavy missing data at 52 weeks (PSG with PAP pause) or GI-driven dropouts diluting the treatment-policy estimate in a 140-patient trial.

sonnet.r: Weight loss from a GLP-1/GIP agonist cuts AHI strongly (tirzepatide -20 to -24 events/h versus placebo), so success is very likely if reported; the real uncertainty is whether the 52-week result appears before mid-2027.

haiku.r: Incretin-class weight loss should cut AHI strongly, but patients on PAP start with lower residual apnea that compresses the effect; the 52-week endpoint also cannot finish before late 2027 given recruitment still open at launch.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerability or refusal to pause PAP therapy for repeat polysomnography at Week 52 could increase missing data and dilute treatment-regimen AHI estimates.

sol.r: OSA in a lower-BMI Chinese population may have a larger non-weight-mediated component, attenuating the AHI benefit despite substantial weight loss.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Intravitreal KSI-101 in Participants With Macular Edema Secondary to Inflammation (MESI) - PINNACLE
trials.ep: Mean change in best-corrected visual acuity from day 1 to the average of weeks 20 and 24

fable.r: Sham eyes can improve through background or rescue anti-inflammatory therapy and fluctuating edema, and the record's CST band of 320 to under 400 microns with BCVA up to 78 letters leaves limited room for a visual gain over sham.

opus.r: PINNACLE restricts to milder edema (CST 320-400 microns) with baseline vision up to 78 letters, limiting room for BCVA gain, while sham patients may improve on background anti-inflammatory therapy or rescue, shrinking the difference.

sonnet.r: Phase 1b showed double-digit letter gains in macular edema secondary to inflammation, but sham arms can gain several letters and the phase 3 effect usually shrinks versus early single-arm data.

haiku.r: A sham-controlled letter gain of about 6 with 150 per arm clears significance comfortably if the dose is adequate; the doses are not stated and the week 24 readout falls near April to May 2027, so disclosure by June 30 is about even.

carbon.r: Restricting enrollment to milder macular edema (CST 320 to <400 microns, BCVA up to 78 letters) creates visual acuity ceiling effects and allows greater spontaneous sham improvement.

sol.r: Mild edema, relatively good baseline acuity and heterogeneous inflammatory causes could yield too little visual-acuity separation from sham despite anatomical improvement.

trials.t: A Phase III Study to Assess the Effect of AZD0780 on LDL-C in Patients With Clinical ASCVD or at Risk for a First ASCVD Event
trials.ep: Percent change in LDL-C from baseline to week 12

fable.r: A 3,100-patient trial of a drug that halved LDL-C in phase 2b is vastly overpowered; only a conduct, supply or safety surprise, or a reporting quirk, could keep it from meeting the primary objective.

opus.r: Efficacy is near-certain given the phase 2b LDL-C reduction of about 50% and about 1,500 patients per arm; only an unexpected safety finding or major data-integrity issue would derail the primary.

sonnet.r: An oral PCSK9 inhibitor gave about -50% LDL-C versus placebo at 12 weeks in phase 2b; with 3,100 patients, failure on the primary is close to impossible, and the open question is only when AstraZeneca reports.

haiku.r: An oral PCSK9 inhibitor on top of high-intensity statins should halve LDL-C with about 1,550 per arm, so the result is near certain if the dose is adequate; the dose is unstated ('xx mg') and disclosure timing before June 2027 is the other uncertainty.

carbon.r: Only an unexpected off-target safety signal halting the trial could prevent this 3,103-patient PCSK9 inhibitor study from achieving statistical significance on Week 12 LDL-C.

sol.r: An unexpected longer-term tolerability problem causing extensive treatment discontinuation is more credible than statistical failure of LDL lowering in this very large trial.

trials.t: A Phase III Study to Assess the Effect of AZD0780 on LDL-C in Patients With HeFH
trials.ep: Percent change in LDL-C from baseline to week 12

fable.r: PCSK9 inhibition works as well in HeFH as elsewhere and about 470 patients give essentially full power for a roughly 50-point LDL-C difference; only a conduct, safety or reporting surprise could cause a miss.

opus.r: PCSK9 inhibition works in heterozygous FH because LDL receptors are partly functional; with about 470 patients randomized 2:1 and an expected 45% placebo-adjusted reduction, only an unforeseen safety or conduct problem would cause a miss.

sonnet.r: Oral PCSK9 inhibition works in HeFH with intact LDL receptors; a 473-patient 2:1 trial should show a large LDL-C reduction, so the open question is only when AstraZeneca reports.

haiku.r: The same oral PCSK9 inhibitor in HeFH with 315 treated versus 158 placebo gives a near-certain LDL-C result if the dose is adequate; the unstated dose and whether AstraZeneca discloses the topline before June 2027 are the open questions.

carbon.r: An unforeseen idiosyncratic safety issue is the only plausible failure mode given robust PCSK9-mediated LDLR upregulation in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia.

sol.r: Unexpected adverse effects forcing substantial discontinuation are the main residual threat, since ordinary variation in HeFH response should not erase a large PCSK9-mediated LDL reduction.

trials.t: RE104 Safety and Efficacy Study in Adjustment Disorder in Cancer and Other Medical Illnesses
trials.ep: RE104 30 mg versus RE104 1.5 mg change from baseline in MADRS total score

fable.r: A single-dose psychedelic trial in medically ill patients with adjustment disorder was still recruiting in the month before its registered completion date, so a slip of a few months is about as likely as not; posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

opus.r: Small-sponsor psychedelic phase 2 still recruiting one month before its registered primary completion; a 7-day endpoint keeps the tail short, but enrolment of medically ill adjustment-disorder patients usually runs a few months past plan.

sonnet.r: Single-dose RE104 trial in adjustment disorder with 100 patients across 32 US sites is still recruiting about 15 months after start. Registered primary completion of Nov 2026 looks tight for cancer and neurological patients, so a slip past Feb 2027 is more likely than not. Private sponsor, so results posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Still recruiting at launch against a November 2026 end date, so a slip past February 2027 is the likeliest registry outcome; termination is unlikely and posting is uncertain.

carbon.r: Enrolling 100 medically ill cancer or neurodegenerative patients meeting strict psychedelic screening rules leaves substantial risk of recruiting past February 2027.

sol.r: The day-7 endpoint permits rapid completion after enrollment, but medical comorbidity, prohibited medications and supervised psychedelic dosing could prolong recruitment.

trials.t: Safety Study of Viaskin® Peanut Patch in Peanut-Allergic Children 1 Through 3 Years of Age (COMFORT Toddlers)
trials.ep: DBPC Treatment Period: Adverse Events (AEs), Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs), and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the 6-month blinded period ends on a fixed schedule that the sponsor needs for its planned filing in toddlers, so a slip of more than 90 days is unlikely; results posting is not due until late 2027.

opus.r: Enrolment is closed and the 6-month double-blind period should finish close to the registered November 2026 date; the study supports DBV's toddler BLA, so stopping is unlikely and posting is likely to come near the 12-month deadline.

sonnet.r: Enrolment is complete (active, not recruiting) and the primary period is only 6 months, so the Nov 2026 primary completion should hold. The record also contains a long open-label extension, and a public sponsor usually posts results later, so posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Active and not recruiting with a registered primary completion in November 2026, so late risk comes from a date update rather than enrolment; stopping is unlikely and posting most likely follows the 12-month results deadline.

carbon.r: Because enrollment of all 480 toddlers is already complete and the blinded safety period lasts 6 months, primary completion is likely on schedule or only briefly delayed.

sol.r: Completed recruitment and a six-month primary safety period favor on-time primary completion, while the optional extension can continue without delaying that milestone.

trials.t: Low-dose Carbon Monoxide (HBI-002) Trial to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Biomarkers in Parkinson's Disease
trials.ep: Frequency and severity of treatment-emergent AEs related to HBI-002 compared to placebo.

fable.r: A small sponsor planned only six months from first patient to primary completion for 36 patients at 8 sites with strict eligibility (non-smoking household, BMI under 30, early PD on levodopa), so a slip past March 2027 is more likely than not.

opus.r: Recruiting 36 Parkinson's patients from mid-2026 across 8 US sites with a December 2026 completion date is ambitious; slippage past March 2027 is more likely than not.

sonnet.r: Small 36-patient, 14-day safety study started June 2026 at 8 US sites with strict criteria (non-smokers, BMI under 30, stable levodopa). Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with primary completion Dec 2026, so a slip beyond Mar 2027 is about a coin flip. Small sponsor and academic collaborators rarely post results within months.

haiku.r: Recruiting at launch against a December 2026 completion date, so a slip past March 2027 is the likeliest outcome; the small private sponsor adds termination risk and posting is uncertain.

carbon.r: Enrolling 36 Parkinson's patients across 8 academic sites within 6 months of study start under strict weight, non-smoking, and contraception criteria will likely slip past March 2027.

sol.r: The short exposure and small sample favor completion, but restrictive eligibility and multicenter startup could extend an aggressive six-month recruitment-and-follow-up schedule.

trials.t: A Study to Compare Uliledlimab Combined With Sintilimab and Chemotherapy Versus Sintilimab Combined With Chemotherapy in Patients With Previously Untreated Locally Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review

fable.r: CD73 blockade has not yet shown a clear randomized benefit, and 150 patients give power only for a hazard ratio near 0.67, beyond what an add-on in an unselected population is likely to deliver.

opus.r: Adding an anti-CD73 antibody to PD-1 plus chemotherapy in an unselected first-line NSCLC population has no positive randomized precedent, and with about 95 PFS events only a hazard ratio near 0.67 or better would reach two-sided significance.

sonnet.r: Anti-CD73 add-on to PD-1 plus chemotherapy has a weak track record in unselected NSCLC, and a 150-patient randomized phase 2 with about 95 PFS events needs HR below roughly 0.67 for significance.

haiku.r: The control is a strong PD-1 chemotherapy regimen, and an add-on antibody needs a hazard ratio near 0.67 to reach significance with about 110 events; add-on combinations rarely deliver that much.

carbon.r: Adding CD73 blockade in unselected first-line non-squamous NSCLC without enriching for high CD73 expression is unlikely to yield a large enough hazard ratio improvement over sintilimab plus chemotherapy for N=150 to reach statistical significance.

sol.r: CD73 blockade may add too little to an already effective immunochemotherapy backbone for a 150-patient trial to establish a significant PFS improvement.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of KDS2010 in Overweight or Obese Patients
trials.ep: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to Week 12

fable.r: A MAO-B inhibitor is unlikely to produce the 2.5 to 3 point placebo-adjusted weight loss needed for significance with 22 versus 11 patients over 12 weeks.

opus.r: A reversible MAO-B inhibitor has no proven weight-loss effect in humans; with 22 versus 11 patients over 12 weeks, the 240 mg dose would need about 2.5 points of placebo-adjusted loss to reach significance.

sonnet.r: A 12-week study of a novel MAO-B inhibitor with only 22 vs 11 patients at the top dose can detect only a difference of about 2.3 percentage points of body weight, while the plausible true effect is smaller.

haiku.r: Only a large drug effect can clear significance with 22 versus 11 patients and a spread near 3 percentage points, and the staged design leaves little time before a June 2027 readout.

carbon.r: Reversible MAO-B inhibition reduced weight in rodent models via astrocytic GABA modulation, but non-incretin central metabolic mechanisms rarely translate into clinically meaningful 12-week human weight loss.

sol.r: MAO-B inhibition may not produce enough additional human weight loss over the structured lifestyle intervention to separate reliably in these small dose cohorts.

trials.t: A Clinical Trial for Participants With DEE to Assess Efficacy, Safety, Tolerability, and PK of Relutrigine
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in monthly motor seizure frequency over the 16-week treatment period

fable.r: The broad, mixed-aetiology DEE population may dilute the effect seen in SCN2A and SCN8A patients, leaving about 53 patients per arm short of power.

opus.r: EMERALD enrols a broad, mixed DEE population rather than the SCN2A/SCN8A gain-of-function patients where relutrigine looked strongest; syndromes that respond poorly to sodium-channel drugs could dilute the effect below significance.

sonnet.r: Enrolment spans heterogeneous developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, so a mix of etiologies may dilute the effect of a sodium channel blocker, and placebo response and seizure variability are high.

haiku.r: Sodium-channel blockade is a plausible mechanism in these epilepsies, but a noisy 16-week seizure-frequency endpoint in a mixed population can show a modest effect, and a smaller true effect is the likeliest miss.

carbon.r: Broadening enrollment from genetically defined gain-of-function SCN2A/SCN8A encephalopathies to heterogeneous developmental and epileptic encephalopathies may dilute the strong anticonvulsant effect of persistent sodium current blockade.

sol.r: The seizure benefit seen in an initially genotype-enriched program may attenuate across the much more heterogeneous DEE population enrolled in EMERALD.

trials.t: A Research Study to Look at How Well CagriSema Helps People Living With Obesity Lose Weight and Maintain Weight Loss in the Long-term
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to Week 80

fable.r: Failure is very unlikely; the only realistic routes are an operational problem or heavy dropout rather than lack of effect.

opus.r: Superiority over placebo on percent weight change at 80 weeks is near certain; the only realistic threat is very high discontinuation diluting the treatment-policy estimate, which would still leave a large significant difference.

sonnet.r: Failure is very unlikely: CagriSema produced about 17-20 points more weight loss than placebo in REDEFINE 1, and this trial has 609 patients. Main uncertainty is only the size of the effect and the timing of disclosure.

haiku.r: Efficacy against placebo is very likely given the REDEFINE program; the realistic failure route is a tolerability or dropout problem that dilutes the 80-week weight loss, not a missed hypothesis.

carbon.r: Only unexpected severe safety findings or extreme gastrointestinal treatment discontinuations could threaten significance, given CagriSema's ~20% weight-loss separation over placebo.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance and treatment discontinuation could attenuate weight loss, although the established effect is far larger than needed to beat placebo.

trials.t: ATI-045 Versus Placebo in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at Week 24

fable.r: TSLP blockade failed with tezepelumab in atopic dermatitis, and the strong open-label phase 2a signal may shrink against a week-24 placebo improvement of about 35%.

opus.r: Anti-TSLP blockade has been weak in atopic dermatitis (tezepelumab missed); with 55 patients per arm, ATI-045 needs about a 15-point placebo-adjusted EASI reduction to win.

sonnet.r: Anti-TSLP antibodies have shown weak efficacy in atopic dermatitis (tezepelumab phase 2a), so a mean EASI difference of at least about 15 points with 55 per arm may not be reached.

haiku.r: A novel systemic mechanism at an undisclosed dose, tested at 55 per arm, needs an EASI gap of roughly 14 points to reach significance; a smaller true effect is the likeliest reason for a miss.

carbon.r: Upstream TSLP blockade previously failed to achieve robust efficacy in randomized atopic dermatitis trials with tezepelumab, and N=110 leaves limited power for a moderate effect size.

sol.r: The encouraging uncontrolled bosakitug signal may regress under blinding, and TSLP blockade has not consistently delivered strong efficacy in atopic dermatitis.

trials.t: A 16-week Trial to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Delgocitinib Cream 20 mg/g in Adult Participants With Mild to Severe Palmoplantar Pustulosis
trials.ep: Proportion of participants achieving PPPASI-75 (at least 75% improvement in PPPASI from baseline) at week 16

fable.r: Topical JAK inhibition is untested in palmoplantar pustulosis, and PPPASI-75 at 16 weeks is a high bar that may leave the gap over vehicle below the roughly 13 points needed.

opus.r: Palmoplantar pustulosis is refractory, and a topical pan-JAK cream has to cross thick palm and sole skin and act on an IL-36/IL-17-driven process; with about 67 per arm, it needs roughly a 13-14 point PPPASI-75 gain over vehicle.

sonnet.r: Topical JAK inhibition is unproven in palmoplantar pustulosis, a mainly IL-17/IL-23-driven disease with thick skin that limits penetration, and a 68 vs 67 proof-of-concept needs a difference of about 13 points on PPPASI-75.

haiku.r: Topical JAK inhibition may help this severe, pustular disease, but a 16-week vehicle-controlled responder test with 68 per arm needs a gap of about 20 points to reach significance, and the effect may be smaller.

carbon.r: Topical pan-JAK inhibition may struggle to penetrate hyperkeratotic palmoplantar pustular lesions deeply enough to achieve PPPASI-75 in a notoriously treatment-refractory neutrophil-driven dermatosis.

sol.r: Topical pan-JAK inhibition may not adequately suppress the deeper, pustular inflammation of PPP to produce enough stringent PPPASI-75 responses.

trials.t: A Recovery and Lifespan Study Using INTERCEPT Red Blood Cells Prepared Using the INTERCEPT Blood System for RBCs With AS-1
trials.ep: The percentage of infused 35-day-old autologous 51Cr-labeled Test/INTERCEPT or Control RBCs remaining in circulation 24 hours post-infusion

fable.r: Recruitment still open six weeks before the registered completion date makes a slip likely, but the study should finish in 2027.

opus.r: A two-site radiolabelled recovery study needing 120 healthy donors, each with a 35-day storage cycle, is still recruiting just before its December 2026 completion date; moderate slippage is likely, but the study supports Cerus's INTERCEPT RBC PMA, so a stop is unlikely.

sonnet.r: A 120-subject radiolabeled red cell recovery study at 2 sites is still recruiting with primary completion registered for Dec 2026. Each subject needs a 35-day storage cycle plus radioisotope work, so recruitment typically drifts. The sponsor is a motivated public company that wants the data for a regulatory filing, so a slip is likely but not certain to exceed 90 days.

haiku.r: Still recruiting at launch against a December 2026 end date with only two sites, so a late completion is the likeliest registry outcome; termination is unlikely.

carbon.r: Enrolling 120 healthy donors across just two US sites for 35-day blood storage and dual 51Cr/99mTc radiolabeled red cell infusions faces substantial logistical bottlenecks, making a >90-day completion delay likely.

sol.r: Healthy-volunteer recruitment is feasible, but two specialized sites and 35-day storage plus serial radiolabel follow-up make modest delays more likely than early termination.

trials.t: REGN7508 Versus Apixaban and Enoxaparin for Thromboprophylaxis After Total Knee Arthroplasty in Adults
trials.ep: Incidence of asymptomatic or symptomatic venous thromboembolism, including VTE-related death, through the Day 12 visit after total knee arthroplasty

fable.r: The risk is not enoxaparin but the hypothesis: if the primary also requires superiority over apixaban, whose VTE rate is about 12-15%, the margin is much thinner.

opus.r: If enoxaparin is dosed US-style (30 mg twice daily) at many sites or venography adequacy is poor, the control VTE rate and evaluable numbers shrink, though FXI antibodies have repeatedly cut venographic VTE by 60-80% vs enoxaparin.

sonnet.r: Factor XI mAb with strong phase 2 signal against enoxaparin in TKA; risk is a smaller-than-hoped effect, a hierarchical testing structure (apixaban non-inferiority/superiority) or an enoxaparin arm that performs better than historical venography rates.

haiku.r: Main risk is that the antibody's Factor XI suppression is too weak to beat enoxaparin on VTE detected by venography; the registered February 2027 primary completion makes a June 2027 readout likely but not certain.

carbon.r: While superiority over enoxaparin is strongly supported by Factor XI class data, co-primary or gated testing against apixaban—a much stronger comparator than enoxaparin—is the primary hurdle.

sol.r: Failure is most likely if this antibody's incremental antithrombotic effect, particularly against apixaban, is smaller than the strong class signal against enoxaparin.

trials.t: A Study Comparing KB803 and Matched Placebo in Patients With Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
trials.c: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa; DEB - Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa; Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
trials.ep: Average number of days per month with corneal abrasion symptoms (weekly diary) during each 12-week crossover treatment period

fable.r: With 16 patients and no washout, carryover of the active effect into the placebo period and noisy diary data could leave a real effect short of significance.

opus.r: Sixteen patients in a two-period crossover with a noisy diary endpoint (days with abrasion symptoms) and episodic events; placebo lubrication effects and possible carryover leave little power unless the effect is large.

sonnet.r: Only 16 patients in a diary-based symptom crossover; placebo response, period effects and high between-patient variance can hide a real effect of ophthalmic B-VEC, though the within-patient design helps.

haiku.r: With 16 patients the crossover is underpowered for a days-per-month difference; a clear diary signal is needed for significance and rare-disease diaries are noisy.

carbon.r: Durable Type VII collagen deposition in the corneal basement membrane from Period 1 KB803 treatment could carry over into Period 2 placebo weeks, blunting the within-patient crossover contrast in N=16.

sol.r: Persistent collagen VII benefit after crossover may improve the placebo period, diluting the treatment contrast in a small, diary-based trial.

trials.t: This is a Multi-centre, Multi-drug, Platform Study in Chinese Participants Living With Obesity / Overweight
trials.ep: Numbers of participant with Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious adverse events (SAEs) (sub-study 1).

fable.r: The trial is past its primary completion date and should close as completed, with results posting due only in October 2027.

opus.r: Small AstraZeneca China platform study; enrolment of 16 versus about 48 planned suggests sub-study 2 may be dropped, which could lead to a terminated status or removal of its primary outcome, while results posting follows AZ's 12-month policy.

sonnet.r: Small safety/PK platform study in China with primary completion already passed; AstraZeneca usually posts results around 12 months after completion, so posting by August 2027 is possible but not likely.

haiku.r: Platform study with safety-only primary outcomes; primary completion passed in October 2026, so it is likely complete, but Chinese phase 2 sponsors often post results late.

carbon.r: With recruitment finished and registered study completion in October 2026, this small Phase 2a AstraZeneca platform study should conclude cleanly with moderate probability of ClinicalTrials.gov results posting within ten months.

sol.r: Small completed-dose cohorts favor routine close-out, but enrollment well below the platform description raises a modest chance that a substudy is dropped.

trials.t: A Clinical Trial to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Xeomin® Injections for Preventing Episodic Migraine
trials.ep: Change in monthly migraine days from baseline (28 days before baseline) to Month 6 (weeks 21-24 after first injection)

fable.r: Earlier onabotulinumtoxinA trials in episodic migraine were negative, so the true gain over a large injection-placebo response may be about half a migraine day, less than 332 per arm can detect reliably.

opus.r: Botulinum toxin has repeatedly failed to separate from placebo in episodic migraine, and injection trials carry a large placebo response at month 6, so the true effect of Xeomin may be under 1 day per month.

sonnet.r: Botulinum toxin has historically failed or been marginal in episodic migraine; placebo response is large with 6-14 migraine days at baseline, so a roughly 0.8 day separation may not reach significance.

haiku.r: Episodic migraine has a large placebo response, and botulinum toxin prophylaxis has a weak record in episodic disease, so the trial needs about a one-day difference at Month 6.

carbon.r: Botulinum toxin type A injections have repeatedly shown minimal or no superiority over placebo in episodic migraine trials despite efficacy in chronic migraine.

sol.r: Botulinum toxin efficacy is much less established in episodic than chronic migraine, so even this large, higher-frequency population may show insufficient placebo-adjusted benefit.

trials.t: A Clinical Trial to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Xeomin® Injections for Preventing Chronic Migraine
trials.ep: Change in monthly migraine days from baseline (28 days before baseline) to Month 6 (weeks 21-24 after first injection)

fable.r: The injection-placebo response in chronic migraine is large (about 6 days) and the toxin's margin is modest (1.5-2 days), so an effect slightly smaller than in PREEMPT would leave 269 per arm short.

opus.r: Chronic migraine injection trials show a large placebo response at month 6 (around 5-6 migraine days), which can erode the roughly 1.5-2 day difference seen with onabotulinumtoxinA in PREEMPT.

sonnet.r: Botulinum toxin A is an established chronic migraine preventive; main failure routes are a large placebo response or Dose A being the lower dose with a smaller effect than PREEMPT-like 1.5-2 days.

haiku.r: Botulinum toxin has an approved chronic migraine effect, but the margin over placebo is modest, and the size of the Xeomin difference will decide significance.

carbon.r: Multi-site cranial placebo injections induce large reductions of 6 or more monthly migraine days in chronic migraine, which can narrow the treatment difference.

sol.r: The toxin class is validated in chronic migraine, but large placebo improvements and uncertain Dose A exposure could leave a smaller separation than in PREEMPT.

trials.t: A Study of SKB518 in Patients With Lung Cancer
trials.ep: AE

fable.r: A multi-arm open-label phase 2 still recruiting four months before its registered primary completion date will probably run past it; no results posting is expected from this Chinese sponsor.

opus.r: Chinese multi-cohort ADC phase 2 still recruiting in late 2026 with a February 2027 primary completion; cohort expansions usually push dates out, and Chinese sponsors rarely post CT.gov results.

sonnet.r: Chinese multi-arm phase 2 with 192 patients still recruiting; registry dates often slip and arms or outcomes (ORR/PFS in specific arms) may be refined, but a China-only sponsor rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

haiku.r: Open-label single-arm phase 2 with three primary outcomes, recruiting at launch against a February 2027 primary completion; a later date or continued recruitment is likely, and a Chinese sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.

carbon.r: Because the 192-patient multi-cohort lung cancer study is still recruiting fewer than four months before its February 2027 registered primary completion date, completion will likely slip by more than 90 days.

sol.r: Continued cohort recruitment and lengthy PFS and safety assessments make an extension more likely than timely completion or early registry results posting.

trials.t: Monthly Dosing of Atacicept in IgAN
trials.ep: Evaluate the effect of atacicept on Gd-IgA1 in patients with IgAN

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the 24-week readout has passed, so the trial should complete; results are not due on ClinicalTrials.gov until about September 2027.

opus.r: Small open-label Vera dosing study, active not recruiting with primary completion around September 2026; likely to complete normally, with results posting due near September 2027, so posting by end-August 2027 is possible but not the base case.

sonnet.r: Exploratory open-label dosing-regimen study with primary completion Sep 2026; Vera will likely post within the 12-month window ending around Sep 2027, so posting before end-August 2027 is possible but not the default.

haiku.r: Open-label phase 2 whose primary completion date of September 2026 has passed; the sponsor is a listed company likely to post results, and the Gd-IgA1 primary is unlikely to change in substance.

carbon.r: With enrollment completed and the 24-week primary biomarker period passed, this open-label atacicept dosing study should proceed smoothly through its September 2027 completion without posted results before August 2027.

sol.r: Closed enrollment and a past scheduled biomarker completion favor continued safety follow-up, with registry posting more uncertain than completion.

trials.t: A Phase III Trial of HRS-1893 in Patients With Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
trials.ep: Clinical response rate (criteria not defined in record) after 24 weeks of treatment

fable.r: The response criterion is undefined in the record; a strict composite or cautious echo-guided titration could shrink the gap, though myosin inhibitors have large, consistent effects in obstructive HCM.

opus.r: The response definition is not public; if it requires a stringent composite (e.g. gradient below 30 mmHg plus NYHA class I) or LVEF-driven dose interruptions are frequent, the difference could shrink, though cardiac myosin inhibitors have shown large gradient effects.

sonnet.r: Cardiac myosin inhibitors have repeatedly beaten placebo in obstructive HCM with large effects; residual risk comes from the undefined response criteria and a high placebo response rate in a Chinese population.

haiku.r: The record does not define the response criteria, so the chosen definition and the 24-week readout drive the outcome; the cardiac myosin inhibitor class has strong precedent in obstructive HCM.

carbon.r: If the unspecified clinical response definition relies heavily on cardiopulmonary exercise testing, background beta-blocker blunting of peak heart rate could attenuate the responder difference.

sol.r: The class strongly reduces obstruction, but the undisclosed clinical-response definition may require exercise or symptom gains beyond gradient reduction.

trials.t: A Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Ninerafaxstat in Patients With Symptomatic Non-obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in KCCQ Clinical Summary Score (0-100, higher is better)

fable.r: The KCCQ benefit in IMPROVE-HCM came from a post hoc subgroup, so the true effect may be 3-4 points against a needed observed gap of about 4.3 with a sizeable placebo improvement.

opus.r: Non-obstructive HCM has resisted symptom-endpoint wins (mavacamten failed ODYSSEY-HCM); a metabolic modulator over 12 weeks may shift KCCQ-CSS only a few points against an SD near 15, below what 82 per arm can detect.

sonnet.r: A metabolic modulator in nHCM has shown only small, noisy KCCQ gains versus a sizeable placebo response, and mavacamten failed in nHCM; a 12-week KCCQ endpoint needs about 5 points to reach significance with 83 per arm.

haiku.r: 165 patients split across two arms give little power for a 4 to 5 point KCCQ gap; with recruitment ongoing at launch, the 12-week primary may not read out until after June 2027.

carbon.r: Metabolic modulators and other pharmacotherapies have repeatedly failed to significantly improve KCCQ symptom scores over strong placebo responses in non-obstructive HCM.

sol.r: Earlier symptom benefits were most persuasive in a subgroup, and substantial placebo KCCQ improvement could erase separation in this modest-sized study.

trials.t: A Study of Prusogliptin Tablets Combined With Dapagliflozin Tablets and Metformin Hydrochloride Extended Release Tablets in Type 2 Diabetes
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24

fable.r: Dapagliflozin plus metformin already lowers HbA1c by about 1 point, leaving a DPP-4 inhibitor add-on effect of roughly 0.3-0.5 that must also beat the prusogliptin dual arm.

opus.r: Adding a DPP-4 inhibitor on top of an SGLT2 inhibitor plus metformin gives a modest incremental HbA1c drop (about 0.3-0.5%); a smaller-than-expected add-on effect is the only realistic path to failure with 163 per arm.

sonnet.r: A DPP-4 inhibitor added to dapagliflozin plus metformin reliably lowers HbA1c by about 0.4-0.6 points; the main uncertainty is the multi-arm comparison structure and whether this exact contrast is the tested primary.

haiku.r: Adding a DPP-4 inhibitor to dapagliflozin and metformin usually gives a further drop of about 0.4 to 0.7 points, so the risk is a small increment; 163 per arm is enough to see a 0.5 point difference.

carbon.r: Because dual therapy with dapagliflozin plus metformin already lowers HbA1c by nearly 1%, multiple co-primary comparisons across five arms slightly compress margin for error.

sol.r: Dapagliflozin plus optimized metformin may lower HbA1c enough to leave only a small incremental prusogliptin effect, especially at lower baseline HbA1c.

trials.t: A Phase II, Placebo Controlled, Clinical Trial of Topical TolaSure Targeting Aggregated Mutant Keratin in Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
trials.ep: Change from baseline in blister surface area of the target lesional area after 2 months of randomized treatment, by clinical photography

fable.r: Twenty per arm, a mixed EBS population and a fluctuating photographic blister-area endpoint over 2 months make a statistically significant primary result unlikely even if the gel has some effect.

opus.r: Forty patients with flare-driven, highly variable blister area and natural regression of flares give little power to show a significant 2-month difference against placebo gel.

sonnet.r: Only 20 per arm with a photo-based blister area endpoint in a heterogeneous rare skin disease; a topical keratin-aggregate targeting gel needs a large effect to reach p<0.05 against a vehicle that also soothes skin.

haiku.r: Forty patients split 20 and 20 on a photographed blister-area change with no stated scale gives little power to show a significant gap, which is the most likely way this trial fails.

carbon.r: With only 20 patients per arm across heterogeneous localized and generalized EBS subtypes, spontaneous blister fluctuation and vehicle gel effects will likely obscure modest topical efficacy.

sol.r: Only 20 patients per arm, mixed EBS phenotypes, and enrollment during a flare create substantial noise and regression to the mean in photographed blister area.

trials.t: Study to Assess Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of a Nail Patch in Patients With Nail Fragility, Mychosis, Psoriasis
trials.ep: Evaluation, based on adverse events numeber of the Multi-Function Hydrogel Nail Patch safety in adult humans affected by Fragility Nails, Onychomycosis and Nail Psoriasis

fable.r: A small single-centre cosmetic patch study is likely to finish somewhat late or leave its record stale, and is unlikely to post results.

opus.r: Single-site Italian cosmetic-patch study by a small sponsor that is still listed as recruiting past the point needed for a November 2026 completion; records like this are often left stale or extended, and results posting is improbable.

sonnet.r: Single-centre Italian cosmetic nail patch study with a safety primary; likely to finish roughly on time, but the record may simply not be updated and no results posting is expected from this sponsor/CRO.

haiku.r: A single-centre Italian nail-patch study of 72 patients, still recruiting at launch against a November 2026 completion date, is more likely to show a registry date past February 2027, or still recruiting in August 2027, than to finish on time.

carbon.r: Still recruiting 72 patients at a single Italian clinic right before its November 2026 registered primary completion date, this 4-month follow-up nail patch trial will likely finish more than 90 days late.

sol.r: The short, low-risk cosmetic study is feasible, but single-center recruitment and limited registry maintenance make delay and non-posting relatively likely.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About Medicine Called Ritlecitinib in Children Aged Between 6 to 12 Years With Severe Alopecia Areata
trials.ep: Proportion of children aged 6 to under 12 with severe alopecia areata achieving absolute SALT score ≤20 at week 24

fable.r: With about 69 per arm, two doses and two region-specific primaries (SALT 20 or less, and the stricter SALT 10 or less), a modest response in children with extensive loss could leave one analysis short.

opus.r: Both region-specific primaries likely need to succeed; the EU/UK SALT<=10 analysis, with low absolute response rates in a treatment-refractory subset of about 69 per arm, is the weaker link, though near-zero placebo regrowth leaves margin.

sonnet.r: Children 6 to <12 with severe AA, many with AT/AU, may respond less than adolescents; a lower-than-expected SALT<=20 or <=10 rate on the higher dose is the main way this misses.

haiku.r: The main risk is a weaker response in children than adults show at the higher dose; at 69 per arm the trial still has high power for a gap of about 20 points, so a miss would mean a small effect rather than an underpowered test.

carbon.r: Achieving the stringent EU/UK SALT <=10 complete hair regrowth threshold by Week 24 with ~69 children per arm carries modest risk if many participants have baseline alopecia totalis or universalis.

sol.r: The main residual efficacy risk is insufficiently complete regrowth by week 24 to satisfy both regional SALT thresholds in this younger population.

trials.t: A Study to Assess Safety and Effectiveness of HArmonyCa Lidocaine Injectable Gel for Restoration and/or Creation of Mid-Face Volume in Adult Participants
trials.ep: Share of participants with at least 1-point MFVDS improvement on evaluating investigator live assessment at month 6

fable.r: The non-inferiority margin is not in the record; with 2:1 allocation and 252 patients, a 10-point margin leaves only moderate power unless HArmonyCa's month-6 responder rate is at least equal to Perlane's.

opus.r: Perlane Lidocaine is an effective approved volumiser, so the trial succeeds only as non-inferiority; if the hidden hypothesis were superiority, or the margin unusually tight, the high comparator responder rate would sink it.

sonnet.r: If it misses, it is most likely a non-inferiority shortfall of the HA/CaHA filler against Perlane at month 6 or a tight margin, but registration-style China filler trials usually succeed.

haiku.r: The main risk is a strict or unstated non-inferiority margin on a subjective live-assessment scale, although with both arms likely near 85 percent responders a typical margin should be met easily.

carbon.r: Restylane Perlane achieves very high 6-month MFVDS responder rates, so modest random variation or a tight non-inferiority margin could cause the lower confidence bound to miss.

sol.r: Both fillers should perform well, but near-ceiling Perlane response and an undisclosed non-inferiority margin leave some risk of an inconclusive comparison.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Study of D-2570 in Subjects With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.c: UC - Ulcerative Colitis; Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Share of participants in clinical remission by modified Mayo score (SF ≤1 with ≥1-point drop, RB 0, ES ≤1) at Week 12

fable.r: Selective TYK2 inhibition failed in ulcerative colitis with deucravacitinib, and a 120-patient trial split across dose groups may miss a moderate remission gain over placebo.

opus.r: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition has failed in UC (deucravacitinib LATTICE-UC), so even a more potent molecule may give only a modest remission gain that about 60 per arm cannot resolve.

sonnet.r: TYK2 inhibition has a weak track record in ulcerative colitis, and with about 60 per arm a placebo remission rate near 8% means the drug needs roughly 22-25% remission to reach significance.

haiku.r: Sixty per arm gives borderline power for a remission difference of about 15 points, so a real but modest effect could miss significance, and a placebo remission near 7 percent leaves little room if the drug is weaker than the class precedent.

carbon.r: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition previously failed to induce Week 12 remission in ulcerative colitis (deucravacitinib LATTICE-UC), leaving target efficacy in gut mucosa uncertain.

sol.r: Without an established UC efficacy signal, D-2570 may produce less remission benefit than the fairly large difference needed in approximately 60 patients per arm.

trials.t: A Study to Find Out Whether BI 765423 Has an Effect on Lung Function in People With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) With or Without Standard Treatment
trials.ep: Absolute change from baseline in forced vital capacity (mL) at Week 12
