fable.r: An 81-patient, 12-week trial can only show a significant FVC difference if the observed gain is near 80 mL, and IL-11 blockade has no clinical proof in fibrosis yet.

opus.r: A 12-week FVC endpoint with about 40 per arm needs a roughly 60 mL effect to reach significance, larger than most antifibrotic candidates show over 3 monthly infusions.

sonnet.r: Only about 40 per arm and a 12-week FVC change with SD around 150 mL means a difference of roughly 65 mL is needed for significance, which a novel IL-11 pathway antibody may not deliver.

haiku.r: With 40 per arm and an FVC change SD near 160 mL, significance needs a gap of about 70 mL by week 12, well above the roughly 30 mL that nintedanib adds over that period, so only a large effect would pass.

carbon.r: With 81 IPF patients mostly on background antifibrotics over just 12 weeks, FVC variability (~190 mL SD) requires a >80 mL effect to achieve two-sided p<0.05.

sol.r: With only 81 patients and 12 weeks of follow-up, a clinically credible slowing of FVC decline may still be too small relative to measurement variability to reach significance.

trials.t: C-Forward: Efficacy and Safety of BEM/RZR vs SOF/VEL in Subjects With Chronic HCV
trials.c: HEPATITIS C VIRUS CHRONIC INFECTION; Hepatitis C, Chronic; Hepatitis C Virus Infection
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with HCV RNA below the lower limit of quantitation at week 24

fable.r: A shorter 8-week regimen may relapse more in genotype 3, cirrhotic or non-adherent patients, and a deficit of 2-3 points against SOF/VEL would breach a margin of about 5 points.

opus.r: The 8-week BEM/RZR course could relapse more often than 12-week SOF/VEL in genotype 3 or cirrhotic patients common in the ex-North America sites, pushing the lower bound past the margin.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority could fail if shorter-duration BEM/RZR underperforms in genotype 3 or cirrhosis, or if losses to follow-up at ex-US sites depress the ITT cure rate in one arm.

haiku.r: The risk is that bemnifosbuvir-ruzasvir lands a few points below sofosbuvir-velpatasvir in the cirrhosis or genotype 3 groups, which would matter only if the non-inferiority margin is tight, since neither arm is likely to fall far below 95 percent.

carbon.r: Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir achieves ~96-98% cure rates, so slightly higher genotype 3 relapse or open-label loss to follow-up on BEM/RZR could breach a tight non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: A small excess of relapse with the experimental regimen, particularly in genotype 3 or compensated cirrhosis, is the main threat to non-inferiority against a highly effective comparator.

trials.t: A Study Comparing the Effect and Safety of Linaprazan Glurate to Lansoprazole in Participants With Erosive Esophagitis (EE) Due to Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
trials.ep: Endoscopic healing of erosive esophagitis at week 4 in participants with baseline Los Angeles grade C/D

fable.r: The primary analysis is limited to LA grade C/D patients, a fraction of the 523 enrolled, so a true 15-20 point healing gain over lansoprazole at week 4 could miss significance.

opus.r: If lansoprazole heals most LA C/D lesions by week 4 or the C/D subset is small, the margin over a P-CAB may not reach significance in the restricted primary population.

sonnet.r: The primary population is the LA C/D subset, probably only 60-100 patients per arm, so even a real 12-15 point healing advantage over lansoprazole at week 4 can miss significance.

haiku.r: The primary analysis is restricted to grade C/D patients and needs a gap of about 10 to 15 points to reach significance, so a true effect of moderate size could still fall short on that subgroup.

carbon.r: Because the primary endpoint restricts analysis to baseline LA grade C/D patients within a 523-patient LA A-D trial, a lower-than-planned C/D share or high lansoprazole healing could reduce power.

sol.r: Stronger-than-expected lansoprazole healing could narrow the advantage enough to miss superiority in the smaller LA C/D primary-analysis population.

trials.t: Confirmatory Study 3 of KPS-0373 in Patients With Spinocerebellar Degeneration
trials.ep: Change from baseline in SARA total score (0-40) after 24 weeks of treatment

fable.r: Two earlier phase 3 trials missed on SARA; the pooled 0.6-point advantage is smaller than the roughly 0.8-point difference this 142-patient trial needs to observe.

opus.r: Rovatirelin (KPS-0373) missed its SARA primary in two earlier phase 3 trials; a sub-1-point true effect against a placebo arm that also improves leaves 71 per arm with limited power.

sonnet.r: SARA effects of a TRH analog in slowly progressive ataxia are small versus placebo noise, and earlier Japanese confirmatory studies of this compound were at best mixed.

haiku.r: Placebo-controlled SARA trial with 71 per arm; a 1-point gap at 24 weeks is hard to reach against placebo drift and a between-patient SD near 2.5, and the dose is unstated, so the drug is most likely too weak to show superiority.

carbon.r: Two prior Japanese Phase 3 confirmatory trials of KPS-0373 (rovatirelin) missed their 24-week SARA primary endpoints due to modest drug effect (~0.4-0.5 points) and placebo stabilization.

sol.r: Earlier rovatirelin phase 3 studies missed their overall SARA endpoints, and this repeat may again show only a small separation from placebo-associated improvement.

trials.t: A Phase III Clinical Study to Compare the Safety and Efficacy of 177Lu-DOTATATE Injection and Long-acting Oxytrexine in Adult Patients With NETs
trials.ep: Progression-free survival, assessed as the 18-month PFS rate, in progressive SSTR-positive G1/G2 gastroenteropancreatic NETs

fable.r: Efficacy is hardly in doubt; the risk is that the trial, still recruiting at its registered completion date, has no mature 18-month PFS analysis and yields only an early or vague statement, or stops.

opus.r: PRRT effect versus octreotide after SSA progression is large (NETTER-1 HR about 0.2); the main residual risk is slow-growing G1 disease keeping the octreotide arm progression-free, or trial conduct issues at a single-site Chinese sponsor.

sonnet.r: 177Lu-DOTATATE against SSA in progressive SSTR-positive NETs gave HR near 0.2 in NETTER-1; failure would come from crossover or an unusual Chinese population, but timing is the bigger issue, as it is still recruiting.

haiku.r: Time-to-event trial whose endpoint is an 18-month PFS rate, and the registry still shows recruiting at launch, so the 18-month read is unlikely to land by mid-2027; the main risk is endpoint timing rather than the drug.

carbon.r: Because 177Lu-DOTATATE efficacy over octreotide LAR in progressive SSTR-positive GEP-NETs is overwhelming, the main risk is immature follow-up or censoring anomalies on the 18-month landmark rate.

sol.r: A large treatment effect is likely, but immature 18-month follow-up or a changed primary analysis could prevent a clean positive readout.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of HRS9531 in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Treated With Basal Insulin
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 40

fable.r: The drug effect is large and the trial well sized; failure would need a conduct problem such as heavy insulin rescue in the placebo arm, dropouts or a data-quality issue.

opus.r: A GLP-1/GIP dual agonist added to basal insulin versus placebo for 40 weeks should lower HbA1c by well over 1 point; only heavy insulin up-titration in the placebo arm or high dropout could narrow the gap enough to matter.

sonnet.r: A GLP-1/GIP agonist added to basal insulin lowers HbA1c far more than placebo; the only realistic failure is a large placebo response from insulin titration, which is unlikely to erase a 1+ point gap.

haiku.r: HRS9531 at the higher dose added to basal insulin should lower HbA1c by about 1.3 to 1.5 points against placebo at about 100 per arm; the main gap is the timing of disclosure, not the effect.

carbon.r: Potent dual GIP/GLP-1 agonism makes efficacy failure versus placebo nearly impossible, leaving operational execution or unexpected safety-related hold as the only residual risk.

sol.r: Aggressive basal-insulin titration could shrink the placebo-adjusted HbA1c benefit, although a substantial incretin effect is expected.

trials.t: A Comparative Study to Valuating the Efficacy and Safety of QL1206 and Prolia®
trials.c: Postmenopausal Women With Osteoporosis at High Risk of Fracture
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in lumbar spine bone mineral density at month 12

fable.r: True difference should be near zero, so failure would come from chance or higher-than-assumed variability relative to the equivalence margins with only 278 patients.

opus.r: Denosumab biosimilars have consistently matched Prolia on LS-BMD; the only real risk is that 278 patients give a confidence interval too wide for a tight protocol margin, or excess dropouts.

sonnet.r: Denosumab biosimilar equivalence trials on lumbar spine BMD at month 12 almost always show equivalence; the likelier problem is timing, since the study is recruiting and 12-month data will come late.

haiku.r: Biosimilar denosumab equivalence on lumbar spine BMD at month 12 usually passes; the main risk is a wide confidence interval at about 139 per arm, since the margin is not stated in the record.

carbon.r: With 278 osteoporosis patients (~139 per arm), slightly higher BMD measurement variance or dropouts could push the 90%/95% confidence bounds outside tight biosimilar equivalence margins.

sol.r: The main residual risk is that BMD measurement variability and attrition make the confidence interval wider than the protocol's equivalence margins.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of SPT-300 (GlyphAllo) in Participants With Major Depressive Disorder, With or Without Anxious Distress (BUOY-1 Study)
trials.c: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD); Major Depressive Disorder With Anxious Distress
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Day 42 in HAM-D-17 total score in adults with major depressive disorder

fable.r: High placebo response in a 61-site MDD trial could swamp a modest 1.5-2 point HAM-D effect typical of GABA-A modulators; six-week durability of effect is untested.

opus.r: MDD monotherapy trials fail often because placebo response of 9-12 HAM-D points swamps a modest GABA-A neurosteroid effect, which in zuranolone trials was largest early and faded by week 6.

sonnet.r: MDD monotherapy trials carry large placebo responses (about 10 HAM-D points at day 42), and an oral allopregnanolone prodrug needs about a 2.5-point effect; neurosteroid MDD results have been mixed.

haiku.r: Phase 2 MDD trial with a high placebo response; the SPT-300 effect on HAM-D-17 at day 42 is unknown, and the main risk is a modest drug effect swamped by placebo response.

carbon.r: Large 6-week placebo HAM-D-17 improvements across 61 multinational MDD sites and potential attenuation of GABA-A neurosteroid separation by Day 42 pose major failure risks.

sol.r: The neurosteroid class has mixed MDD results, and a large six-week placebo response could erase the modest drug-placebo separation.

trials.t: A Study of AMC6156 in People With Sarcopenia
trials.ep: Change in Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score from baseline to week 12

fable.r: With about 20 patients per arm and an SPPB change SD near 1.6, only a difference of roughly 1.4 points would reach significance, more than any sarcopenia drug has shown over a placebo arm that also improves with exercise and nutrition advice.

opus.r: With about 20 patients per arm, exercise and nutrition guidance in both arms, and SPPB changes near 1 point SD 1.6, only an implausibly large drug effect would reach significance in 12 weeks.

sonnet.r: With about 20 patients per arm and SPPB change SD near 1.7, only a large effect would reach significance; sarcopenia drug trials rarely show clear SPPB benefit in 12 weeks.

haiku.r: Small four-arm phase 2 with 20 per arm on SPPB; a gap near 1 point is needed to reach significance, and the main risk is that the sample is too small to show it even if the drug works.

carbon.r: Pharmacotherapies in age-related sarcopenia have consistently struggled to improve composite physical function scores like SPPB over 12 weeks, especially against background exercise and nutrition guidance in a small 20-patient-per-arm trial.

sol.r: Twenty patients per dose provide limited power for a variable functional endpoint, particularly when exercise and nutrition guidance can improve placebo performance.

trials.t: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy in Cancer Patients With Adjustment Disorder
trials.c: Adjustment Disorder; Adjustment Disorder With Anxious Mood; Cancer
trials.ep: Anxiety Severity

fable.r: Recruiting 87 cancer patients with adjustment disorder for psilocybin sessions at five Australian sites is slow and the sponsor is small, so the March 2027 primary completion is likely to slip by more than 90 days.

opus.r: A small-cap psychedelic sponsor running single-dose psilocybin therapy in cancer patients with adjustment disorder at 5 Australian sites will likely enrol slowly, pushing primary completion past mid-2027.

sonnet.r: A small Australian psilocybin trial with specialised dosing sessions and an 87-patient target, started Oct 2025 and still recruiting; enrolment is likely slower than the 2027-03 completion date, and a small sponsor carries some funding risk.

haiku.r: No efficacy goal, so only operations apply: the record shows recruiting at launch with 87 planned and a 10-week outcome plus follow-up, so completion will likely slip past the registry date.

carbon.r: Recruiting 87 oncology patients with adjustment disorder across five Australian sites for intensive 8-hour psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy sessions faces substantial screening and scheduling bottlenecks, making completion delays past June 2027 highly likely.

sol.r: Therapist-intensive dosing and restrictive cancer and psychiatric screening make recruitment slippage more likely than an on-time finish.

trials.t: A Study to Assess Bioequivalence of Two Subcutaneous (SC) Formulations of Ocrelizumab in Participants With Multiple Sclerosis (MS)
trials.ep: Ocrelizumab AUC over the first 12 weeks and maximum serum concentration (Cmax)

fable.r: A change in concentration, volume or hyaluronidase content could shift Cmax enough that its 90% interval leaves the equivalence bounds even if AUC passes.

opus.r: Two SC formulations of the same antibody should match on AUC; the realistic failure is Cmax falling outside 0.80-1.25 because of absorption differences or body-weight variability in a parallel design of about 96 per arm.

sonnet.r: Roche's formulation bridging studies usually show bioequivalence; failure would come from a true formulation PK difference or high between-patient variability in AUC or Cmax.

haiku.r: Bioequivalence of two subcutaneous ocrelizumab formulations on AUC and Cmax under the standard 80 to 125 percent limits; most such studies pass, and the main risk is a formulation-driven exposure gap.

carbon.r: Subcutaneous monoclonal antibody formulations can exhibit slightly altered absorption rates affecting Cmax geometric mean ratios even when total exposure (AUC) matches closely.

sol.r: A formulation-related shift in absorption could move Cmax outside the bioequivalence limits even if total exposure remains similar.

trials.t: Proof of Concept Study to Assess the Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics of Nemolizumab in Adults With Chronic Pruritus of Unknown Origin (CPUO)
trials.ep: Population Pharmacokinetics (PopPK) Model of the Elimination of nemolizumab During the 16-week Treatment Period Point

fable.r: Recruitment is closed in a short 50-patient PK/PD study, so it should complete on time, with results posting likely only after the read date.

opus.r: A 50-patient PK/PD study that has finished enrolling, with a 16-week treatment period, should complete close to its registered Dec 2026 date under an experienced sponsor.

sonnet.r: A small Galderma PK/PD proof-of-concept study that is no longer recruiting with primary completion 2026-12; unlikely to slip beyond March 2027, and results posting by August 2027 is possible but not routine for a phase 2.

haiku.r: Exploratory PK/PD study with no efficacy goal; the record shows active and not recruiting with completion in December 2026, so it should finish on time and post results within the year.

carbon.r: Because enrollment of 50 participants is already complete as of late October 2026 for a 16-week treatment period, this Galderma PK/PD study should wrap up close to its December 2026 primary completion target.

sol.r: Recruitment is already closed and follow-up is short, supporting completion near schedule, although registry results may not appear until later.

trials.t: A Research Study to See How a Weekly Insulin, Insulin Icodec, Helps in Reducing the Blood Sugar Compared to Daily Insulin Glargine, Both in Combination With Insulin Aspart, in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes
trials.ep: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26

fable.r: A more cautious icodec titration aimed at limiting hypoglycaemia in type 1 diabetes could leave HbA1c meaningfully higher than with glargine and push the interval past the non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: If the revised titration, likely meant to cut hypoglycaemia, makes icodec dosing more conservative, HbA1c lowering could trail glargine enough for the upper CI bound to cross the likely 0.3-point margin.

sonnet.r: ONWARDS 6 showed icodec non-inferior to degludec in T1D (ETD 0.04); with 877 patients a 0.3-0.4 point margin is very likely met, and the only realistic risk is a surprise efficacy gap versus glargine.

haiku.r: Insulin icodec against glargine in type 1 diabetes at 26 weeks; a non-inferiority design with 438 per arm should pass unless weekly insulin covers slightly less, which is the main risk.

carbon.r: Once-weekly insulin icodec provides slightly less day-to-day basal flexibility in type 1 diabetes than daily basal analogues, creating a small risk of trailing glargine U100 if hypoglycemia-avoidance titration limits dosing.

sol.r: Conservative icodec titration to limit hypoglycaemia could leave HbA1c above the non-inferiority threshold despite adequate intrinsic glucose-lowering activity.

trials.t: Study of the Efficacy, Safety, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Immunogenicity of BCD-261 in Subjects With Moderate to Severe Active Ulcerative Colitis
trials.ep: Clinical remission at week 14: modified Mayo score ≤2 with endoscopic subscore ≤1, stool blood 0, stool frequency ≤1

fable.r: With roughly 40 patients per arm, a true remission gain of 15-20 points over placebo can easily miss significance, especially if placebo remission in largely biologic-naive Russian patients runs above 10%.

opus.r: About 40 patients per arm gives only moderate power for a 15-20 point remission gap; a higher placebo remission rate in a partly biologic-naive Russian population could erase significance.

sonnet.r: Class effect of anti-TL1A is large, but about 40 per arm in a refractory Russian population leaves a real chance that no dose clears p<0.05 on week-14 remission.

haiku.r: About 40 patients in the high-dose and placebo arms gives limited power for a remission gap near 14 points at week 14, and the registry still shows recruitment against a January 2027 primary completion.

carbon.r: With roughly 40 patients per arm across five groups, chance variation or a higher-than-expected placebo remission rate in biologic-naive patients could mask a clinically meaningful anti-TL1A induction effect.

sol.r: Roughly 40 patients per regimen leave substantial sampling and dose-multiplicity risk, especially if placebo remission is higher than in the strongest prior anti-TL1A trial.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of HDM1002 Tablets in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
trials.sp: Hangzhou Zhongmei Huadong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 40

fable.r: Dapagliflozin may lower HbA1c by about 1 point in Chinese patients with baseline near 8.5%, so HDM1002 must deliver orforglipron-like potency to show a clear advantage.

opus.r: Dapagliflozin lowers HbA1c about 0.8-1.0% on metformin; if HDM1002 400 mg is less potent than orforglipron or GI intolerance limits titration, the gap may not reach superiority.

sonnet.r: An oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist at the top dose should beat dapagliflozin on HbA1c, but the margin may be modest if the dose is limited by GI tolerability.

haiku.r: Dapagliflozin is a strong add-on comparator, so a win depends on HDM1002 400 mg lowering HbA1c about half a point more than dapagliflozin at week 40. With 200 per arm the test is precise if the gap is real.

carbon.r: High-dose oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonists cause substantial gastrointestinal adverse events and occasional transaminase elevations that could elevate treatment discontinuations and attenuate estimand efficacy.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance or other safety findings with prolonged high-dose oral GLP-1 agonism could increase withdrawals and attenuate the advantage over dapagliflozin.

trials.t: A Study of IBR854 Combined With Pazopanib Versus Pazopanib in Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma
trials.ep: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1 (radiological progression or death), followed for approximately 2 years

fable.r: Thirty patients randomized 2:1 with short follow-up cannot show a significant progression-free survival difference unless the hazard ratio is near 0.35 or lower.

opus.r: With 30 patients randomized 2:1 and perhaps 12-18 PFS events, only a hazard ratio near 0.35 or lower would reach significance, and the trial is likely descriptive.

sonnet.r: Only 30 patients (20 vs 10) and perhaps 15-20 PFS events: even a real benefit would rarely reach p<0.05, and OS will be immature.

haiku.r: Only 30 patients (20 vs 10) on a time-to-event primary: a significant PFS gain needs a hazard ratio near 0.4, and a two-year PFS with a registry still showing recruitment pushes results late.

carbon.r: Enrolling only 30 patients randomized 2:1 (20 experimental vs 10 control) yields fewer than 25 PFS events, making statistical significance unattainable unless the observed hazard ratio is extreme.

sol.r: With only ten control patients and roughly twenty PFS events, the study needs an unusually large treatment effect to establish superiority.

trials.t: Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Meropenem and Pralurbactam in Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacteriaceae Infections
trials.c: Hospital-acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP); Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pneumonia (VABP); Complicated Intra-abdominal Infection (cIAI)
trials.ep: Overall success (clinical plus microbiological response) at test-of-cure visit (day 12-23) in participants with complicated urinary tract infection

fable.r: Eighty patients spread over several infection types and three primary outcomes leave each comparison far too small for significance, and best available therapy with ceftazidime-avibactam is effective.

opus.r: Eighty patients split across five infection types leave only small cUTI, mortality and cIAI subsets; such CRE-vs-best-available-therapy trials are usually descriptive, and all three co-primaries would have to be met.

sonnet.r: 80 patients split over five infection types leave very few cUTI patients per arm, and all co-primaries must be met, so formal superiority on every one is unlikely.

haiku.r: The round rule requires all co-primaries (cUTI success, day-28 mortality, cIAI response) to be met; with about 80 patients and a small cUTI subset, that bar is hard to clear.

carbon.r: Splitting 80 patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae across three distinct infection-specific co-primary endpoints leaves each subgroup too small for reliable formal hypothesis testing, especially against ceftazidime-avibactam in best available therapy.

sol.r: Eighty patients split among several infection syndromes leave very small co-primary cohorts, while modern best-available therapy makes superiority harder to establish.

trials.t: To Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety and Population Pharmacokinetics of GST-HG141 in Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) Who Have an Inadequate Response to Antiviral Drug Treatment
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with serum HBV DNA below the lower limit of quantification at week 48

fable.r: Failure would need viral breakthrough from capsid-inhibitor resistance or poor adherence to erase a suppression advantage that phase 2 showed to be large.

opus.r: Capsid assembly modulators suppress residual viremia on top of NAs, but if neracorvir's add-on effect in HBeAg-positive low-level viremia is modest, the gap over continued NA could narrow, though 263 per arm still gives large power.

sonnet.r: A capsid assembly modulator on top of NA should clearly lower HBV DNA, but the main risk is spontaneous HBV DNA decline to below the limit on placebo plus NA over 48 weeks.

haiku.r: With 263 per arm the trial can detect a 20-point gap easily, so the risk lies in the loosely stated measure and in whether the sponsor reports the week-48 result in the form the card names.

carbon.r: Improved adherence to background nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy under clinical trial monitoring can drive spontaneous HBV DNA suppression in placebo recipients, though capsid assembly modulation remains far more potent.

sol.r: Improved adherence and another year of nucleos(t)ide therapy could suppress residual viraemia in the placebo group, shrinking the add-on advantage.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of Add-On Therapy With Empagliflozin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes on a Background of Alogliptin and Metformin
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c at week 24

fable.r: Failure would need an underpowered multi-arm split (171 may be three arms of 57) combined with an unusually weak HbA1c response; the class effect on this background is consistent at about -0.7 points.

opus.r: Little risk: SGLT2 inhibitor add-on to metformin plus DPP-4 inhibitor reliably lowers HbA1c 0.6-0.8 points versus placebo; only an unusually low baseline HbA1c could shrink the effect.

sonnet.r: Placebo-controlled add-on of a well-established SGLT2 inhibitor to metformin plus DPP-4 inhibitor; a 0.5-0.7 point placebo-adjusted HbA1c drop is near certain to be significant at 85 per arm.

haiku.r: Empagliflozin is a known add-on agent and an effect near 0.6 points is well above the noise at 85 per arm, so the main risk is a smaller effect on this background than expected.

carbon.r: Empagliflozin has robustly established glycemic efficacy as an add-on to metformin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor, leaving operational execution or incomplete reporting detail as the only plausible ways to miss.

sol.r: Improved adherence to background therapy could narrow the HbA1c difference, although the established empagliflozin effect should usually remain detectable.

trials.t: An Open-Label, Randomized, Cross-Over Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Mexiletine PR Compared to Mexiletine IR
trials.ep: To compare the safety of mexiletine PR vs mexiletine IR by incidence of treatment emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs), treatment-related TEAEs, serious AEs, and patient discontinuation rate between mexiletine PR and mexiletine IR after 12 weeks of treatment.

fable.r: Rare-disease crossover with 29 weeks per patient and still recruiting three months before the registered completion date, so primary completion will probably slip past April 2027; no results posting expected by August 2027.

opus.r: A 24-patient crossover in genetically confirmed non-dystrophic myotonia still recruiting in late 2026 is likely to finish beyond its January 2027 date; results will likely go to the EU registry rather than ClinicalTrials.gov.

sonnet.r: Small 24-patient crossover in a rare disease at a single Belgian site; recruitment likely slips, results are unlikely to be posted on the registry by August 2027, and the long list of safety primaries invites edits.

haiku.r: A 24-patient crossover with enrolment still open in October 2026 and a January 2027 completion date: slippage past late April 2027 is likely. Termination risk is modest for a crossover of an established drug.

carbon.r: Recruiting 24 genetically confirmed non-dystrophic myotonia patients including 12 mexiletine-naive subjects at a single Belgian center for a 25-week crossover design carries substantial enrollment delay risk.

sol.r: Recruiting a treatment-naïve subgroup in a rare genetic disorder and completing two 12-week periods makes delay more likely than termination.

trials.t: A Clinical Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of HRS-7249 in Treating Patients With Hyperlipidemia
trials.ep: Triglyceride level, taken as percent change from baseline, at about week 28

fable.r: The exact target and potency of HRS-7249 are not public, so the main way to miss is a weaker triglyceride drop than other siRNAs in a dose arm of only about 45-55 patients with a noisy endpoint.

opus.r: Low risk: if HRS-7249 is an APOC3 or ANGPTL3 silencer, TG falls 40-60% versus placebo; failure would require a weak molecule or a very small highest-dose arm.

sonnet.r: A triglyceride-lowering injectable dosed at the top level against saline should give a large, significant drop; failure would mainly come from reporting on a different form of the measure.

haiku.r: Dose-finding phase 2 with a placebo control: the highest dose is compared on triglyceride percent change at about week 28. The primary completion was September 2026, yet the record still shows the trial as active, so updates are slow.

carbon.r: Because the molecular target and dose regimen of HRS-7249 are undisclosed in the registry, weaker-than-expected triglyceride lowering at 28 weeks is the main efficacy uncertainty.

sol.r: The principal uncertainty is whether HRS-7249 delivers sustained triglyceride lowering at the tested doses; its target and earlier human efficacy are not specified.

trials.t: A Study of the Effect of (S)-Pindolol Benzoate (ACM-001.1) on Lean Body Mass (LBM) in Obese Patents During (PROACT 1), and Post-semaglutide Therapy (PROACT 2)
trials.ep: Change in DEXA lean body mass (grams per 4 weeks) over 20 weeks while receiving semaglutide (PROACT 1)

fable.r: No human data show that S-pindolol preserves lean mass during GLP-1 weight loss; the anabolic signal comes from cancer cachexia, and with about 40 per arm it must prevent roughly a third of the lean loss.

opus.r: Espindolol's anabolic signal comes from cancer cachexia; during semaglutide-driven weight loss a 100-200 g per 4 weeks lean-mass benefit is plausible but underpowered with ~40 per arm, and both primaries (during and after semaglutide) must be met.

sonnet.r: A beta-blocker-derived lean-mass preserving drug needs about 150 g per 4 weeks over placebo to be significant at 40 per arm, and both primaries (on and after semaglutide) must be met.

haiku.r: Two co-primary lean-mass rates (during and after semaglutide) must both be met, and the pindolol effect on lean mass is unknown. The registry still shows recruiting against a March 2027 completion, which suggests late and slipping timelines.

carbon.r: Preserving lean mass against active semaglutide weight loss and post-semaglutide washout across two separate co-primary outcomes with roughly 40 patients per arm leaves the study severely underpowered.

sol.r: The anabolic signal in cancer cachexia may not translate to obesity, while spontaneous lean-mass recovery after semaglutide withdrawal makes meeting both primaries harder.

trials.t: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of Early in Hospital Initiation of Inclisiran Treatment in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
trials.ep: Percent change in LDL-C from baseline to Day 150 after in-hospital start in acute coronary syndrome

fable.r: Statin initiation after ACS lowers LDL-C sharply in the placebo arm too, which narrows the percentage-point gap, but not nearly enough to threaten significance; only conduct problems could.

opus.r: Statin initiation or intensification after ACS cuts LDL-C substantially in the placebo arm, shrinking the absolute percent difference, but inclisiran's ~50% relative lowering still leaves a large, highly significant gap.

sonnet.r: Inclisiran's LDL-C effect is robust and 150 per arm is ample, so only an unusually strong placebo-arm LDL fall after ACS (statin intensification) could shrink the gap.

haiku.r: Inclisiran reliably lowers LDL-C, so the superiority hypothesis is very likely to hold; the risk is mainly timing of the public statement, with a Novartis topline likely to come with a congress or the quarterly report.

carbon.r: Intensive in-hospital statin and ezetimibe initiation in statin-naive ACS patients compresses the additive difference in percent LDL-C change from baseline, though not nearly enough to threaten significance.

sol.r: Rapid post-ACS intensification of statins and other lipid therapy could reduce the incremental percentage-point effect, although outright efficacy failure is unlikely.

trials.t: A Study Evaluating BFB759 in Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) at week 16

fable.r: BFB759 has no published phase 2 efficacy in atopic dermatitis; if its targets lie outside the IL-4/IL-13, OX40 or IL-31 axes, the top dose may not separate from a placebo arm improving EASI by 35-40%.

opus.r: BFB759 is a novel-target biologic from a private biotech with little public clinical data; a high and variable placebo EASI response in modern AD trials can swamp a modest drug effect.

sonnet.r: Dose-ranging phase 2 in moderate-to-severe AD with 225 patients over several arms; the top dose only needs to beat placebo on percent change in EASI at week 16, but the mechanism is undisclosed and a private sponsor may be slow or selective in disclosure.

haiku.r: Dose-ranging phase 2 with the highest dose undisclosed; the main risk is a highest-dose EASI effect over 16 weeks too small to reach significance at this size.

carbon.r: Unproven clinical target validation for BFB759 in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis combined with substantial placebo EASI responses creates meaningful risk of insufficient efficacy.

sol.r: Without a specified mechanism or earlier BFB759 efficacy, the main risk is inadequate separation from a substantial placebo response across the registered assessments.

trials.t: Phase II, Open-label, Multicenter Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HLX43 (an Anti-PD-L1 ADC) in Subjects With Advanced Colorectal Cancer
trials.ep: Objective response rate (ORR) (assessed by the Independent Radiology Review Committee [IRRC] as per RECIST v1.1).

fable.r: Still recruiting two months before the registered primary completion with a staged three-dose design, so completion is likely to move into mid-2027 or later; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.

opus.r: Small Chinese dose-optimisation study of an anti-PD-L1 ADC in CRC still recruiting with an ORR endpoint; the end-2026 primary completion will probably be pushed back if the record is updated.

sonnet.r: Small two-site randomized dose-exploration phase 2 in Chinese CRC with an enrollment pause and dose selection step, so the registered end date of 2026-12-30 is likely to slip or the status to stay recruiting; early stopping and posted results are unlikely.

haiku.r: Two-site Chinese phase 2 with 60 planned patients, still recruiting at launch; the registered December 2026 primary completion is likely to slip, and dose selection may change the record.

carbon.r: Staged dose-selection enrollment pauses, only two listed clinical sites, and RECIST response follow-up in refractory colorectal cancer make registry primary completion slippage beyond March 2027 likely.

sol.r: The planned enrollment pause for dose selection and subsequent response follow-up can push completion beyond March 2027 despite the small cohort.

trials.t: Clinical Trial of TQC2731 Injection in Patients With Chronic Sinusitis and Nasal Polyps
trials.sp: Shanghai Chia Tai Tianqing Pharmaceutical Technology Development Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 24 in endoscopic Nasal Polyp Score (NPS, 0-8) in all CRSwNP patients

fable.r: Four co-primaries (NPS and congestion, overall and eosinophilic) must all hold, and a large non-eosinophilic share in Chinese patients could dilute the overall-population effect of TSLP blockade.

opus.r: All four primaries (NPS and NCS overall and in the ECRSwNP subset) must be met; anti-TSLP is validated in CRSwNP, but a Chinese population with more non-eosinophilic polyps and the smaller ECRSwNP subset NCS test are the weak points.

sonnet.r: Anti-TSLP in CRSwNP has strong precedent, so NPS and NCS in all patients should be met; the extra risk is that all four co-primaries, including the two in the smaller eosinophilic subgroup, must pass.

haiku.r: Anti-TSLP polyp effects are expected to be smaller than in anti-IL-4R trials, and four co-primary outcomes must all be met, so the risk is a modest NPS difference that misses on one of them.

carbon.r: Requiring simultaneous statistical significance across four registered primary endpoints spanning both Nasal Polyp Score and Nasal Congestion Score in overall and eosinophilic subsets adds a modest hurdle.

sol.r: Inflammatory-endotype heterogeneity could dilute the overall response, and success requires both polyp and congestion outcomes in the full population and eosinophilic subgroup.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of Boric Acid Inserts for Treatment of Vulvovaginal Candidiasis
trials.c: Vulvovaginal Candidiases; Vulvovaginal Candidiasis, Genital; Vulvovaginal Candidiasis (VVC)
trials.ep: Share of patients with clinical cure (composite vulvovaginal signs and symptoms score 0, no extra antifungal) at test-of-cure visit, day 28

fable.r: Spontaneous resolution by day 28 can push placebo clinical cure to 35-45%, leaving boric acid, never tested against placebo under the strict cure definition, with too small a margin in about 80 culture-confirmed patients per arm.

opus.r: Clinical cure needs every sign and symptom at zero on day 28, two weeks after treatment; a sizable placebo response and boric-acid local irritation could shrink the gap below what 111 per arm can detect.

sonnet.r: Strict clinical cure (all signs and symptoms zero) at day 28 carries a placebo response around one third; with about 111 per arm, a 15-point benefit gives only moderate power, though two active arms give two chances.

haiku.r: The composite cure endpoint (zero signs and symptoms at day 28) is strict and placebo cure is uncertain; a clear boric acid effect over placebo is still likely with 111 per arm.

carbon.r: Fourteen days of daily placebo vaginal inserts and spontaneous resolution can elevate Day 28 complete symptom-absence rates in the vehicle arm, narrowing the treatment delta.

sol.r: Complete absence of every sign and symptom at Day 28 is stricter than fungal eradication, and residual irritation or spontaneous placebo improvement could erase superiority.

trials.t: A PHASE II PROSPECTIVE RANDOMIZED DOUBLE-MASKED CONTROLLED STUDY ASSESSING THE SAFETY & EFFICACY OF RHPRG4 (450 µG/ML RECOMBINANT HUMAN PROTEOGLYCAN 4) COMPARED TO VEHICLE FOR THE TREATMENT OF SJÖGREN'S RELATED DRY EYE DISEASE
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with complete resolution of total corneal fluorescein staining (Oxford scale) at Day 28

fable.r: Complete clearing of corneal staining is a strict binary endpoint and 40 patients per arm need a gap above about 20 points over a lubricating vehicle, which dry eye drugs rarely achieve in 28 days.

opus.r: With 40 per arm and a binary complete-clearance endpoint from a mild baseline (Oxford 1-2), a vehicle response near 20% means the drug needs a gap of over 20 points to reach significance.

sonnet.r: About 40 per arm and a demanding endpoint (staining fully resolved in a Sjogren's population with mild baseline staining) leave little power; vehicle effects on staining and symptoms are sizeable in dry eye trials.

haiku.r: Only about 40 patients per arm with a complete-resolution endpoint, so a real 15-point gain over vehicle may not reach significance; the design is small and vehicle response is uncertain.

carbon.r: Achieving statistically significant complete corneal staining clearance across eyes by Day 28 in Sjögren's syndrome dry eye with only 40 patients per arm requires an unrealistically large responder difference.

sol.r: With approximately 40 patients per arm, a modest improvement in complete staining clearance may not separate significantly from a lubricating vehicle at Day 28.

trials.t: A PHASE II PROSPECTIVE RANDOMIZED DOUBLE-MASKED CROSSOVER STUDY ASSESSING THE SAFETY & EFFICACY OF RHPRG4 (450 μG/ML RECOMBINANT HUMAN PROTEOGLYCAN 4) COMPARED TO VEHICLE FOR THE TREATMENT OF OCULAR GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST DISEASE (OGVHD)
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Day 28 in total corneal fluorescein staining (Oxford scale) in ocular GVHD dry eye

fable.r: Fifteen crossover patients must show significance on both corneal staining and total symptom VAS against a lubricating vehicle; vehicle responses in dry eye are large, and a larger vehicle-controlled dry-eye programme of rhPRG4 was not taken forward.

opus.r: Only 15 patients in a crossover with two co-primary endpoints (corneal staining and total symptom VAS) that must both reach significance; a 14-day washout may also allow carryover.

sonnet.r: Crossover with only about 15 patients and two co-primary outcomes (corneal staining and total symptom VAS) that must both be met; enrolment of a rare population is slow.

haiku.r: Fifteen patients per crossover arm with two co-primary outcomes, both of which must be significant; a half-grade staining gain is plausible but the paired test on a small sample is fragile.

carbon.r: With only 15 crossover patients, achieving statistical significance on both co-primary sign and symptom endpoints in fibrotic ocular GVHD after a short 14-day washout is severely underpowered.

sol.r: Fifteen crossover participants may show a staining benefit but still miss the requirement for significant improvements in both staining and total symptom score.

trials.t: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Immunogenicity of SV001 in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
trials.ep: Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events

fable.r: Small Chinese multiple-ascending-dose study in IPF still recruiting two months before its registered completion, with adverse events followed for about a year; a completion date slipping past March 2027 is more likely than not, and results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.

opus.r: Chinese multiple-ascending-dose IPF safety study still recruiting near its registered end-2026 primary completion, so any update will probably push the date out; posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Phase 2a multiple ascending dose study with about one year of follow-up per patient and 48 planned; it was still recruiting in October 2026, so the registered end of 2026-12-31 cannot hold and the date is very likely to move.

haiku.r: Multiple ascending dose study of 48 patients in China with an end-2026 primary completion date that is likely to slip as the cohorts take longer than planned.

carbon.r: Recruiting 48 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients across 12 Chinese centers with an approximately 1-year safety observation timeframe makes primary completion by December 2026 unlikely.

sol.r: Ascending-dose cohort sequencing and the lengthy adverse-event assessment window make a schedule slip more likely than early termination; prompt ClinicalTrials.gov results posting is unlikely.

trials.t: Study of MT1013 for the Treatment of Patients With Secondary Hyperparathyroidism
trials.sp: Shaanxi Micot Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Percentage with more than 50% reduction from baseline in mean iPTH during the efficacy assessment phase (weeks 22-27)

fable.r: If the trial tests superiority on both iPTH responder thresholds, a well-titrated double-dummy cinacalcet arm could leave a gap of about 10 points that 212 patients per arm detect only part of the time; non-inferiority would be met comfortably.

opus.r: A first-in-class dual agonist must at least match titrated cinacalcet on both the >50% and >30% iPTH responder endpoints; unknown dosing and a margin not stated in the record leave room for a non-inferiority miss.

sonnet.r: Phase 3 versus cinacalcet needs only non-inferiority (margin unknown) on the share with more than 50% iPTH reduction; a new dual-target agonist is likely to match or beat an oral calcimimetic, but dose and margin are undisclosed.

haiku.r: Non-inferiority against cinacalcet on the share with a 50 percent iPTH fall; the margin is unstated, so the main risk is a true efficacy gap that pushes the lower confidence bound past it.

carbon.r: Titrated active-control cinacalcet robustly lowers iPTH in compliant double-dummy dialysis trials, leaving little margin if MT1013 underdoses or requires meeting both co-primary responder thresholds.

sol.r: MT1013 must preserve adequate efficacy against titrated cinacalcet on both response thresholds; its undisclosed dose, prior efficacy and actual testing margins remain important uncertainties.

trials.t: IBI363 Combined With Chemotherapy or Pembrolizumab Combined With Chemotherapy as Neoadjuvant Therapy in Resectable Stage IB-III Non-Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
trials.c: Resectable Stage IB-III Non-Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
trials.ep: Pathologic complete response (no residual viable tumor in lung and sampled nodes) after neoadjuvant therapy, assessed at surgery

fable.r: With about 85 patients per arm the pCR gap over pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy must reach roughly 14 points for nominal significance, and the phase 2 may not carry a formal superiority hypothesis at all.

opus.r: With 85 per arm and a pembrolizumab-chemo control near 20% pCR in non-squamous disease, IBI363 needs an improvement of about 14 points or more to reach significance, and the randomized phase 2 may be reported descriptively without a formal test.

sonnet.r: Randomized phase 2 with about 85 per arm and no stated hypothesis; pCR may look higher with IBI363 but a significant gap needs about 18 points, and event-free survival will be immature at any reading.

haiku.r: Superiority on pCR over pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy needs a large gap with 85 per arm; IBI363 must clearly beat a strong immunotherapy standard for the trial to be called a win.

carbon.r: Beating an active pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy regimen on pathologic complete response in non-squamous NSCLC with 85 patients per arm requires a large absolute pCR gain to reach formal significance.

sol.r: With approximately 85 patients per arm, IBI363 needs a large absolute pCR improvement over an effective pembrolizumab-chemotherapy regimen to establish superiority.

trials.t: A Phase III Clinical Study of Cabergoline Tablets Compared With Bromocriptine Mesylate Tablets
trials.ep: Percentage of women whose serum prolactin returned to normal at week 14

fable.r: Failure would need bromocriptine to normalise prolactin nearly as often as cabergoline over 14 weeks, or heavy dropout; both are unlikely given the consistent historical advantage of cabergoline in efficacy and tolerability.

opus.r: Cabergoline is established as more effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine; the main risk is a well-titrated bromocriptine arm over 14 weeks narrowing the gap, but non-inferiority should still hold.

sonnet.r: Cabergoline is established as more effective than bromocriptine for normalizing prolactin; the trial only needs non-inferiority (margin unknown), so failure would come from conduct or a tight margin.

haiku.r: Non-inferiority on normalised prolactin at week 14 with 191 per arm and no stated margin; bromocriptine is an established active control, so the main risk is a tight margin rather than a weak drug.

carbon.r: Because cabergoline is pharmacologically far more effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine, failure would almost certainly stem from reporting vagueness or operational issues rather than efficacy.

sol.r: Optimized bromocriptine titration could narrow cabergoline's established advantage, particularly if the actual protocol requires superiority rather than non-inferiority.

trials.t: Study on BT-114143 Reducing Perioperative Bleeding in Total Knee Arthroplasty（TKA）
trials.ep: Total perioperative blood loss calculated by the Gross formula (hematocrit change) on postoperative Day 3 after unilateral total knee arthroplasty

fable.r: Tranexamic acid is already a highly effective antifibrinolytic, so a new agent is unlikely to show significantly less blood loss; success depends on whether the phase 2 defines its objective as non-inferiority or comparability rather than superiority.

opus.r: Tranexamic acid is already a highly effective antifibrinolytic in TKA, so a 90-per-arm phase 2 has little room to show a significant further cut in Gross-formula blood loss, whose between-patient SD is near 250-300 mL.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 head-to-head against IV tranexamic acid, an effective standard; beating it on Day-3 Gross-formula blood loss with 90 per arm needs a clear advantage, and the record states no non-inferiority design.

haiku.r: Tranexamic acid is a proven, inexpensive comparator in knee arthroplasty, so the novel injectable has to beat it on Gross-formula blood loss in a single-country phase 2.

carbon.r: Intravenous tranexamic acid before and after incision already potently inhibits perioperative fibrinolysis in total knee arthroplasty, leaving a small ceiling for further blood loss reduction.

sol.r: Repeated perioperative IV tranexamic acid already prevents substantial bleeding, leaving limited room for a new agent to produce a statistically persuasive additional reduction.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Tobevibart+Elebsiran in Participants With Chronic HDV Infection Not Virologically Suppressed With Bulevirtide
trials.ep: HDV RNA below lower limit of quantification, target not detected, at week 24

fable.r: The only real threat is the short 24-week window for a strict target-not-detected endpoint after switching from bulevirtide; even a response rate of 25-30% would still clear a continued-bulevirtide arm expected to stay in single digits.

opus.r: Undetectable HDV RNA (target not detected) is a strict bar and week 24 is early; if tobevibart+elebsiran mostly drives patients below LLOQ but still detectable, the TND rate gap over continued bulevirtide could be smaller than planned.

sonnet.r: Control patients are by definition not suppressed on bulevirtide, so TND is near zero; the combination only needs a modest TND rate for significance. The durability co-primary after end of treatment is the main uncertainty.

haiku.r: The main risk is timing, since the 24-week post-treatment second primary could push the registered completion date and delay any public statement past June 2027.

carbon.r: While Week 24 virologic suppression should overwhelmingly beat continued bulevirtide, the second registered primary outcome (24 weeks post-treatment) will remain immature at the Week 24 readout.

sol.r: Week-24 antiviral superiority looks likely, but success under the round's rules also requires the registered post-treatment co-primary to demonstrate durable suppression and be reported in time.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study of VVN461 Ophthalmic Solution for Noninfectious Anterior Uveitis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in anterior chamber cell (ACC) grade (SUN criteria) in the study eye at Day 14

fable.r: A topical JAK inhibitor may clear anterior chamber cells somewhat less than intensive prednisolone acetate; a shortfall of 0.2-0.3 grade would threaten a typical 0.5-grade non-inferiority margin with 77 patients per arm, and superiority is out of reach.

opus.r: Prednisolone acetate 1% clears most anterior chamber cells within 14 days; a topical JAK inhibitor is unlikely to beat it and may fall short of a non-inferiority margin if its intraocular penetration is weaker than the steroid's.

sonnet.r: Likely a non-inferiority design versus prednisolone acetate, which is a strong comparator; a JAK-class topical may be slightly less potent at Day 14. If the hypothesis is superiority, success is unlikely.

haiku.r: Prednisolone acetate 1 percent is a potent steroid, so the novel drug has to match or beat it on day 14 cell grade with only 77 patients per arm.

carbon.r: Topical 1.0% prednisolone acetate clears anterior chamber cells rapidly over 14 days, making non-inferiority challenging for a non-steroidal JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor drop and superiority unlikely.

sol.r: Prednisolone should rapidly suppress anterior-chamber inflammation; VVN461 may match it without beating it, making the actual non-inferiority versus superiority hypothesis decisive.

trials.t: A Study of Modified Release RTN-001 In Patients With Uncontrolled Hypertension
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 4 in pre-dose office-seated systolic blood pressure in uncontrolled hypertension

fable.r: Trough office systolic pressure at 4 weeks demands a sustained effect; the drug appears to act through the nitric oxide-cGMP pathway, where reductions are modest, and 70 per arm needs about a 4.5 mmHg placebo-adjusted fall for significance.

opus.r: The exclusions for nitrates and PDE5 inhibitors point to an NO/cGMP-pathway vasodilator, whose add-on office SBP effect may be only a few mmHg, too small to separate from a large office-BP placebo response with about 70 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Phase 2b dose-ranging in resistant hypertension with 70 per arm; the highest dose needs about 5 mmHg placebo-corrected effect, and placebo response in office SBP is sizeable.

haiku.r: The record shows no dose response and the highest dose is my assumption, so if that dose is not much stronger than placebo the trial will miss on office SBP.

carbon.r: Measuring pre-dose trough office systolic blood pressure tests end-of-dosing-interval persistence, where vasodilatory NO-cGMP effects can wane and office measurement noise is substantial.

sol.r: The main vulnerability is insufficient trough BP lowering at the pre-dose week-4 assessment, compounded by adherence-related placebo improvement and office-measurement variability.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Tobevibart+Elebsiran Versus Bulevirtide in Chronic HDV Infection
trials.ep: HDV RNA below the lower limit of quantification, target not detected, at week 48

fable.r: Failure would require the combination to fall far short of its phase 2 clearance rate while bulevirtide overperforms, or substantial dropout in the open-label combination arm counted as non-response.

opus.r: With about 50 patients per arm, a 20-point difference in undetectable HDV RNA at week 48 is only borderline significant, and a phase 2b may report the comparison descriptively rather than as a formal superiority test.

sonnet.r: Bulevirtide monotherapy rarely produces target-not-detected HDV RNA at week 48, while the antibody plus siRNA combination reached high rates in phase 2; the co-primary sustained response after end of treatment is the main risk.

haiku.r: The main threat is the strict HDV RNA target-not-detected endpoint at week 48, which can read lower than expected even when the drug works.

carbon.r: Although Week 48 undetectable HDV RNA rates should strongly exceed bulevirtide monotherapy, co-listing 24-week post-treatment TND as a primary outcome creates ambiguity at the Week 48 readout.

sol.r: A large on-treatment difference may not satisfy all registered primary objectives: suppression must also persist 24 weeks after treatment ends, with that result available by the deadline.

trials.t: Study of Reformulated Levulan Kerastick Plus PDT for Actinic Keratosis on Face and Scalp
trials.ep: Complete clearance of all actinic keratosis lesions in the face or bald scalp treatment area at week 12, after up to two PDT sessions

fable.r: Only about 40 patients per arm: if the reformulated product with short incubation clears all lesions in only 25-30% of patients, as in the 2016 short-incubation study, a single-arm comparison could miss significance despite low vehicle clearance.

opus.r: With only about 40 patients per active arm, an unexpectedly high vehicle-PDT clearance rate or a weaker reformulation could shrink the gap, though ALA-PDT effects on face and scalp have historically been large.

sonnet.r: ALA PDT versus vehicle PDT for face and scalp AK has consistently shown large complete clearance differences; only the small sample size (40 per arm) and a possible weaker new formulation or short incubation are risks.

haiku.r: The main risk is the strict complete-clearance definition at week 12, which needs every lesion in the treated area gone after up to two PDT sessions.

carbon.r: Splitting 160 participants across four treatment and incubation arms yields roughly 40 patients per arm, though the very large historical effect of 20% ALA blue-light PDT keeps power high.

sol.r: Whole-field complete clearance is more demanding than clearing individual lesions, and an insufficient incubation period could reduce the established efficacy of ALA-PDT.

trials.t: Study of Reformulated Levulan Kerastick Plus PDT for Actinic Keratosis on Upper Extremities
trials.ep: Complete clearance of all actinic keratosis lesions in the upper-extremity treatment area at week 12, after up to two PDT sessions

fable.r: The reformulated ALA would have to perform clearly worse than the original on the arms, where complete clearance was only 31% versus 13% for vehicle, for a 260-patient trial to miss.

opus.r: Actinic keratoses on the arms are thicker and respond less to ALA-PDT than facial lesions, so complete clearance with the reformulated Kerastick could be modest, though 130 per arm leaves ample power for a 15-point gap.

sonnet.r: Upper-extremity AK clears less well than face/scalp with ALA PDT, so the gap is smaller, but with 130 per arm a 25-35 point difference is very likely significant.

haiku.r: The strict complete-clearance endpoint at week 12, applied to a larger treatment area, is the main way this trial misses.

carbon.r: Upper-extremity actinic keratoses are thicker and less responsive to topical ALA penetration than facial lesions, yielding lower complete clearance rates if the reformulated vehicle underperforms.

sol.r: Upper-extremity AK is less responsive to PDT than facial disease, making adequate delivery by the reformulated product the main residual efficacy risk.

trials.t: Pharmacokinetic Study of QL2107 Versus Keytruda® for Adjuvant Therapy of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
trials.ep: Pembrolizumab AUC over one 21-day interval after the first dose and at steady state (cycle 7)

fable.r: Both first-dose and cycle-7 AUC must fall within the equivalence bounds in about 146 patients with 30-40% PK variability and dropouts before steady state, so a wide interval or a small true exposure difference could fail one co-primary.

opus.r: Failure would most likely come from a true exposure difference between QL2107 and Keytruda (for example from glycosylation or charge-variant differences) or from attrition reducing the cycle-7 steady-state PK set.

sonnet.r: Pembrolizumab biosimilar PK equivalence on two AUC endpoints with about 73 per arm; both must fall within the margins, and interpatient PK variability in patients can make the 90% interval tight.

haiku.r: The main risk is wide exposure variability in adjuvant patients, which could push one of the two AUC ratios outside the protocol margins.

carbon.r: Early treatment discontinuations, relapse, or immunogenicity before Cycle 7 could shrink the steady-state PK evaluable set and widen the 90% confidence interval past equivalence bounds.

sol.r: Unexpected exposure variability or loss of evaluable patients by cycle 7 could prevent both AUC confidence intervals from fitting within the equivalence margins.

trials.t: Study of CM512 Injection in Subjects With Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria(CSU)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in weekly Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7) at Week 16

fable.r: With 48 patients and a UAS7 change SD near 12, only an effect of 8-10 points reaches significance, more than TSLP or IL-13 pathway blockade has shown by week 16 in CSU.

opus.r: TSLP/IL-13 blockade is unproven in CSU (tezepelumab missed at week 16) and IL-13 alone lacks dupilumab's IL-4 arm, so with 24 per arm and a sizeable placebo response a 5-point gap would not reach significance.

sonnet.r: Only 24 patients per arm with a UAS7 SD near 11 needs a difference of about 6.5 points; a TSLP/IL-13 bispecific has an uncertain CSU effect and placebo response on background antihistamine is sizeable.

haiku.r: With 24 patients per arm and a UAS7 standard deviation near 9.5, the standard error of the difference is about 2.8 points, so a true effect of about 6 points is needed to reach significance. The dose and mechanism are not stated.

carbon.r: With only 48 participants total and high UAS7 spontaneous remission and patient-to-patient variance, a moderate treatment benefit could easily miss two-sided p<0.05.

sol.r: With approximately 24 patients per arm, ordinary UAS7 variability and a substantial placebo improvement could obscure a clinically useful treatment effect.

trials.t: A Study Evaluating TRIV-509 in Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants with improvement of atopic dermatitis at week 16 (response threshold not defined in record)

fable.r: KLK5/7 inhibition is clinically unproven in atopic dermatitis and a systemic antibody may not change skin inflammation enough within 16 weeks to beat a 15-25% placebo response.

opus.r: KLK5/KLK7 inhibition targets barrier proteases, a mechanism with no randomized AD efficacy data; with about 48 per arm the responder difference must be around 15-17 points to be significant, more than a barrier-directed antibody is likely to deliver.

sonnet.r: First-in-class KLK5/7 barrier mechanism in AD is unproven; upstream or novel mechanisms often show only a modest margin over placebo in a phase 2a of about 48 per arm, and the response threshold is undefined.

haiku.r: Two arms of about 47 to 48 patients give a standard error near 9 points for a responder difference, so only an effect of about 18 points or more reaches significance. The undefined improvement threshold makes the control rate uncertain.

carbon.r: Dual kallikrein 5/7 protease inhibition is an unvalidated epidermal-barrier mechanism in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, where non-Th2 targets have historically shown low efficacy.

sol.r: TRIV-509 may not produce enough stringent week-16 responses to separate from placebo, and the undefined improvement threshold adds uncertainty.

trials.t: A Study to Compare the Effectiveness and Safety of T1695 Versus Ciclosporin in Participants With Moderate to Severe Vernal Keratoconjunctivitis
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Day 29 in corneal fluorescein staining grade (0-5 modified Oxford scale) in the study eye

fable.r: Ciclosporin emulsion is an effective comparator, so a 4-week difference in corneal staining is likely to be small (about 0.2-0.3 grade) relative to the 0.4 grade needed for superiority with 60 per arm.

opus.r: Ciclosporin emulsion is an effective active comparator, so showing superiority on a coarse 0-5 staining scale at day 29 with 60 children per arm is unlikely; the trial may be estimation-only or non-inferiority.

sonnet.r: Active comparator ciclosporin already lowers corneal staining well in VKC; the unknown T1695 must match or beat it at 4 weeks in 60 children per arm, and superiority is much harder than non-inferiority.

haiku.r: Ciclosporin is an established VKC treatment, so beating it on corneal staining by a clear margin in pediatric patients is hard to show. A standard deviation near 0.9 grade points with 60 per arm detects a difference of about 0.3 points, but the true advantage is likely small.

carbon.r: Topical ciclosporin ophthalmic emulsion already produces substantial 4-week reductions in corneal fluorescein staining in pediatric VKC, leaving narrow headroom for superiority.

sol.r: Ciclosporin is an effective active comparator, leaving limited room for a statistically convincing additional reduction in corneal staining after only four weeks.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate LY3537021 for the Treatment of Nausea and Vomiting Caused by Chemotherapy in Adults With Cancer
trials.c: Nausea; Vomiting; Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
trials.ep: Complete response (no vomiting, no rescue medication) in the delayed phase, 24 to 120 hours after first chemotherapy infusion

fable.r: On top of guideline triple or quadruple antiemetic prophylaxis the control delayed complete response is already about 65-70%, leaving a GIP receptor agonist with unproven clinical anti-emetic efficacy little room to add the 13 points needed.

opus.r: GIP receptor agonism is antiemetic in ferrets and shrews but unproven in humans; on top of guideline triple or quadruple prophylaxis the delayed-phase CR is already near 65-75%, leaving little room to show a 13-point gain with about 100 per arm.

sonnet.r: Placebo plus standard antiemetics (NK1, 5-HT3, dexamethasone) already gives roughly 60-75% delayed-phase complete response, leaving a ceiling; about 100 per arm needs roughly +13 points to reach significance.

haiku.r: Delayed-phase complete response on a standard antiemetic backbone is already high, so a novel add-on needs about 15 points over placebo to be significant with 102 per arm. The dose is not stated and the mechanism is new for this indication.

carbon.r: Modern triple or quadruple standard-of-care antiemetic prophylaxis already achieves ~70-80% delayed complete response, making incremental superiority hard to power with 204 patients.

sol.r: Modern multidrug antiemetic prophylaxis may leave too few delayed-phase failures for a novel add-on to show a significant benefit with about 102 patients per arm.

trials.t: Aleniglipron Phase 2 Body Composition Study
trials.sp: Gasherbrum Bio, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Structure Therapeutics
trials.c: Obesity, Overweight, or Chronic Weight Management
trials.ep: Percent change in total body fat mass by DXA from baseline to week 44

fable.r: The 5:1 design leaves about 12 placebo patients, so the comparison could be reported descriptively or blurred by discontinuations, although the expected fat-mass difference of 15-20 points is large.

opus.r: Only 12 placebo patients, but a GLP-1 agonist giving 11-15% placebo-adjusted weight loss cuts fat mass by about 20%, far beyond the noise; failure would need unexpected dropouts or very poor adherence.

sonnet.r: Effect is very likely large (aleniglipron gave 11-15% placebo-adjusted weight loss), so the main risk is only that the sponsor reports no explicit significance test or that only 12 placebo patients widen the variance.

haiku.r: The placebo arm has only about 12 patients, so the control estimate is noisy, but the expected fat mass effect of a weekly oral agent in this class is large enough to be significant despite that. The main uncertainty is whether a primary-result statement is public by June 2027.

carbon.r: Oral small-molecule GLP-1 escalation causes ~10-15% GI discontinuations and the 12-patient control arm adds variance, though the huge fat-mass effect preserves >95% power.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance and missing week-44 DXA measurements are the main residual threats despite a strong expectation of substantial fat loss.

trials.t: Brivekimig for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Hidradenitis Suppurativa
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving HiSCR75 at Week 16

fable.r: Placebo HiSCR response is high and variable in HS trials and each dose arm has only about 40-50 patients, so a 20-point HiSCR75 gain could miss significance in a given arm.

opus.r: HS trials have variable placebo responses, and HiSCR75 with roughly 50 per arm in a multi-dose design needs about a 20-point gap, so a high placebo rate could sink an otherwise active TNF/OX40L bispecific.

sonnet.r: HiSCR75 is a demanding endpoint and a dose-ranging design leaves only about 50 patients per arm, so even a real TNF/OX40L effect of 15 points sits near the significance threshold.

haiku.r: Dual TNF and IL-17A blockade should clear HiSCR75 well above placebo at the highest dose, so a significant result is likely. The main risks are a weaker-than-expected top dose in a dose-ranging design and the chance that the readout slips past June 2027.

carbon.r: Dividing 208 biologic-naive and biologic-experienced HS patients across multiple dose arms leaves roughly 50 patients per arm to achieve significance on the stringent HiSCR75 endpoint.

sol.r: Dose-ranging likely leaves substantially fewer than 104 patients at the highest dose, making the stringent HiSCR75 endpoint vulnerable to sampling noise and placebo response.

trials.t: Safety in Adult Participants With Atrial Fibrillation Who Are Treated With Anticoagulation
trials.ep: Incidence of any bleeding

fable.r: Enrolment of 1200 patients was still open about three months before the registered primary completion, so a moderate delay is plausible; early termination and results posting by August 2027 are both unlikely.

opus.r: Large 1,200-patient AF safety study still recruiting with a February 2027 primary completion, so recruitment will likely run past late 2026 and the registered date is likely pushed back; Regeneron keeps records current and the FXI programme is a priority, so stopping or early posting is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Large (1200) open-label safety trial in AF with a primary completion of Feb 2027 while still recruiting; slippage of a quarter is plausible but Regeneron usually posts results about a year after completion.

haiku.r: Large safety-focused trial of 1200 patients with a registered primary completion in February 2027, so the main timing risk is slow enrolment that pushes completion past May 2027.

carbon.r: With 89 cardiology sites across the Americas enrolling 1,200 common atrial fibrillation patients for a short 12-week bleeding endpoint, ROXI-ATLAS should complete with low termination risk and modest schedule risk.

sol.r: Recruiting 1,200 anticoagulated patients on a tight schedule creates appreciable delay risk, while short primary follow-up and a well-resourced sponsor favor eventual completion.

trials.t: A Clinical Study of Tulisokibart (MK-7240) to Treat Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) (MK-7240-014)
trials.ep: Share of participants achieving ACR20 response at week 12, on background methotrexate

fable.r: TL1A blockade has no clinical proof of concept in RA; a modest true effect would be swamped by a 35-45% placebo ACR20 with only about 60 patients per arm.

opus.r: Anti-TL1A has no clinical RA efficacy data and many cytokine-targeted mechanisms beyond TNF, IL-6, JAK, CD80/86 and CD20 have failed in MTX-IR RA; with about 62 per arm ACR20 needs a 17-point gap.

sonnet.r: TL1A blockade has no proven efficacy in RA; with about 62 per arm, ACR20 needs roughly +17 points over a 35-40% placebo+MTX response, and a multiple-dose design adds multiplicity.

haiku.r: TL1A blockade is established in gut inflammation, but its benefit in rheumatoid arthritis is unproven, and the placebo plus methotrexate response is high. Any dose beating placebo meets the objective, which lifts the chance to about even.

carbon.r: TL1A blockade has proven clinical efficacy in inflammatory bowel disease, but its effect size in methotrexate-refractory rheumatoid arthritis is unproven and could fall short of the roughly 18-point ACR20 separation needed with about 62 patients per arm.

sol.r: TL1A blockade may produce too little incremental joint improvement over methotrexate to separate from a substantial placebo ACR20 response in approximately 62 patients per arm.

trials.t: A Research Study on How Well Different Doses of the Medicine NNC0662-0419 Help People Living With Overweight or Obesity
trials.ep: Part B: percent change in body weight from baseline to end of treatment at week 36

fable.r: Efficacy failure is unlikely; the realistic miss is GI-driven dropouts at the top dose or a disclosure that gives no clear statement on the Part B primary.

opus.r: A once-weekly incretin-class agent built for over 25% weight loss should beat placebo by a wide margin at 36 weeks; the realistic failure route is GI intolerance and dropouts eroding the top dose, not lack of efficacy.

sonnet.r: A potent weekly incretin/amylin-class candidate versus placebo over 36 weeks should win clearly; residual risk is only that smaller Part B arms or tolerability dropouts blunt the effect, or the headline gives no formal test.

haiku.r: A weekly obesity agent at its highest Part B dose should lose well over placebo's 2 to 3 percent by week 36, so superiority is likely. The main risk is that the public statement covers the combined study or comes after June 2027, not an isolated Part B result.

carbon.r: Potent next-generation obesity peptides targeting greater than 25% weight loss frequently cause gastrointestinal intolerance or premature discontinuations, or may be summarized only briefly in pipeline updates if tolerability limits advancement.

sol.r: The principal threat is that tolerability limits sustained high-dose exposure or causes enough discontinuation to compromise the week-36 efficacy analysis.

trials.t: A Study to Compare the Efficacy, Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Trifarotene 50 mcg/g Cream in Chinese Subjects With Acne Vulgaris
trials.ep: Facial IGA success (IGA 0 or 1 with at least a 2-grade improvement from baseline) at Week 12

fable.r: A high vehicle response or a smaller IGA delta, as in PERFECT 1 (about 10 points), could leave the IGA co-primary short even though lesion counts should separate.

opus.r: Three co-primaries must all be won; a high vehicle IGA success rate, common in acne trials, could squeeze the IGA difference below significance even though lesion counts should separate.

sonnet.r: Trifarotene already won two global phase 3 trials with 10-17 point IGA gains; with 280 per arm a China bridging study should replicate, but all three co-primaries (IGA plus two lesion counts) must be met.

haiku.r: Phase 3 of a retinoid-class topical agent against vehicle with 561 patients split evenly, a sample large enough to detect a gap similar to the US phase 3 result. The main uncertainty is whether a public statement on the facial IGA result comes out by June 2027.

carbon.r: Daily vehicle cream application and skincare routines in acne trials can elevate vehicle IGA response rates above 25%, narrowing the Week 12 responder margin across the three co-primary facial endpoints.

sol.r: A high vehicle response could narrow the facial IGA difference enough to miss significance, even if lesion-count outcomes confirm activity.

trials.t: QA108 Phase III Study in Subjects With Intermediate AMD
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in drusen area in the study eye at Week 24

fable.r: No oral agent has reliably shrunk drusen, and drusen area over 24 weeks is noisy, so a small or absent true effect is the main way to miss.

opus.r: No oral agent has convincingly shrunk drusen in 24 weeks; percent change in drusen area is noisy and a TCM granule may have no measurable anatomical effect against a placebo arm whose drusen change little.

sonnet.r: Drusen area percent change over 24 weeks is a noisy imaging surrogate with drift in placebo; a Chinese herbal granule may show a modest drusen reduction but a short window and measurement variability could blur it.

haiku.r: Main risk is a noisy drusen-area imaging endpoint at 24 weeks with an unproven herbal mechanism; recruitment still open at launch makes a late completion date likely.

carbon.r: Anatomical regression of macular drusen area over just 24 weeks has proven refractory to systemic pharmacotherapy in intermediate AMD, making a statistically significant imaging improvement over placebo unlikely.

sol.r: An unvalidated oral treatment may not change retinal drusen over 24 weeks enough to overcome imaging variability and heterogeneous natural changes in drusen area.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate KYN-5356 in Adults With Cognitive Impairment Associated With Schizophrenia
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Day 28 in the BAC App (digital Brief Assessment of Cognition for Schizophrenia) composite T-score

fable.r: Four weeks of an untested mechanism is unlikely to move BACS beyond placebo practice effects, as larger CIAS programmes have repeatedly shown.

opus.r: CIAS has a long record of failed pro-cognitive mechanisms; with about 37 per arm over 28 days and practice effects on the BAC App, a KAT-II inhibitor needs a large effect to reach significance.

sonnet.r: A 28-day DAAO-type cognition trial with about 37 per arm has low power against a modest true effect, and prior DAAO inhibitors (luvadaxistat, iclepertin) failed on cognition.

haiku.r: Efficacy risk is a weak cognitive effect at 37 per arm on a hard-to-move CIAS endpoint; the record does not state the milligram dose, so the dose is uncertain.

carbon.r: Cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia has an exceptionally low clinical success rate, and 37 patients per arm over 28 inpatient days face large BACS practice effects and high threshold effect sizes.

sol.r: KAT-II inhibition may not deliver a sufficiently large cognitive benefit beyond retesting and residential-care effects within only 28 days.

trials.t: A Study of GR1014 Cutaneous Gel for the Prevention of Skin Reactions Caused by Radiation Therapy for Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Percentage of participants with no radiation dermatitis (CTCAE grade 0) at any time from first radiotherapy session to 4 weeks after the last

fable.r: A topical thiol may not reach basal skin cells in protective amounts, and keeping patients at grade 0 throughout is a demanding endpoint requiring a roughly 20-point gain.

opus.r: Grade 0 throughout requires no faint erythema at any weekly visit; with 26 Gy in 5 fractions most patients still get grade 1, and topical radioprotectors have rarely shown clear benefit, so a 91-per-arm trial may not separate.

sonnet.r: With 5-fraction radiotherapy most patients develop at least grade 1 erythema, so the grade 0 responder rate is low in both arms and a topical radioprotector needs about a 14 point gain to reach significance with 91 per arm.

haiku.r: Risk is power: 91 per arm on a low-base-rate grade 0 endpoint where a 6 to 7 point gain is hard to detect at 0.05.

carbon.r: Preventing even faint CTCAE Grade 1 erythema entirely over 4 weeks post-radiotherapy requires substantial epidermal radioprotection from brief pre-fraction topical amifostine thiol application.

sol.r: Topical delivery may not protect basal skin cells sufficiently to prevent even mild erythema throughout follow-up, despite amifostine's established systemic radioprotective activity.

trials.t: Investigation of the Efficacy of a Probiotic Mixture in Moderate Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Mechanistic Trial
trials.c: MASLD - Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease; Fatty Liver Disease, Nonalcoholic; Overweight (BMI > 25)
trials.ep: Change in liver steatosis by FibroScan controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) from baseline to 6 months

fable.r: With 30 per arm and noisy CAP readings, any plausible probiotic effect on steatosis is too small to reach significance.
