opus.r: With 30 per arm and a between-patient SD of CAP change around 35 dB/m, only an effect of about 25 dB/m would reach significance, larger than probiotics usually achieve.

sonnet.r: Thirty per arm and a CAP change with SD around 40 dB/m leave only about 20 dB/m detectable; probiotics usually shift CAP by 10 to 15 dB/m at best, and the primary also names FAST score.

haiku.r: Risk is an underpowered 30-per-arm test of a modest liver-fat effect, and the trial was still recruiting at launch, so completion is likely late.

carbon.r: Oral probiotics exert minimal direct hepatic defatting effects when body weight is stable, and 30 participants per arm cannot reliably overcome large FibroScan CAP variability and dual CAP/FAST assessment.

sol.r: A modest probiotic effect may not exceed CAP measurement noise or also improve FAST in patients whose fibrosis-related measures already have little room to improve.

trials.t: AURA-IPF: A Randomized Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of AP02 (Nintedanib Solution) in IPF
trials.ep: Change from baseline in morning pre-dose forced vital capacity at week 12

fable.r: Twelve weeks and about 53 per arm leave the trial short of power unless inhaled nintedanib nearly halts FVC decline.

opus.r: About 53 per arm over 12 weeks with an FVC-change SD near 140 mL gives roughly 35-45% power even for an oral-nintedanib-sized effect of about 50 mL, so a real benefit can miss significance.

sonnet.r: Twelve-week FVC change with about 53 per arm and SD near 150 mL can only detect an effect of roughly 60 mL, while oral nintedanib shows about 30 to 40 mL benefit over 12 weeks.

haiku.r: Risk is a 12-week FVC test at 53 per arm where a plausible effect of about 25 to 35 mL sits below the significance threshold; still recruiting at launch makes late completion likely.

carbon.r: Twelve weeks is very short to detect an antifibrotic FVC slope difference in 53 IPF patients per arm because untreated 12-week FVC decline averages only about 50 to 60 mL against high spirometric noise.

sol.r: Twelve weeks may be too short for slowing fibrosis to create an FVC difference large enough to distinguish from spirometric variability in approximately 53 patients per arm.

trials.t: Comparability Trial of the MVA-BN Vaccine Manufactured in Different Production Cells
trials.ep: Vaccinia neutralizing antibody titres (PRNT) two weeks after the second dose

fable.r: Equivalence would fail only if the quail-cell process changes potency or particle quality enough to shift PRNT titres outside the margins, or if assay variability widens the interval.

opus.r: The main risk is that MVA-BN grown in the CCX.E10 quail line yields lower neutralizing titres than chicken-fibroblast Jynneos so the GMT-ratio lower bound falls below the margin.

sonnet.r: A quail-cell versus chicken-cell comparability design with about 485 per arm is well powered for a standard GMT-ratio margin; the main risk is a real shift in immunogenicity from the new production cells or a co-primary safety endpoint.

haiku.r: Risk is a quail-cell lot with lower neutralizing titres that falls outside a tight protocol margin on the GMT ratio; the margin is not stated in the record.

carbon.r: Transitioning MVA-BN production from primary chicken embryo fibroblasts to the continuous CCX.E10 quail cell line could shift vaccinia neutralizing antibody geometric mean titres outside strict equivalence margins.

sol.r: The production-cell change could alter effective potency or antigen presentation enough to place neutralizing-antibody titres outside the protocol's comparability margins.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate HM15275 in Obese or Overweight Subjects Without Diabetes Mellitus
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from week 1 to week 37 (36 weeks of treatment)

fable.r: Efficacy is very likely; the main threat is GI intolerance and dropouts at the top dose blurring the estimate, or vague wording of the topline.

opus.r: Efficacy against placebo is near certain for an incretin triple agonist at 36 weeks; the only plausible failure route is high GI-driven discontinuation diluting the treatment-policy estimate.

sonnet.r: A weekly triple-agonist class drug at its top dose over 36 weeks is very likely to beat placebo on percent weight change; the risk is a lower-than-expected effect from tolerability-limited titration.

haiku.r: Efficacy is very likely given the incretin class; the risk is a top dose that falls short of the class effect, and the registry date fits an early-2027 readout.

carbon.r: Triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon receptor agonism carries gastrointestinal, heart-rate, and hepatic safety risks that represent the only realistic threat to meeting a 36-week weight-loss primary endpoint.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance or other triple-agonist adverse effects could limit titration and sustained exposure, rather than ordinary sampling error preventing superiority.

trials.t: Immunogenicity, Safety, and Tolerability of rF1V-1018 Vaccine in Adults 18 to 55 Years of Age
trials.c: Prevention of Pneumonic Plague Resulting From Aerosol Exposure to Yersinia Pestis
trials.ep: Anti-rF1V antibody level

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the immunogenicity primary is fixed four weeks after the last dose, so the trial should finish close to its registered date, with results posted only after the read date.

opus.r: Fully enrolled DoD-funded dose-finding vaccine study with a January 2027 primary completion; likely finishes near schedule, though Part 2 selection could push dates, and posting by August 2027 is unlikely before the FDAAA deadline.

sonnet.r: Dose-finding plague vaccine trial with descriptive immunogenicity, DoD collaboration; Part 2 selection from Part 1 could stretch the registered timeline but a stop is unlikely, and posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Active, not recruiting with a January 2027 primary completion; DoD co-funding and four US sites make a slip possible, and CT.gov posting by August 2027 is uncertain.

carbon.r: Because enrollment is already complete for this US DoD-backed Phase 2 vaccine trial, primary completion in early 2027 is likely on schedule, though ClinicalTrials.gov results posting typically trails primary completion by close to a year.

sol.r: Closed enrollment and established vaccine components favor completion near schedule, while registry results may await completion of longer safety follow-up.

trials.t: A Study of NT 201 in Adults With Moderate to Severe Platysma Prominence in Europe (PLATINUM EU)
trials.c: Neuromuscular Agents; Peripheral Nervous System Agents; Physiological Effects of Drugs
trials.ep: Composite: MAPSD grade 1 or 2 with at least 2-grade improvement from baseline, by both investigator and participant, at week 2 of main period

fable.r: The only realistic failure route is the stringent composite, which needs a 2-grade gain on Merz's own scale from both investigator and participant at week 2, giving an active response well below the usual toxin responder rates.

opus.r: The composite needs investigator and patient to agree on a 2-grade gain at week 2, which caps responder rates near 40%, but placebo rates are near zero so failure is very unlikely.

sonnet.r: Botulinum toxin has a clear, fast effect on platysma bands, so a 2-grade composite at week 2 versus a near-zero placebo rate is very likely met; the composite of two raters is the only real risk.

haiku.r: Botulinum toxin for platysma prominence is well established; the main risk is the strict two-assessor, two-grade composite pulling the response rate below expectation.

carbon.r: Stringent dual investigator-and-participant 2-grade composite responder criteria could lower absolute response rates if dosing is conservative, though placebo response near zero preserves very high statistical power.

sol.r: Insufficient dosing could limit the stringent response agreed by both raters, although peak botulinum-toxin activity and very low placebo response make separation highly likely.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, Safety, Radiological and Clinical Effects of Subcutaneous Ublituximab in Participants With Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis (RMS)
trials.ep: Area Under the Curve From Week 0 to Week 24 (AUC0-W24) of Ublituximab

fable.r: A fully enrolled pharmacokinetic bridging study whose week-24 primary date has passed should run to completion, with registry results delayed past the read date while the subcutaneous formulation is under regulatory review.

opus.r: Fully enrolled PK bridging study with October 2026 primary completion and long extension; termination is unlikely and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given non-US sites and a possible delayed-submission certification for the new route.

sonnet.r: Open-label PK bridging trial of SC versus IV ublituximab; the registered primary (Week 24 AUC) is already past, long extension to 2028 delays posting, and a stop or primary change is unlikely.

haiku.r: PK-only open-label trial, active and not recruiting, with a registered study completion in late 2028; posting is voluntary as no site is in the US.

carbon.r: Enrollment is complete and the Week 24 pharmacokinetic primary completion window is passing, making termination or primary outcome amendments unlikely while results posting before August 2027 remains modest.

sol.r: Closed enrollment and a short objective pharmacokinetic primary assessment favor continued follow-up rather than termination, but registry posting may wait beyond August 2027.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of ZL-1109 in Chinese Participants With Active Thyroid Eye Disease
trials.ep: Proptosis responder rate: percentage with ≥2 mm proptosis reduction in the study eye without ≥2 mm increase in fellow eye, at Week 24

fable.r: Failure would need subcutaneous VRDN-003 exposure to fall well short of intravenous anti-IGF-1R antibodies, cutting the proptosis response enough that a small placebo arm could blur the difference.

opus.r: Anti-IGF-1R antibodies give very large proptosis responses against a low placebo rate; the only real risk is that the subcutaneous VRDN-003 regimen gives lower exposure than the IV agents and a smaller-than-expected separation in 54 vs 54 patients.

sonnet.r: IGF-1R blockade gives large proptosis responder gains over placebo in active TED; a Chinese phase 3 of 108 patients is well powered, so failure would need an unexpectedly weak effect or a high placebo response.

haiku.r: A 2 mm responder threshold at week 24 with 54 patients per arm is sensitive to exophthalmometry noise near the cut-off, though a large responder gap over placebo is expected.

carbon.r: Subcutaneous VRDN-003 dosing could theoretically underperform intravenous anti-IGF-1R benchmarks if trough exposure is lower, though class effect sizes in active TED far exceed the threshold needed for significance.

sol.r: The main threat is inadequate sustained exposure or activity from the subcutaneous regimen, rather than insufficient power for the large effect established for IGF-1R blockade.

trials.t: A Study of S-337395 in Symptomatic Nonhospitalized Adults With Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Who Are at High Risk of Progression to Severe Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline in RSV RNA viral load (nasopharyngeal swab, qRT-PCR) at Day 2

fable.r: Three viral-load time points are registered as primary and day 2, one day after the first dose in patients whose virus is already falling, may not separate from placebo even if days 4 and 6 do.

opus.r: All three viral-load time points are registered primaries; the Day 2 change comes after barely a day of dosing in older outpatients treated up to 72 h after symptom onset, when viral load is already falling, so the early difference may not reach significance even if Day 4 and Day 6 do.

sonnet.r: Three co-primary viral-load time points must all hit; Day 2 is early and placebo viral load also falls on its own, and enrolment of high-risk RSV outpatients is seasonal and may run past the registered date.

haiku.r: Early RSV antivirals usually show modest Day 2 viral-load effects, and all three co-primary timepoints (Days 2, 4, 6) must be significant with 96 per arm, so an effect below about 0.35 log10 would fail.

carbon.r: In naturally acquired adult RSV enrolled up to 72 hours after symptom onset, viral load is already peaking or declining, making simultaneous statistical significance across Days 2, 4, and 6 challenging.

sol.r: Natural-infection timing and RNA persistence may blunt separation at Day 2 or Day 6, and all three registered primary time points must succeed.

trials.t: Phase 2 EL219 Versus Liposomal Amphotericin B or Voriconazole for Early Antifungal Therapy
trials.ep: All-cause mortality by day 21 (plus or minus 3 days) in the intent-to-treat set

fable.r: Sixty patients with day-21 mortality near 8% per arm cannot show a mortality difference, so the trial can only describe safety and survival rather than meet a tested efficacy objective.

opus.r: With 30 patients per arm and an expected day-21 mortality around 10-15%, no plausible difference in all-cause mortality can reach significance; the phase 2 is built for safety and estimation, not to show superior survival over LAmB or voriconazole.

sonnet.r: A 60-patient phase 2 focused on safety cannot show a significant day-21 mortality difference when comparator mortality is only around 10%; at most a numerical trend will be reported.

haiku.r: Day-21 mortality with 30 patients per arm can only show superiority if the effect is very large, which an early antifungal in this population is unlikely to deliver, and the trial may run late.

carbon.r: With only 60 patients randomized against active first-line antifungals (voriconazole or liposomal amphotericin B), the trial is severely underpowered for superiority or standard non-inferiority on Day 21 mortality.

sol.r: About 30 participants per arm and relatively few deaths by Day 21 make mortality superiority improbable even if tolerability improves enough to justify further development.

trials.t: A Study of LY3938577 in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Previously Treated With Basal Insulin
trials.ep: Change from baseline in percentage of time with glucose 70-180 mg/dL (time in range), baseline through week 20

fable.r: With about 50 patients per arm and a between-patient SD near 15 points of time in range, even a small true deficit against well-titrated degludec leaves the confidence bound short of the non-inferiority margin.

opus.r: With 50 per arm and a between-patient SD of about 13 points in time-in-range change, the 95% CI on the difference spans roughly plus or minus 5 points, so unless the unstated non-inferiority margin is generous a novel basal insulin with similar true efficacy can still fail to exclude the margin.

sonnet.r: Non-inferiority on CGM time in range with only 50 per arm gives a confidence interval about 6 points wide, and the margin is not stated, so a miss is plausible even if the new insulin is truly equivalent.

haiku.r: A non-inferiority test with 50 patients per arm and an unstated margin is only as strong as its margin; if the margin is tight, the lower bound of the time-in-range difference may miss it.

carbon.r: With 100 participants split across arms and between-patient CGM variability around 16-17 percentage points, random sampling noise or conservative initial titration in an open-label Phase 2 could miss a tight non-inferiority margin.

sol.r: Titrated degludec should improve time in range substantially, while an undisclosed non-inferiority margin and roughly 50 patients per arm leave uncertainty about adequate precision.

trials.t: Safety and Tolerability of a Newcastle Disease Virus-Based Mucosal COVID-19 Vaccine in Previously Vaccinated Adults
trials.ep: Safety and Tolerability of the NDV-HXP-S-KP.2 Vaccine Compared With an Approved mRNA COVID-19 Vaccine

fable.r: A fully enrolled phase 2a safety study whose 180-day follow-up date has passed should complete, with results more likely posted at or after the 12-month deadline in September 2027 than before the read date.

opus.r: Enrolment and the 180-day follow-up appear finished, so the trial should close out normally; a small BARDA-funded sponsor may post results near or after the 12-month deadline in September 2027.

sonnet.r: Safety-only phase 2a that has finished its 180-day follow-up; small private sponsor makes a results posting within a year of completion uncommon.

haiku.r: Safety-only trial with no efficacy goal; it is likely to finish on schedule, and the main question is whether a small US-only sponsor posts its results within a year of the September 2026 primary completion.

carbon.r: This 200-participant US mucosal COVID-19 vaccine Phase 2a study has passed its registered September 2026 completion date without stopping, making timely completion and statutory 1-year results posting fairly likely.

sol.r: With enrollment closed and six-month safety follow-up already scheduled to finish, completion is much more likely than termination, although results posting could lag the deadline.

trials.t: A Study of Macupatide (LY3532226) and Eloralintide (LY3841136), Alone or in Combination, in Adults With Obesity or Overweight and With Type 2 Diabetes
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline to Week 32 in body weight in adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes

fable.r: Against placebo the combination should win easily; the risk is that the protocol's primary comparison is with the single agents and macupatide adds too little weight loss on top of eloralintide to show it with about 50 per arm.

opus.r: Combining an amylin agonist with a second incretin-class peptide should give double-digit placebo-adjusted weight loss; the main way to miss would be heavy GI-driven discontinuation in the combination arm eroding the treatment-regimen estimate in a 50-patient arm.

sonnet.r: An amylin plus incretin combination should clearly outperform placebo on weight at week 32; the realistic downside is GI-driven dropouts diluting the effect.

haiku.r: Risk is low: a combination with amylin and GLP-1-class mechanisms should clearly beat placebo on weight at 50 per arm; the residual risk is a weak dose arm or a readout that lands after June 2027.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerability from co-administering an incretin agonist with an amylin agonist is the main operational risk, though efficacy over placebo at Week 32 is virtually assured.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance and discontinuations could compromise combination exposure, while dose uncertainty and unproven additivity matter more than separating an amylin-based regimen from placebo.

trials.t: Clinical Study to Investigate the Antihypersensitivity Efficacy of a Novel Dentifrice
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Schiff sensitivity score to an evaporative (air) stimulus at week 8

fable.r: The objective needs the combination to beat stannous fluoride alone on both Schiff score and tactile threshold, and stannous fluoride by itself already gives most of the relief, leaving little for potassium nitrate to add at week 8.

opus.r: The trial's own hypothesis is superiority of the combination over SnF2 alone and KNO3 alone as well as vehicle, on both Schiff and tactile endpoints; beating an active stannous fluoride dentifrice by a significant margin on both measures is the hard part.

sonnet.r: Superiority over vehicle is almost certain, but the stated hypothesis also compares the combination with SnF2-only and KNO3-only dentifrices on two primary endpoints, where the margin of benefit is small.

haiku.r: The test dentifrice must beat each of three active references and vehicle on both co-primary endpoints, so the likely miss is that the stannous fluoride plus potassium nitrate combination is not clearly superior to stannous fluoride alone.

carbon.r: While superiority over vehicle is nearly certain, meeting the trial's full co-primary objective requires beating active stannous fluoride and potassium nitrate single-ingredient dentifrices on both evaporative and tactile sensitivity.

sol.r: The combination should beat vehicle, but superiority over both effective single-ingredient dentifrices on both air sensitivity and tactile threshold is considerably harder.

trials.t: A Clinical Study of Enlicitide in Participants With High Cholesterol (MK-0616-037)
trials.ep: Mean percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol at week 8

fable.r: Failure would require an operational or analysis problem, since an oral PCSK9 inhibitor plus rosuvastatin against double placebo should lower LDL-C by about 75% in untreated adults.

opus.r: Failure is nearly impossible: oral PCSK9 inhibition plus a statin against double placebo in lipid-therapy-naive adults yields a 70-plus point LDL-C difference; only a gross conduct problem would change that.

sonnet.r: Enlicitide alone cuts LDL-C by over 50% and rosuvastatin adds more, against a flat placebo, so the primary is essentially certain; the open question is disclosure timing.

haiku.r: The control arm is placebo with no statin, so superiority on LDL-C is close to certain; the residual risk is an unexpectedly weak oral effect on top of rosuvastatin, which is unlikely at this size.

carbon.r: Only severe operational, regulatory, or unexpected safety disruption could prevent coadministered enlicitide plus rosuvastatin from outperforming double placebo on Week 8 LDL-C.

sol.r: Combined LDL-C lowering should be very large; unexpectedly poor adherence or tolerability is the main residual threat to the registered comparison.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate Bowel Cleansing With PLENVU® Compared to Sodium Picosulfate in Participants Aged 1 to < 18 Years of Age in Preparation for Colonoscopy
trials.c: Bowel Cleansing Prior to Clinical Procedures
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving adequate bowel cleansing based on Boston Bowel Preparation Scale (BBPS)

fable.r: Enrolling 212 children across age bands within a year looks optimistic, so primary completion probably slips past April 2027, and results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is unlikely.

opus.r: Paediatric bowel-preparation trials requiring a scheduled colonoscopy enrol slowly across many European sites, so the January 2027 primary completion will probably be pushed back.

sonnet.r: Paediatric colonoscopy-prep trials recruit slowly and this one was still recruiting 10 months in; completion likely slips past April 2027, and a European sponsor is unlikely to post results by August.

haiku.r: Paediatric bowel-prep trial with descriptive efficacy only; recruitment was still open at launch against a January 2027 completion date, so the registry date is likely to slip.

carbon.r: Multi-country paediatric colonoscopy trials across ages 1 to 17 often face slower-than-planned recruitment in younger weight/age cohorts, creating a substantial risk of exceeding the 90-day completion window.

sol.r: Paediatric recruitment, especially in the youngest age bands, is the main threat to the January 2027 finish despite very short follow-up.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Effect of AZD0780 Tablets in Combination With Rosuvastatin Tablets on Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels (LDL-C) in Adult Participants With Dyslipidaemia
trials.ep: Percent change in LDL-C from baseline to week 12, on background rosuvastatin

fable.r: Only an operational failure or a much lower dose than in PURSUIT could prevent a significant LDL-C difference, since oral PCSK9 inhibition roughly halves LDL-C on statin background.

opus.r: With 38 per arm the trial is small, but the expected 50-point placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction is more than ten standard errors from zero, so failure is very unlikely.

sonnet.r: AZD0780 gave about 50% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction at 30 mg on background statin in PURSUIT, so a 76-patient trial should be strongly significant; the main risk is a lower dose or odd baseline definition.

haiku.r: With 38 per arm and a large expected LDL-C gap on top of rosuvastatin, failure on the primary is unlikely; the more likely miss is that AstraZeneca does not put the week-12 result in the public record by June 2027.

carbon.r: Poor adherence or high laboratory variance in a small single-country cohort is the main residual risk given AZD0780's large established LDL-C lowering effect.

sol.r: The residual efficacy risk is unexpectedly low exposure or an inadequately active dose, rather than an unusually strong placebo response after the statin run-in.

trials.t: A Study to Learn About Ritlecitinib for the Potential Treatment of Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria in Adults.
trials.ep: Change from baseline in weekly Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7, range 0-42) at Week 12

fable.r: Ritlecitinib's JAK3 and TEC-family inhibition may give a smaller UAS7 effect than dedicated BTK inhibitors, and with about 50-67 patients per arm and a large placebo response a 4-point effect would miss significance.

opus.r: Ritlecitinib's BTK inhibition is weaker than remibrutinib's and JAK3 blockade is unproven in CSU, so the UAS7 gain over a ~10-point placebo response may fall short of the ~4.5 points needed with about 67 per arm.

sonnet.r: Ritlecitinib (JAK3/TEC inhibitor) is unproven in CSU and CSU placebo response is large (about -10 UAS7 at Week 12), so roughly 4-5 points of separation is needed with about 67 per arm.

haiku.r: Ritlecitinib's UAS7 improvement over placebo at week 12 is likely modest, and the large CSU placebo response leaves little margin with about 67 per arm, though either active dose can carry the result.

carbon.r: Ritlecitinib's covalent BTK/TEC and JAK3 inhibition at 50-100 mg daily may not achieve sufficient mast-cell FceRI blockade in skin to clearly separate from CSU's sizable placebo response.

sol.r: JAK3/TEC inhibition may provide less CSU activity than hoped, leaving insufficient separation from a sizeable antihistamine-background placebo response.

trials.t: A Study on the Immune Response and Safety of Vaccine Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus Given to Chinese Adults 18 to 59 Years of Age at Increased Risk of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease
trials.ep: RSV-A neutralizing titers expressed as group Geometric Mean Titers (GMTs)

fable.r: Completed-enrolment single-dose immunobridging study; GSK usually posts results about a year after primary completion, so posting by the end of August 2027 is somewhat more likely than not.

opus.r: Enrolment is complete and the Day 31 immunogenicity primary has passed, so the trial should run to its December 2026 completion without incident, with results posting likely around mid-2027.

sonnet.r: Immunobridging study with primary completion already passed (July 2026); GSK generally posts CT.gov results within about 12 months of primary completion, so posting by Aug 2027 is more likely than not; stop or primary-outcome change is unlikely.

haiku.r: No efficacy goal, so the run depends on GSK's usual timely posting after a primary completion that has already passed, with little risk of stopping.

carbon.r: As an active, not-recruiting GSK immuno-bridging study whose July 2026 primary completion date has already passed, the trial is on track to finish follow-up and post results within 12 months.

sol.r: Enrollment and primary immunogenicity follow-up appear essentially complete, making routine completion and sponsor disclosure much more likely than stopping.

trials.t: A Phase IIb Study to Evaluate the Effect of Dapagliflozin in Combination With Baxdrostat Compared With Baxdrostat on Albuminuria in Participants With Chronic Kidney Disease and High Blood Pressure.
trials.ep: Change from baseline in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) at week 12 in CKD with hypertension

fable.r: UACR is highly variable and dapagliflozin's add-on effect on top of an aldosterone synthase inhibitor may be only 15-20% in participants without diabetes, leaving 111 per arm short of power.

opus.r: UACR is noisy and baxdrostat may already lower intraglomerular pressure, so dapagliflozin's add-on reduction could be nearer 15% than 25-30%, which 111 per arm may not detect.

sonnet.r: Dapagliflozin's UACR lowering is well established and roughly additive with MRA-type drugs, so the combination should beat baxdrostat alone; the residual risk is the high variance of UACR with about 105 per arm.

haiku.r: Baxdrostat alone should cut albuminuria sharply, leaving less room for the dapagliflozin add-on, though 111 per arm is well sized for an effect of this scale.

carbon.r: Large UACR lowering from background baxdrostat initiated at randomisation could compress the incremental Week 12 albuminuria reduction achievable by adding dapagliflozin.

sol.r: Baxdrostat may already lower UACR substantially, leaving a smaller and noisier incremental dapagliflozin effect than this 222-patient study can establish.

trials.t: Phase 2 Study to Evaluate EI-001 in Non-segmental Vitiligo Patients
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI) at Week 24

fable.r: With about 22 patients per arm and highly variable F-VASI change, only a JAK-inhibitor-sized effect from an antibody with no patient efficacy data would reach significance at week 24.

opus.r: An unproven immune-modulating antibody in treatment-refractory vitiligo, with 22-23 per arm, needs about a 20-point F-VASI gain at week 24, larger than most systemic agents achieve.

sonnet.r: Unproven first-in-patient antibody with only healthy-volunteer data, 23 vs 22 patients, and a noisy facial VASI endpoint; only a large effect (about 25+ points) reaches significance.

haiku.r: With about 22 patients per arm, F-VASI noise is large, so a clinically meaningful effect can still miss significance, and a small antibody sponsor adds reporting uncertainty.

carbon.r: With roughly 22-23 patients per arm and slow melanocyte repigmentation over 24 weeks, only a very large systemic antibody effect could achieve statistical significance on F-VASI.

sol.r: With only 45 participants and prior-treatment failure, a moderate 24-week repigmentation effect may not separate significantly from placebo.

trials.t: A Study of Brenipatide in Adults Who Quit Smoking Cigarettes and Want to Avoid Relapse
trials.ep: CO-confirmed continuous abstinence from cigarette smoking with allowed slips, week 1 through week 24

fable.r: A plausible 5-10 point gain in continuous abstinence is below the roughly 13 points that 111 per arm can detect, and GI-related dropouts count as relapse.

opus.r: Incretin-type drugs have not consistently improved smoking abstinence, and with 111 per arm the trial needs about a 13-point gain over a placebo continuous-abstinence rate near one third.

sonnet.r: GIP/GLP-1 agonists have shown inconsistent, modest effects on smoking abstinence, and with about 111 per arm a 10-15 point gain is borderline for significance against a sizeable placebo abstinence rate.

haiku.r: With 111 per arm and placebo abstinence near 20 to 30 percent, an effect of roughly 11 or more points is needed for significance, and I expect something smaller than that.

carbon.r: Incretin agonists have yet to show robust clinical-trial efficacy on smoking abstinence, and gastrointestinal intolerance may raise treatment discontinuations counted against continuous abstinence.

sol.r: A modest reduction in craving may not translate into the roughly 13-point abstinence advantage needed for this small relapse-prevention trial.

trials.t: A Trial to Investigate the Safety and Efficacy of Intra-articular 4P004 Injection in Subjects With Knee Synovitis and Osteoarthritis
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 4 in weekly average of daily WOMAC pain subscore in the target knee

fable.r: Intra-articular saline typically gives about 2 points of pain relief at week 4, so a single liraglutide injection would need a steroid-like effect of about 0.75 points to separate with 65 per arm.

opus.r: Intra-articular saline gives a large placebo response, and a single GLP-1 agonist injection may not add the ~0.7-point WOMAC pain gain at week 4 that 65 per arm require.

sonnet.r: Intra-articular saline in knee OA gives a large placebo response on pain at Week 4, and with 65 per arm a 0.8-point separation on a 0-10 scale is needed.

haiku.r: Saline injection placebo gives a sizeable short-term pain response, so the single 4P004 injection must beat it by about 1.5 WOMAC points at week 4 to reach significance with 65 per arm.

carbon.r: Intra-articular saline injection plus joint aspiration in synovitic knee osteoarthritis produces a large Week 4 analgesic placebo response that is difficult to beat with 65 patients per arm.

sol.r: A substantial saline-injection response may overwhelm a modest rapid analgesic effect, even after enriching for synovitis.

trials.t: Phase III Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of SL1002 for Osteoarthritis Knee Pain
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in weekly mean average daily knee pain intensity while walking (NRS)

fable.r: A large saline-injection placebo response in diagnostic-block responders could shrink the difference below the roughly 0.8 NRS points that 75 patients per arm can detect.

opus.r: Injection procedures in knee OA carry a large saline placebo response, and 75 per arm leave little room if SL1002's 12-week benefit is under one NRS point.

sonnet.r: Saline placebo in knee OA pain trials produces a large response and a block-response-enriched population may inflate it further; the drug needs about 0.8-1 NRS points of separation at Week 12 with 75 per arm.

haiku.r: A single saline-controlled injection with a 12-week walking-pain endpoint has a modest expected effect, and 75 per arm leaves little margin if the drug's benefit is near one NRS point.

carbon.r: Even after diagnostic nerve-block enrichment, sham saline injection in 75 patients per arm typically yields a ~2-point NRS pain drop at Week 12 with high inter-patient variability.

sol.r: Even diagnostic-block responders may show a strong saline or procedural response, eroding the modest week-12 pain difference in only 150 patients.

trials.t: Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study in Adults With Major Depressive Disorder
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Day 29 in MADRS total score

fable.r: SPN-820, the same mechanism, missed MADRS separation in a Phase 2b TRD trial; the new intermittent 2400 mg regimen rests on a small open-label study, and US adjunctive MDD trials carry large placebo responses over 4 weeks.

opus.r: A high placebo response in adjunctive MDD and an unvalidated mTORC1 mechanism make a separation of 2.3 MADRS points or more at day 29 unlikely.

sonnet.r: Adjunctive MDD trials have placebo MADRS improvement of about 9-11 over 4 weeks and a typical SD near 9.5, so a novel agent needs about 2.3 points of separation with 115 per arm; the sponsor's prior adjunctive MDD candidate missed.

haiku.r: Adjunctive MDD trials often show a placebo response near 10 MADRS points that drugs only partly beat, and with 115 per arm a 2.5 point effect is needed for significance.

carbon.r: Large placebo improvements in 4-week US adjunctive MDD trials frequently mask modest drug-placebo separation on MADRS.

sol.r: A modest antidepressant effect may not separate from substantial placebo improvement over four weeks, despite excluding screening-period improvers.

trials.t: A 16-Week Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called Ritlecitinib in Adults With Long Lasting Painful Red Skin Lumps, Known by the Medical Term, Hidradenitis Suppurativa, or HS.
trials.ep: Proportion of adults with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa achieving HiSCR50 at week 16

fable.r: JAK3/TEC inhibition is untested in HS; with 64 per arm and placebo HiSCR50 often 30-40%, a true gain of about 15 points gives only around half power.

opus.r: Ritlecitinib lacks JAK1 inhibition, so its HiSCR50 gain may be under the ~16 points needed with 64 per arm against a placebo response near 30%.

sonnet.r: Ritlecitinib's JAK3/TEC profile and AA-type dosing are unproven in HS; with 64 per arm and placebo HiSCR50 near 30%, roughly a 16-point gain is needed for significance.

haiku.r: With 64 per arm, a 14 point HiSCR50 difference against a placebo rate near 22 percent sits close to the significance threshold, so a modest effect could miss.

carbon.r: Selective JAK3/TEC inhibition lacks direct JAK1/TYK2 blockade of IL-6, IL-23 and Type I IFN signaling that drove prior JAK inhibitor efficacy in hidradenitis suppurativa.

sol.r: Selective JAK3/TEC inhibition may not suppress HS inflammation as reliably as JAK1 inhibition, leaving a moderate treatment difference vulnerable to variable placebo response.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of ZT006 in Overweight and Obese Participants
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 28 (end of main-study treatment)

fable.r: Oral incretin agents reliably beat placebo on weight at 28 weeks; the residual risk is weak oral exposure at the top dose or a terse disclosure that never states the primary result.

opus.r: ZT006 appears to be an oral incretin (GLP-1 class exclusions, calcitonin screen, up-titration); a weak or poorly absorbed molecule giving under ~3-4% placebo-adjusted loss at 28 weeks is the main way it misses with 46 per arm.

sonnet.r: An oral incretin-type tablet at the top dose for 28 weeks should clearly beat placebo even with about 46 per arm; the main risk is a weak molecule or poor tolerability at the high dose.

haiku.r: Main risk is a potency shortfall: a high-dose gap of only about 2 points would sit near the significance threshold with 46 per arm, and the placebo arm is not expected to be unusually strong.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance during up-titration to the high oral dose or ambiguity around co-listed extension safety outcomes could dilute reported success.

sol.r: The design suggests an incretin-like obesity treatment, but undisclosed mechanism, doses and prior efficacy leave uncertainty about whether oral exposure produces the expected weight loss.

trials.t: A Study of JNJ-95597528 in Participants With Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Proportion of participants achieving EASI-75 (at least 75% improvement from baseline in EASI) at week 12.

fable.r: The compound's identity and potency are not public; if type 2 blockade is incomplete or slow, week 12 may be too early for a clear EASI-75 gap in arms of about 50 patients.

opus.r: Novel mechanism (possibly the IL-13/TSLP bispecific from the Proteologix deal, unconfirmed); several new AD mechanisms have given only modest EASI-75 gains at week 12, which with ~50-60 per arm could miss significance.

sonnet.r: Janssen phase 2b dose-ranging in AD with about 63 per arm; a mechanism with real activity should beat a 15-20% placebo EASI-75 at the top dose, but a novel target could underdeliver and placebo response varies.

haiku.r: A flat dose-response would leave even the top dose short, and placebo EASI-75 near 13 percent gives little room if the drug's effect is modest.

carbon.r: Novel mechanisms in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis frequently show modest Week 12 EASI-75 separation insufficient for significance at ~63 patients per arm.

sol.r: The principal uncertainty is whether this molecule and its selected doses reproduce the large EASI benefits of established cytokine inhibitors; a merely moderate effect could be inconclusive.

trials.t: HRS-7450 Injection Phase II Clinical Trial for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with modified Rankin Scale score 0-1 at 90 days

fable.r: With about 52 patients per arm, a 90-day mRS 0-1 difference needs roughly 18 points to reach significance, far above the 8-10 points seen with late-window thrombolysis.

opus.r: About 52 patients per arm cannot detect the 5-10 point gains in mRS 0-1 that even effective late-window reperfusion therapy delivers; a significant highest-dose-vs-placebo difference is unlikely.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 with about 52 per arm and four arms; mRS 0-1 at 90 days in a late-window population needs roughly a 15-20 point gain to reach significance, while plausible effects are about 8-10 points.

haiku.r: Reaching significance on 90-day mRS 0-1 with about 52 patients per arm needs a large gain, and a late-window stroke drug without reperfusion therapy seldom delivers one, so the highest dose is probably too weak.

carbon.r: With roughly 52 acute ischemic stroke patients per arm, only an unusually large ~20 percentage point gain in 90-day mRS 0-1 achieves statistical significance.

sol.r: Imaging-selected late-window reperfusion treatment can improve outcomes, but roughly 52 patients per dose offers limited power for a realistic 8–12-point absolute gain in mRS 0–1.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of OTX-TKI (Axitinib Implant) in Participants With Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy
trials.ep: Proportion of study eyes with at least 2-step DRSS improvement from baseline at Week 52 (outcome recorded as improvement, worsening or no change)

fable.r: TKI sustained release may regress DRSS less than anti-VEGF injections (EYP-1901 missed in PAVIA); also the registered March 2027 completion is unrealistic for 930 patients followed 52 weeks, so no readout is likely by mid-2027.

opus.r: OTX-TKI produced little 2-step DRSS improvement in the HELIOS phase 1, so success rests on the ordinal endpoint capturing fewer worsening eyes than sham; a modest worsening rate in sham could leave too little separation.

sonnet.r: Large phase 3 (about 310 per arm) of a sustained-release VEGFR inhibitor against sham; anti-VEGF in NPDR gives 65-80% 2-step improvement vs about 15% with sham, so failure would mostly come from low implant exposure or trial conduct.

haiku.r: A two-step DRSS improvement at week 52 against sham is a demanding grading endpoint, and enrolment was still open at launch, so no readout is likely before the June 2027 deadline.

carbon.r: Sustained tyrosine kinase release from the hydrogel implant must maintain sufficient pan-VEGF blockade at Week 52 without intraocular inflammation or rescue therapy confounding DRSS grading.

sol.r: The efficacy uncertainty is whether sustained axitinib exposure produces enough favorable DRSS change at 52 weeks; ongoing recruitment also makes unusually early public statements more likely to represent a stop than a scheduled readout.

trials.t: Study of the Efficacy and Safety of ICP-332 in Participants With Prurigo Nodularis
trials.sp: Beijing InnoCare Pharma Tech Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline to Week 16 in weekly average Peak Pruritus NRS (0-10) in prurigo nodularis

fable.r: Small arms and a subjective itch endpoint: a high placebo response or early dropouts in a five-country study could blunt a real JAK-pathway effect.

opus.r: With ~45 per arm and SD near 30 points, a placebo arm that improves itch by 30%+ (as seen in some PN trials) could shrink the difference below significance.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 with about 45 per arm; itch scores in PN carry large placebo responses of 20-30% and SD near 35%, so a TYK2 inhibitor must show a 15+ point gap at the top dose to reach significance.

haiku.r: With about 45 patients per arm and a wide spread in percent change, a moderate itch effect near 15 points could miss significance, and placebo itch responses in prurigo are large.

carbon.r: With roughly 45 patients per arm across five countries, high patient-level variability in pruritus diaries and placebo itch improvement could attenuate statistical significance.

sol.r: Immune-directed treatment can substantially reduce PN itch, but ICP-332's efficacy in nodular disease is unestablished and small dose groups remain vulnerable to a variable placebo response.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of LNK01001 in Adults With Ankylosing Spondylitis
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving ASAS40 response at week 16

fable.r: JAK1 inhibition is proven in AS; the residual risk is an unusually high placebo ASAS40 rate in a Chinese multicentre trial.

opus.r: JAK1 inhibition is well validated in AS; the main failure path is an unusually high placebo ASAS40 rate in a Chinese population with low baseline CRP, narrowing a well-powered comparison.

sonnet.r: JAK1 inhibitors reliably beat placebo on ASAS40 at week 16 in AS (about 50% vs 25%); with 176 per arm failure would need an unusually weak dose or high placebo response.

haiku.r: The primary is ASAS40 at week 16 with 176 per arm, which gives good power for an effect near 15 points, so the main risk is a smaller true effect than hoped at this twice-daily dose.

carbon.r: Subjective pain and global disease activity ratings in NSAID-refractory ankylosing spondylitis could inflate placebo ASAS40 responses if baseline CRP elevation is not required.

sol.r: An unusually high placebo ASAS40 response could shrink an otherwise credible JAK1-class effect; the planned sample is adequate for a conventional 25–30-point advantage.

trials.t: A Study in Healthy Adults to Compare the Bioavailability of EPA + DHA From Two Microalgal Sources to One Fish Source and Placebo
trials.c: Absorption of Omega-3; Omega-3 Supplementation; Healthy Participants
trials.ep: The change in plasma phospholipids EPA+DHA µg/ml levels from baseline to week 6 between MEG-3 3223, O1035DS nTG and O3020DS nTG and placebo

fable.r: Completed single-site Australian supplement bioavailability study run by a CRO; it cannot now be stopped and registry results posting is unlikely.

opus.r: Completed nutritional bioavailability study by an Australian CRO with an ingredient-company partner; not an FDA-regulated product trial, so results posting is unlikely and the record will probably stay as is.

sonnet.r: Completed single-site Australian bioavailability study of omega-3 products in healthy adults; low chance of stopping, an amended primary outcome or posted results, as the sponsor is a CRO/nutrition partner without a regulatory posting duty.

haiku.r: Completed on launch day with the primary already measured, so the open questions are whether results reach ClinicalTrials.gov, which a single-site Australian study with no US site rarely does, and whether the primary wording shifts.

carbon.r: This single-center Australian omega-3 bioavailability study in healthy volunteers is already completed and is unlikely to post structured results on ClinicalTrials.gov or amend its primary endpoint.

sol.r: This short, single-site supplementation study is already completed, making later stoppage unlikely; disclosure is more likely through a nutrition publication than ClinicalTrials.gov results.

trials.t: A Phase III Clinical Study of Rezvilutamide in Patients With Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with total PSA below 0.2 ng/mL (central laboratory) within 6 months after randomization

fable.r: Enzalutamide is an equally potent drug of the same class, so a superiority test on 6-month undetectable PSA would probably fail; success depends on the protocol testing non-inferiority, which the record does not state.

opus.r: Enzalutamide already drives PSA undetectable in about two-thirds of low-volume mHSPC patients; showing superiority of another AR inhibitor with ~103 per arm needs a 15+ point gap, though an unstated non-inferiority design would raise the odds.

sonnet.r: Head-to-head against enzalutamide, which already clears PSA below 0.2 in most low-volume patients; with about 103 per arm a difference under about 13 points will not reach significance.

haiku.r: Superiority over enzalutamide on a six-month undetectable PSA rate with about 100 patients per arm needs a clear head-to-head gap, and enzalutamide is a strong comparator, so a tie is the most likely failure.

carbon.r: Enzalutamide plus ADT already achieves ~68-75% undetectable PSA within 6 months in low-volume mHSPC, leaving virtually no room for superiority and tight margins for non-inferiority at N=206.

sol.r: Enzalutamide plus ADT already produces frequent deep PSA responses, leaving little room for rezvilutamide to demonstrate superiority in only 206 patients.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of SCT650C in Participants With Moderate to Severe Hidradenitis Suppurativa
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving HiSCR75 (≥75% reduction in abscess and inflammatory nodule count, no increase in abscesses or draining fistulas) at Week 16

fable.r: With about 20 patients per arm, a true HiSCR75 gain of roughly 20 points over placebo would reach two-sided p<0.05 only about a third of the time.

opus.r: About 20 patients per arm gives a standard error near 14 points on the HiSCR75 difference, so even a bimekizumab-sized 15-20 point effect would usually miss p<0.05.

sonnet.r: Only about 20 per arm: a HiSCR75 gap of 30+ points is needed for significance at week 16, while a plausible effect for an IL-17-class agent is about 25 points.

haiku.r: About 20 patients per arm cannot separate a moderate effect on HiSCR75 from chance, and the placebo response is small and noisy, so only a very large effect reaches significance.

carbon.r: With roughly 20 participants per arm across three groups, statistical power at Week 16 to detect a realistic 15 to 20 percentage point gain in HiSCR75 is low.

sol.r: With about 20 participants per group, even a clinically meaningful HiSCR75 improvement may not produce a statistically significant comparison.

trials.t: Cantharidin Application in Patients With Common Warts (Verruca Vulgaris) (COVE-2)
trials.c: Common Warts; Common Warts (Verruca Vulgaris); Human Papilloma Virus (HPV)
trials.ep: Complete clearance of all treatable common warts (baseline and new) at the day 84 end-of-treatment visit, by blinded assessor

fable.r: The blinded, vehicle-controlled clearance rate could fall well below the 51% seen in open-label COVE-1, especially in patients with many or large warts, though even 22% vs 10% would be significant.

opus.r: Complete clearance of every treatable wart within four sessions is a stringent bar; cantharidin may clear many but not all warts per patient, narrowing the gap over a vehicle arm that also gets paring and occlusion.

sonnet.r: Cantharidin clears warts well in small series, but complete clearance of all baseline and new warts at Day 84 is a demanding bar, especially in adults with many warts; the vehicle arm should stay low.

haiku.r: Main risk is a weak drug effect: the 28-point gap needed over vehicle is large, and vehicle clearance under occlusion may run high. Blinded-assessor scoring and 151 per arm make the test itself sound; timing looks fine.

carbon.r: Hyperkeratotic common warts are thicker and harder to eradicate completely—including any new warts by Day 84—than molluscum contagiosum lesions, risking lower-than-expected complete clearance.

sol.r: Paring, occlusion and spontaneous regression could raise vehicle clearance enough to narrow the separation seen in the uncontrolled phase 2 study.

trials.t: Study of AHB-137 in Participants With Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) Treated With Nucleos(t)Ide Analogues (NAs)(AUSHINE)
trials.ep: Share of patients with persistent HBsAg below detection limit and HBV DNA below LLOQ, 24 weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment

fable.r: Efficacy over a near-zero placebo cure rate is close to certain, so the residual risk is a safety signal (ALT flares after stopping NA, injection-site or platelet effects) or a conduct problem that prevents a clean result.

opus.r: Durable functional cure requires stopping NA therapy; relapse after cessation could shrink the off-treatment response, but a placebo rate near zero makes significance likely, so the risk is mostly magnitude and timing rather than outright failure.

sonnet.r: The endpoint needs HBsAg loss and DNA suppression held 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, so relapse after NA withdrawal could erode the effect; placebo cure should be near zero.

haiku.r: Main risk is a weak effect: sustained HBsAg loss off all therapy is rare, and an injectable HBV agent may give only a modest response at 24 weeks off treatment. The primary is a strict functional-cure endpoint, and the trial is close to its primary completion date.

carbon.r: Off-treatment viral or HBsAg rebound during the 24-week discontinuation window after stopping nucleos(t)ide analogues could erode end-of-treatment seroclearance.

sol.r: Antigen suppression may not remain durable after both AHB-137 and nucleos(t)ide therapy are stopped, even if on-treatment responses are strong.

trials.t: Study of a Single Dose of a 21-valent Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine in Children and Adolescents With Sickle Cell Disease
trials.ep: Number of participants reporting immediate adverse events (AEs)

fable.r: The record still recruited ten weeks before a primary completion date that includes 6 months of follow-up, so the date will probably slip past April 2027, while stopping and early posting are unlikely.

opus.r: Still recruiting a 100-child sickle cell population in the US and Dominican Republic with a day-181 safety primary outcome; enrollment pace will likely push primary completion into mid-to-late 2027, with no results posting by the read date.

sonnet.r: Sanofi vaccine safety and immunogenicity study in 100 children with sickle cell disease; it was still recruiting in Oct 2026 and the primary set includes safety through day 181, so the registered Jan 2027 completion probably slips. Results likely come after the Aug 2027 read.

haiku.r: Recruiting at launch with 100 children still to enrol against a January 2027 primary completion, so the registry date is likely to slip. Sanofi usually posts vaccine results within a year of completion, but the window to August 2027 is short.

carbon.r: Because the trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 and includes a 181-day post-vaccination primary safety window, primary completion is likely to slip more than 90 days past January 2027.

sol.r: Six-month safety follow-up makes January completion unlikely if recruitment truly remains open in late October; a date extension is more likely than discontinuation.

trials.t: Study Testing the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of EDI048 in Cryptosporidium Infection Model in Healthy Adults
trials.ep: Average stool grade on Days 3 to 5 after starting treatment, following Cryptosporidium parvum challenge

fable.r: Challenge cryptosporidiosis in healthy adults resolves on its own within days, so stool grade on days 3-5 may be near normal on placebo and leave little room to show benefit.

opus.r: Challenge-model cryptosporidial diarrhea is self-limited and wanes by days 3-5 on its own, so a parasiticidal drug started after onset may not lower average stool grade enough to separate with about 40 per arm.

sonnet.r: Illness in the challenge model resolves on its own within days, so the Day 3-5 stool grade window may leave little room to show a drug effect with only 40 per arm.

haiku.r: Main risk is an underpowered design: 40 per arm on a mild, noisy stool-grade score, and the scale is undefined in the record. Recruiting at launch with a March 2027 primary completion, so the registry date may slip; Novartis is unlikely to publish before mid-2027.

carbon.r: Cryptosporidium diarrhea in healthy immunocompetent adult volunteers is often mild and rapidly self-limiting, narrowing the window to show significant stool grade reduction on Days 3 to 5.

sol.r: Rapid spontaneous recovery in healthy adults could compress the Days 3–5 stool-grade difference despite genuine antiparasitic activity.

trials.t: A Study of Telitacicept in Patients With Ocular Myasthenia Gravis (OMG)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Myasthenia Gravis Impairment Index patient-reported (MGII PRO) ocular score at Week 24

fable.r: The patient-reported ocular subscore may respond less and more noisily than generalised MG scales, and seronegative ocular patients may dilute the effect.

opus.r: Ocular MG symptoms are mild and fluctuating, with placebo improvement on stable standard care; a narrow ocular PRO scale and AChR-negative patients may dilute telitacicept's effect with only 60 per arm.

sonnet.r: Patient-reported ocular scores in mild ocular-only myasthenia on stable background therapy carry a large placebo response, and 60 per arm leaves little margin if the effect is only modest.

haiku.r: Main risk is a small single-centre trial (60 per arm) on an ocular PRO subscale with few items, so a real effect may not reach significance. Recruiting at launch with a 2026 primary completion date, so the registry will likely slip; a readout around mid-2027 is plausible.

carbon.r: Ocular myasthenia gravis symptoms fluctuate and respond noticeably to background standard-of-care therapy and placebo, while inclusion of AChR-seronegative patients may dilute the overall effect.

sol.r: Benefit in generalized autoimmune MG may not fully translate to isolated ocular disease, especially in antibody-negative patients.

trials.t: A Trial of SHR0302 Tablets and SHR0302 Base Gel in Patients With Non-segmental Vitiligo
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in facial vitiligo area scoring index (F-VASI) at week 24

fable.r: With roughly 44-59 patients per arm and an SD near 38 points, a smaller-than-expected F-VASI difference at 24 weeks could miss significance.

opus.r: Repigmentation at week 24 is still early; if SHR0302 doses are low or the single-centre population has long-standing stable lesions, the F-VASI response could be modest, though prior JAK data point to a clear win.

sonnet.r: Vitiligo repigments slowly, so a 24-week facial percent change vs placebo may be modest relative to between-patient variation with only about 59 per arm.

haiku.r: Main risk is high spread in percent change on the facial score, with only 59 per arm. A large gap is still likely for an oral JAK inhibitor plus topical base. Recruiting at launch with a March 2027 primary completion, so the registry will probably move later.

carbon.r: Melanocyte repigmentation in vitiligo progresses slowly, so 24 weeks without phototherapy can yield high inter-patient variability in F-VASI percent change.

sol.r: JAK inhibition may suppress inflammation before enough repigmentation occurs, leaving a smaller-than-expected facial response at week 24.

trials.t: Efficacy of SALI-10 Oral Probiotics in Experimental Gingivitis
trials.ep: Change in percentage of sites with bleeding on probing from baseline to end of the 3-week no-brushing induction phase (Week 5)

fable.r: A probiotic lozenge is unlikely to offset three weeks of unchecked plaque by the roughly 7 points of bleeding sites that 30 per arm can detect.

opus.r: A probiotic lozenge is unlikely to counteract three weeks of unchecked plaque; the expected bleeding-on-probing difference is small relative to between-person variability with 30 per arm.

sonnet.r: A probiotic lozenge is likely to have a modest effect on bleeding on probing against the large inflammatory rise in the no-brushing model, and 30 per arm gives limited power.

haiku.r: Main risk is a small study (30 per arm) on a noisy bleeding-on-probing measure, where a modest probiotic effect may not reach significance. The trial is closed to recruitment, so the readout is near and the registry should be close to correct.

carbon.r: During 21 days of complete oral hygiene abstinence, heavy supragingival plaque accumulation frequently overwhelms the modest antimicrobial effect of an oral probiotic lozenge on clinical bleeding on probing.

sol.r: A strain-specific probiotic effect may be too modest to counter three weeks of plaque accumulation without brushing.

trials.t: A Phase II Study of PEG-rhGH Injection for Short Children Born Small for Gestational Age: Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics
trials.c: Short Stature Children Born Small for Gestational Age (SGA)
trials.ep: Annualized height velocity at Week 26 of treatment in short children born small for gestational age

fable.r: Daily growth hormone is an effective active control, so the higher PEG-rhGH dose is expected to match rather than significantly beat it with 24 children per arm.

opus.r: Daily hGH already produces strong catch-up growth in SGA children, so the higher PEG-rhGH dose is unlikely to show statistically superior height velocity with about 24 per arm.

sonnet.r: A weekly long-acting growth hormone against daily growth hormone is designed to match it rather than beat it, so a significant superiority result on height velocity is unlikely in 24 per arm.

haiku.r: Main risk is size: 24 per arm to show a superiority gap over active hGH on height velocity. Recruiting at launch with a December 2026 primary completion, so the registry will likely slip, and a readout near mid-2027 is uncertain.

carbon.r: Active daily recombinant human growth hormone produces strong ~10 cm/year catch-up growth in prepubertal SGA children, making formal statistical superiority or hypothesis testing difficult with 24 patients per arm.

sol.r: Daily hGH already produces substantial catch-up growth, making superiority difficult for a small weekly-treatment comparison.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2a Study With an Open-Label Extension Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of VENT-03 in Adult Participants With Active Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus With or Without Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
trials.c: Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus (CLE); Systemic Lupus Erythematosus; SLE
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in skin interferon gene signature at day 28

fable.r: About 12 patients per arm and a variable biopsy gene score mean only a very large drop in interferon signature after 4 weeks would be significant.

opus.r: cGAS inhibition may not suppress the skin interferon signature enough in four weeks if interferon in CLE is driven mainly by plasmacytoid dendritic cell TLR7/9 signalling; 12 per arm leaves little power.

sonnet.r: With 12 per arm and a variable skin biopsy gene-signature readout at day 28, even a real pharmacodynamic effect may miss significance; enrolment across 34 sites for 24 patients is slow.

haiku.r: Main risk is size: 12 per arm on a pharmacodynamic score with wide patient-to-patient spread, so a real drug effect may miss significance. Recruiting at launch with a December 2026 primary completion, so the registry date may move later.

carbon.r: Endosomal TLR7/9 signaling independently drives Type I interferon in cutaneous lupus skin lesions, so inhibiting cytosolic cGAS alone for 28 days in 24 patients may not sufficiently suppress the skin IFN signature.

sol.r: CLE skin interferon activity can arise through pathways other than cGAS, potentially limiting suppression despite adequate drug exposure.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of 608 in Adult Subjects With Active Ankylosing Spondylitis(AS)
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving an ASAS40 response at week 16

fable.r: An IL-17A antibody in a 500-patient AS trial should clear ASAS40 easily; the residual risk is an unusually high placebo response or conduct problems at Chinese sites rather than lack of drug effect.

opus.r: IL-17A blockade reliably beats placebo on ASAS40 in AS; the only realistic failure route is an unusually high placebo response in a large Chinese multicentre trial shrinking the gap.

sonnet.r: An IL-17A antibody in AS with 250 per arm is very likely to beat placebo on ASAS40; the main risk is a higher than expected placebo response.

haiku.r: Class-validated mechanism in active AS with 250 per arm; the main risk is an unstated or low dose of 608, which would shrink the placebo-adjusted ASAS40 gain.

carbon.r: High placebo ASAS40 response rates occasionally occur in radiographic axial spondyloarthritis trials if baseline inflammatory activity is not strictly enriched.

sol.r: Failure would most likely reflect unexpectedly weak activity of 608 rather than inadequate statistical power in this large placebo-controlled study.

trials.t: A Study of Solbinsiran (LY3561774) in Participants With Severe Hypertriglyceridemia
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in triglycerides, time-averaged over weeks 16 to 24

fable.r: Triglyceride changes vary enormously between severe-hypertriglyceridemia patients, so with about 60 patients a real 40-50% lowering could still miss significance, especially if chylomicron-dominant patients respond poorly to ANGPTL3 silencing.

opus.r: ANGPTL3 silencing works through LPL, so patients with impaired LPL function in a severe-HTG population respond less; with only about 30 per arm, a diluted effect plus noisy TG could still miss.

sonnet.r: ANGPTL3 siRNA should cut triglycerides strongly, but 30 per arm with very variable TG values leaves some sampling risk; the larger issue is the timing of any public report.

haiku.r: Solbinsiran's ANGPTL3 knockdown should cut triglycerides sharply, but the dose is not stated and 30 per arm limits precision; the main risk is a dose too low for a clear effect.

carbon.r: Triglyceride levels above 500 mg/dL exhibit substantial intra-individual variability and regression to the mean in small cohorts of 60 patients.

sol.r: Marked triglyceride variability and heterogeneous residual lipoprotein-lipase function could weaken ANGPTL3 inhibition in severe hypertriglyceridemia despite excluding familial chylomicronemia.

trials.t: A Phase II Clinical Trial of HRS-1893 in the Treatment of Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
trials.c: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
trials.ep: Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs).

fable.r: Small Chinese phase 2 safety study in a narrow HFpEF group; it was still recruiting five months before its registered primary completion despite 24 weeks of treatment, so a delay is likely, with no ClinicalTrials.gov results posting expected.

opus.r: Small single-country HFpEF phase 2 still recruiting with a 24-week endpoint and March 2027 primary completion, so a date slip past mid-2027 is about as likely as not; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.

sonnet.r: Single-site Chinese phase 2 safety study of 48 patients with 24-week treatment; plausible modest slippage of the primary completion date, low odds of stopping, and Chinese sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

haiku.r: Single-site Chinese phase 2 of 48 patients, still recruiting at launch against a March 2027 completion date; a slip past June 2027 is likely, and with no US sites results posting is unlikely.

carbon.r: Because recruitment in HFpEF with LVEF >=60% was ongoing in late October 2026 and follow-up spans 24 weeks, primary completion is moderately likely to slip past June 2027.

sol.r: The small enrollment is feasible, but restrictive HFpEF eligibility and 24 weeks of follow-up create a meaningful risk of completion slipping beyond the registered schedule.

trials.t: Taldefgrobep Alfa in Adults With Overweight and Obesity
trials.ep: Percent change in total body weight from baseline to week 24

fable.r: Myostatin-pathway blockade without an incretin mainly swaps fat for lean mass, so total body weight, the registered primary, may move only 1-2% against placebo and miss significance even if body composition improves.

opus.r: Myostatin-pathway blockade shifts body composition (less fat, more lean) more than it lowers total body weight, so the net weight change versus placebo at 24 weeks may be too small to reach significance.

sonnet.r: Myostatin-pathway inhibition alone is expected to give modest weight loss; the trial needs about a 2-point gap versus placebo at 24 weeks, which is plausible but not certain.

haiku.r: Myostatin blockade alone should give only modest weight loss over 24 weeks; a placebo-adjusted gap of a few points is the main risk, and 75 per arm leaves little margin for a small effect.

carbon.r: Selective myostatin inhibition increases lean mass while only modestly reducing fat mass, yielding minimal net change in total scale body weight as monotherapy over 24 weeks.

sol.r: An increase in lean mass could offset fat loss, leaving insufficient total body-weight reduction to meet the week-24 primary endpoint.

trials.t: A Study of Weekly Oral Ecnoglutide (VRB-101) in Participants Who Have Obesity or Overweight With Weight-Related Comorbidities
trials.ep: Mean percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 21

fable.r: Failure would most likely come from low or erratic oral absorption of a weekly peptide tablet leaving exposure too low to separate from placebo with about 34 patients per arm.

opus.r: Weekly oral peptide delivery is unproven; low or variable oral bioavailability plus a short 20-week titration could leave the top Schedule A dose with a modest weight gap in an arm of only about 34 patients.

sonnet.r: Oral GLP-1 peptide at the top regimen over 20 weeks should separate clearly from placebo; the main risk is poor oral exposure at the highest Schedule A regimen.

haiku.r: Phase 2b with about 34 per arm and a large expected incretin effect; the main risk is that the highest Schedule A dose falls short of injectable benchmarks or oral absorption varies.

carbon.r: Weekly oral peptide GLP-1 regimens require high single-dose exposure that can cause gastrointestinal intolerance, vomiting, and early discontinuations.

sol.r: Variable oral absorption or inadequate exposure across the weekly dosing interval could make the selected regimens less effective than injectable GLP-1 therapy.

trials.t: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effect and Side Effect of a New Artificial Tear Formulation (ABBV-444) Compared to Refresh Optive Unit Dose in Adult Participants With Dry Eye Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI, 0-100) score at Day 90

fable.r: Refresh Optive is itself an effective tear, so ABBV-444 can at best match it; the objective is met only if the trial's own hypothesis is non-inferiority, as in earlier Allergan tear studies, and is reported as such.

opus.r: Two artificial tears usually improve OSDI by similar amounts; if the protocol tests superiority over Refresh Optive rather than non-inferiority, the comparator is likely too strong for ABBV-444 to beat.

sonnet.r: Two artificial tears usually differ by only a few OSDI points, and the comparator also improves symptoms; superiority needs about 4-5 points at 130 per arm.

haiku.r: Two artificial tears usually differ by only a few OSDI points, and with about 130 per arm the superiority test has limited power unless the new formulation is clearly better.

carbon.r: Refresh Optive UD produces substantial 12-to-16-point OSDI symptom improvements over 90 days, making superiority very hard if the protocol is not testing non-inferiority.

sol.r: Both artificial tears should improve symptoms substantially, making superiority difficult and leaving success dependent on the actual non-inferiority hypothesis and margin.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study of TS-172 in Hyperphosphatemia Patients on Hemodialysis With Phosphate Binders
trials.ep: Share of hemodialysis patients on phosphate binders reaching the target serum phosphorus level at Week 8

fable.r: The drug should lower phosphorus clearly; the main threat to a responder endpoint in 100 patients is diarrhoea-driven dose limitation or discontinuation counting as non-response, or a high placebo target rate on continued binders.

opus.r: Add-on to existing binders over only 8 weeks; if TS-172's extra phosphorus lowering is smaller than tenapanor's, or diarrhoea forces dose limits, the gap in target achievement with 50 per arm could fall short.

sonnet.r: A phosphate absorption inhibitor added to stable binders should raise the share reaching the target range clearly above placebo; 50 per arm is small but the expected gap is large.

haiku.r: Add-on to existing binders in 100 Japanese patients; the risk is a smaller share reaching target than assumed, and the record does not define the target level.

carbon.r: Intestinal phosphate transport inhibitors commonly induce diarrhea and gastrointestinal discontinuations when added to background phosphate binders.

sol.r: With about 50 patients per arm, target attainment may be too noisy to distinguish a moderate add-on effect from responses occurring with continued binders.

trials.t: A Study Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of HRS9531 Injection With Semaglutide Injection in Subjects With Obesity
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in body weight after 52 weeks of treatment

fable.r: Semaglutide is a strong comparator, but HRS9531's phase 3 weight loss was about 5 points greater than semaglutide achieves in Chinese patients, so failure would need the semaglutide arm to overperform or the tested dose to be low.

opus.r: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a strong comparator; if the HRS9531 dose used is not the top dose or open-label discontinuations dilute the gap, superiority at 52 weeks could be narrower than expected.

sonnet.r: A GLP-1/GIP dual agonist should beat semaglutide on 52-week weight loss, but the semaglutide dose is unknown and a head-to-head gap may be only a few points.

haiku.r: Head-to-head superiority against semaglutide with about 286 per arm; the main risk is that the dual agonist's margin over semaglutide at week 52 is smaller than assumed.

carbon.r: Open-label semaglutide 2.4 mg achieves ~12-14% weight loss in Chinese non-diabetic adults, narrowing headroom if HRS9531 dose escalation is limited by tolerability.

sol.r: Failure would most likely occur if semaglutide performs near its best while the chosen HRS9531 dose delivers less incremental weight loss than expected.

trials.t: Phase 2 Study of SAT-3247 in Pediatric Ambulatory Patients
trials.ep: Change from baseline in muscle force measured by dynamometry at week 12 (placebo-controlled Part 1)

fable.r: Twelve weeks and about 17 boys per arm give little power to show a strength gain on dynamometry, a noisy measure in 7-9 year olds, for an unproven regenerative mechanism.

opus.r: About 17 boys per arm over 12 weeks, with noisy dynamometry and growth-related strength gains on placebo, gives little power to show a significant strength difference even if the drug acts.

sonnet.r: Exploratory phase 2a with about 17 boys per arm, a noisy dynamometry endpoint over 12 weeks, and a first-in-class mechanism makes a significant strength gain unlikely.

haiku.r: Only 17 patients per arm for the efficacy primary, measured by dynamometry over 12 weeks in a slowly changing disease, so a detectable placebo-adjusted gain is unlikely.

carbon.r: Twelve weeks of weekday dosing in ~17 boys per arm is likely too brief and small for muscle regeneration to yield statistically significant dynamometry gains.

sol.r: Small dose groups and noisy dynamometry over only 12 weeks may prevent a genuine but modest regenerative effect from reaching statistical significance.

trials.t: Phase II Clinical Study of HRS-9563 in Patients With Mild to Moderate Hypertension
trials.ep: Change from baseline in 24-hour mean systolic blood pressure by ambulatory monitoring at month 6

fable.r: If the siRNA silences angiotensinogen less deeply or durably than zilebesiran, the month-6 ambulatory effect could shrink to a few mmHg, and with patients split over several dose arms that might miss significance.

opus.r: If the long-acting injection loses much of its effect by month 6 or the highest dose is modest, the 24-h ambulatory SBP gap versus placebo in a split multi-dose design could shrink toward non-significance.

sonnet.r: If HRS-9563 is an RAAS-pathway siRNA like zilebesiran, a 10-15 mmHg ambulatory SBP drop versus placebo is expected, and 119 per arm is ample; main risk is a weak lowest or only tested dose.

haiku.r: Phase 2 with an unstated dose and about 119 per arm; the risk is a placebo-adjusted six-month 24-hour systolic effect smaller than the assumed 6 mmHg.

carbon.r: If subcutaneous RNAi knock-down wanes before Month 6 or rescue antihypertensive therapy confounds estimands, Month 6 ABPM SBP separation could attenuate.

sol.r: The principal efficacy risk is that the selected injection doses do not sustain enough blood-pressure reduction through month six.

trials.t: A Trial Evaluating Brelovitug vs Delayed Treatment for the Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis Delta Infection (AZURE-4)
trials.ep: Composite of virologic response (HDV RNA ≥2 log10 IU/mL decline or undetectable) and ALT normalization: week 24 on brelovitug versus week 12 delayed treatment

fable.r: Untreated response is near zero and phase 2 combined response on brelovitug was above 50%, so a miss would need ALT normalization to lag badly at week 24 or a report that does not state the primary endpoint.

opus.r: ALT normalization can lag viral suppression, so the week-24 composite could be lower than hoped, but with an untreated control near 0% even a modest response rate should be significant.

sonnet.r: Untreated chronic HDV rarely achieves a 2-log RNA drop plus ALT normalization in 12 weeks, so the comparison against brelovitug 300 mg weekly is very likely to be met; the trial mainly supports a larger pivotal programme.

haiku.r: The main risk is the endpoint: a strict composite of HDV RNA and ALT response at week 24 on brelovitug against an untreated week-12 control, with only 40 and 20 patients. The expected gap is large, so the risk is mostly timing and reporting.

carbon.r: Lower-than-expected ALT normalization at Week 24 in patients with compensated cirrhosis or high baseline viral load is the main risk, though spontaneous composite response in untreated controls is near zero.

sol.r: ALT normalization may lag virologic suppression, reducing the week-24 composite response despite strong antiviral activity.

trials.t: Study of ENV-294 in Adults With Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in EASI score at week 12

fable.r: The mechanism is new and unproven in a placebo-controlled trial; if the true gain over a placebo change near -35% is under about 15 points, 52 per arm will not show it.

opus.r: A novel oral first-in-class agent with no published efficacy data must beat a placebo arm that typically improves EASI by about a third, with only about 52 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Novel oral mechanism with unproven AD efficacy; about 52 per arm needs a roughly 15-point EASI percent difference to reach significance against a placebo arm that typically improves 25-40%.

haiku.r: An oral drug with no known efficacy signal in atopic dermatitis is likely to show a modest EASI effect over placebo. With about 53 per arm, a significant result needs a gap of roughly 15 points, which is a large effect for an oral agent.

carbon.r: Novel oral non-JAK anti-inflammatory small molecules have frequently shown modest efficacy against substantial moisturizer-driven placebo improvements in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

sol.r: The novel oral treatment may deliver insufficient incremental EASI improvement against a variable and potentially substantial placebo response.

trials.t: Study of VYD2311 for the Prevention of COVID-19
trials.ep: RT-PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 through day 90 after the first injection

fable.r: With about 590 per arm and a 90-day placebo attack rate near 2-3%, only about 14 placebo cases are expected, so a quiet COVID period or efficacy near 60% would leave the comparison short of significance.

opus.r: With about 590 per arm and a 90-day window, a low 2026 symptomatic COVID-19 attack rate (around 1-2%) could leave too few events for significance even with a strong antibody effect; variant escape is a second risk.

sonnet.r: Event-driven prevention trial: a potent mAb should show large relative efficacy, but low placebo attack rate over 90 days or variant escape could leave too few events for significance.
