haiku.r: The antibody is expected to work strongly, so the main risk is a low number of COVID cases in the placebo arm, which would leave the hazard ratio too imprecise to reach significance.

carbon.r: SARS-CoV-2 variant drift reducing neutralization potency or lower-than-expected 90-day symptomatic attack rates between seasonal waves could underpower the trial.

sol.r: Short follow-up in a highly immune population may yield too few symptomatic cases, while variant escape could further dilute protection.

trials.t: ENV-294 for Moderate-to-Severe Asthma: A 12-Week Study in Adults
trials.ep: Incidence and Severity of Adverse Events

fable.r: A 50-patient US asthma study with strict lung-function and reversibility criteria at 20 sites; likely to complete, with a fair chance of finishing a few months late.

opus.r: Small 50-patient safety-primary asthma study at 20 US sites, still recruiting two months before its registered primary completion; enrolment of exacerbation-prone ICS/LABA patients usually slips by a quarter or more.

sonnet.r: Small safety-primary phase 2 in moderate-to-severe asthma with strict spirometry and ACQ criteria and 20 US sites; the registered December 2026 completion looks optimistic while still recruiting in late October 2026, so a slip beyond March 2027 is about a coin flip. Private sponsor, so results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: The trial is still recruiting with a December 2026 primary completion, so a date slip past March 2027 is likely. Termination is possible for a small phase 2, and results posting before August 2027 is unlikely.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Use of Topical Ocular BL1332 for the Management of Postoperative Ocular Pain Following Photorefractive Keratectomy
trials.ep: Ocular pain intensity on a 0-10 numeric rating scale during the 24 hours after photorefractive keratectomy (PRK)

fable.r: A TRPV1 antagonist is likely to lower post-PRK pain by under 1 point on a 10-point scale, which a parallel trial of about 43 per arm detects only about half the time.

opus.r: PRK pain is a sensitive model, but with about 43 eyes per arm and a pain SD near 2.4 points the drug needs roughly a 1-point mean reduction over vehicle in the first 24 hours to reach significance.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 topical analgesic with two doses against vehicle in a PRK pain model; n of about 43 per arm gives only modest power for a 0.5 to 1 point NRS difference, and the vehicle arm gets bandage lens and rescue medication.

haiku.r: A 0.7-point gain over vehicle on a 0-10 scale with SD near 2.3 sits near the significance line at 43 per arm; dose strength is not stated.

carbon.r: Novel topical ocular analgesics often produce modest incremental pain relief below the ~0.9-point threshold needed for significance in a 43-patient-per-arm PRK trial.

sol.r: An uncertain analgesic effect may be diluted by rescue medication and perioperative care, leaving insufficient separation from vehicle.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of YD0743 Treatment for Sepsis-Associated ARDS
trials.sp: Shanghai Yidian Pharmaceutical Technology Development Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Ventilator-free days within 28 days after start of treatment

fable.r: Drugs for ARDS have rarely improved ventilator-free days, and this trial needs a gain of about 2.4 days to reach significance.

opus.r: Pharmacological treatments for sepsis-associated ARDS have almost uniformly failed to improve ventilator-free days; with a VFD SD near 10 days, about 155 per arm needs a gain of 3+ days, which few agents have ever shown.

sonnet.r: ARDS drug trials on ventilator-free days have a very poor record, VFD has a large SD driven by deaths, and the drug is a new injectable of unknown mechanism; a one-site record with 309 patients will also likely slip.

haiku.r: Ventilator-free days need a gain of about 2 days to be significant at 155 per arm with SD near 9; Phase 2 ICU drugs often miss on this endpoint.

carbon.r: Sepsis-associated ARDS is biologically heterogeneous with high mortality noise, and pharmacologic candidates rarely achieve a >2.2-day gain in 28-day ventilator-free days.

sol.r: Sepsis-associated ARDS is heterogeneous, and a modest biological effect may not translate into enough additional ventilator-free days to overcome high outcome variability.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Effectiveness and Safety of IPN10200 in Adults With Moderate to Severe Wrinkle-like Lines Between the Eyebrows
trials.ep: North America: responders with ≥2-grade improvement and None/Mild score on both investigator (ILA) and subject (SSA) assessments at maximum frown, week 4

fable.r: Failure is unlikely for a botulinum toxin versus placebo; the residual risk is the strict composite needing a 2-grade gain on both investigator and subject scales, or a release that does not state the primary result plainly.

opus.r: Botulinum toxins essentially never fail placebo-controlled glabellar-line trials; the only plausible failure is an unexpectedly weak dose or formulation of the new recombinant neurotoxin.

sonnet.r: Glabellar line toxin trials against placebo almost always succeed; the only realistic failure is an unexpectedly weak product or an unusual dose, and the composite ILA plus SSA endpoint is stricter but still easily met.

haiku.r: The strict dual-rater composite (investigator and subject) is the main failure route rather than the drug; the expected gap is large, so a miss would be surprising.

carbon.r: With botulinum neurotoxins showing massive Week 4 treatment effects over near-zero placebo composite response rates, the main risk is an early top-line press release omitting explicit confirmation of all co-primary endpoints.

sol.r: The small residual efficacy risk is an unexpectedly low response at the selected dose, particularly on the stringent combined investigator and subject assessment.

trials.t: Study of Olatorepatide in Adult Participants Living With Overweight or Obesity in the US
trials.ep: Occurrence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and the 30-week follow-up ends within weeks of the registered date, so the trial should complete on time; results posting within nine months is unlikely for an unapproved drug.

opus.r: A small three-site US PK/safety phase 2 of Regeneron's in-licensed GLP-1/GIP agonist that is already active, not recruiting, so it should complete close to its November 2026 date; results posting is due only by late 2027.

sonnet.r: Active, not recruiting phase 2 with a registered primary completion in November 2026; Regeneron tends to post results close to the 12-month deadline, so posting before September 2027 is unlikely.

haiku.r: Active, not recruiting with a November 2026 primary completion; the risk is a registry date revised past February 2027, and the results posting clock runs to late 2027.

carbon.r: Because enrollment is already complete with primary completion scheduled two weeks after the October 2026 snapshot, the trial should finish on time with results posted closer to the one-year statutory deadline.

sol.r: With recruitment complete and only short remaining follow-up, this small pharmacokinetic and safety study should finish close to schedule; registry results are less likely before the one-year reporting anniversary.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate the Potential Effects of KH-001 on Intravaginal Ejaculatory Latency Time (IELT), Patient-Reported Outcomes, and Safety in Men With Lifelong Premature Ejaculation (LPE)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in geometric mean intravaginal ejaculatory latency time (IELT) during each 4-week crossover treatment period

fable.r: An on-demand sublingual SERT inhibitor taken 15 minutes before intercourse may not reach effective levels fast enough, so the IELT gain over placebo could be small in a 40-man crossover.

opus.r: On-demand SERT inhibition (dapoxetine) lengthens IELT only modestly over a sizable placebo response; a 4-week crossover in 40 men can detect a dapoxetine-sized effect but not much less.

sonnet.r: On-demand SERT inhibitors reliably prolong IELT in lifelong premature ejaculation and a within-patient crossover with 40 men is well powered; the risk is a novel agent with weak sublingual exposure or a large placebo response.

haiku.r: Small crossover with a stopwatch endpoint on a baseline near one minute; a real effect of about half a minute or more is needed, and this on-demand dosing is not one I can benchmark.

carbon.r: Dosing only 15 minutes before intercourse leaves minimal time for sublingual SERT inhibitor absorption, CNS penetration, and serotonergic delay of ejaculation.

sol.r: The SSRI mechanism is credible, but dosing only 15 minutes before intercourse may not provide sufficient exposure, and 40 crossover participants leave limited protection against noisy measurements.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Effectiveness and Safety of IPN10200 Over Time in Adults With Moderate to Severe Wrinkle-like Lines Between the Eyebrows
trials.ep: Double-blind phase, North America: responders with ≥2-grade improvement and None/Mild score on both ILA and SSA at maximum frown, week 4

fable.r: Failure is unlikely for a botulinum toxin versus placebo; the residual risk is two region-specific primaries that must both be reported as met, or a release that does not state the primary result plainly.

opus.r: Large placebo-controlled glabellar-line toxin trials are near-certain wins; failure would require an unexpectedly weak dose of the new recombinant neurotoxin.

sonnet.r: Large placebo-controlled toxin pivotal; the North America and EU/ROW primaries each need to be met and the Japan and European subsets are smaller, but a high-potency toxin should clear both comfortably.

haiku.r: The risk is the North America subset of a four-country trial being small, not the drug effect; the composite endpoint is the same as in LAURITE 1.

carbon.r: Efficacy failure at Week 4 is extremely unlikely for a botulinum neurotoxin in glabellar lines, leaving incomplete endpoint specificity in a top-line press release as the primary scoring risk.

sol.r: Failure would most plausibly require unexpectedly weak activity at the chosen dose; ordinary sampling variation is unlikely to erase a large week-4 toxin-versus-placebo difference.

trials.t: Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of ICP-488 in Subjects With Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus (CLE) Double-blind Study
trials.sp: Beijing InnoCare Pharma Tech Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in CLASI-A (cutaneous lupus activity score) at week 16

fable.r: With about 35 patients per arm and a placebo response in CLASI-A that has ranged from roughly -15% to -50% across cutaneous lupus trials, a real TYK2 effect could still miss significance.

opus.r: About 35 patients per arm with a CLASI-A percent-change SD near 40% and a placebo response of 15-30% on stable background therapy leaves power near 60-70% even for a real TYK2 effect.

sonnet.r: TYK2 inhibition acts on the type I interferon axis that drives CLE, but percent change in CLASI-A has a wide SD and a large placebo response, and 35 per arm leaves little margin.

haiku.r: A 35-per-arm trial on a percent-change endpoint with large spread; a real effect near 20 points is needed, and the March 2027 completion pushes any report close to the June deadline.

carbon.r: High placebo CLASI-A improvement on stable background lupus therapy with 35 patients per arm could narrow separation despite active TYK2 inhibition.

sol.r: Fluctuating skin disease and stable background treatment can generate substantial placebo improvement, leaving an uncertain incremental effect in only about 35 patients per dose.

trials.t: Study of Lotilaner Ophthalmic Gel in Patients With Ocular Rosacea (KORE)
trials.ep: Incidence of Treatment Emergent Adverse Events

fable.r: A 155-patient safety study with a week-16 primary and a year-end 2026 date; the main uncertainty is whether enrolment closed early enough to keep primary completion within 90 days of that date.

opus.r: A two-site safety-primary phase 2 enrolling by invitation; 155 patients with 16-week follow-up make a primary completion slip past March 2027 plausible but not likely, and results posting is due only by end-2027.

sonnet.r: Enrolling by invitation with a registered primary completion of December 2026 and a week-16 primary, so last-patient timing could push the date past March 2027; Tarsus is a US-listed company that tends to post results near the deadline.

haiku.r: Safety-only Phase 2 at two US sites, enrolling by invitation with a December 2026 completion; a registry slip past March 2027 is possible but not likely, and results posting is uncertain.

carbon.r: Still enrolling by invitation across only two US sites in late October 2026 for a 16-week primary endpoint makes slipping past March 2027 moderately likely, with results posting unlikely before December 2027 study completion.

sol.r: This invitation-enrolled safety study should usually continue, but its two-site footprint and extended follow-up create moderate scheduling risk; early registry posting is unlikely.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of HRS-9190 Compared to Cisatracurium for Continuous Intravenous Infusion in Adults
trials.ep: Minutes from stopping the continuous infusion to recovery of train-of-four ratio (TOFr) to ≥0.9

fable.r: The record states no formal superiority hypothesis, so a report may describe recovery times without declaring the primary objective met, or HRS-9190 may not recover clearly faster than cisatracurium.

opus.r: If HRS-9190 is not a genuinely faster-offset agent than cisatracurium, or the small four-arm phase 2 is reported descriptively without a formal test, recovery time will not show significant superiority.

sonnet.r: The stated hypothesis is only effective relaxation with acceptable safety, so a formal superiority test may not be reported; a differentiating shorter recovery than cisatracurium would give a clear significant result, but publication is uncertain.

haiku.r: Four arms in 67 patients; an 8-minute recovery gain over cisatracurium needs clean separation at about 34 per arm, so small size is the main risk.

carbon.r: Although rapid-recovery neuromuscular blockers easily beat cisatracurium on spontaneous TOFr >=0.9 recovery time, this small four-subgroup Phase 2 could report descriptive arm-level recovery times without formal pooled superiority testing.

sol.r: HRS-9190 must offer materially faster spontaneous recovery than cisatracurium; a modest difference could be obscured by anesthesia type and variable infusion exposure.

trials.t: Effect of FB301 on Vaginal Bacterial Profile in Women With Asymptomatic Vaginal Dysbiosis Undergoing a Mock Frozen Embryo Transfer Cycle
trials.ep: Proportion of participants with Lactobacillus-dominant vaginal microbiome (≥90% combined relative abundance of five specified species, metagenomic sequencing) at day 16 of mock FET cycle

fable.r: Ten women per arm means only a very large difference, about 60% against 10%, reaches significance on a strict 90% Lactobacillus threshold.

opus.r: With about 10 women per arm, even a 50-point difference in Lactobacillus dominance (6/10 vs 1/10) misses two-sided p<0.05 on Fisher's test, and estrogen priming in the mock cycle may raise the placebo response.

sonnet.r: With about 10 women per arm a significant difference needs roughly 5 of 10 against 0 of 10; the biology (chlorhexidine clearing plus Lactobacillus supplementation) points to a large effect but the sponsor may report descriptively without a formal test.

haiku.r: Ten per arm is too few to show a responder-rate gap with confidence unless it is very large, and the spontaneous placebo shift is unknown.

carbon.r: With only 10 participants per arm and a stringent >=90% metagenomic Lactobacillus dominance cutoff, even a substantial biologic effect can easily miss two-sided p<0.05.

sol.r: With roughly ten participants per arm, even substantial microbiome conversion may miss significance; cleansing and spontaneous microbiome shifts add uncertainty.

trials.t: Gut Microbiome and Metabolic Health Study
trials.ep: Change in plasma imidazole propionate concentration from baseline to week 8

fable.r: No prior human evidence that oleoylethanolamide lowers imidazole propionate, a highly variable microbial metabolite, so a real effect in healthy adults over 8 weeks is unlikely.

opus.r: Oleoylethanolamide has no human evidence of lowering plasma imidazole propionate; a novel, highly variable gut-metabolite endpoint in 90 healthy adults over 8 weeks is unlikely to move significantly.

sonnet.r: A single-site 8-week supplement study in healthy adults with a research metabolite (ImP) that varies a lot between people; a real shift in ImP is biologically uncertain and 45 per arm gives modest power.

haiku.r: Small 90-person healthy-volunteer study of a noisy gut-derived marker; the mechanistic link from OEA to imidazole propionate is unproven, so a significant week-8 drop is far from assured.

carbon.r: Oral oleoylethanolamide has an unproven link to gut bacterial histidine-to-imidazole propionate conversion, and healthy non-diabetic adults have low baseline imidazole propionate levels.

sol.r: Oleoylethanolamide's metabolic rationale does not establish a meaningful reduction in imidazole propionate, especially without selecting participants for elevated baseline levels.

trials.t: A Phase II Clinical Study on the Efficacy and Safety of HRS-1780 in Participants With Primary Aldosteronism
trials.ep: Change from baseline in office systolic blood pressure at Week 8

fable.r: With about 30 patients per arm and blood-pressure change SD near 14 mmHg, a placebo response larger than expected or a modest dose could leave a real effect short of significance.

opus.r: Blocking the aldosterone pathway lowers blood pressure strongly in primary aldosteronism, but with about 30 per arm, background antihypertensives and office-BP noise, a modest dose could still miss significance.

sonnet.r: About 30 patients per arm with an 8-week office SBP endpoint; a presumed aldosterone synthase inhibitor should lower SBP by roughly 8 to 12 mmHg versus placebo, but the small sample leaves a real chance of a miss.

haiku.r: Only 61 patients, but an aldosterone synthase inhibitor should give a large placebo-adjusted SBP fall in primary aldosteronism, so a significant week-8 difference is likely; the dose and timing details are unstated.

carbon.r: With 61 total participants—potentially split across multiple HRS-1780 dose groups—office blood pressure variability could obscure a clinically meaningful antihypertensive effect.

sol.r: Aldosterone-driven disease favors a treatment signal, but approximately 31 participants per arm leave substantial uncertainty from office blood-pressure variability, background therapy and undisclosed dose potency.

trials.t: A Study Comparing Safety and Efficacy of SHR-3167 Fixed-Dose Titration and Individualized-Dose Titration in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Inadequately Controlled With Oral Antihyperglycemic Agents
trials.ep: The percentage of participants who experienced at least one hypoglycemic event.

fable.r: Enrolment is closed and treatment lasts 20 weeks, so the trial should complete close to its registered date; the sponsor seldom posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

opus.r: Enrolment of 102 is complete with a 20-week treat-to-target period, so Hengrui should hit the December 2026 primary completion; Chinese sponsor rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

sonnet.r: Open-label phase 2 titration comparison with a hypoglycemia-incidence primary; last participant already enrolled and a 20-week treatment fits the registered completion, so on-time completion is likely. Hengrui rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

haiku.r: Open-label Chinese titration study of 102 patients with a safety primary; the registry date should be updated on time and little slippage is expected.

carbon.r: Because recruitment of all 102 participants had already finished by late October 2026 for a 20-week treatment period, the trial is very likely to complete on time without stopping or posting early results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

sol.r: Recruitment is already closed and follow-up is short, making major delay unlikely, but early ClinicalTrials.gov results posting is unlikely.

trials.t: IBI306 Monotherapy in Non-Familial Hypercholesterolemia and Mixed Hyperlipidemia
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 with IBI306 monotherapy

fable.r: Failure is very unlikely for a PCSK9 antibody on LDL-C at week 12; the residual risk is a disclosure that only calls the result positive without a statement on the primary endpoint.

opus.r: A PCSK9 antibody versus placebo on percent LDL-C change almost never fails; only an operational or data-integrity problem would sink it.

sonnet.r: Tafolecimab (anti-PCSK9) is already approved in China with a roughly 60 to 70 percent LDL-C lowering; a placebo-controlled monotherapy trial of about 99 per arm will almost certainly be positive, so the risk is only reporting or analysis quirks.

haiku.r: A PCSK9 antibody lowering LDL-C against placebo at week 12 is a well-established mechanism, so the realistic risk is the timing of a public announcement rather than the result.

carbon.r: Because tafolecimab is an approved PCSK9 antibody with overwhelming statistical power for week-12 LDL-C reduction, the main risk to scoring met is a brief corporate update calling the trial positive without explicitly stating the primary endpoint result.

sol.r: Failure would most likely require unexpectedly inadequate exposure or LDL-C lowering at the tested regimen, given the established efficacy of PCSK9 antibodies.

trials.t: A Study to See How Safe and Effective Alirocumab is When Given Weekly to Adult Participants Who Have Hypercholesterolemia
trials.ep: Percent change in LDL-C

fable.r: Enrolment closed within about four months and the endpoint is at week 12, so completion should be on time; results posting is not due until about a year after primary completion.

opus.r: Enrolment of 438 at 34 US sites is complete with a 12-week primary, so primary completion should land on time; Regeneron typically posts results close to the 12-month deadline (end of 2027), after the read date.

sonnet.r: Descriptive dose-ranging study of weekly alirocumab by Regeneron; enrollment already closed with 438 participants and a 12-week primary, so on-time primary completion is likely, and Regeneron typically posts results around the 12-month deadline.

haiku.r: Open-label US dose-ranging study by a large sponsor, not recruiting at launch, so the registry date should be updated on time and results posting is due within a year of completion.

carbon.r: With enrollment of 438 US participants already completed by late October 2026 and only a 12-week primary follow-up, primary completion should occur on schedule in December 2026 or January 2027.

sol.r: Closed recruitment, an established drug and a 12-week lipid endpoint make timely completion likely, although results posting may wait until the usual one-year window.

trials.t: A Phase 2a Efficacy, Safety, Tolerability, and PK Study of SYT-510 in Participants With Generalized Anxiety Disorder
trials.ep: Amygdala BOLD fMRI response to fearful stimuli 7 hours after a single dose (Day 2 of each crossover period)

fable.r: Nine registered primary outcomes in a 24-patient single-dose crossover make it very unlikely that all are met, and the sponsor may only describe the data as supportive.

opus.r: The record lists nine primary outcomes (fMRI, JORT, learning indices, STAI) and the round needs all of them met; a single-dose 24-person crossover will not make every one significant.

sonnet.r: Nine co-primary measures must all be met in a 24-person crossover, which is very unlikely even if the drug has real effects; sponsors of such phase 2a studies typically report mixed or exploratory pharmacodynamic signals.

haiku.r: Single-dose crossover in 24 patients with nine co-primary outcomes that must all be significant for the same arm; a one-day anxiolytic effect on amygdala BOLD is unlikely to clear that bar.

carbon.r: Listing nine distinct fMRI, behavioral, and self-report primary outcomes in a single-dose N=24 crossover study creates a high bar under co-primary rules and high likelihood of exploratory biomarker reporting without formal primary significance.

sol.r: Twenty-four crossover participants are unlikely to demonstrate consistent significant benefits across all nine heterogeneous registered primary measures after one dose.

trials.t: Chlorhexidine and/or Metronidazole Plus FB301 Pre-treatment Trial
trials.ep: The change in vaginal microbiome in terms of relative abundance of combined Lactobacillus crispatus and jensenii species

fable.r: Recruiting 120 women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis at two German research units on a menstrual-cycle-timed schedule is likely to run somewhat behind plan, but the study should finish without stopping.

opus.r: Recruitment of 120 symptomatic BV patients across four arms at two German sites, with menses-timed dosing and 10 weeks of follow-up, is tight for a March 2027 primary completion.

sonnet.r: Open-label microbiome study at two German sites that is still recruiting; the one-month recruitment tail and week-3 primary make a slip beyond June 2027 plausible but not the base case. Small private sponsor, so results unlikely to be posted by August 2027.

haiku.r: Small German multi-arm biotherapeutic study with two menstrual-cycle treatment courses; cycle-based dosing and strict screening can stretch enrolment past the registered date.

carbon.r: Enrolling 120 symptomatic premenopausal women with bacterial vaginosis under strict contraception, menses-timed dosing, and sexual abstinence rules across just two German sites carries substantial risk of recruitment extending past June 2027.

sol.r: The short primary assessment limits follow-up risk, but two-site recruitment, menstrual-cycle scheduling and abstinence requirements could delay enrollment.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Zelicapavir in Participants Aged ≥28 Days to ≤36 Months of Age Infected With Respiratory Syncytial Virus
trials.c: RSV Infection; RSV; Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)
trials.ep: Time to complete resolution of clinical signs of RSV, measured with the RESOLVE-P instrument, from Day 1 through Day 14

fable.r: With about 150 children the trial is powered only for a large acceleration of symptom resolution, and zelicapavir's clinical benefit has so far been modest outside the highest-risk adults.

opus.r: Zelicapavir's earlier pediatric and adult phase 2 studies showed modest, inconsistent clinical benefit; a 150-child trial on time to complete resolution needs a hazard ratio near 1.5 to reach significance.

sonnet.r: Oral RSV antivirals have struggled to show clinical benefit on symptom-resolution endpoints in treated patients, and 75 children per arm with a noisy clinician-rated endpoint leaves little power; zelicapavir's adult phase 2b missed or gave only subgroup signals.

haiku.r: Oral RSV replication inhibitor in young children with a 14-day clinical-resolution endpoint; antivirals often show viral-load effects without a clear symptom benefit, so the drug is probably too weak here.

carbon.r: Initiating an oral RSV replication inhibitor up to 72 hours after symptom onset typically produces modest acceleration of complete clinical sign resolution relative to the ~1.43 hazard ratio needed for significance in 150 children.

sol.r: Antiviral activity may not sufficiently shorten complete clinical resolution when treatment begins after symptom onset and residual cough dominates recovery.

trials.t: Study to Evaluate Tulisokibart in Adults With Psoriatic Arthritis (MK-7240-015)
trials.ep: Percentage of participants achieving ACR20 response at Week 16

fable.r: TL1A blockade has no clinical proof in psoriatic arthritis, and small dose arms need a difference of about 20 points in ACR20 to reach significance.

opus.r: Anti-TL1A has proven efficacy in IBD but none yet in psoriatic arthritis; if joint efficacy is modest (about 15 points over placebo), 47 per arm gives limited power.

sonnet.r: TL1A blockade has no proven efficacy in psoriatic arthritis, and with about 47 per arm a true 15 to 20 point ACR20 gain gives only borderline power; placebo ACR20 of 25 to 35 percent compresses the gap.

haiku.r: TL1A blockade in PsA rests on a mechanism well supported in IBD but not yet in joints; an ACR20 gain of about 20 points at the top dose would be significant at 47 per arm, but a smaller effect would not.

carbon.r: Although TL1A blockade downregulates Th1 and Th17 pathways relevant to psoriatic arthritis, tulisokibart lacks prior clinical proof-of-concept in joint disease and ~35-47 patients per arm requires a ~20-point ACR20 gain.

sol.r: TL1A blockade's activity in intestinal inflammation may not translate into the sizable joint-response advantage required by these small PsA dose groups.

trials.t: A Study of AND017 to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety in Patients With Anemia Due to Non-Dialysis-Dependent Chronic Kidney Disease (NDD-CKD)
trials.c: Anemia Due to Chronic Kidney Disease
trials.ep: Mean hemoglobin level averaged over weeks 23 to 27 in non-dialysis CKD anemia, AND017 vs ESA

fable.r: The main risk is that the AND017 dosing algorithm leaves hemoglobin lower than with ESA in a mixed naive and ESA-treated population, although the HIF-PHI class has reliably shown non-inferiority.

opus.r: HIF-PH inhibitors routinely match ESAs on titrated hemoglobin; failure would need AND017 dosing or titration to underperform against an unstated non-inferiority margin.

sonnet.r: Oral HIF-PH inhibitors have matched ESA on Hb maintenance in non-inferiority designs; the main risks are an unstated margin, an open-label design with titration noise and slower-than-registered enrolment.

haiku.r: A non-inferiority test on mean Hb at weeks 23 to 27 in 240 open-label patients; the risk is a margin the drug misses or a mixed naive and treated population widening the spread.

carbon.r: Treat-to-target oral HIF-PHI titration reliably achieves hemoglobin non-inferiority versus ESA, leaving vague topline press-release wording without explicit primary endpoint confirmation as the main scoring risk.

sol.r: Inadequate dose titration or weaker hemoglobin maintenance after ESA switching is the clearest efficacy risk under a conventional non-inferiority margin.

trials.t: QLS1410 in Participants With Uncontrolled Hypertension
trials.ep: Change from baseline in mean seated systolic blood pressure at week 12

fable.r: A large placebo response on background therapy, as in the HALO trial of baxdrostat, could erase the difference with only about 65 patients per arm.

opus.r: Mechanism is not disclosed; if QLS1410 is not as potent as the aldosterone synthase inhibitors its design mirrors, a 65-per-arm comparison against a sizeable Chinese placebo response could miss.

sonnet.r: Highest of three doses against placebo on 2+ background drugs with 65 per arm; a placebo-adjusted drop near 8 mmHg is detectable, but a large placebo response or a weak dose could erase it.

haiku.r: The dose is not quantified; the highest of three dose arms is the likeliest to clear significance at 65 per arm, but a weak dose-response or a large placebo fall would fail it.

carbon.r: Large placebo office systolic blood pressure drops from regression to the mean and improved background adherence frequently compress treatment differences in uncontrolled and resistant hypertension trials.

sol.r: Improved adherence to background treatment could create a large placebo blood-pressure fall and erase a moderate incremental QLS1410 effect.

trials.t: A Trial to Investigate Safety, Exposure, and Efficacy of HU6 Compared With Placebo in Adult Participants With Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatohepatitis (MASH)
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in liver fat content by MRI-PDFF at week 26

fable.r: A smaller liver-fat effect at 26 weeks than in the 61-day study, compounded by dropouts at the highest dose, is the most likely way to miss one of the two efficacy primaries.

opus.r: Doses chosen for long-term safety of a DNP-derived mitochondrial uncoupler may be lower than those that cut liver fat in short studies, and both PDFF co-primaries (percent change and >=30% responders) must be met with ~45 per arm.

sonnet.r: Phase 2a with about 45 per arm and several co-primaries; HU6 likely cuts liver fat substantially, but the placebo response and a lower than expected dose effect could blur significance.

haiku.r: With 45 per arm and a liver-fat SD near 25 percent, a drug effect of about 10 points is needed for significance; a smaller effect or a late topline would sink the trial.

carbon.r: Because safety and PK measures are co-listed alongside two MRI-PDFF endpoints as primary outcomes in this Phase 2a study, the main risk is descriptive topline reporting that omits formal hypothesis-test statements on all efficacy primaries.

sol.r: Longer high-dose mitochondrial uncoupling may cause tolerability-related discontinuations, weakening both liver-fat and responder contrasts despite prior short-term activity.

trials.t: A Study of AND017 to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety in Dialysis-Dependent Chronic Kidney Disease (DD-CKD) Patients With Anemia
trials.c: Anemia Due to Chronic Kidney Disease
trials.ep: Mean hemoglobin averaged over Weeks 23 to 27 in dialysis-dependent CKD patients with anemia

fable.r: A titration scheme that leaves mean haemoglobin clearly below the ESA arm, or an unusually tight margin, is the main way an ESA-conversion HIF-PHI trial misses non-inferiority; the larger practical risk is that this small sponsor reports late or not at all.

opus.r: Non-inferiority on mean Hb is usually met by HIF-PH inhibitors versus ESA; the residual risk is under-correction from a conservative oral dose-titration scheme or an unexpectedly tight margin.

sonnet.r: Oral HIF-PH inhibitor against ESA in dialysis, a class that reliably shows non-inferior Hb maintenance; risk is a tight margin or unusual control-arm stability, not the drug.

haiku.r: An ESA comparator is strong and the margin is not stated; a tight non-inferiority margin on a hemoglobin level would fail an oral agent that is only slightly lower.

carbon.r: Higher gastrointestinal intolerance or thromboembolic discontinuations in the open-label oral HIF-PHI arm versus established ESA therapy could dilute treatment maintenance and narrow the non-inferiority cushion.

sol.r: Switching stable ESA-treated patients to AND017 could transiently destabilize hemoglobin enough to miss an unexpectedly tight non-inferiority margin.

trials.t: A Study of mRNA-1018-H5 Pandemic Influenza Vaccine in Healthy Adults
trials.ep: Percentage of participants with H5 hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titer ≥1:40 at Day 43, after two doses

fable.r: Failure would need the older-adult stratum or the seroconversion co-primary to fall short of the regulatory thresholds, or Moderna to describe the data without stating that the endpoints were met.

opus.r: The trial's own success is likely judged on CBER-style lower confidence bounds for seroprotection and seroconversion by age group; the main threat is a weaker response in adults 65 and older missing the 60%/30% bounds.

sonnet.r: mRNA H5 vaccine in naive adults should produce HAI 1:40 in most recipients versus a few percent on placebo; the risk is how the sponsor frames the result, as thresholds or descriptive rather than a stated test.

haiku.r: Immunogenicity against a fixed threshold, so the risk is a lower-than-hoped response rate in older adults rather than a placebo problem; success is likely if the vaccine works.

carbon.r: Avian H5 hemagglutination inhibition assays can exhibit lower sensitivity and higher assay variability than microneutralization, risking a miss against strict CBER lower-bound seroprotection thresholds despite robust neutralizing immunity.

sol.r: The principal efficacy risk is an unexpectedly weak H5 HAI response in older adults against age-specific immunogenicity thresholds rather than failure to beat placebo.

trials.t: Evaluation of the Safety and Efficacy of Abenacianine (VGT-309) to Identify Cancer in Subjects Undergoing Surgery for Cancer in the Lung
trials.ep: Share of participants with at least one clinically significant event (NIR imaging finds lesions missed by white light, palpation or preoperative imaging) on surgery day

fable.r: Only an event rate far below the 40-55% seen in earlier lung fluorescence-imaging trials, or disputes over what counts as a clinically significant event, would sink a single-arm threshold test; slow enrolment is the bigger threat to a timely readout.

opus.r: If surgeons with good preoperative CT localization rarely miss lesions, the share of patients with a clinically significant event could fall near the pre-specified lower-bound threshold.

sonnet.r: Fluorescence imaging in lung surgery routinely finds additional lesions in a substantial share of patients, so a significant event rate is likely; the odd control group of 12 with no imaging adds a statistical formality risk.

haiku.r: The endpoint is a responder rate of intraoperative finds against a performance-style bar with no stated comparator; a 'positive' statement without a formal primary test would count as not met.

carbon.r: More thorough preoperative CT/PET staging or surgeon localization under standard white-light/palpation in academic thoracic centers could lower the fraction of occult or unlocalized lesions below the threshold needed.

sol.r: Incremental findings could be less frequent than expected when experienced surgeons use thorough standard localization, especially if suspected additional lesions require stringent confirmation.

trials.t: Phase 2 Trial of Icovamenib in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Who Are Not Achieving Glycemic Targets
trials.ep: Mean change in HbA1c from baseline at week 26, after 12 weeks of treatment

fable.r: The large HbA1c effects came from small subgroups of COVALENT-111, so regression toward the modest whole-trial effect (about 0.4 points) would leave 64 patients underpowered.

opus.r: Icovamenib's durable off-treatment HbA1c effect has been modest in unselected patients; with 32 per arm a true effect below ~0.5 points will not reach significance at week 26.

sonnet.r: Only 32 per arm with a modest expected placebo-adjusted HbA1c effect off treatment at week 26; a true effect near 0.6 points only gives moderate power.

haiku.r: Week 26 includes 14 weeks off treatment after a 12-week dosing period, so the drug's HbA1c effect may drift back before the measurement and erase a modest benefit.

carbon.r: Measuring glycemic superiority at Week 26—fourteen weeks after stopping a 12-week icovamenib course—in only 64 total participants leaves low statistical power against typical HbA1c drift and variability.

sol.r: The proposed beta-cell regenerative effect may not produce a sufficiently large placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction fourteen weeks after treatment stops.

trials.t: An Exploratory Efficacy and Safety Study of DFL24498 Topical Ophthalmic Solution Compared With Vehicle in Participants With Dry Eye Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in total corneal fluorescein staining score (NEI scale 0-15) in the study eye

fable.r: Vehicle drops usually improve corneal staining by 1.5 to 2 points over 12 weeks, leaving little room for an untested compound to separate.

opus.r: Vehicle drops themselves improve corneal staining in dry eye trials, compressing the treatment difference; many phase 2 dry-eye programmes miss on CFS despite large samples.

sonnet.r: Dry eye corneal staining shows a large vehicle response and phase 2 trials often miss the sign primary; a modest true effect with 209 per arm gives roughly one in three odds of significance.

haiku.r: Vehicle arms in dry eye improve a lot, so the drug must add about 1 NEI point; phase 2 eye drugs often fail to do this, and the record calls the study exploratory.

carbon.r: Frequent instillation of ophthalmic vehicle drops produces substantial corneal surface lubrication and regression to the mean on NEI fluorescein staining, often masking modest Phase 2 active drug effects.

sol.r: Vehicle lubrication, regression to the mean and trial-related care may substantially improve staining, leaving too little incremental benefit for DFL24498.

trials.t: Pivotal Open-label Phase 3 Clinical Study of QTX-2101 in Adult Patients With Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
trials.c: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL); Acute Promyelocytic Leukaemia; Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia With PML-RARA
trials.ep: Molecular complete remission rate (no detectable PML-RARA in bone marrow) after induction (up to 60 days) and three 8-week consolidation cycles

fable.r: Molecular remission needs about eight months of therapy per patient and 150 newly diagnosed APL patients take years to enrol, so no remission result can be mature by mid-2027; anything public by then is an early stop or a partial pharmacokinetic statement.

opus.r: Molecular CR is near-universal with arsenic plus ATRA, so non-inferiority would fail mainly through early deaths, differentiation syndrome or dropouts counted as non-responders, or a PK co-primary judged unmet.

sonnet.r: Oral arsenic should match IV arsenic on molecular remission, with rates near 95 percent in both arms; the main risk is an unstated margin or small-number noise, and the result will not come out before 2028.

haiku.r: With 75 per arm, a 10-point non-inferiority margin is hard to pass even when the two drugs are equal, so the margin size will decide most of the outcome.

carbon.r: Satisfying both pharmacokinetic Cmax comparability and high molecular CR non-inferiority bounds in 150 APL patients leaves vulnerability to PK Cmax divergence between oral capsules and IV infusion or random early induction dropouts.

sol.r: Both the pharmacokinetic bridge and molecular-remission objective must succeed, while incomplete early remission data or variable oral exposure could prevent a formal overall win.

trials.t: MIST (Metabolic Intervention With Semaglutide and THR-β Therapy) Trial
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline (week 9) to week 20, ECC4703 or placebo added to semaglutide

fable.r: THR-beta agonists lower liver fat but have not reduced body weight in people, so the body-weight primaries are unlikely to separate from semaglutide alone over 11 weeks.

opus.r: THR-beta agonists have shown little or no weight loss on their own; over an 11-week window on escalating semaglutide, any added weight effect is likely under 1 point and the five primaries (weight and liver fat) must all be met.

sonnet.r: A THR-beta agonist adds little weight loss on top of semaglutide over 11 weeks, and five co-primaries including proportion with 5 percent loss must all be met.

haiku.r: A THR-beta agonist is expected to add only a modest weight effect on top of semaglutide, and the co-primary liver-fat outcomes must also be met by the same arm.

carbon.r: Liver-selective THR-beta agonists reliably reduce hepatic steatosis on MRI-PDFF but historically exert minimal systemic body-weight loss, making co-primary incremental weight reduction over active semaglutide in 11 weeks unlikely.

sol.r: THR-beta agonism may reduce liver fat without adding enough short-term weight loss to semaglutide to meet both weight-related co-primary outcomes.

trials.t: Study of Efficacy and Safety of Tonlamarsen in Participants With a Recent Hospitalization and a Concurrent Episode of Acute Severe Hypertension
trials.c: Hypertension; Acute Severe Hypertension; Hypertensive Emergency
trials.ep: Percent change in plasma angiotensinogen (AGT) from baseline to week 4 (Part B)

fable.r: Antisense knockdown of angiotensinogen is reliable, so the threats are a week-4 reading taken before monthly dosing reaches full effect in an unstable post-discharge population, and a two-part trial that will not finish on the registered schedule.

opus.r: AGT knockdown by a GalNAc antisense is near-certain; failure would come from operational issues (slow enrolment of recently hospitalized patients, Part A redesigning Part B) rather than the drug.

sonnet.r: The Part B primary is a pharmacodynamic knockdown of angiotensinogen, which an antisense agent achieves in nearly all treated patients; the only risk is reporting or design change.

haiku.r: The primary is a week-4 biomarker, so the risk is timing or a dose that knocks down angiotensinogen less than designed; blood pressure is secondary and does not decide the primary.

carbon.r: Although hepatic ASO knockdown of plasma AGT is robust, the sequential Part A-to-Part B structure could delay or modify Part B reporting, or acute post-discharge renin-angiotensin shifts could inflate AGT variability.

sol.r: AGT knockdown should be large, but renal dysfunction, hyperkalemia or hypotension on intensive background therapy could interrupt treatment in this vulnerable population.

trials.t: A Study of LY4515100 in Participants With Pain Following Third Molar Removal
trials.ep: Change from baseline in self-reported pain intensity up to Day 1 after impacted third molar removal, single oral dose

fable.r: The mechanism is undisclosed and a single oral dose must act within hours; a slow-onset or modestly effective agent would not separate from placebo before rescue medication blurs the comparison.

opus.r: Undisclosed novel mechanism; the third-molar model separates NSAIDs easily but has rejected many novel analgesic mechanisms, so failure would most likely reflect insufficient single-dose analgesic efficacy.

sonnet.r: Third molar model is highly sensitive to real analgesics, so the main risk is a novel-mechanism compound that is simply not efficacious at the tested single doses, or a small highest-dose arm.

haiku.r: A single-dose third-molar pain model separates active analgesics well, but the placebo response is high and this is an early look at a new agent, so a clear NRS gap at the top dose is only moderately likely.

carbon.r: Novel non-opioid oral analgesic mechanisms frequently exhibit insufficient acute analgesic magnitude or delayed onset after bony third-molar extraction compared with established inflammatory pain pathways.

sol.r: Without an established human analgesic effect, LY4515100 may provide insufficient relief before rescue medication despite the sensitive dental-surgery model.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate Abdominal Symptoms With Camlipixant Compared With Placebo in Adults With Irritable Bowel Syndrome - Diarrhea (IBS-D) and Irritable Bowel Syndrome - Mixed (IBS-M)
trials.ep: Change from baseline in weekly average abdominal pain intensity (0-10 NRS), averaged over Weeks 7 to 12

fable.r: P2X3 antagonism has no clinical proof in IBS and has disappointed in other non-cough indications, while placebo typically cuts abdominal pain by nearly 2 points.

opus.r: P2X3 antagonism has no human proof of visceral analgesia; against a 1.5-2 point placebo improvement in IBS abdominal pain, a modest true effect would not separate with about 100 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: P2X3 antagonism has no established proof of concept in IBS-D/M, and IBS pain trials carry a large placebo response, so a dose-ranging phase 2b may well show no separation on the primary.

haiku.r: Abdominal pain in IBS responds strongly to placebo, and P2X3 blockade has no proven effect on visceral pain, so a modest gap of about 0.3 points on the 0-10 scale is the likeliest outcome.

carbon.r: Selective peripheral P2X3 antagonism may inadequately block multifactorial visceral hypersensitivity in IBS-D and IBS-M against the large placebo pain reductions typical of Rome IV diary trials.

sol.r: P2X3 blockade may help only a visceral-hypersensitivity subset, diluting its effect in a heterogeneous IBS-D and IBS-M population with substantial placebo improvement.

trials.t: Biweekly Long-term Occidiofungin Study for Suppression of Mycotic Recurrence
trials.ep: Clinical cure (vulvovaginal signs and symptoms total score 0, no additional antifungal therapy) at the Day 8 test-of-cure visit

fable.r: With 18 women per arm a cure-rate gap of about 35 points is needed for significance, and occidiofungin gel has no prior human efficacy data to suggest an effect that large over a placebo gel.

opus.r: With 18 per arm there is under 50% power even for a 30-point cure-rate gain over placebo gel, and a small phase 2a may report only descriptively, which counts as not met.

sonnet.r: With 18 per arm, only a very large cure-rate gap reaches p<0.05 at Day 8, and the strict VSS=0 definition keeps placebo cure low but also caps drug cure.

haiku.r: With 18 patients per arm the trial needs a very large cure-rate gap to reach significance; a novel topical antifungal could produce one, but placebo cure in acute VVC is substantial by Day 8.

carbon.r: With only 18 participants per arm and strict complete symptom resolution (VSS=0) potentially required across multiple visits, statistical power is modest even if topical occidiofungin has meaningful antifungal activity.

sol.r: Only 18 patients per arm and stringent complete-resolution criteria make a statistically convincing result uncertain even if occidiofungin has meaningful antifungal activity.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of HDM1005 Compared to Tirzepatide in Obese Adults Without Diabetes
trials.sp: Hangzhou Zhongmei Huadong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 40

fable.r: Tirzepatide is the strongest marketed comparator and HDM1005 is in the same GLP-1/GIP class, so a gap of more than 2 points in its favour, needed for superiority with 93 per arm, is unlikely unless the top dose is pushed well beyond tirzepatide-equivalent exposure.

opus.r: Tirzepatide gives roughly 13-17% weight loss in Chinese adults; showing significant superiority at week 40 needs about a 3-point edge that another incretin agonist is unlikely to deliver.

sonnet.r: Beating tirzepatide on weight loss at week 40 in a 93-per-arm open-label phase 2 needs a 2+ point advantage, which few incretin candidates deliver; tirzepatide itself loses about 12-14% by then.

haiku.r: Superiority over tirzepatide over 40 weeks is a high bar, since the comparator is among the most effective approved obesity drugs and HDM1005 would need a clearly larger weight loss than it has likely shown.

carbon.r: Tirzepatide produces ~15% mean body weight reduction and ~90% 5%-responder rates in Chinese adults with obesity, making statistical superiority extremely difficult unless a pre-specified non-inferiority margin applies.

sol.r: Tirzepatide is a demanding comparator, and matching its substantial weight loss would not establish superiority.

trials.t: A Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of NS-136 in the Treatment of Schizophrenia
trials.ep: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 5

fable.r: M4 positive allosteric modulation has not held up in schizophrenia: emraclidine failed two phase 2 trials, so the true effect of NS-136 may be only a few PANSS points, too small to detect with 50 patients per arm.

opus.r: High placebo response in acute schizophrenia sank the emraclidine M4 PAM trials; with 50 per arm a modest drug effect would be lost in placebo noise.

sonnet.r: Acute schizophrenia phase 2 with about 50 per arm detects only a 7-8 point PANSS difference; novel mechanisms have a high miss rate and placebo response in Chinese sites is sizeable.

haiku.r: Placebo response in acute schizophrenia trials, especially at Chinese centres, is large, so a PANSS gap of several points at week 5 is needed; 120 mg in 50 per arm gives a reasonable but uncertain chance of clearing it.

carbon.r: Selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulation lacks proven clinical efficacy in acute schizophrenia following the Phase 2 failures of emraclidine, and 50 patients per arm offers limited power against inpatient placebo improvement.

sol.r: With 50 patients per arm, a modest PANSS advantage can be obscured by patient variability and placebo improvement.

trials.t: Efficacy and Safety of FID 123472 Ophthalmic Solution for Ocular Redness in Adults
trials.ep: Change from baseline in investigator-assessed ocular redness (Ora Calibra scale, 0-4) at 15 minutes post-instillation on day 1

fable.r: The 15-minute endpoint should be met easily, but the co-primary at 14 hours after a single dose asks for a duration beyond the 8 hours shown for low-dose brimonidine, and the late effect may be too small to reach significance.

opus.r: The 15-minute whitening effect is near-certain; the risk sits in the second primary, durable redness reduction 14 hours after a single dose, which exceeds what approved redness relievers claim.

sonnet.r: The 15-minute effect of an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor is near certain; the co-primary at 14 hours after Day 2 dosing is the risk because vasoconstrictor effect wanes and vehicle returns to baseline.

haiku.r: Both co-primary time points must be met, and the 14-hour redness effect of a short-acting alpha agonist is the weak point; the 15-minute effect itself should separate from vehicle.

carbon.r: Although apraclonidine 0.125% will reliably blanch ocular redness at 15 minutes, meeting both co-primary endpoints requires maintaining statistically significant vasoconstriction 14 hours (840 minutes) after a single drop.

sol.r: Rapid redness reduction is highly plausible, but superiority must also persist at the much more demanding 14-hour co-primary assessment.

trials.t: A Clinical Trial Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of HSK55718 in Patients for Postoperative Pain Treatment in Abdominal Surgery
trials.ep: Sum of pain intensity differences over the first 24 hours after abdominal surgery (SPID 0-24)

fable.r: The mechanism of HSK55718 is not disclosed and each arm has only about 40 patients; if its analgesic effect is modest, rescue opioid use in the placebo arm can narrow the SPID gap below significance.

opus.r: Mechanism undisclosed; if HSK55718 is a non-opioid or peripheral analgesic, its SPID advantage over placebo with rescue opioids allowed may be too small to detect with about 40 patients per arm.

sonnet.r: Postoperative pain models are assay-sensitive and any of three doses may win, so failure would need an unexpectedly weak compound or a high placebo plus rescue-medication effect.

haiku.r: Forty patients per arm across five arms is small for a SPID endpoint; a clear gap over placebo at the top dose is plausible in post-operative pain, but power for each comparison is limited.

carbon.r: Frequent rescue analgesia use in the placebo group after abdominal surgery can compress SPID24 differences if HSK55718 has modest analgesic potency or short duration.

sol.r: The principal uncertainty is whether any tested dose produces enough sustained analgesia to separate from placebo despite rescue treatment.

trials.t: A Proof-of-Concept Study of LAD328 in Adults With Hidradenitis Suppurativa
trials.ep: Proportion of participants achieving at least 55% reduction from baseline in IHS4 (IHS4-55) at week 12

fable.r: With 25 patients per arm, significance on IHS4-55 needs a gap of roughly 35-40 points over placebo, more than established HS biologics achieve, so even an active drug would probably miss.

opus.r: With 25 per arm a roughly 35-point IHS4-55 difference is needed for significance, larger than effective HS biologics usually achieve over placebo at week 12.

sonnet.r: A 25-per-arm proof-of-concept needs a 30+ point IHS4-55 gap for p<0.05; even a truly effective biologic has only about 40% power.

haiku.r: Twenty-five patients per arm gives little power to show a responder gap of 25 points or less; an effective agent could clear it, but a phase 2 HS signal of this size is often marginal.

carbon.r: With only 25 participants per arm and volatile Week 12 placebo response rates (~25-35%) in hidradenitis suppurativa, achieving two-sided p<0.05 requires an unusually large treatment delta exceeding typical biologic benchmarks.

sol.r: Twenty-five patients per arm leave limited power for the moderate placebo-adjusted response differences commonly seen in hidradenitis suppurativa.

trials.t: A Clinical Study Evaluating Licaminlimab for Dry Eye Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Day 29 in global ocular discomfort severity score, in participants with the specific TNFR1 genotype

fable.r: The symptom benefit in TNFR1 genotype carriers rests on small subgroup analyses of earlier trials and may shrink on replication, while dry eye symptom scores improve a lot on vehicle alone.

opus.r: The genotype hypothesis comes from an exploratory subgroup of the earlier phase 2; if it does not replicate, the drug's effect on ocular discomfort is too small against a large vehicle response.

sonnet.r: Dry eye symptom trials have a very high failure rate from vehicle response; genotype enrichment and an earlier signal improve odds, but a 28-day symptom endpoint with about 80 per arm stays fragile.

haiku.r: The primary is a genotype subgroup chosen before randomisation, so the effect may be diluted or the subgroup finding may not hold; a discomfort score with a vehicle response also limits the gap.

carbon.r: Retrospectively identified pharmacogenetic responder subgroups in dry eye disease frequently exhibit regression toward the mean on subjective discomfort endpoints when tested prospectively against an active lubricating vehicle.

sol.r: A genotype-associated ocular-sign signal may not translate into a reproducible Day-29 symptom benefit against a vehicle with substantial therapeutic activity.

trials.t: A Phase II Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of FXS5626 in Patients With NIU
trials.sp: Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical Industrial Development Co. Ltd.
trials.ep: Percentage of patients meeting treatment failure criteria from week 6 to week 24

fable.r: Twenty patients against ten on placebo cannot show a significant difference in treatment failure unless the gap is about 45 points or more, larger than adalimumab achieved in VISUAL I.

opus.r: With 20 versus 10 patients, only a very large reduction in treatment failure reaches p<0.05; a typical 25-30 point benefit would leave p around 0.1.

sonnet.r: With 20, 10 and 10 patients, a treatment-failure difference must be around 40+ points to reach p<0.05, so even a working oral agent will often miss.

haiku.r: Ten placebo patients and twenty in the group 1 arm leave little room for significance on a treatment-failure proportion; a large benefit is needed, and the active dose is not identified.

carbon.r: With only 10 placebo patients and 20 patients in the primary FXS5626 arm, statistical significance requires a dramatic ~40 percentage point reduction in post-steroid-taper treatment failure.

sol.r: Only ten placebo patients make the failure-rate comparison unstable and require a very large treatment effect for statistical superiority.

trials.t: Phase 2a Dose Finding Study of Nu-3 Gel in Subjects With Mild iDFU
trials.ep: Primary Efficacy Outcome

fable.r: A 24-patient dose-comparison trial run by a small company across six sites, with outside adjudication of every eligibility decision, is likely to enrol slowly and finish after its January 2027 target.

opus.r: Small private sponsor running a 24-patient, 6-site dose comparison in tightly defined mild iDFU with external specialist eligibility review; enrolment is likely to run past the January 2027 target, with no results posting expected by mid-2027.

sonnet.r: Tiny 24-patient dose-comparison study by a small sponsor, 6 US sites, started Aug 2026 with a short Jan 2027 primary completion; enrolling mildly infected DFU patients with expert image confirmation will likely run slower than registered, and no results are likely on CT.gov by Aug 2027.

haiku.r: Small 24-patient Phase 2a at six US sites with a strict specialist image check that can slow enrolment; completion slipping past May 2027 is more likely than not.

carbon.r: Complex eligibility criteria requiring vascular perfusion testing, caregiver attendance, and same-day external specialist consensus review make recruitment delays past the five-month window highly likely.

sol.r: Despite the small enrollment target, restrictive mild-infection criteria, external eligibility review, and caregiver requirements create meaningful recruitment and delay risk.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Vehicle-Controlled, Double-Masked to Open-Label Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Lacripep in Subjects With Neurotrophic Keratitis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in central corneal fluorescein staining (NEI scale, 0-3) in the study eye at week 8

fable.r: Lacripep missed its primary endpoints in its only earlier controlled trial, and patients entering at the top of the staining scale will improve on vehicle alone, leaving little room for the half-grade gap that 27 per arm requires.

opus.r: With about 27 eyes per arm on a coarse 0-3 NEI staining grade and a vehicle (artificial tear) arm that also improves, a plausible 0.3-grade benefit gives well under 50% power.

sonnet.r: Only about 27 per arm on a coarse 0-3 staining grade after a vehicle run-in; vehicle response and regression to the mean will absorb much of any effect, so a significant difference is a coin-flip at best.

haiku.r: 27 per arm on a 0-3 grade scale gives roughly half power for a 0.5-point gap, and vehicle arms in stage 1 NK improve slowly, so a clear benefit is needed.

carbon.r: Frequent thrice-daily vehicle lubrication and regression from mandatory Grade 3 baseline staining produce substantial control-arm improvement in Stage 1 neurotrophic keratitis, while Lacripep showed modest staining effects in prior ocular surface studies.

sol.r: The vehicle run-in limits but does not eliminate staining improvement, so 27 patients per arm may not distinguish a modest peptide effect from ocular-surface care.

trials.t: Phase II Study of Dysplasix™ Intravaginal Suppositories in Patients Patients With High-Risk HPV and Mild Cervical Cytologic Abnormalities
trials.c: High-risk HPV (Any Strain); LSIL, Low Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion; ASC-US
trials.ep: Regression of baseline ASC-US or LSIL cytology to NILM at the Day 50 visit, 30 days after the 15-day course

fable.r: With about 22 women per arm, frequent spontaneous normalisation of ASC-US/LSIL cytology within weeks, and two efficacy primaries (cytology regression and hr-HPV clearance) that must both be significant, this proof-of-concept study has little power even if the suppository has some activity.

opus.r: About 22 per arm, high spontaneous regression of ASC-US/LSIL and a second efficacy primary (hr-HPV clearance at day 50) that must also be met make a significant result on both unlikely.

sonnet.r: With 22-23 per arm and spontaneous regression of ASC-US/LSIL and HPV clearance in the placebo arm, both co-primary efficacy endpoints would need an implausibly large difference to reach significance.

haiku.r: 45 patients split 23 and 22 on a yes-or-no cytology regression needs a gap of roughly 27 to 30 points over placebo to reach significance, which a topical suppository is unlikely to deliver.

carbon.r: With only 45 participants and multiple primary endpoints assessed just 30 days after a 15-day intravaginal course, the trial lacks statistical power to show both cytologic regression and hr-HPV clearance over spontaneous resolution.

sol.r: Only about 22 patients per arm must demonstrate both cytologic regression and rapid HPV clearance, requiring unusually large treatment effects.

trials.t: A Phase II Study of 9MW3811 in Patients With Pathological Scar
trials.ep: Change from baseline in modified Vancouver Scar Scale (mVSS, 0-18) total score at week 12

fable.r: Fifteen patients per arm cannot detect much less than a 2-point mVSS difference, and anti-IL-11 efficacy in established scars is unproven; 12 weeks may also be too short to remodel mature scar tissue.

opus.r: Fifteen patients per arm, a 12-week window and an insensitive mVSS scale for established keloid or hypertrophic scars leave little power for a modest systemic anti-IL-11 effect.

sonnet.r: A systemic anti-IL-11 antibody must visibly change established scars (pliability, thickness) within 12 weeks in 15 patients per arm; placebo response on patient-reported items is sizable and the proof-of-concept is unproven.

haiku.r: Only 15 per arm on a 0-18 scar score: a gap of about 2.5 to 3 points over placebo is needed for significance, which a 30-patient Phase 2 reaches only if the effect is large.

carbon.r: Established pathological scars that have shown no spontaneous regression for 6 months are densely fibrotic and rarely remodel enough within 12 weeks of anti-IL-11 therapy in a 30-patient trial to achieve statistical superiority.

sol.r: IL-11 blockade may inhibit ongoing fibrosis without reversing enough established scar tissue to produce a clear clinical difference within 12 weeks.

trials.t: An Investigation of FID 123472 Ophthalmic Solution to Vehicle for the Reduction of Ocular Redness in Adults
trials.ep: Change from baseline in investigator-assessed ocular redness (Ora Calibra 0-4 scale) at 15 minutes after instillation on Day 1

fable.r: The 15-minute endpoint is near-certain for an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor; the risk is the co-primary at 600 minutes, where the drug-vehicle gap will be small and must still reach significance with 89 per arm.

opus.r: The 15-minute effect of an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor is near certain; the risk sits with the co-primary at 600 minutes, when blanching may have worn off enough to lose significance.

sonnet.r: The 15-minute effect is near certain; the risk lies in the co-primary at 600 minutes, where vasoconstrictor effect wanes and a smaller difference must still be significant.

haiku.r: The 600-minute co-primary is the likeliest miss, since the alpha-agonist effect fades by then; both time points must be met by the same arm.

carbon.r: While apraclonidine 0.125% reliably blanches conjunctival vessels at 15 minutes, meeting the co-primary endpoint at 600 minutes (10 hours) post-instillation risks waning vasoconstrictor duration at this diluted concentration.

sol.r: The acute vasoconstrictor effect should be clear at 15 minutes; maintaining significant separation at the co-primary 600-minute assessment is the larger efficacy risk.

trials.t: Intra-Articular Allocetra in Patients With Primary Knee Osteoarthritis
trials.ep: Change from baseline in WOMAC Pain score (0-50) at 3 months

fable.r: The hypothesis comes from a post-hoc age subgroup of a phase 2a that missed in the overall population; with large intra-articular placebo responses, the true effect is probably too small for both WOMAC pain and function to reach significance.

opus.r: The age-enriched design follows a subgroup signal from the earlier phase I/II; against the large intra-articular placebo response, a modest true effect is unlikely to reach significance on both WOMAC pain and function.

sonnet.r: Knee OA injection trials have a large placebo response on WOMAC pain, and both pain and function co-primaries must be significant for a cell-based product with limited controlled evidence.

haiku.r: Placebo injections in knee OA produce a large pain response, leaving a gap of about 2.3 points on the 0-50 WOMAC pain scale that Allocetra must clear with 91 per arm; cell-based therapies have a mixed record here.

carbon.r: Three ultrasound-guided intra-articular placebo injections generate a large and variable analgesic response in knee osteoarthritis, making superiority on both WOMAC Pain and WOMAC Function at 3 months difficult to achieve.

sol.r: Three image-guided placebo injections can produce substantial pain and function improvements, potentially obscuring a modest immunomodulatory effect.

trials.t: RBD5044 in Chinese Participants With Hypertriglyceridemia
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in fasting serum triglycerides at week 16

fable.r: Failure would need an unexpectedly weak or short-lived knockdown, or very noisy triglyceride values in a 40-patient study; APOC3 silencing has reliably halved triglycerides in this population.

opus.r: APOC3-targeting siRNAs consistently cut triglycerides by about half against placebo; failure would require an unexpectedly low dose or weak GalNAc-siRNA potency, which 20 patients per arm would still likely detect.

sonnet.r: An apoC-III-lowering agent should cut triglycerides by about half or more; the main uncertainty is that the dose is unknown and n=20 per arm leaves the variance in percent change large.

haiku.r: Twenty per arm on a volatile percent-change endpoint; a drug of this class should clear the bar comfortably, so the main threat is a small or noisy sample rather than a weak effect.

carbon.r: Although GalNAc-siRNA knockdown of apoC-III yields large triglyceride reductions, splitting 40 participants across multiple dose cohorts could reduce per-arm sample size if high fasting triglyceride variability occurs.

sol.r: The main risk is failure of the undisclosed dose to deliver class-like triglyceride lowering; a significant LDL-C benefit is considerably less assured.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Vehicle Controlled Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of VC005 Gel in Adult Subjects With Mild to Moderate Atopic Dermatitis
trials.sp: Jiangsu vcare pharmaceutical technology co., LTD
trials.ep: Change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at week 4

fable.r: Vehicle gels improve mild-to-moderate eczema by a quarter or more in four weeks; if skin delivery of VC005 is modest or the 120 patients are split over several dose arms, the EASI gap may not reach significance.

opus.r: Mild-to-moderate AD starts from low EASI, so vehicle emollient response compresses the window; an unknown-potency topical may separate too little in four weeks.

sonnet.r: Topical JAK-type agents usually beat vehicle clearly on EASI at week 4; risks are a strong vehicle response in mild disease, a low concentration or a lower baseline EASI shrinking absolute change.

haiku.r: Concentration and regimen are not stated, and a topical gel against a strong vehicle response needs a clear gap to clear 60 per arm; a near-1-point EASI effect would be enough.

carbon.r: Moisturizing vehicle gel effects and regression to the mean over 4 weeks in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis can narrow the EASI difference if baseline disease severity is low.

sol.r: Mild disease and a moisturizing gel vehicle may leave little incremental EASI improvement for an incompletely characterized topical agent to demonstrate.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Clinical Activity of ABS-1230 in Pediatric and Young Adult Participants With KCNT1-related Epilepsy
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in countable motor seizures per 28 days over 12 weeks of treatment (Part 2)

fable.r: KCNT1 epilepsy is ultra-rare, so the randomized part will be small and slow; seizure counts vary widely, and any statement by mid-2027 will probably be open-label Part 1 data, not a Part 2 efficacy test.

opus.r: Around 20 per arm in an ultra-rare epilepsy with highly variable seizure counts means only a very large effect will reach significance, and mean percent change is dragged by outliers.

sonnet.r: About 20 per arm in a rare, highly variable epilepsy, where seizure counts are noisy and placebo responses large; a potent KCNT1 inhibitor could still give a clear effect.

haiku.r: About 20 per arm on a seizure-count percent change with wide spread: a 30-point gap is needed for significance, and KCNT1 agents have a mixed record, so a moderate effect would leave the trial underpowered.

carbon.r: High week-to-week seizure diary variability, small Part 2 sample size, and CNS/cardiac dose-limiting tolerability constraints of KCNT1 channel blockade make statistical superiority over 12 weeks challenging.

sol.r: Mutation-dependent responses, developmental heterogeneity and highly variable seizure counts can overwhelm a modest effect in roughly 20 randomized patients per arm.

trials.t: To Assess the Efficacy of Two Brushing Regimens: in the Reduction of Established Dental Plaque and Gingivitis.
trials.ep: Change from baseline in whole-mouth mean Loe-Silness Gingival Index at 24 weeks

fable.r: The only real risk is a small single-centre sample meeting a strong brushing (Hawthorne) improvement in the control arm, or the plaque index missing while gingivitis is met.

opus.r: With about 42 per arm and plaque index as a co-primary, the stannous fluoride benefit on plaque (smaller and less consistent than on gingivitis) could miss significance even if gingivitis is clearly reduced.

sonnet.r: Colgate stannous fluoride vs regular fluoride 24-week gingivitis/plaque studies almost always report significant benefit; the only real risk is one of the two co-primaries missing with n=85.

haiku.r: A small in-house sponsor trial of about 42 per arm looking for a modest stannous-versus-sodium-fluoride gingivitis gap of about 0.1 index points, so a non-significant result is the main risk.

carbon.r: If public disclosure occurs only via abbreviated summary without reporting formal statistical tests on both Gingival Index and Plaque Index co-primaries, technical resolution could fail despite strong clinical efficacy.

sol.r: Study-driven improvements in brushing with the control regimen could narrow the formulation's incremental plaque and gingivitis benefits.

trials.t: Phase 3 Clinical Study Evaluating Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Obicetrapib Vs Bempedoic Acid to Treat Dyslipidemia in Adults With Primary Non-familial Hypercholesterolemia or Mixed Dyslipidemia at High to Very High Cardiovascular Risk, During a Treatment Period of Approximately 84 Days
trials.ep: Percent change in LDL cholesterol from baseline to Day 84

fable.r: Failure would need bempedoic acid to perform far better than in CLEAR or obicetrapib far worse than in BROADWAY; the expected 15-point LDL-C gap is many standard errors wide with 426 patients.

opus.r: Bempedoic acid is an active comparator lowering LDL-C about 16-18%; failure would need obicetrapib to underperform its roughly 30-33% placebo-adjusted effect seen in BROADWAY/BROOKLYN, which is unlikely with 213 per arm.

sonnet.r: Obicetrapib lowers LDL-C about 30% on statins versus about 15-18% for bempedoic acid, so superiority with 213 per arm is near certain; residual risk is a sponsor non-announcement or odd analysis.

haiku.r: Obicetrapib should lower LDL-C far more than the modest bempedoic acid response, so a superiority miss is unlikely and the main risks are timing and whether the sponsor announces results by June 2027.

carbon.r: Non-adherence to double-dummy oral regimens could slightly dilute treatment differences, although obicetrapib's substantially greater LDL-C lowering over bempedoic acid leaves wide statistical margin.

sol.r: Unexpectedly strong bempedoic-acid lowering, particularly among participants on little or no statin, could narrow obicetrapib's expected LDL-C advantage.

trials.t: A Study to Compare Safety of 4 Weeks Exposure to Propellants Hydrofluoroalkane 1,1-difluoroethane (HFA-152a) and HFA-1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (134a)
trials.ep: Number of participants with adverse events (AEs)

fable.r: A short crossover safety study in stable asthma run by GSK should enrol and finish close to schedule; results are due on the registry within a year of completion, so posting by August 2027 is possible but not the default.

opus.r: A short GSK crossover safety study supporting the low-GWP HFA-152a propellant switch; likely to complete close to schedule, with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov within about a year of completion, often after August 2027.

sonnet.r: GSK propellant safety crossover in 110 asthma patients at 18 sites; no efficacy goal. Start was September 2026, so enrolment drift of a few weeks is likely but a delay beyond late May 2027 is less common. Results posting normally follows within about a year of completion.

haiku.r: A safety-only propellant crossover of 110 patients, so the main delays would come from recruitment across 18 sites rather than from any efficacy issue.

carbon.r: This 18-site GSK 8-week crossover safety study in stable adult asthma uses straightforward inclusion criteria and should complete close to schedule with routine ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.

sol.r: Broad stable-asthma eligibility, short exposure periods and many sites favor timely completion, while registry results posting may lag completion by six to twelve months.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Elismetrep (K-304) in the Acute Treatment of Migraine
trials.ep: Percentage of participants pain-free at 2 hours post-dose after treating a migraine attack

fable.r: A novel TRPM8 mechanism backed by a single phase 2b could regress to a placebo-adjusted gain too small on 2-hour pain freedom or on the most-bothersome-symptom co-primary.

opus.r: Elismetrep is a first-in-class TRPM8 antagonist with a single phase 2 behind it; phase 3 effects are often smaller than phase 2, and both co-primaries (pain freedom and MBS freedom) must be met.

sonnet.r: Two co-primaries (2-hour pain freedom and MBS freedom) must both win; with 900 per arm power is high if the drug has gepant-like activity, but a novel mechanism carries real failure risk.

haiku.r: Both co-primaries must hit in the same arm, and freedom from the most bothersome symptom at 2 hours is usually the harder of the two, so the endpoint choice is the main risk.

carbon.r: As a non-triptan TRPM8 antagonist, elismetrep may yield a modest single-attack treatment effect insufficient to clear both 2-hour pain freedom and MBS freedom co-primary endpoints.

sol.r: The large sample supports modest effects, but uncertain drug-specific efficacy may prevent simultaneous improvement in pain freedom and the most bothersome symptom.

trials.t: Study Evaluating the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of ASY202 (Dihydroergotamine Mesylate [DHE] Inhalation Powder Delivered Via a Multidose Dry Powder Inhaler) for the Acute Treatment of Migraine in Adult Patients
trials.ep: Freedom from headache pain at 2 hours after a single dose for a moderate or severe migraine attack

fable.r: A 108-patient crossover loses power if patients fail to treat both attacks or if lung delivery from the dry-powder inhaler gives a smaller 2-hour pain-free gain than MAP0004 did.

opus.r: About 100 evaluable crossover patients give good but not overwhelming power; if the inhaled DHE effect is nearer 10 points than the 18 seen with MAP0004, or many patients fail to treat both attacks, significance could be missed.

sonnet.r: Inhaled DHE has shown about 38% vs 13% pain freedom at 2 hours in earlier work, so a 108-patient paired crossover should win; the risks are small size, patients missing a second attack, and a weaker dry powder delivery.

haiku.r: A 108-patient two-period crossover in which the paired design gives power only for a difference of about 12 points or more, so underpowering is the main risk.

carbon.r: Patient self-administration via a dry powder inhaler during an acute migraine attack can cause variable pulmonary drug delivery and attenuate 2-hour pain-free rates.

sol.r: The crossover improves efficiency, but approximately 100 evaluable patients leave pain freedom vulnerable to attack variability and uncertain pulmonary delivery.
