trials.t: A Phase 3 Study in India to Describe the Safety and Immunogenicity of RSVpreF
trials.ep: Proportion of participants reporting local reactions within 7 days following investigational product administration

fable.r: Short descriptive Pfizer vaccine study likely to finish close to schedule, with results posted near the 12-month deadline rather than by August 2027.

opus.r: A Pfizer local-registration safety and immunogenicity study of Abrysvo in India with 1-month immunogenicity and 3-month safety follow-up; likely completes near schedule, with ClinicalTrials.gov posting usually 6-12 months later.

sonnet.r: Pfizer descriptive safety and immunogenicity study of RSVpreF in India (540 adults, 13 sites) with no efficacy hypothesis; short follow-up and a registered completion of January 2027 make a large delay unlikely, and Pfizer usually posts results about a year after completion.

haiku.r: A descriptive safety and immunogenicity study in India with no efficacy hypothesis, so the risks are a registry date slip and whether results reach ClinicalTrials.gov on time.

carbon.r: Pfizer's descriptive Phase 3 safety and immunogenicity bridging trial of Abrysvo (RSVpreF) across 13 sites in India has short 1-to-3-month follow-up and should complete quickly with low termination risk.

sol.r: An established vaccine, modest regional sample and short follow-up favor completion near schedule, although registry results posting may lag database lock.

trials.t: A Phase II Clinical Trial of Efficacy and Safety of SAL0140 at Different Doses in Patients With Uncontrolled Hypertension
trials.ep: Change from baseline in mean seated systolic blood pressure at Week 12

fable.r: A large placebo fall in blood pressure, as in the HALO trial of baxdrostat, could hide the effect in arms of about 63 patients.

opus.r: SAL0140 is an unvalidated aldosterone synthase inhibitor; insufficient selectivity or dosing, plus a sizeable placebo response in Chinese office-BP trials, could shrink the placebo-adjusted fall below what 63 per arm can detect.

sonnet.r: Aldosterone synthase inhibitors lowered seated SBP by 8-11 mmHg over placebo in phase 2; the high dose should win, though placebo response and dose choice in a 63-per-arm study add noise.

haiku.r: Aldosterone synthase inhibitors have shown placebo-adjusted systolic falls near 9 mmHg in phase 3 (BaxHTN, 2025), so the high dose should separate from placebo unless SAL0140 is weaker than the class.

carbon.r: Large placebo blood pressure reductions from Hawthorne effects and regression to the mean in uncontrolled hypertension trials can compress treatment differences.

sol.r: Improved adherence to background antihypertensives and regression to the mean could produce enough placebo-arm blood-pressure reduction to obscure the incremental effect.

trials.t: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Pharmacodynamics, Safety and Tolerability of BGE-102 in Participants With Obesity and Cardiovascular Risk Factors
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in hsCRP at week 12

fable.r: hsCRP is highly variable and arms are small, so only poor exposure, adherence or tolerability at the tested doses would prevent a significant reduction.

opus.r: Only a much weaker NLRP3 pathway effect at the phase 2 doses than in phase 1, combined with the noisy, skewed hsCRP distribution in 40 per arm, could prevent significance.

sonnet.r: BGE-102 (brain-penetrant NLRP3 inhibitor) cut hsCRP by up to about 86% in obese phase 1 volunteers; at the top dose the win is near certain, with hsCRP variability the only noise.

haiku.r: Forty per arm with hsCRP percent changes spread near 50 points means only a large dose effect reaches significance, so the main risk is an underpowered and skewed outcome.

carbon.r: Oral small-molecule NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors carry class-related hepatotoxicity and tolerability risks that could trigger dose holds, discontinuations, or early termination.

sol.r: NLRP3 inhibition may not suppress chronic obesity-associated inflammation enough to separate reliably from a noisy, regression-prone hsCRP control response.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of BGM0504 Tablets in Overweight or Obese Participants Without Diabetes
trials.c: Overweight or Obese Participants Without Diabetes
trials.ep: Percent change from baseline in fasting body weight at week 20

fable.r: Oral bioavailability of the peptide tablet may give weight loss well below the injection, though even a few percent beyond placebo should be significant.

opus.r: An oral tablet of a GLP-1/GIP peptide depends on absorption enhancement; low or erratic bioavailability could leave the top dose with only a small weight effect at 20 weeks.

sonnet.r: An oral incretin agonist at its top dose over 20 weeks should separate clearly from placebo on percent weight change; the main risk is weak oral exposure or a published absolute-kg form.

haiku.r: With only 40 per arm at the highest dose, a 5 to 7 point weight difference should be significant, so the main risk is that this compound is weaker than the class expectation.

carbon.r: Oral tablet formulations of peptide incretin agonists face low and variable gastrointestinal bioavailability that could limit weight loss relative to injectable BGM0504.

sol.r: The main uncertainty is whether the tablet formulation achieves sufficient sustained exposure, since injectable incretin efficacy does not guarantee comparable oral activity.

trials.t: Evaluation of NuvastaticTM in Reducing Cancer-Related Fatigue in Colon Cancer Patients Undergoing First-Line Chemotherapy
trials.ep: Change from screening in Brief Fatigue Inventory score at 12 weeks

fable.r: A herbal extract with thin independent evidence faces a sizeable placebo response on self-rated fatigue during chemotherapy, and both fatigue scales must be met.

opus.r: A botanical polyphenol extract has little proven pharmacology against chemotherapy-related fatigue, placebo responses on BFI are large, and two fatigue primaries must both reach significance.

sonnet.r: Nutraceutical against placebo on a subjective fatigue score with two co-primaries that must both be met; placebo response and chemo-related fatigue swings can hide a small effect, though sponsor-run trials that report tend to be positive.

haiku.r: Nutraceutical-type sachet from a small sponsor with two near-duplicate co-primary fatigue measures that must both be met; subjective fatigue endpoints carry a large placebo response in chemotherapy patients, and 90 per arm gives limited power for a modest effect.

carbon.r: Botanical extracts rarely demonstrate reproducible superiority over placebo across co-primary subjective fatigue scales amid fluctuating chemotherapy toxicity.

sol.r: A small symptomatic benefit may be overwhelmed by chemotherapy-related fatigue changes and placebo response, with both registered primary fatigue measures needing to succeed.

trials.t: A Clinical Study to Compare BupiZenge With Lidocaine for Pain Due to Oral Mucositis in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer.
trials.ep: Total reduction in oral cavity pain (0-10 NRS) over 3 hours after a dose on the last day of radiotherapy

fable.r: The primary is a single-dose 3-hour pain reduction on the last radiotherapy day, when opioid use, attrition and lozenge intolerance in severe mucositis can blur the difference from lidocaine.

opus.r: Viscous lidocaine also gives real topical analgesia; over a 3-hour window the advantage of a slow-release bupivacaine lozenge may be too small for 75 per arm, and dropouts by the last day of radiotherapy shrink the analysed set.

sonnet.r: Open-label lozenge versus short-acting viscous lidocaine on the last day of radiotherapy; the longer duration of bupivacaine should favour the lozenge over 3 hours, but pain scores are subjective and the sample is modest.

haiku.r: Open-label pain integral over 3 hours on one radiotherapy day, with an unclear combined scale and an active lidocaine comparator; the endpoint definition and the short window are the likeliest failure points rather than the drug.

carbon.r: Severe late-radiotherapy oral mucositis and dysphagia may cause substantial attrition or missing pain assessments on the final day of radiotherapy.

sol.r: Severe mucositis, rescue analgesic use and missing ratings on the last radiotherapy day could erode a plausible duration-of-action advantage over lidocaine.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase Ⅲ Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of WD-890 Tablets for the Treatment of Moderate to Severe Plaque Psoriasis
trials.ep: Proportion achieving Physician's Global Assessment of clear (0) or almost clear (1) at week 16

fable.r: Failure would require WD-890 to be much less active than other TYK2 inhibitors on sPGA 0/1 or PASI 75, which its progression from phase 2 makes unlikely.

opus.r: The only realistic failure is a WD-890 dose with too little exposure to beat placebo on both PGA 0/1 and PASI 75 at week 16; placebo rates in Chinese psoriasis trials are low.

sonnet.r: Oral psoriasis agents in placebo-controlled week-16 trials almost always beat placebo on PGA 0/1 and PASI 75 by a wide margin; the main uncertainty is an unknown compound with a possibly weak dose.

haiku.r: The record gives no mechanism or dose; if WD-890 is weaker than validated oral psoriasis agents, a modest gap over placebo could leave one of the two co-primaries (PGA 0/1 or PASI 75) short of significance.

carbon.r: Unexpected opportunistic infections, laboratory abnormalities, or skin tolerability issues could reduce response rates under non-responder imputation.

sol.r: Without dose or earlier efficacy information, the principal risk is that WD-890 has insufficient activity to improve both PGA clearance and PASI 75 reliably.

trials.t: A Trial Comparing GQ1005 and T-DM1 in Patients With HER2-Positive Unresectable or Metastatic Breast Cancer
trials.ep: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1, up to about 24 months

fable.r: If GQ1005 is less active than deruxtecan-type conjugates, a 228-patient trial against T-DM1 could miss, and slow accrual against reimbursed T-DXd delays the readout.

opus.r: Failure would need GQ1005 to be clearly less potent than other topoisomerase-I-payload HER2 ADCs, or ILD and toxicity-driven dropouts to erode its PFS advantage over T-DM1.

sonnet.r: Next-generation HER2 ADC against T-DM1 in a pretreated population has a large expected effect; the main risks are a payload or dose that is not clearly better than T-DM1 and OS being immature at the PFS analysis.

haiku.r: A novel HER2 ADC against a strong T-DM1 comparator; if GQ1005 is only modestly better, 228 patients and roughly 150 PFS events may not reach significance, and overall survival is likely immature at the PFS readout.

carbon.r: Interstitial lung disease or hematologic toxicity associated with topoisomerase-I payload HER2 ADCs could trigger early discontinuations and censor BICR progression events.

sol.r: The small pivotal trial needs a substantial PFS advantage, and superiority of other HER2 ADCs over T-DM1 does not establish sufficient differentiation for GQ1005.

trials.t: Study on the Treatment of Adolescent Patients With Seasonal Allergic Rhinitis
trials.ep: Mean change from baseline in daily reflective total nasal symptom score (rTNSS, 0-12) over the first 2 weeks of treatment

fable.r: With 68 per arm and strong background therapy, an effect smaller than the adult -1.3 points (noisy adolescent diaries, large placebo response, possibly patients with low eosinophils) could leave the 2-week rTNSS difference short of significance.

opus.r: Adult data suggest about a 1-point rTNSS benefit over placebo on top of background therapy; with 68 per arm and an SD near 2.4, power is only about 60-70%, and pollen-season variability can shrink the difference.

sonnet.r: Anti-IL-4R alpha biologic as add-on in adolescents with SAR should beat placebo; the main risk is a short autumn pollen season with low symptom scores and a high placebo response in a 68-per-arm trial.

haiku.r: Only 68 patients per arm against a 0 to 12 symptom score with SD near 2.6 leaves the 2-week effect near the edge of significance if the adolescent gap is smaller than in adults.

carbon.r: High adherence to background intranasal corticosteroids and antihistamines or variable pollen exposure in adolescents could narrow the treatment difference over two weeks.

sol.r: Background therapy and declining pollen exposure may produce a large placebo-arm improvement, obscuring a roughly one-point incremental benefit in this small adolescent cohort.

trials.t: A Clinical Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of SHR-1819 Injection in Patients With Seasonal Allergic Rhinitis
trials.ep: Mean change from baseline in daily reflective total nasal symptom score (rTNSS) over the first 2 weeks of treatment

fable.r: If the population is not enriched for high eosinophils, the IL-4Ra effect on 2-week rTNSS may be only about -0.6 points, as in the stapokibart all-comer phase 2, against a large placebo response in a short pollen-season trial.

opus.r: The anti-IL-4Ra benefit on rTNSS over a strong placebo-plus-background response is only about 1 point; a mild pollen season or modest exposure could shrink it below significance even with 110 per arm.

sonnet.r: IL-4R alpha blockade works in SAR and 110 per arm is well powered; residual risk is a weak autumn pollen season lowering symptom scores and compressing the treatment difference.

haiku.r: With 110 per arm the trial is well powered, so the main risk is a smaller effect than assumed at a 2-week primary with a high pollen-season placebo response; the mechanism and dose are not stated in the record.

carbon.r: Substantial placebo and background medication improvement or waning seasonal pollen counts could attenuate the 2-week rTNSS separation.

sol.r: Rapid seasonal improvement and concomitant symptom treatment could reduce the incremental rTNSS effect below the roughly 0.6-point difference needed for significance.

trials.t: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of SC0032, a Magnesium Salt Oral Spray, in Adults With Refractory or Unexplained Chronic Cough
trials.c: Refractory Chronic Cough and Unexplained Chronic Cough
trials.ep: Percent change in 24-hour cough frequency (HYFE monitor) from baseline (days -8 to -2) to days 13-19 of treatment

fable.r: A magnesium salt oral spray has only small exploratory support for cough suppression; with about 30 per arm and highly variable cough counts, only an unusually large placebo-adjusted effect (roughly 35%) would reach significance.

opus.r: A magnesium-salt oral spray has no proven antitussive mechanism in refractory chronic cough, placebo arms cut cough frequency by about 20-30%, and 30 per arm can detect only a large effect.

sonnet.r: Topical magnesium oral spray is an unproven mechanism in refractory chronic cough; a 30-per-arm pilot on a noisy cough count has little power unless the effect is large.

haiku.r: A pilot with about 30 per arm on a noisy 24-hour cough count; the placebo-adjusted gap has to be large to clear 0.05, so a modest real effect would most likely be missed.

carbon.r: Topical airway magnesium salt spray lacks strong clinical validation for suppressing refractory chronic cough reflex hypersensitivity against a large placebo response.

sol.r: A magnesium salt spray has limited established evidence for suppressing objective chronic cough, while placebo response and between-patient variability are substantial.

trials.t: A Study of CA201A Eye Drops to Prevent Corneal Endothelial Cell Loss in Patients Undergoing Cataract Surgery
trials.c: Corneal Endothelial Cell Loss; Corneal Endothelial Damage Following the Hard Nuclear Cataract Surgery
trials.ep: Change from baseline in central corneal endothelial cell density (specular microscopy) in the study eye at week 12 after cataract surgery

fable.r: Modern phacoemulsification in mostly grade 3 nuclear cataract causes modest endothelial loss (about 8-10%), leaving little room for a topical antioxidant to show a significant difference when the between-patient SD is near 300 cells/mm2.

opus.r: Topical ascorbic acid may protect the endothelium only modestly; with endothelial cell loss SD near 300 cells/mm2 and 100 per arm, a benefit under about 80 cells/mm2 is unlikely to reach significance.

sonnet.r: Endothelial cell density change after phaco is noisy (SD near 280 cells/mm2) and a topical antioxidant is likely to preserve only a modest number of cells; 100 per arm detects roughly 80 cells.

haiku.r: A protective gap of about 40 cells/mm2 against a loss near 190 with SD near 200 gives limited power at 100 per arm; if the true effect is small, the trial misses its primary endpoint.

carbon.r: Topical 5% ascorbic acid drops four times daily may not maintain high enough intraoperative aqueous humor antioxidant concentrations to meaningfully reduce phacoemulsification endothelial loss.

sol.r: Topical ascorbate may add little to existing surgical protection, and variation in cataract hardness and phacoemulsification energy can overwhelm a modest antioxidant effect.

trials.t: A Clinical Trial of HRS5580 for Injection Combined With Palonosetron Hydrochloride for the Prevention of Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting
trials.c: Prevention of Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting
trials.ep: Complete response (no vomiting and no rescue therapy) within 72 hours after extubation

fable.r: With about 87 per arm, a 10-15 point gain in 72-hour complete response over palonosetron alone gives only about 30-55% power per dose; rescue use driven by nausea dilutes an NK1-type benefit that is mainly on vomiting.

opus.r: Palonosetron alone already gives roughly half of high-risk patients a complete response, and rescue use is partly nausea-driven, so the NK1 add-on benefit may be only about 10-15 points, borderline with about 87 per arm.

sonnet.r: Adding a likely NK1-class agent to palonosetron in high-risk PONV patients should raise vomiting-free rate; with a dose-finding design any dose meeting the objective suffices, but 87 per arm is limited if palonosetron control is already strong.

haiku.r: Palonosetron alone is a strong 72-hour control, so the add-on must lift complete response by about 12 points with 87 per arm; a flat dose response at the higher dose is the most likely failure.

carbon.r: With roughly 87 patients per arm, higher-than-expected complete response on palonosetron alone could leave a real additive antiemetic benefit short of statistical significance.

sol.r: Palonosetron may already prevent much of the vomiting, leaving an incremental complete-response benefit too small for approximately 87 patients per dose.

trials.t: A Multicenter, Randomized, Parallel-Group, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase II Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of QY201 Tablets in Subjects With Non-Segmental Vitiligo
trials.ep: Percentage change from baseline in Facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI) at week 24

fable.r: Percent change in F-VASI is noisy (SD about 40) and 50 per arm gives only about 65% power per dose for a 20-point difference at 24 weeks; a high placebo response in a single-country trial would erode it further.

opus.r: Facial repigmentation by week 24 is often still partial with oral JAK-pathway inhibitors, and with about 50 per arm and a high SD in percent F-VASI change, a weaker compound may miss significance.

sonnet.r: Phase 2 dose-ranging in vitiligo with three doses and a placebo; any dose beating placebo on F-VASI percent change at week 24 suffices, but facial repigmentation is slow and noisy with 50 per arm.

haiku.r: Oral agent at three doses against placebo, with 50 per arm at the top dose; any dose meeting the bar counts, but a flat dose response or a weak class effect would fail the 24-week F-VASI comparison.

carbon.r: Facial repigmentation at 24 weeks can lag behind longer treatment durations if baseline vitiligo activity is high or ambient UV exposure is low.

sol.r: An oral immunomodulator may arrest disease activity before producing enough facial repigmentation for the week-24 endpoint, particularly in longstanding stable lesions.

trials.t: Phase II Clinical Trial of SHR-1139 Injection in Patients With Psoriasis
trials.ep: Proportion of patients achieving 100% improvement in PASI from baseline (PASI 100) at week 12

fable.r: Arms are small (60 patients split across dose groups and placebo), so a PASI 100 rate near 25-30% at week 12 could miss significance against a near-zero placebo rate.

opus.r: PASI 100 at week 12 is a demanding endpoint; with about 30 per arm and near-zero placebo response, the drug needs roughly 15-20% complete clearance to reach significance, which a weaker or slow-onset biologic could miss.

sonnet.r: Placebo PASI 100 at week 12 is near zero, so even an IL-23-class response of 15-20% with 30 per arm is borderline significant; an IL-17-class response would clear it easily. Main risk is a weaker-than-expected antibody.

haiku.r: Phase 2 with 30 per arm and no stated dose. A potent biologic should clear placebo on PASI 100, but the small size and dose choice leave room to miss, and a public statement by June 2027 is uncertain.

carbon.r: If the 60 patients are split across multiple unstated dose arms, small per-arm sample sizes could reduce power for the stringent week-12 PASI 100 threshold.

sol.r: Complete clearance is a demanding 12-week endpoint, so an effective but slower or lower-exposure antibody could produce too few PASI100 responders in this small study.

trials.t: A Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of AT673 Co-administered With Semaglutide in Adult Participants With Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) and Overweight or Obesity
trials.c: Adults With Overweight/Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 13, with background semaglutide

fable.r: Whether a GIP receptor antagonist adds weight loss to semaglutide in humans is unproven; over 13 weeks with semaglutide only up to 1.0 mg, an extra loss under about 1.2 points would not be significant with 50 per arm.

opus.r: Whether GIPR antagonism adds meaningful weight loss on top of semaglutide in people with type 2 diabetes is unproven in humans; over only 13 weeks during semaglutide titration the add-on effect may be about 1% or less, below what 50 per arm can detect.

sonnet.r: Only 13 weeks of exposure on top of semaglutide titration, so incremental weight loss from AT673 may be small relative to a noisy 50-per-arm comparison; HbA1c add-on benefit is even less certain.

haiku.r: Add-on to semaglutide with 50 per arm. The extra weight loss from AT673 may be only about 1.5 points, near the edge of significance, and the 50 mg dose is the one that counts for the card.

carbon.r: Thirteen weeks during initial semaglutide titration in patients with type 2 diabetes is short to separate incremental weight loss over active GLP-1 therapy.

sol.r: GIP antagonism may add less than about 1.5 percentage points of early weight loss to semaglutide, while semaglutide itself drives most of the observed response.

trials.t: Phase 2 Trial of a Haemophilus Influenzae Serotype a (Hia) Glycoconjugate Vaccine
trials.c: Haemophilus Influenzae; Haemophilus Influenzae Type a
trials.ep: Immediate Adverse Events Following Immunization

fable.r: Small safety and immunogenicity vaccine study that is already fully enrolled; follow-up to 240 days after dose 2 should finish close to the registered date, and results posting is unlikely before late 2027.

opus.r: Enrollment is done, but the registered primary completion of Feb 2027 looks computed from the study start, while the 240-day post-dose-2 SAE window for the last enrollees likely runs into mid-2027.

sonnet.r: Small safety/immunogenicity phase 2 with 47 enrolled and a 240-day post-dose-2 safety window; the registered end date looks slightly early versus the 29 April 2026 start, and the adaptive design could add enrolment, so a slip past early May is plausible.

haiku.r: Safety-only phase 2 vaccine trial with 47 adults in Canada and no efficacy goal. It should run to its February 2027 primary completion with little change; the open questions are registry updates and results posting.

carbon.r: Enrollment is already complete at two experienced Canadian vaccine centers, so follow-up through February 2027 should finish on schedule with minimal risk of termination or amendment.

sol.r: Recruitment appears complete and remaining safety follow-up should finish near schedule, although registry results posting may lag completion considerably.

trials.t: Safety and Efficacy of HRS-9190 Compared to Rocuronium for Tracheal Intubation and Bolus Maintenance in Adults
trials.ep: Proportion of patients with excellent or good intubation conditions (Cooper score) within 5 minutes after study drug administration

fable.r: Non-inferiority would fail only if the chosen HRS-9190 dose gives slower or weaker block at the intubation time point, since rocuronium yields good or excellent conditions in nearly all patients.

opus.r: Rocuronium gives good or excellent intubation conditions in over 90% of patients; if HRS-9190 has a slower onset at the chosen intubation time, its rate could fall below the non-inferiority margin.

sonnet.r: Rocuronium sets a ceiling of roughly 95% good/excellent conditions, so non-inferiority is likely unless the unknown margin is tight or HRS-9190 onset is slower at the assessed time.

haiku.r: Bolus NMBA tested for non-inferiority against rocuronium with no margin in the record. Failure would mean a slower or less reliable onset of intubating conditions at 5 minutes.

carbon.r: Slightly slower neuromuscular onset at the selected bolus dose could lower the rate of excellent or good intubation conditions within 5 minutes relative to rocuronium.

sol.r: A slower or less reliable onset than rocuronium could make a tight non-inferiority margin difficult despite the generous five-minute assessment window.

trials.t: Study of d-MAPPS™ Ophthalmic Solution in Adults With Chronic Ocular Graft-Versus-Host Disease (oGVHD)
trials.c: oGVHD; Ocular Graft Versus Host Disease
trials.ep: Change from baseline to day 90 in Modified Oxford corneal staining score (0-5) in the study eye

fable.r: With 15 patients per arm and two co-primary endpoints that must both be significant, the trial needs an implausibly large advantage over a lubricating vehicle to succeed.

opus.r: With about 15 patients per arm and two co-primary endpoints (corneal staining and OSDI) that must both reach significance against a vehicle with a sizeable placebo response, the trial has low power even if the drops work.

sonnet.r: Only 15 per arm with two co-primary endpoints that must both be significant; vehicle response in dry-eye type endpoints is large and an unproven agent needs a big effect on both staining and OSDI.

haiku.r: Co-primary design, so both corneal staining and OSDI must be significant. With 15 per arm the OSDI comparison is underpowered unless the true benefit is large.

carbon.r: With only 15 patients per arm and substantial vehicle lubrication responses, the study is severely underpowered to hit both corneal staining and OSDI symptom co-primary endpoints simultaneously.

sol.r: Fifteen patients per arm provide little protection against heterogeneous staining responses, and both staining and OSDI must improve significantly.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety in Participants With Uncontrolled Hypertension on Two or More Medications Including Participants With Resistant Hypertension
trials.ep: Change from baseline to week 12 in seated systolic blood pressure

fable.r: A large placebo fall in office systolic pressure, as in HALO, or weak dose selection could blur separation when each arm has only about 64 patients.

opus.r: The design mirrors aldosterone synthase inhibitor trials, where the effect is about 8-10 mmHg; a weaker drug or a large Chinese placebo response, plus the second primary needing week 4 and 8 significance too, could sink it.

sonnet.r: Placebo-controlled 12-week BP trials on top of two or more drugs show large placebo responses of 7-9 mmHg; the top dose must beat that by about 5-6 mmHg at n=64 per arm, which is likely for an active antihypertensive but not certain.

haiku.r: Three doses against placebo on week 12 seated SBP, with 64 per arm and one dose needed. The main risk is a high dose that falls short of a clear SBP effect; the record lists Phase 3 but describes a Phase 2.

carbon.r: Large placebo office blood pressure reductions and requirement to demonstrate consistent efficacy across listed timepoints could attenuate the placebo-adjusted treatment difference.

sol.r: Improved adherence and regression to the mean may produce a substantial placebo-arm pressure reduction, leaving insufficient separation across the registered time points.

trials.t: Phase 2 Study of MWN109 Tablet in Participants With Overweight or Obesity
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 20

fable.r: The oral formulation might give too little exposure for a clear separation by week 20, or the result may be disclosed only as positive without an explicit primary-endpoint statement.

opus.r: An oral incretin peptide's success depends on adequate oral bioavailability; if exposure at the top dose is low, weight loss at 20 weeks could be only a few percent, though 48 per arm still detects about 3%.

sonnet.r: Top dose of an oral incretin-type agent over 20 weeks in about 50 per arm should clearly separate from placebo; residual risk is a weak molecule or the announcement not stating the primary was met.

haiku.r: Oral once-daily weight-loss agent with titration against placebo at 20 weeks, 51 per arm. The highest dose is assumed to be MWN109 4; a weak effect or poor tolerability would be the main way to miss.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal adverse events during 20-week oral dose titration could drive early treatment discontinuations and attenuate intention-to-treat weight loss at the highest dose.

sol.r: The main efficacy uncertainty is whether the undisclosed oral formulation achieves enough exposure during titration to deliver a substantial 20-week weight-loss effect.

trials.t: Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of MWN109 Injection in Non-Diabetic Participants With Overweight
trials.ep: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 36

fable.r: Failure would need an unexpectedly weak drug or heavy dropout in arms of about 31, or a public statement that only calls the result positive without a primary-endpoint finding.

opus.r: Injectable incretin agonists reliably beat placebo by 10% or more over 36 weeks; the only plausible failure is an unexpectedly weak molecule or high dropout in a 31-per-arm trial.

sonnet.r: With about 31 per arm and SD near 5.5%, only a very weak injectable would fail to beat placebo on 36-week weight change at the top dose.

haiku.r: Injectable weight-loss agent at 36 weeks with three doses against placebo, about 31 per arm. The high-dose effect is large enough to be significant even at this size; the main risk is GI-driven dropout or AE discontinuation.

carbon.r: Gastrointestinal intolerability at top titrated subcutaneous doses is the main risk, though multiple dose arms buffer overall primary endpoint success.

sol.r: Gastrointestinal intolerance and treatment discontinuation could substantially dilute the highest-dose effect over 36 weeks, particularly with only about 31 patients per arm.

trials.t: Phase 2 Clinical Study of MWN109 Tablets in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
trials.ep: Change from baseline in HbA1c at week 20 versus placebo

fable.r: Inadequate oral exposure at the tested doses, or a strong placebo response on background metformin, could shrink the HbA1c gap in arms of about 40 patients.

opus.r: Incretin agonists lower HbA1c by about 1 point versus placebo in metformin-treated T2D; failure would need very poor oral exposure, since 40 per arm detects about 0.5 points.

sonnet.r: A GLP-1-class agent at top dose in T2D with baseline HbA1c 7.5-11% reliably lowers HbA1c by more than 1 point vs placebo; the residual risk is mostly whether and when results are made public.

haiku.r: Placebo-controlled HbA1c at week 20 on a metformin background, 40 per arm. The highest MWN109 dose is assumed; a weaker-than-hoped effect is the main way to miss.

carbon.r: High gastrointestinal discontinuation or limited oral bioavailability at tolerated doses could narrow the HbA1c separation from placebo.

sol.r: Inadequate oral exposure or a poorly tolerated titration could leave the HbA1c effect too small after adjustment for multiple doses.

trials.t: Phase 2 Study of MWN109 Tablet for Weight-Loss Maintenance in Participants With Overweight or Obesity
trials.ep: Percentage change in body weight compared to baseline after 24 weeks of drug administration

fable.r: The 24-week extension has passed its registered primary completion and should close quietly, with no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, as is usual for Chinese phase 2 sponsors.

opus.r: Open-label maintenance extension that is fully enrolled and past its registered completion; it will most likely just be marked completed without posted results.

sonnet.r: Small open-label weight-maintenance extension that has already passed its registered primary completion; a Chinese private sponsor rarely posts results or edits primary outcomes, and no stop is expected.

haiku.r: Open-label 24-week extension comparing two MWN109 dosing schedules, with no control arm and no efficacy goal. The record is active, not recruiting with a passed primary completion date, so it should run to close with little change.

carbon.r: With enrollment of 71 rollover responders completed and status active, not recruiting past its September 2026 registered completion date, this open-label China extension should finish cleanly without posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027.

sol.r: With recruitment closed and the planned endpoint already passed, administrative completion is more likely than termination, but prompt ClinicalTrials.gov results posting is unlikely.

trials.t: Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of TJO-087
trials.ep: Change from baseline in corneal fluorescein staining score (NEI scale) at week 12

fable.r: With 30 patients per arm, the modest edge of an anti-inflammatory drop over a lubricating vehicle on corneal staining is unlikely to reach significance.

opus.r: With about 30 patients per arm and a large vehicle response typical of dry eye trials, a realistic staining difference under one NEI point is unlikely to reach p<0.05 even with two doses tested.

sonnet.r: Vehicle drops usually improve corneal staining a lot over 12 weeks, and with about 30 per arm in a single-site phase 2 a modest true effect is easily lost; two doses give one extra chance.

haiku.r: Two-dose phase 2 with only 30 per arm on a noisy corneal staining endpoint; the higher dose can carry it, but a one-point gap is hard to detect at this size.

carbon.r: Lubricating vehicle eye drops and regression to the mean from baseline NEI staining >=4 typically produce large control improvements relative to ~30 patients per arm.

sol.r: Vehicle lubrication and regression to the mean can improve staining enough that a 30-per-arm comparison misses significance despite some biological activity.

trials.t: Platform Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Anti-malarial Agents in Participants With Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria (Cohort C2)
trials.ep: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at Day 29 in children aged 2 to under 12 years

fable.r: Coartem cures about 95-99% of children on PCR-corrected day-29 response, so a single-dose combination cannot show a statistically significant improvement in a 120-patient cohort.

opus.r: Coartem cures about 95% of African children by PCR-corrected ACPR, leaving no room for a significant superiority result with 60 per arm; the cohort is descriptive and not built to beat the standard of care.

sonnet.r: Coartem already gives PCR-corrected ACPR near 97 to 99 percent in African children, so superiority with 60 per arm is nearly impossible; this open-label phase 2 platform cohort is estimation-oriented with no formal test.

haiku.r: Superiority over Coartem at 60 per arm needs a gap near 7 points, unlikely if the control cures about 94 percent; the answer depends on whether the sponsor framed a non-inferiority hypothesis.

carbon.r: Three-day Coartem cures ~96-98% of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children, leaving virtually no room for superiority and high risk of late recrudescence after a single oral dose.

sol.r: Coartem already cures nearly all evaluable cases, leaving little room for a 120-child trial to demonstrate superiority even if the single-dose combination is highly effective.

trials.t: A Phase 3 Study Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of TRIESENCE® (Injectable Suspension) for the Treatment of Ocular Inflammation and Pain After Ophthalmic Surgery
trials.c: Postoperative Ocular Inflammation; Postoperative Ocular Pain
trials.ep: Proportion of subjects with no anterior chamber cells (grade 0) at Day 14 after ophthalmic surgery

fable.r: A high rate of spontaneous anterior chamber cell clearing by day 14 in untreated micro-incision cataract eyes could shrink the gap, and both the inflammation and pain endpoints must be met.

opus.r: Two co-primaries must both be met; the anterior chamber cell endpoint is the weaker one, as Dextenza's second phase 3 missed day-14 cell clearing when the vehicle arm cleared 31% of eyes on its own.

sonnet.r: A depot corticosteroid versus untreated sham should clear anterior chamber cells clearly, but both co-primaries must be met and the Day 8 no-pain endpoint has a high placebo rate and smaller expected gap.

haiku.r: A steroid depot against no treatment should separate clearly on day-14 cell grade; both co-primaries must be met by the same arm, and the day-8 pain endpoint is the likelier miss.

carbon.r: Spontaneous resolution of postoperative pain by Day 8 or mild inflammation in micro-incision cataract surgery could narrow sham-controlled responder differences.

sol.r: The most vulnerable requirement is pain freedom at Day 8, when uncomplicated small-incision cataract surgery may already leave many sham patients pain-free.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of GW906 in Patients With Essential Hypertension
trials.ep: Change from baseline to Week 12 in mean sitting office systolic blood pressure

fable.r: If the tested doses give less angiotensinogen knockdown than zilebesiran, or patients stay on background therapy, the office systolic effect could shrink toward the roughly 5 mmHg seen in KARDIA-3.

opus.r: With 160 per arm and an SD near 14 mmHg, any placebo-adjusted office SBP fall beyond about 4 mmHg is significant; failure needs a weak dose or a large placebo response in office readings.

sonnet.r: A long-acting subcutaneous antihypertensive with a 6-month double-blind design in 319 patients is very likely to separate from placebo on week 12 office SBP; the main uncertainty is the effect size at the lower dose and the chance it is not reported.

haiku.r: Single undisclosed dose against placebo in about 160 per arm; the main risk is a placebo-adjusted fall too small to show, since placebo responses in Chinese BP trials are large.

carbon.r: Regression to the mean and white-coat blood pressure habituation in office sphygmomanometry could inflate placebo reductions if pharmacodynamic knockdown is suboptimal.

sol.r: The principal risk is insufficient sustained pharmacologic activity at week 12 rather than inadequate statistical power in the 319-patient comparison.

trials.t: Clinical Evaluation of a Toothpaste for Dental Plaque Reduction and Prevention of Gum Problems
trials.ep: Whole-mouth Lobene Modified Gingivitis Index score, change from baseline at 6 months

fable.r: All three indices (gingivitis, bleeding, plaque) must be significant for the same arm; plaque, or a required win over the active 67% bicarbonate paste, is the least certain, and a result posted without a clear statement on the primary outcomes would also count as not met.

opus.r: Three primaries (gingivitis, bleeding, plaque) must all be significant with about 40 per arm; the plaque index is the likeliest to miss against a regular fluoride paste.

sonnet.r: Stannous fluoride usually beats regular fluoride toothpaste on gingivitis, bleeding and plaque over 6 months, but about 40 per arm and three co-primaries that must all be met leave a real chance one misses.

haiku.r: Small study where the gingivitis gap over fluoride is near the detection limit; all three co-primaries must be met, and the registry date looks out of date.

carbon.r: If the primary hypothesis requires statistical superiority across all three co-primary plaque and gingivitis indices against the active 67% sodium bicarbonate comparator in addition to the negative fluoride control, the narrower margin against bicarbonate could prevent full primary success.

sol.r: With about 40 patients per arm, a modest plaque effect or near-tie against 67% bicarbonate could prevent all registered primary outcomes from meeting the required comparisons.

trials.t: A Study to Evaluate ENERGI-F703EB Cream in Epidermolysis Bullosa
trials.c: Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB); Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa; Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
trials.ep: Incidence of Local Target Lesion Adverse Events

fable.r: Adults with epidermolysis bullosa and paired chronic wounds of 10-40 cm2 are scarce in Taiwan, so enrolling 24 in five months with one site listed is unlikely; expect the completion date to slip well past June 2027 and no results posted by the read date.

opus.r: A 24-adult EB trial in Taiwan with matched lesion pairs started in October 2026 and must finish enrolment and 12 weeks of treatment and follow-up by March 2027, which a rare-disease sponsor will likely miss.

sonnet.r: Tiny phase 2 safety study in a rare disease at Taiwanese sites: slow recruitment of 24 adults with matched EB lesion pairs makes primary completion slippage likely, with some risk of early closure; a small sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027.

haiku.r: Rare-disease trial of 24 that only started recruiting in October 2026; slippage beyond the registry dates is the likeliest event, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

carbon.r: Recruiting 24 adult epidermolysis bullosa patients in Taiwan who each have two matched chronic 10-40 cm2 non-joint target lesions and completing up to 16 weeks of participation within five months of study start makes a substantial completion delay highly likely.

sol.r: Recruiting 24 adults with two persistent, size-matched qualifying EB wounds in Taiwan is likely to take substantially longer than the initial schedule allows.

trials.t: A Study of Cebranopadol for Opioid Withdrawal Symptoms in Adults With Chronic Pain
trials.ep: Peak Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale total score (0-48) over 48 hours after first dose, adjusted for rescue medication

fable.r: Fifteen patients per arm leave little margin: if placebo withdrawal is milder than expected in pain patients on 50-90 MME, or the rescue adjustment narrows the gap, a real 3-point difference in peak COWS would miss significance.

opus.r: With 15 per arm, a moderate placebo withdrawal peak and the slow onset of cebranopadol could leave early withdrawal unsuppressed, so the peak-COWS difference may not reach significance.

sonnet.r: A full opioid agonist like cebranopadol should blunt precipitated withdrawal, but with 15 per arm and a noisy peak COWS the result is borderline-powered even for a sizeable effect.

haiku.r: Only 15 per arm, so a significant peak-COWS gap needs about 4 points; a strong opioid-receptor agonist should suppress withdrawal, but rescue medication and the small sample leave a real chance of a miss.

carbon.r: With only 15 participants per arm, substantial inter-patient variability in acute opioid withdrawal trajectories, rescue medication adjustments, and potential multiplicity testing across two dose regimens could leave a real pharmacological effect short of statistical significance.

sol.r: Peak withdrawal may be driven by the hours before cebranopadol reaches effective concentrations, while small groups and rescue-medication adjustments amplify variability.
